verdict.summary: In ConcatShapeHelper, the attacker-controlled concat axis value flows into `const int min_rank = concat_dim < 0 ? -concat_dim : concat_dim + 1` (line 47). For any concat_dim >= 2^31-1 or <= -2^31 (full int64 domain admitted by the DT_INT64 read at line 44; boundary INT32_MAX for the DT_INT32 read), the int64 computation is narrowed into `int`, yielding a negative or zero min_rank, and `concat_dim + 1` overflows at INT64_MAX / `-concat_dim` at INT64_MIN. The negative min_rank nullifies the protective `WithRankAtLeast(input, min_rank, ...)` gates (lines 51, 67), so the unvalidated concat_dim reaches `Subshape(..., concat_dim, ...)` (lines 52, 68) and `Dim(input, concat_dim)` (lines 53, 69) as an out-of-domain index/length with no visible bound, enabling an out-of-bounds read in shape inference from a crafted graph.

evidence.reason: Primary CWE-190 sink. concat_dim is read unvalidated from the entry-point axis tensor (full int32/int64 domain, line 42/44); only its container shape is checked (line 4), never its value. The int64 result of `-concat_dim`/`concat_dim + 1` is narrowed into `int`: concat_dim = 2147483648 (in-domain DT_INT64) yields 2147483649 truncated to -2147483647; concat_dim = INT64_MAX wraps concat_dim+1 to INT64_MIN then truncates to 0; concat_dim = INT64_MIN wraps `-concat_dim`. The negative/zero min_rank then defeats WithRankAtLeast (lines 51, 67), whose admitted set becomes every shape, so the input-derived concat_dim reaches Subshape (52, 68, 57, 73) and Dim (53, 69) as an index/length with no effective capacity bound (CWE-125 consequence).

Consuming sink for the corrupted bound. On the witness path (concat_dim = 2147483648, min_rank = -2147483647, WithRankAtLeast at line 51 admits any rank, so rank is unbounded relative to concat_dim), the index argument concat_dim = 2^31 is outside the domain a shape-index operation requires ([0, rank)); no visible check connects concat_dim to the shape's rank, so the call receives an out-of-domain index while the only protective gate was nullified by the line-47 overflow/narrowing.

assumptions: concat_dim_t is the Concat axis input tensor; line 4 constrains only its shape (rank 0), leaving the scalar's int32/int64 value at the full declared domain.

Two's-complement truncating narrowing of int64 to int on the supported platforms (implementation-defined but universal for TensorFlow's targets); unsigned integral wrap for the INT64_MAX/INT64_MIN arithmetic.
WithRankAtLeast(input, r) admits shapes whose (non-negative) rank is >= r; a negative r therefore admits all shapes.
Dim(shape, index)/Subshape(shape, start, end) index into the shape's dimension list in [0, rank); arguments outside that range are out of the operation's domain at the call site.
limitations: The exact callee-side consequence of the out-of-domain index (bounds-checked error vs raw out-of-bounds read) is inside Dim/Subshape bodies, which are not shown; the confirmed defect is the shown derivation of the out-of-domain argument and the defeat of the shown guard.
Negative concat_dim values other than -1 (e.g., -2) pass min_rank >= 2 but their safety depends on unshown negative-index semantics inside Dim/Subshape; not confirmed here.

Loop `for (int i = end_value_index - 2; i >= start_value_index; --i)` could in principle wrap (i-- past INT_MIN) only for extreme internal start_value_index/end_value_index values with no shown constraint; rejected as an internal-helper hypothesis with no attacker-visible provenance in the fragment.
dims.reserve(rank) (line 32) scales an allocation with c->Rank, but rank magnitude is framework-supplied with no shown cap; unconfirmable as resource exhaustion.

concat_dim = INT32_MAX via the DT_INT32 read is a single-edge witness; the DT_INT64 witness range (concat_dim >= 2^31 or <= -2^31) is a wide, non-degenerate range and is the basis for the calibrated confidence.

verdict.summary: Tensor::FromProto decodes the attacker-controlled tensor_content() with an element count N derived from the shape (N > 0, line 7-8) without validating content.size() against N (or N * sizeof(T)), so a non-empty short content with a larger N causes an out-of-bounds read inside Helper<T>::Decode at line 12 (CWE-125). FromProtoField<T> at line 15 is invoked with the same unvalidated N against proto value fields whose count the fragment never bounds. The p == nullptr check at line 18 runs after the read and only covers allocation failure, not short-buffer decode.

evidence.snippet:
CASES_WITH_DEFAULT(proto.dtype(), p = Helper<T>::Decode(a, content, N),
                         dtype_error = true, dtype_error = true);
evidence.reason: Sink: Decode consumes N elements from content. N (const int64_t, line 7) has residual range [1, INT64_MAX] after the N > 0 guard (line 8); content (line 11) has residual range [1, +oo) bytes after the non-empty guard (line 10). No shown statement relates content.size() to N or N*sizeof(T), so an admitted input (shape {2} -> N=2, dtype DT_UINT8, content.size()=1) reaches Decode needing 2 bytes with 1 available, producing an out-of-bounds read of content (CWE-125). The p == nullptr check at line 18 executes after the read and admits the non-null result, so it does not protect the sink; the missing validation (a size/equality check before line 12) is the defect.

evidence.snippet:
CASES_WITH_DEFAULT(proto.dtype(), p = FromProtoField<T>(a, proto, N),
                         dtype_error = true, dtype_error = true);
evidence.reason: Sink: FromProtoField consumes N values from the proto's typed fields. N retains residual range [1, INT64_MAX] (lines 7-8) and the fragment neither counts nor bounds the supplied values, so a proto declaring more elements than it supplies values makes FromProtoField read past the available field values (CWE-125, same missing-bound class as the Decode sink). The line 18 check only tests p == nullptr and runs after the call, so it cannot prevent the out-of-domain consumption.

assumptions: proto is an entry-point input: the function parses an externally supplied serialized TensorProto, so no caller-side trust bound is assumed.
Helper<T>::Decode consumes N elements of type T from the content byte string (name-implied decode semantics), requiring content.size() >= N * sizeof(T).
FromProtoField<T> consumes N element values from the proto's typed value fields.
CASES_WITH_DEFAULT dispatches valid DataType values to the case body and sets dtype_error for invalid/default dtypes.
DT_UINT8 has sizeof(T) = 1 (standard scalar semantics used only for the illustrative witness; the finding is a missing-bound flow independent of the exact byte size).
limitations: The exact byte-level arithmetic of Decode/FromProtoField is not shown, so the finding is anchored as a validated missing-bound flow at the call sites (lines 12, 15) rather than a fully demonstrated in-function overread; confidence is correspondingly range-based (0.62).

CHECK_NOTNULL(a) (line 2) can abort on a NULL allocator, but NULL 'a' is a caller contract not produced by the proto and not attacker-directed in the fragment; treated as a robustness concern, not a finding.

The incomplete-shape path (lines 19-28, N = -1) assigns buf_ = p with p == nullptr and returns true; no dereference of buf_ occurs inside the fragment and the only shown use (line 35) is NULL-guarded, so downstream null-consumption cannot be confirmed here.
Potential integer overflow of N * sizeof(T) inside Decode/FromProtoField is not computable from the fragment and is not reported.

If a patched Decode/FromProtoField internally rejected short buffers, the overread would be contained; however, the fragment itself still lacks the local size validation that a fix would add, so the missing-bound defect stands.

The guard admits every `alloc_size > 0`, including positive values produced by int wrap of the byte-size computation for large admitted counts; the resulting line-4 allocation is smaller than the `size` elements stored at line 6, making later `ret->data[]` accesses out of bounds. Primary mechanism: CWE-190 integer overflow corrupting an allocation-size/count pairing.

Stores the unvalidated int parameter `size` (residual range: full int domain; line 3 bounds only the derived `alloc_size`) into the returned object's element-count field after line 4 allocated `alloc_size` bytes. No shown statement establishes that the allocation holds `size` elements, so negative or wrapped-positive counts make the advertised length inconsistent with the backing capacity, and consumers using `ret->size` as the bound for `ret->data[]` exceed the allocation. Same CWE-190 root cause; this field is the count consumed as the downstream index/length.

`TfLiteIntArrayGetSizeInBytes` returns the total bytes for a `TfLiteIntArray` with `size` elements (name-implied semantics); only its result type `int` and its consuming use are visible.
`TfLiteIntArray` has an `int size` field (line 6) and a flexible `data[]` array that callers index using `ret->size`.
Line 3's guard admitted set for `alloc_size` is `[1, INT_MAX]`; line 5 excludes NULL before the line-6 dereference.
`malloc`'s `size_t` parameter receives the admitted non-negative `int` range by exact widening.
limitations: The exact body of `TfLiteIntArrayGetSizeInBytes` is not shown, so a single concrete `size` value that wraps int to a small positive byte count cannot be demonstrated from the fragment; the witness is a residual-range claim, capping confidence at 0.55.

The downstream out-of-bounds access (callers reading/writing `ret->data[0..ret->size-1]`) is outside the fragment; the confirmed in-fragment mechanism is the unvalidated count / overflowing byte-size derivation (CWE-190), and a secondary memory-corruption CWE is not independently confirmed.

Negative counts (e.g., `ret->size = -1`) can also pass the line-3 guard whenever the helper yields a positive byte size; their downstream effect depends on unshown consumers and is not separately confirmed.
`malloc` failure returns NULL through line 5 and no security-relevant operation runs on the failure state; not a finding.

The zero-length variant (`alloc_size == 0` leading to a write through `malloc(0)`) is excluded by the `<= 0` comparison at line 3; that is line 3's genuine protective role, which does not cover the overflow-to-positive case.

Line 36 then invokes post_shuffle(input), whose body line 27 evaluates tensor.dim_size(3) / num_groups = 1 / 0 -> division by zero; pre_shuffle line 21 contains the identical expression. The only path guards (NHWC DCHECK at lines 7-9, formatting only) are satisfied, so the crash is reachable on an admitted input; CWE-369.

verdict.summary: The unbounded byte-copy loop in diST_box_read copies attacker-controlled bytes from the bitstream bs into the fixed 1024-byte stack buffer str (declared at line 4) using a u32 index i that is never checked against the buffer size. Any run of 1024 or more non-zero bytes causes a write past the end of str at line 10 (first out-of-bounds write at i=1024), and the zero-byte break at line 11 executes only after the write, so it cannot prevent the overflow. evidence.reason: Stack out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). The destination str is declared at line 4 as `char str[1024];`, giving capacity 1024 with valid indices 0..1023. The index i (u32, line 3) starts at 0 (line 7) and is incremented once per non-zero byte read from the entry-point bitstream bs (line 12), with no bound check in the `while (1)` loop at line 9. A byte run of length n writes at str[0..n]; for n >= 1024 the iteration i=1024 at this sink writes 1 byte past the buffer, and every further non-zero byte writes deeper out of bounds. The only conditional on the path (line 11, `if (!str[i]) break;`) executes after this write on the same iteration and cannot prevent it. The byte stream from bs is unconstrained by the fragment, so the overflow is fully attacker-directed.

assumptions: gf_bs_read_u8(bs) returns the next byte of the parsed bitstream bs, which carries attacker-controlled file/network data; no constraint on the byte stream is shown in the fragment.
The capacity of str is 1024 bytes as declared at line 4, so valid indices are 0..1023.

limitations: Missing NULL checks on the four Tensor* parameters: no shown statement can produce NULL on any path, so under TensorFlow's non-null Tensor contract this is a robustness/hardening concern, not a CWE finding.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability in the shown fragment. The dangerous-looking operations are protected by visible statements: line 16 initializes qeh->qeh_tsu_sz to exactly sizeof(qeh->qeh_tsu_buf) before passing it as the in/out capacity to lsqpack_enc_init (lines 17-19), lines 17-23 convert any init failure into an early return -1 before QEH_HAVE_SETTINGS is set (line 25), and line 8 blocks double-initialization. The unsigned settings parameters (max_table_size, dyn_table_size, max_risked_streams) flow unvalidated into lsqpack_enc_init at line 18, but the fragment performs no arithmetic on them and derives no index, length, capacity, or pointer from them, so no out-of-domain consumption is demonstrable from the shown code; the remaining hypotheses (NULL qeh, field narrowing, unshown-callee overflow, assert abort) are unconfirmable or caller-contract robustness concerns.

assumptions: qeh->qeh_tsu_buf's capacity is sizeof(qeh->qeh_tsu_buf), and line 16 assigns exactly that value to qeh->qeh_tsu_sz before it is passed as the callee's in/out size at line 19.
lsqpack_enc_init honors the in/out *tsu_sz capacity contract (the post-init used size is logged at line 24) and reports failure through its return status, which is checked at lines 17-23.
QEH_HAVE_SETTINGS is the only re-entry gate and is set only after successful initialization (line 25), so the line 8 guard fully prevents double-initialization in the shown code.
All log statements (lines 10, 21, 24, 28-29) use literal format strings whose %zu/%u specifiers match their unsigned/size_t arguments.
limitations: max_table_size/dyn_table_size/max_risked_streams (lines 1-2) reach lsqpack_enc_init (line 18) with their full unsigned domain and no visible bound, but no shown statement performs arithmetic on them or derives an index/length/capacity from them, and the callee's internal validation behavior is not shown; the missing-bound hypothesis requires callee behavior beyond the fragment and is therefore not confirmed.

qeh is dereferenced at lines 6 and 8 without a NULL check, but NULL is not producible by any shown statement and the assert at line 6 encodes the initialization contract; treated as a robustness/caller-contract concern, not a confirmed CWE-476.

Potential narrowing of the size_t return of lsqpack_enc_header_block_prefix_size into qeh_max_prefix_size (lines 26-27) and of sizeof(qeh_tsu_buf) into qeh_tsu_sz (line 16) cannot be evaluated because the destination member types are not shown in the fragment.

The assert at line 6 would abort only if QEH_INITIALIZED were clear; no shown path can clear it, it is compiled out under NDEBUG, and no attacker-directed value in the fragment reaches it — not a reachable CWE-617.
The return value of qeh_begin_out (line 31) is discarded, but no security-relevant state in the fragment depends on it (CWE-754 not confirmed).
The fragment contains no loops, so no iteration-bound, parser-position, or non-termination analysis applies.
qeh_conn, qeh_enc_sm_out, and the qeh_encoder field contents are framework state consumed only by unshown code paths; no invariant about them is needed for the verdict.

verdict.summary: The splice implementation is protected at every dangerous sink. `start` is clamped to [0,length] (line 26), `delete` to [0,length-start] (lines 32/42), so `start+items <= length+delta`; the final length is capped by `(length+delta) > NJS_MAX_LENGTH` (line 47), `deleted` is allocated with capacity `delete` (line 54) for the indexed loops (lines 61-62, 68-83), and the fast path grows storage via `njs_array_expand` before relocation and the `memcpy` (lines 102-106, 120-122). No input-derived index or size can exceed a visible capacity, so no memory-safety, arithmetic, or logic flaw is confirmed in the fragment.

assumptions: Fast njs arrays satisfy capacity >= recorded length, so indices < array->length into array->start are valid; the in-fragment delete loop at lines 61-63 already relies on this.
njs_array_alloc(vm, 0, delete, 0) (line 54) allocates deleted->start with capacity for `delete` elements, so indices in [0, delete) are in bounds.
njs_array_expand(vm, array, 0, delta) (line 103) grows the elements buffer to hold at least array->length + delta entries, per the standard helper's name-implied semantics.
The engine guarantees args[0..nargs-1] exist, so &args[3] with items*sizeof(njs_value_t) bytes (items = nargs-3) is a valid source range.
NJS_MAX_LENGTH is the framework's maximum array length; the check at line 47 enforces length+delta <= NJS_MAX_LENGTH.
limitations: The received fast array's capacity (>= its length) is a framework invariant not declared in the fragment; for delta <= 0 the memcpy at lines 121-122 writes within the first `length` slots relying on it.

The expansion guarantee (capacity >= length+delta) is name-implied, not shown; if it were weaker, the delta>0 relocation and memcpy could be out of bounds, but no such defect is demonstrable from the fragment.

If a generic object exposed a length property greater than NJS_MAX_LENGTH, `delete` could drive a very large njs_array_alloc and a long tail-delete loop; allocation failure is handled by returning NJS_ERROR (lines 55-57), so this is an availability concern, not a confirmed memory-safety flaw.
The `backward` flag passed to njs_array_copy_within (0 at line 110, delta<0 at line 129) affects element order inside a standard library helper, not memory safety, and was not treated as a finding.

verdict.summary: The fragment contains no confirmed security vulnerability. The only input-derived hazard with a visible path, an empty key tensor reaching map->put, is fully excluded by the guard at lines 14-15 (key_tensor->NumElements() > 0), which executes before every use of key. The values loop is bounded by the collection's own size, and the unvalidated indices_tensor/values tuple are forwarded unchanged to an unshown callee, which cannot be confirmed as a flaw from the shown code.

assumptions: OP_REQUIRES_OK and OP_REQUIRES return from Compute before any later statement when their condition fails, so pointers map, key_tensor, indices_tensor, and values_tensor are valid non-null on the continued path (standard macro semantics used by the fragment).
values_tensor.size() returns the exact number of elements in the OpInputList and is the capacity used by the loop at lines 21-23.
Tensor copy construction (lines 18 and push_back at line 22) is a shallow refcounted copy of an already-allocated tensor; no attacker-scaled new allocation originates in the fragment.
NumElements() returns the non-negative element count of a Tensor, which is why the guard at line 14 restricts the residual range to >= 1 element.
limitations: map->put (line 26) is not shown; any requirement put imposes on the key, indices, or tuple contents (such as indices/values consistency or non-empty values) cannot be confirmed, and no index/size/length is derived from those inputs at the call site.
indices_tensor is an unconstrained entry-point input but is never consumed by any shown statement; a missing-validation claim has no visible sink and is not a confirmed finding.

An empty values list or empty indices tensor are admitted by the shown code, but no visible operation fails on them; the only empty-input hazard with a visible path (empty key) is excluded by lines 14-15.

Large attacker-controlled tensors could cause resource pressure, but copies are shallow and the tensors are pre-allocated by the runtime; treated as a robustness/DoS concern, not a confirmed memory-safety finding.
If the intended post-fix behavior of map->put requires exactly one key element (rather than merely >= 1), that requirement is not visible in the fragment and cannot be used to assert a vulnerability.

verdict.summary: A rank-0 (scalar) input tensor reaches `input.dim_size(ndims - 1)` (line 5) and `rhs.dim_size(ndims - 1)` (line 6) before the `ndims >= 2` guard executes (line 9), producing a shape index of -1 (out of the valid `[0, ndims-1]` domain, which is empty for rank 0). The unvalidated, entry-point-derived shape index triggers a bounds-checked abort/CHECK-failure (or out-of-domain shape access) in the accessor, causing a reachable denial of service (CWE-617).

evidence.reason: Entry-point tensor shape: `ndims = input.dims()` (line 4) is unconstrained at this point, retaining the full domain including 0; the only rank guard, `ndims >= 2` (lines 8-11), executes AFTER this sink on every path, so it admits the witness `ndims = 0`. Then `ndims - 1 = -1` is passed to `input.dim_size(...)`, whose index domain is `[0, ndims-1]` (empty for rank 0); the out-of-domain index triggers the shape accessor's bounds-checked abort (or an out-of-bounds shape read), a reachable DoS: CWE-617.

Same ordering flaw: with rank-0 `rhs`, index `ndims - 1 = -1`; additionally, for `input` of rank 2 (`ndims = 2`, index 1) and `rhs` of rank 0 or 1, index 1 exceeds `rhs`'s valid index domain. The guard that would reject these, `rhs.dims() == ndims` (line 12), executes after this sink and cannot protect it. Out-of-domain index reaches a bounds-checked shape accessor (CWE-617 reachable abort / DoS).

assumptions: `Tensor::dim_size(d)` is a shape-index accessor whose parameter is an index with domain `[0, dims()-1]`, as implied by the shown code's own valid uses at indices `ndims - 2` (lines 18-20) and `dim` (line 30) under the `ndims >= 2` guard.
`Tensor::dims()` returns a non-negative `int`, so the adversarial rank-0 value is within the declared type domain.
`context->input(0)` and `context->input(1)` shapes are entry-point data; the fragment provides no earlier constraint on them.
limitations: The rank-0 witness is a degenerate (zero-length shape) input whose minimum is not established by any shown derivation, and the exact abort behavior lives in the unshown `dim_size` implementation; confidence capped accordingly.
Shown-code validations at lines 9, 12, 17-21, 22-27, and 28-34 correctly protect the later `dim_size(ndims - 2)`/`dim_size(dim)` uses, which are in-domain after `ndims >= 2`.

Potential non-termination/UB in `for (int batch = 0; batch < batch_size; ++batch)` (lines 105-107, 119-125) for `batch_size > INT_MAX` is demoted: it needs an input of at least 2^31 elements, and the wrap semantics of signed increment are outside the fragment.

Potential int64 overflow of `kMaxMatrixSizeToBatchSizeRatio * batch_size` (line 98-99) needs `batch_size > 2^55` and has no demonstrated security-relevant consumer; `NumElements() * sizeof(Scalar)` overflow needs > 2^61 elements and is physically infeasible.
`uint8` scratch space (lines 94-96, 103-104) reinterpreted as an aligned pointer array is a robustness concern, not attacker-scaling in the shown code.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. start/delete are clamped to [0, length] and [0, length - start] (lines 26, 42), and the check at line 47 bounds length + delta (and therefore start + items, the memcpy destination end, and both length stores) by NJS_MAX_LENGTH. Every write loop matches the count passed to the visible allocation/expansion (lines 54, 97), the memcpy source is exactly the in-bounds args[3..nargs-1] span (items = nargs - 3, line 35), and all return values are checked. Confidence is moderate only because the backing capacities of array->start / deleted->start, njs_array_alloc's parameter types, and the value of NJS_MAX_LENGTH are not visible in the fragment.

assumptions: args is an array of nargs elements; when nargs > 2, args[3..nargs-1] holds exactly items = nargs - 3 elements (lines 34-35), so the memcpy source range at lines 115-116 is exactly the in-bounds argument span.

length (line 16) is the object's element count for the object `this`; the fragment uses it as the clamp bound (line 26), the delete base (lines 32, 42), the copy count source (lines 103-104, 122-123), and the final length base (line 145).
NJS_MAX_LENGTH (line 47) is a non-negative constant, so the guard admits length + delta <= NJS_MAX_LENGTH and excludes length + delta > NJS_MAX_LENGTH.

njs_array_expand (line 97) and njs_array_alloc (line 54) honor the count arguments passed to them (their contracts are used to argue the write loops and memcpy are consistent with the visible requests).
limitations: The capacities of array->start and deleted->start are not visible; an OOB at lines 62 or 115-116 would require the callee to under-allocate relative to the delete/items arguments the fragment derives (or an unshown int64-to-uint32 truncation in njs_array_alloc's length parameter). This cannot be confirmed from the shown statements and is not a demonstrated excess.

njs_array_alloc's parameter types are not shown, so a narrowing of delete > 2^32-1 (possible only for a non-fast object with an unbounded `length`, e.g., nargs==2 with start=0 at line 32) is unconfirmable; the direct deleted->start[i] write additionally requires the fast-array branch at line 59, for which length is the object's own length.
The value of NJS_MAX_LENGTH is not visible, so whether the derived destination bound (start + items <= length + delta <= NJS_MAX_LENGTH) is within real backing allocations cannot be fully verified.
sizeof(njs_value_t) is not shown; items * sizeof(njs_value_t) with items <= 2^32-4 does not overflow size_t on a 64-bit target, but the exact byte count is unverifiable.
A near-INT64_MAX value for `length` has no shown producer, so integer-overflow candidates in the line-47 expression are unconfirmable in both directions.
The sparse-copy semantics at lines 74-80 (skipping NJS_DECLINED property reads) is not a defect: absent elements are intentionally not copied, and array length is set explicitly at lines 83 / 145.

verdict.summary: Out-of-bounds read in the GPU MatrixSolve ComputeAsync: `rhs.dim_size(ndims - 1)` (line 6) and `input.dim_size(ndims - 1)` (line 5) index tensor dim lists using `input`'s rank before the rank checks at lines 9 and 12 execute, so a rank-mismatched or rank-0 tensor (e.g., input rank 2, rhs rank 1) reads past the dim-vector capacity (CWE-125).

evidence.reason: Entry-point tensor rhs (line 3) has unconstrained rank at this point, and index `ndims - 1` is taken from input's rank (lines 4-5) with no preceding guard: with input rank 2 (ndims=2) and rhs rank 1, the index is 1 while rhs's dim list has capacity 1 (valid indices 0..0), so the read immediately overruns by one element. The rank-equality check at line 12 and the ndims>=2 check at line 9 execute after this sink, so they cannot protect it (CWE-125 out-of-bounds read).

With a scalar input (ndims=0, capacity 0), `ndims - 1` is -1, reading input's dim list before the `ndims >= 2` check at line 9 executes. Same unvalidated-index/out-of-bounds-read mechanism as line 6 (CWE-125); the post-sink rank guard does not cover this read.

assumptions: TensorShape::dim_size(d) is used as its name/contract implies: it consumes an index that must satisfy 0 <= d < dims(); in TensorFlow it is enforced only by DCHECKs, which are compiled out in release builds, making the shown out-of-domain index an unchecked OOB read.
Tensor dim values and ranks are non-negative (TensorShape invariant), so index validity reduces to 0 <= index < dims().
The empty-input early return at lines 38-41 guarantees NumElements() > 0 and batch_size >= 1 on all remaining paths, which is why no degenerate zero-element witness is used.
limitations: The `for (int batch = 0; batch < batch_size; ++batch)` loops (lines 98, 112, 145) use an int counter against an int64 bound; a batch_size above INT_MAX would overflow the counter, but that magnitude cannot be demonstrated from the shown statements and is capped by the unshown tensor allocation, so it is demoted.
Extremely large n/nrhs feeding cuSolver/cuBlas calls are bounded by the input tensors' own (unshown) allocation; no demonstrated excess.
The dim reads at lines 18 and 22 are in-domain because they execute after the ndims>=2 check (line 9) and the rank-equality check (line 12) on their paths.
No injection, crypto, file, or authorization sinks are present in the fragment.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the guarded/fixed form of mrb_ary_shift_m. The input n is bounded on every path that reaches a sink: line 14 returns when len==0 || n==0, line 15 raises for n<0, and line 16 clamps n to len. The residual range is therefore 1 <= n <= len with len >= 1, which keeps mrb_ary_new_from_values (line 17), the shared-branch pointer/length updates (lines 20-21), and the in-place shift loop (lines 35-38; maximum read index n + size - 1 == len - 1, line 39 length len-n >= 1) inside the len-element buffer. No OOB, truncation, underflow, NULL-deref, or error-status flaw is derivable from the shown statements.

assumptions: ARY_LEN(a) (line 10) and ARY_PTR(a) (lines 17, 32) are the standard mruby RArray macros: the element count and a pointer to a buffer holding exactly len elements; for a shared array, ARY_LEN(a) reads a->as.heap.len, so len bounds the pointer/length updated at lines 20-21.
mrb_get_args with format '|i' (line 5) either returns 0 (early return at line 6, n unused) or stores a valid mrb_int in n.
limitations: NULL-dereference concerns for mrb_ary_ptr(self) (line 9) and ARY_PTR(a) (lines 17, 32) are not findings: no shown statement can produce a NULL pointer, and the receiver is a Ruby Array value whose macro conversion semantics are framework-guaranteed.
The no-argument delegation path to mrb_ary_shift (line 6) is outside the fragment.

Allocation/exception behavior of ary_make_shared (line 25) and mrb_ary_new_from_values (line 17) is not shown and is not attacker-directed here; no security-relevant operation runs on any failure state in the fragment.
ARY_SHIFT_SHARED_MIN is an unshown macro constant; its value does not affect the bounds analysis because the clamp at line 16 executes before every branch.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the patched 1-bit decode path of ReadPSDChannelPixels. The inner decode loop is clamped by number_bits=min(8, columns-x) at lines 61-63 before the SetPSDPixel writes, so indices stay in [0, columns-1] and q advances exactly image->columns times against the columns-pixel row obtained at line 27; the x re-alignment at lines 70-71 preserves chunk boundaries. No confirmed vulnerability: no out-of-domain index/size, integer wrap, injection, NULL deref, or status-handling flaw is derivable from the shown statements.

assumptions: GetAuthenticPixels(image,0,row,image->columns,1,exception) at line 27 returns a non-NULL row buffer of exactly image->columns pixels; this is the visible capacity used for the q/x bound analysis.
Outer loop invariant: at every entry to the loop body, x < (ssize_t) image->columns (line 32), so number_bits at line 61 is always >= 1 and <= 8 after the clamp at lines 62-63.
packet_size takes values {1, 2, else(4)} per the branch chain at lines 34, 37, 42.
limitations: The capacity of the pixels buffer is not shown in the fragment; the read pattern (ceil(columns/8) bytes for depth<=1, columns*packet_size for depth>1) is self-consistent with the decode layout, so an over-read cannot be confirmed from the shown arithmetic (potential caller/allocation mismatch is out of scope).

indexes = GetAuthenticIndexQueue(image) at line 30 is forwarded to SetPSDPixel without a NULL check; confirming a NULL dereference would require SetPSDPixel's body and the image's storage class, neither of which is shown.
GetPSDPacketSize's derivation is not shown; only the values 1, 2, and the float fallback branch are observable in the fragment.
The cast (ssize_t) image->columns could wrap negative for columns > SSIZE_MAX, but that only skips the loop body; no overflow of x (ssize_t) is reachable within the shown bounds.
The depth<=1 bit-mask decode assumes packet content from ScaleCharToQuantum (line 35); truncation of pixel to unsigned char at line 67 is lossless for that path and is only used in a mask test.

verdict.summary: adts_decode_extradata copies attacker-controlled PCE data from the extradata bitstream into adts->pce_data, whose only visible capacity is the MAX_PCE_SIZE token passed to init_put_bits at line 40, without any check that the copied size fits that capacity. A crafted AudioSpecificConfig with chan_config==0 and a large PCE (many channel elements) passes every guard (lines 19, 23, 27, 31, 35, 39) and causes ff_copy_pce_data (line 43) to write beyond the destination, a heap/struct out-of-bounds write (CWE-787).

evidence.reason: Sink: ff_copy_pce_data(&pb, &gb) copies input-derived PCE bits from gb (positioned after skip_bits_long at line 14, content from entry-point buf/size unvalidated by any shown statement) into pb, whose destination buffer adts->pce_data has the visible capacity token MAX_PCE_SIZE set at line 40 (init_put_bits(&pb, adts->pce_data, MAX_PCE_SIZE)). The PCE element counts are admitted by every guard on the path (line 19 >3U rejects only objecttype outside {0..3}; line 23 rejects only index 15; lines 27/31/35 reject only flag bits 1; line 39 admits chan_config==0), and no shown statement bounds the copied bit count against MAX_PCE_SIZE. The fragment's own arithmetic (X+3)/8 on the un-bounded, un-error-checked return would yield pce_size > MAX_PCE_SIZE for any PCE longer than the capacity, and the out-of-bounds write occurs inside the copy itself — missing-bound OOB write, primary CWE-787.

assumptions: init_put_bits(&pb, adts->pce_data, MAX_PCE_SIZE) at line 40 fixes the destination capacity of pb; MAX_PCE_SIZE is the only capacity token visible for adts->pce_data in the fragment.
ff_copy_pce_data(&pb, &gb) copies the PCE data remaining in gb into pb, with the copied amount derived from input bitstream element counts (name-implied semantics of the helper).
Standard GetBitContext behavior: get_bits returns 0 once the read position passes the initialized end; used only where noted (past-end reads), not to justify the verdict.
limitations: The exact overflow byte count and the numeric value of MAX_PCE_SIZE are outside the fragment, so the OOB write is established as a sound range claim (any PCE longer than MAX_PCE_SIZE bytes), capping confidence at 0.65.

ff_copy_pce_data's return value is not checked for a negative error before computing adts->pce_size (line 43) and calling flush_put_bits (line 44); the downstream security-relevant consumer of pce_size is not in the fragment, so the error/status-handling concern is demoted (no confirmed in-fragment impact).

The upper bound of off from avpriv_mpeg4audio_get_config2 (line 11) is not re-validated before skip_bits_long (line 14); no shown overread results because subsequent get_bits reads clamp past the end, so this is not a finding.
The unsigned comparison (adts->objecttype > 3U) at line 19 already rejects the object_type==0 -> objecttype==-1 case; no issue there.

verdict.summary: The parser can be driven into a never-advancing infinite loop by a CDATA section whose first ']' is not followed by ']]>' (e.g. ``), because `pj_scan_get_until_ch` (pinned by the PI/comment branches to stop at, not consume, the delimiter) cannot advance when `curptr` already sits on ']' inside the while body (lines 98-101); the guard at line 98 keeps admitting the same bytes forever (CWE-835). Independently, `xml_parse_node` recurses with no depth bound at lines 24/40/83, so attacker-controlled nesting or repeated PIs/comments cause unbounded recursion and stack exhaustion (CWE-674).

evidence.reason: Non-termination sink (CWE-835): entry-point XML admitted by guards at lines 8, 12, 28, 50, 53, 76, 80, 88, 93-94 reaches the CDATA loop. Line 97 leaves curptr AT the first ']' (semantics pinned by lines 16-19/32-35, which test *curptr immediately after the call and consume the delimiter only via pj_scan_advance_n). When the bytes there are not ']]>' (guard line 98 admits them), the body's only advancing call, pj_scan_get_until_ch(scanner,']',&dummy) at line 100, starts with curptr already on ']' and makes zero progress, so line 98's condition is byte-identical forever. Demonstrated witness: ``.

Uncontrolled-recursion sink (CWE-674): the sub-node loop at lines 80-85 calls xml_parse_node once per child element while the guards at lines 80-81 admit every '<' whose next byte is not '/' or '!'. The fragment contains no depth cap, so recursion depth equals attacker-chosen input nesting depth (range claim, up to message length); peak stack growth is unbounded and exhausts the stack (or trips the unshown PJ_CHECK_STACK limit).

Same uncontrolled-recursion flaw (CWE-674) reachable without element nesting: a message of consecutive processing instructions (`<?x?><?x?>...`) makes each PI branch recurse at line 24 before parsing the next PI, so recursion depth equals the attacker-chosen count of PIs with no shown bound.

Same uncontrolled-recursion flaw (CWE-674) via consecutive comment constructs (`<!...><!...>...`): each comment branch recurses at line 40, so recursion depth equals the attacker-chosen comment count with no shown bound.

assumptions: pj_scan_get_until_ch leaves scanner->curptr AT the delimiter without consuming it; this is pinned by the fragment's own PI branch (lines 16-19: *curptr tested right after the call, then pj_scan_advance_n(2) skips '?>') and comment branch (lines 32-35).
The XML byte stream in `scanner` is externally supplied (entry-point provenance); the fragment is the parser's consume site.
The exact stack size at which uncontrolled recursion crashes is an external runtime invariant, not visible in the fragment.
limitations: attr->value.slen -= 2 (line 62) producing a negative length for unquoted/empty attribute values depends on the unshown pj_scan_get_quotes contract (line 59); not confirmable from the fragment alone, so demoted with no CWE.
Potential attribute-loop non-termination for inputs with empty attribute names (e.g. `<a >`) depends on unshown pj_scan_get_until_chr delimiter/EOF positioning semantics; demoted.
Reads of *(scanner->curptr+1)/+2 (lines 12, 80-81, 93, 17) at buffer edges rely on scanner framing (NUL-terminated input buffer / endptr) that is not shown; no OOB-read claim was confirmed.
alloc_node/alloc_attr NULL returns (lines 44, 54) would be dereferenced, but allocation failure is not attacker-directed and is a robustness concern, not a finding.
on_syntax_error paths (lines 9, 71, 77, 108, 114, 118) are the parser's intentional malformed-input error handling; not treated as reachable-abort findings.
The exact recursion depth that exhausts the stack is runtime-dependent; recursion is reported as a range claim (CWE-674), calibrated to 0.62.

verdict.summary: digest_generic_verify passes the unvalidated parameter `md` into crypto_memneq at line 13 with no NULL check anywhere in the fragment; supplying `md == NULL` with any positive `len` (line 4, unconstrained int) on the digest_final success path (line 10 admits ret==0) dereferences NULL, causing a NULL-pointer access/crash.

evidence.reason: `md` is a pointer-typed parameter (line 1) with no NULL or capacity validation in the shown code (lines 3-19 contain no test of `md`); `len` (line 4, `int len = digest_length(d);`) is unconstrained, so positive values are admitted. On the path line 4 -> line 7 -> line 9 -> line 10 (guard `if (ret)` admits `ret == 0`) -> line 13, `md == NULL` with `len > 0` makes crypto_memneq read from NULL, a NULL-pointer dereference (CWE-476). The guard at line 10 covers only digest_final's status and does not protect `md` or `len`.

assumptions: digest_length(d)'s return is stored in `int` and the fragment imposes no constraint, so `len` retains the full `int` domain, including the positive values the witness requires.

xmalloc(len) (line 7) yields a valid `len`-byte buffer on the ordinary success path; its failure is an unchecked allocation treated as a robustness concern, not attacker-directed, since the size does not scale with attacker data.
crypto_memneq(a, b, n) reads `n` bytes from both buffers, as implied by its name and constant-time-comparison use.
limitations: An OOB read of `md` when `len` exceeds the caller's buffer is not separately confirmed: no capacity for `md` is visible and the true range of digest_length's return depends on its unshown body.

The negative-length variant (`len < 0` converting to a huge `size_t` at line 13, CWE-195) is demoted: reaching the comparison with a negative `len` requires xmalloc/digest_final to succeed on an out-of-range size (unshown allocator/callee semantics), and it is subsumed by the confirmed NULL dereference at the same sink.
tmp is used unchecked after xmalloc (line 7 -> line 9); this is an environment-failure robustness concern, not a confirmed vulnerability.
No loops, injection, weak-crypto, file, or authz sinks exist in the fragment; crypto_memneq provides the constant-time comparison (no timing side channel).

verdict.summary: num_slices = input.dim_size(axis_) flows unvalidated into the loop at line 49 and indexes output_min_tensor/output_max_tensor (allocated with minmax_shape, i.e. input(1)'s element count) and the min/max range vectors at lines 51-54. No shown check binds num_slices to minmax_shape.num_elements(), so any input where the axis dimension exceeds the range-tensor element count causes out-of-bounds writes (and reads) inside the kernel.

evidence.reason: Index i (0..num_slices-1, loop line 49) derives from num_slices = input.dim_size(axis_) (line 8) with axis_ >= 0 admitted by the only axis guard (line 7). output_min_tensor is allocated with minmax_shape (lines 31-34), whose element count from line 11 is the only visible capacity. No statement binds num_slices to that capacity, so for any admitted input with dim_size(axis_) > minmax_shape.num_elements() (range claim, e.g. 4 slices vs 1-element min tensor) i reaches values exceeding capacity and this flat write is out of bounds -- CWE-787 OOB write, missing-bound flow.

Same unvalidated i (loop line 49, sourced from input.dim_size(axis_) at line 8, no relation to minmax_shape.num_elements() from lines 11/31-34) writes output_max_tensor beyond its allocated element count whenever num_slices exceeds that count -- CWE-787 OOB write.

min_ranges(i) reads input_min_range at index i (0..num_slices-1 per line 49); the tensor's element count equals minmax_shape.num_elements() (line 11) and is never validated against num_slices (line 8). When num_slices exceeds that count, indices at/after the capacity are out-of-bounds reads -- CWE-125 read, same missing bound as the primary write.

max_ranges(i) reads input_max_range at the same unvalidated index i; no shown capacity or bound links num_slices (line 8) to input(2)'s element count, so indices beyond that count are out-of-bounds reads -- CWE-125, same missing-bound root cause.

assumptions: output tensors 1 and 2 have capacity minmax_shape.num_elements() because they are allocated with minmax_shape (lines 31-34), with minmax_shape taken from ctx->input(1).shape() (line 11).
On the loop path axis_ >= 0: axis_ <= -1 leads to num_slices == 1 and the early return at line 18.
The 3-D views built at lines 36-46 place the slice dimension with extent num_slices at dimension 1.
Tensor dim sizes and min/max tensor element counts are entry-point-supplied runtime values with no shown upper constraints.
limitations: The primary witness is a range claim (num_slices > num_elements(minmax_shape)); magnitudes are chosen attacker values read by the shown statements rather than constants, capping confidence at 0.65.
The OOB reads at lines 51-52 share the same missing bound as the primary write, so no independent secondary CWE is added.
Scalar-branch reads flat<float>()(0) at lines 21-22 assume an empty min/max tensor (no shown minimum element count); possible CWE-125 but not reported as the primary finding.

axis_ is unbounded above: axis_ >= input.dims() makes output->dim_size(i) (lines 40/43) and flat_inner_outer_dims(axis_-1) (line 37, negative when axis_==0) out-of-domain; callee-dependent, not separately confirmed.
Possible narrowing of input.dim_size(axis_) into int num_slices (line 8) cannot be confirmed because dim_size's return type is not visible in the fragment.
Int64 overflow of pre_dim/post_dim products would require a tensor with > INT64_MAX elements, an invariant not establishable from the shown code.

verdict.summary: afra_box_read is the guarded (patched) form: the line 14 guard bounds entry_count by floor(size/16) when long_offsets is set and floor(size/12) otherwise, matching the per-entry byte consumption exactly (16 or 12 bytes), and every stream read in both the local and global entry loops is individually preceded by an ISOM_DECREASE_SIZE bounds check. No value admitted by the shown guards can read past the remaining box payload or write out of bounds, so no vulnerability is confirmed from the fragment alone.

assumptions: ISOM_DECREASE_SIZE(ptr, N) verifies at least N payload bytes remain and returns GF_ISOM_INVALID_FILE otherwise, decrementing ptr->size by N on success (name-implied from the ten call sites in the fragment).
gf_bs_read_u32/u64/u16 and gf_bs_read_int consume exactly their nominal bit widths from bs.
gf_malloc allocations are fixed-size (sizeof(GF_AfraEntry) / sizeof(GF_GlobalAfraEntry)) and their results are checked at lines 19 and 39.
gf_list_insert manages a dynamically sized list, so ascending insert indices i cannot exceed a fixed capacity.
limitations: A NULL dereference of s/ptr is not reported: no shown statement can produce NULL for the box parameter, and its validity is a framework allocator invariant outside the fragment.

The global entry loop has no pre-loop count guard (only ISOM_DECREASE_SIZE(ptr, 4) before reading global_entry_count), but every field read is individually guarded; any deficit returns GF_ISOM_INVALID_FILE before the read.

Truncated-stream overreads inside gf_bs_read_* and the maximum admissible declared box size depend on the bitstream/box-parser framework, which is not shown, so a huge-entry_count resource-exhaustion scenario (up to 2^32-1 iterations if the declared size exceeds ~2^36 bytes) is unconfirmed here.
The gf_list_insert return value is discarded at lines 31 and 61; an insertion failure would only leak an already-allocated entry, and no NULL list state is shown.
ISOM_DECREASE_SIZE is a macro whose body is not expanded in the fragment; its protective effect is taken from its name and usage as a bounds check.

verdict.summary: simplifyBroadcast indexes shape_and_rank_for_dim[0] without any non-emptiness guard: when all input shapes are rank-0 (or shapes is empty), maxRank stays 0 (lines 6, 11), the vector is empty (line 16), llvm::is_splat(empty) is true, and lines 36-37 perform an out-of-bounds read of one element.

evidence.reason: Out-of-bounds read (CWE-125): shape_and_rank_for_dim is sized by maxRank on line 16 (SmallVector<std::pair<Value, int64_t>> shape_and_rank_for_dim(maxRank);). With all shape ranks 0, line 11 keeps maxRank = 0, so the vector holds 0 elements; line 35 is_splat(empty) evaluates true and line 36 reads element 0 of that 0-element vector. No shown statement guarantees maxRank >= 1 or non-emptiness; the only prior guard (line 9, non-null GetValueInfo) admits the witness with maxRank traceable entirely to lines 6 and 11.

Second out-of-bounds read of the same empty vector (CWE-125): when maxRank == 0 (line 11 admits rank-0 shapes; line 16 sizes the vector to 0) and is_splat of the empty range is true (line 35), this return re-reads shape_and_rank_for_dim[0] and returns the garbage element, which can crash the compiler or drive miscompilation. Sink capacity is the line 16 declaration; no emptiness/rank>=1 guard protects this read.

assumptions: llvm::is_splat of an empty range is true by standard STLExtras semantics (vacuous splat).
Indexing an empty SmallVector with operator[] is an out-of-bounds read / triggers the debug index assert.
GetValueInfo returns a non-null ArrayRef whose size() is the shape rank, which is 0 for a 0-d ranked tensor; the fragment shows no constraint excluding rank-0 shapes.

shape_and_rank_for_dim[i].second (line 27) stores the originating shape's rank, so the mixed-sign expression at line 52 evaluates in size_t to r - k in [0, r-1]; the wrap cancels and the ExtractOp index at lines 53-54 is in-range, so line 51-54 is the fixed/safe side of the arithmetic.
limitations: The mixed-sign wrap in 'i - maxRank + ...' (line 52) cancels geometrically for all entries (k = maxRank - i = j + 1 <= r), so no OOB flows to tensor::ExtractOp; not reported as a finding.
A rank > INT_MAX would overflow the 'int i' loop (line 41), but such a magnitude is not derivable from any shown statement; confidence below the reporting threshold.

An entirely empty 'shapes' ValueRange also yields maxRank == 0 and the same line 36/37 OOB, but broadcast operand-count validation lives outside the fragment; the rank-0 witness above is already sufficient and is the reported path.
Read of uninitialized inline storage is a DoS/miscompile risk in a compiler, not an information-disclosure channel by itself; intent is captured via the CWE-125 mechanism.
No crypto, injection, file, or authz sinks exist in this fragment; none were analyzed beyond the memory-safety and arithmetic inventory above.

verdict.summary: Modular-2^64 wrap in `length += dir->length` (line 12) lets `length` pass the `length > NJS_MAX_PATH` guard (line 25) while the copies at lines 32/39 use the unwrapped lengths, overflowing the stack buffer `src[NJS_MAX_PATH + 1]` (line 6): stack buffer overflow (CWE-121) enabled by integer overflow (CWE-190). A separate 1-byte OOB read at line 18 when `dir->length == 0` is noted in limitations and omitted from the CWE list to keep a single primary plus one secondary.

evidence.reason: info->name.length and dir->length are unconstrained size_t operands (residual [0, SIZE_MAX]); the addition at line 12 wraps mod 2^64, so length=1 passes guards at lines 14 and 25 (1 != 0, 1 <= NJS_MAX_PATH) for e.g. dir->length=2, info->name.length=SIZE_MAX, trail=0, while this copy writes SIZE_MAX bytes into src whose capacity is NJS_MAX_PATH+1 (declared line 6) — stack buffer overflow, CWE-121; the guard admits the wrapped value but never bounds the copy operand.

size_t addition wraps mod 2^64 for admitted operand pairs (e.g., dir->length=2, info->name.length=SIZE_MAX yields length=1, since 2^64-1+2 ≡ 1); the wrapped value is consumed by the length guard at line 25, bypassing it and enabling the CWE-121 stack overflow at line 39 — independently confirmed integer overflow, CWE-190.

assumptions: njs_cpymem(dst, src, n) copies n bytes and returns dst advanced by n, as implied by its use as an advancing copy pointer.
NJS_MAX_PATH is a positive compile-time path-length constant (>= 1), so the wrapped length 1 satisfies length <= NJS_MAX_PATH, and C requires src[NJS_MAX_PATH + 1] to be a valid array.
realpath() NUL-terminates its output on success, so njs_strlen(info->file.start) at line 54 is bounded.
njs_str_t provides .start (u_char*) and .length (size_t) fields as used in the fragment.
limitations: Conversationally confirmed but excluded from the CWE array to honor the single-primary-plus-one-secondary rule: line 18 `trail = (dir->start[dir->length - 1] != '/')` reads one byte out of bounds (CWE-125, index SIZE_MAX) when dir->length == 0 and info->name.length > 0, because guard line 14 checks the total length (nonzero here) and line 25 runs after line 18; the byte only feeds the boolean trail.
realpath(&src[0], &info->path[0]) at line 42 writes into info->path whose capacity is not declared in the fragment; overflow there cannot be confirmed or refuted.
TOCTOU between realpath (line 42) and open (line 47) is not reported — it would require an unshown resource-swap model.
open() without O_CLOEXEC and the unused vm parameter are robustness concerns, not confirmed flaws.

The overflow witness depends on extreme (SIZE_MAX-scale) string lengths whose admission follows from the unconstrained size_t residual range; realistic attacker reachability would additionally require the caller to materialize such strings, which the fragment does not show.

verdict.summary: Stack buffer overflow in njs_module_path(): on the dir != NULL path, the length guard at line 25 bounds only dir->length (+ optional trailing '/') because line 12 overwrites the local 'length' and drops info->name.length from the guarded value. The name is then copied unconditionally at line 39 and NUL-terminated at line 40 into src declared as char src[NJS_MAX_PATH + 1] (line 6). Any module name longer than NJS_MAX_PATH - dir->length - trail overflows src (e.g., dir->length=1, no trailing slash, info->name.length=NJS_MAX_PATH writes NJS_MAX_PATH+3 bytes, exceeding capacity by 2).

evidence.reason: info->name.length has residual range 0..SIZE_MAX on the dir != NULL path: line 9 initializes 'length' to it, but line 12 overwrites 'length' with dir->length, and the only size guard (line 25, length > NJS_MAX_PATH) then bounds only dir->length + trail. The copy at line 39 therefore writes an unconstrained count of bytes into src (capacity NJS_MAX_PATH + 1 bytes, line 6) already holding dir->length + trail bytes, with NUL at line 40 following; total written = dir->length + trail + info->name.length + 1, overflowing by info->name.length - (NJS_MAX_PATH - dir->length - trail) bytes. Witness: dir->length=1, trail=1, info->name.length=NJS_MAX_PATH (all admitted: line 14 passes, line 25 gives length=2 <= NJS_MAX_PATH) writes NJS_MAX_PATH + 3 bytes into NJS_MAX_PATH + 1 — a 2-byte stack overflow (CWE-121), growing with attacker-controlled module name length.

On the same overflow path, p points at src[dir->length + trail + info->name.length] after the out-of-domain copy at line 39; for the witness dir->length=1, trail=1, info->name.length=NJS_MAX_PATH this NUL write lands at src[NJS_MAX_PATH + 2], one byte past the src[NJS_MAX_PATH + 1] capacity declared at line 6, extending the out-of-bounds write of the primary CWE-121 finding.

assumptions: info->name.length and dir->length are treated as size_t: each is assigned into the size_t local 'length' (lines 9, 12) with no narrowing cast shown, matching njs_str_t semantics.

NJS_MAX_PATH is the positive constant used both for the src capacity (line 6, size NJS_MAX_PATH + 1) and the guard (line 25); the witness uses NJS_MAX_PATH >= 3, which the declaration 'char src[NJS_MAX_PATH + 1]' implies.
njs_cpymem has memcpy semantics (copies exactly the byte count given and returns the advanced destination pointer), and njs_strlen is strlen-like; both are consumed by name in the shown code.
NJS_DECLINED, NJS_ERROR, and NJS_OK are status returns; their exact values are irrelevant to the finding.
limitations: realpath() at line 42 writes into info->path whose capacity is not visible in the fragment, so any overflow of info->path is unconfirmable and was not reported.
On the dir == NULL path the guard at line 25 DOES bound info->name.length (length is not overwritten), so that path is safe; the vulnerability is specific to the dir != NULL path.

Integer wraparound of length sums (e.g., dir->length + info->name.length near SIZE_MAX) is theoretically possible but requires ~2^64-byte strings and is subsumed by the direct overflow finding; not reported separately.
Kernel/library failures of realpath/open are correctly checked (lines 43, 48) and are not findings; dir->start being NULL despite dir->length >= 1 is not derivable from any shown statement.

The exact overflow magnitude chosen in the witness (2 bytes) is one member of a range claim; every value of info->name.length in the unconstrained residual range above NJS_MAX_PATH - dir->length - trail overflows by at least 1 byte.

verdict.summary: iloc_box_read derives item_count/extent_count directly from the bitstream with no cap, and each extent loop iteration consumes 0 box bytes when offset_size=length_size=0, so a ~400KB crafted file drives up to 65,535 × 65,535 = ~4.29e9 gf_malloc/gf_list_add allocations (hundreds of GB), exhausting process memory and hanging the parser.

evidence.reason: extent_count (gf_bs_read_u16, line 50, residual range 0..65535 with no cap in the fragment) bounds the loop at line 52, whose body performs this allocation and a gf_list_add at line 56. On the admitted path version=0, offset_size=length_size=index_size=0 (4-bit fields, lines 7-11), every guard passes: the per-item ISOM_DECREASE_SIZE checks (lines 16/29/42/49) admit a box of >= 6*65535=393,210 bytes (per-item consumption 2+2+2, derived from the shown macro amounts) and the inner guard at line 64 is ISOM_DECREASE_SIZE(ptr, 0), which admits and consumes nothing. The loop therefore executes 65,535 x 65,535 = 4,294,836,225 iterations each allocating an extent entry plus a list node, an attacker-scaled uncontrolled-allocation resource exhaustion (CWE-770) from entry-point file data.

Secondary sink of the same confirmed finding: executed inside the extent_count-driven loop (line 52), this call allocates a list node on every iteration — also 4,294,836,225 times on the admitted witness (extent_count=65535, item_count=65535, zero-size 4-bit fields), with no fragment cap on extent_count or on total allocations. Adds to the CWE-770 memory-volume exhaustion.

assumptions: ISOM_DECREASE_SIZE(ptr, n) is the standard GPAC macro: it returns an error when ptr->size < n and otherwise decrements ptr->size by n; the fragment's own byte amounts are used consistently with the reads they guard.
ptr->size is the box's remaining payload size, attacker-influenced through the file's box header (u32 header admits >= 393,210 bytes used by the witness).
ptr->location_entries is initialized by the box constructor, so gf_list_add at line 27 is treated as framework-provided.
sizeof(GF_ItemExtentEntry)/GF_ItemLocationEntry and gf_list node sizes are constants; only the iteration counts scale with attacker input.
limitations: The version >= 2 item_count=u32 path admits the same unbounded-allocation mechanism (outer loop throttled only by box bytes, minimum 8 bytes/item from lines 32, 42, 49); reported under the same CWE-770 finding rather than as a separate CWE.
gf_list_new() (line 51) and gf_list_add (lines 27, 56) unchecked returns are only NULL on non-attacker-scaled allocator failure; demoted as robustness.

No memory-safety (OOB read/write, truncation) finding: every bitstream read is preceded by a matching ISOM_DECREASE_SIZE byte guard (lines 6-64), and the only in-fragment allocations have constant sizeof sizes.
No non-termination: both loops strictly increment their counters on every iteration; the defect is the unbounded allocation *volume*, not loop progress.

verdict.summary: Missing validation relating out_backprop's batch/depth to orig_input_tensor_shape's in_batch/in_depth: when out_batch > in_batch (or out_depth > in_depth), the coeffRef(d, in_index) access at line 132 addresses outside the in_backprop_tensor_temp buffer and lines 133-134 write through it, producing a heap out-of-bounds write.

evidence.reason: in_batch/in_depth come from orig_input_tensor_shape (lines 55, 58) and out_batch/out_depth from out_backprop.dim_size (lines 33, 36); the only guards on these are the != 0 checks at lines 59-70, which never relate out_batch to in_batch or out_depth to in_depth. in_backprop_tensor_temp is allocated with in_shape (lines 80-83) and mapped at lines 86-88 as an Eigen matrix with in_depth rows and in_cols*in_rows*in_batch columns. In the loops, in_index = (b*in_rows+in_r)*in_cols+in_c (line 126) with b up to out_batch-1 (line 96) reaches out_batch*in_rows*in_cols-1, while in_row_end is clamped only to in_rows-1 (line 102). Witness: in_shape={1,2,2,1}, out_backprop shape={2,1,1,1}, row_seq/col_seq={0,2} passes every guard (lines 25-26, 38, 44, 59-70, 103, 114); at b=1, in_r=1, in_c=1, d=0, in_index=7 but the matrix has only 4 columns, so coeffRef(0,7) at line 132 yields a reference past the 4-double buffer and line 133-134 writes through it: heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787).

assumptions: in_backprop_tensor_temp is heap-allocated by forward_input_or_allocate_temp (lines 80-83) with in_batch*in_rows*in_cols*in_depth elements.

Eigen::Map<Eigen::Matrix<double, Dynamic, Dynamic>>(data, in_depth, in_cols*in_rows*in_batch) creates an in_depth x (in_cols*in_rows*in_batch) matrix and coeffRef(row, col) requires row < in_depth and col < cols on the underlying flat buffer (standard Eigen Map semantics).

row_seq_tensor_flat(r+1) and col_seq_tensor_flat(c+1) reads are in-bounds because lines 38 and 44 require NumElements() > out_rows/out_cols, so the maximum index r+1/c+1 <= out_rows/out_cols <= NumElements()-1.
On any path reaching the write, in_rows >= 1 and in_cols >= 1: negative values make in_max_* negative and fail the >= 0 checks at lines 103/114, combined with the != 0 checks at lines 63/66.
limitations: No out_backprop.dims() == 4 check precedes dim_size(3) at line 36; a plausible out-of-bounds read inside TensorShape, but TensorShape internals and op shape-function registration are not shown, so it is not confirmed.

Negative in_batch/in_depth pass the != 0 checks (lines 59-70) and could produce nonsensical allocation sizes, but the failure path depends on unshown allocator/TensorShape behavior; the confirmed finding uses only strictly positive dims.
out_depth > in_depth triggers the identical OOB write at line 132 via row index d >= in_depth; same root cause, not a separate CWE.
Division by zero at line 134 was ruled out: inner loops execute only when start <= end with both endpoints >= 0 (lines 103/114), so num_elements_in_pooling_cell >= 1 whenever the division is reached.
The read at line 130 (out_backprop_mat.coeffRef) was audited and is in-bounds (out_index <= out_cols*out_rows*out_batch-1, d < out_depth).

verdict.summary: gf_odf_av1_cfg_read_bs_size reads an attacker-decoded OBU payload length (obu_size, u64, set at L49 without any prior constraint) as the byte count of gf_bs_read_data at L67; the only bound (if (size<obu_size), L72) executes after the read, so a nonzero-size config whose OBU header claims more bytes than the config budget causes a heap out-of-bounds read of up to (u32)obu_size bytes. Independently, size-=4 at L40 underflows for the admitted sizes 1..3 (L9 excludes only 0), corrupting the loop bound and range comparison and amplifying the unvalidated-size flow.

evidence.reason: obu_size is decoded from the stream at L49 (entry-point class) and retains its full u64 declared domain because no shown statement constrains it before this sink. The read length (u32)obu_size can exceed the size-byte config budget (size residual is {1..2^32-1} per L8/L9, reduced by only 4 at L40) and can exceed the underlying stream; the sole bound, if (size<obu_size) at L72-L75, follows L67 in path order (L49->L60->L62->L66->L67->L72) so it cannot protect the read. Witness: 7-byte stream with valid 4-byte header (passes L28) and an OBU header whose leb128 size decodes to obu_size=1000; L49 returns GF_OK, allocations pass L60/L62, L67 reads 1000 bytes when only 3 bytes of config/3 stream bytes remain — heap out-of-bounds read, CWE-125.

size is u32 with residual range {1..2^32-1} (L9 excludes only 0, no size>=4 guard precedes this statement); for admitted size in {1,2,3} the unsigned subtraction wraps to 2^32-1..2^32-3. The wrapped value is consumed by the while(size) loop condition at L42 and the range comparison at L72, which gate how many attacker-sized OBUs are read at L67, so the wrap corrupts security-relevant control values — integer underflow, CWE-191 (independent root cause enabling the L67 over-read).

assumptions: size is the byte budget of the av1c config region: L8 substitutes gf_bs_available when size==0, and L72-L75 treat obu_size exceeding size as a config-size error, so reads beyond size are outside the intended region.
obu_size (u64) has no shown pre-sink constraint in this fragment, so its full declared domain is analyzed as the taint range.
The bitstream backing bs is caller-provided and may end exactly at the size bytes, making reads beyond size out-of-bounds.
limitations: L53 assert(obu_size == gf_bs_get_position(bs) - pos) could abort before L67 in assert-enabled builds depending on gf_av1_parse_obu's position-advance semantics (callee body not shown); NDEBUG/release builds are unaffected, so it is recorded here, not as a confirmed finding.

The discarded return of gf_bs_read_data followed by a->obu_length=obu_size (L68) and gf_list_add (L70) can store a partially filled buffer as complete; downstream consumption is outside the fragment, so no independent impact is demonstrable.
L73 passes u64 obu_size-size to a %d format specifier (log-side UB only).
Huge obu_size allocation is mitigated by the L62 check (handled allocation failure).
Loop non-termination (CWE-835) would require gf_av1_parse_obu to return GF_OK without advancing position, which is callee behavior not shown here.
The witness value 1000 is representative of the sound range obu_size in [size+1, 2^32-1]; it is not a single brittle boundary.

verdict.summary: No confirmed security vulnerability in the shown fragment. All pointer-valued error paths from alloc_nfs_open_context and the open_context call are covered by IS_ERR guards (lines 33-34 and 44-56) whose excluded set is the ERR_PTR range, so put_nfs_open_context (line 65), nfs_file_set_open_context (line 60) and nfs_fscache_open_file (line 61) only receive guard-admitted values; every path to return err (line 68) has err assigned; dput(parent) (line 67) is only reachable after parent is assigned at line 28. The unguarded dereferences of the inode/dir parameters (lines 40, 43, 57) would require NULL or negative-dentry values that no shown statement can produce, so they are robustness concerns relying on out-of-fragment invariants; that caps the safe verdict at 0.6.

assumptions: Comment at lines 11-17 asserts that this code is only reached for a cached positive dentry; this is prose, not an executable bound, and is not used to protect any sink.

dget_parent()/d_inode()/file_dentry() are treated per their name-implied semantics (no NULL production); consequently the dir-dereference chain at lines 28-29 and 43 is not provably NULL from shown statements.
struct iattr is consumed by the open_context call only under the ia_valid bitmask set at lines 36-39, per the name-implied iattr convention.
Reference/bailout behavior of nfs_file_set_open_context() and put_nfs_open_context() is inside unshown callees.
limitations: NULL dereference of the inode parameter at line 40 (filemap_write_and_wait(inode->i_mapping)) and of dir at line 43 (NFS_PROTO(dir)): no shown statement can produce NULL; demoted because a NULL cannot be produced on any shown path.

Possible NULL inode passing the IS_ERR(inode) check at line 44 would be deflected by the pointer inequality at line 57 (inode != d_inode(dentry)) unless both were NULL simultaneously, which is not derivable from the fragment; demoted.

Use-after-free/double-put of ctx around lines 60-65 would depend on unshown reference semantics inside nfs_file_set_open_context() and put_nfs_open_context(); the fragment derives no out-of-domain value at the call site, so this is a thin-wrapper/demoted concern.

Discarded return of filemap_write_and_wait (line 40): failure is not attacker-directed and no security-relevant operation consumes the failure state (ia_size = 0 and ATTR_SIZE are set regardless); robustness concern only.
Uninitialized iattr fields (line 8) are never read outside the ia_valid contract in the shown code; demoted.
dprintk at line 19 uses a constant format string; no format-string injection.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability in the shown fragment. The allocation flow is protected by `if (alloc_size <= 0) return NULL;` (line 3), which under unsigned `size_t` semantics excludes only `alloc_size == 0` and admits `>= 1`, and by the NULL check at line 5 that precedes the `ret->size = size` store at line 6. A helper failure folds into either the excluded zero path or a huge `size_t` that `malloc` rejects and line 5 absorbs. An undersized-but-nonzero allocation that could make the line-6 store overflow cannot be demonstrated from the fragment because neither the `TfLiteIntArray` layout nor the helper's output domain is visible; those candidate OOB/unvalidated-size claims are recorded as limitations without a CWE.

assumptions: `size_t` is unsigned, so `alloc_size <= 0` at line 3 excludes only `alloc_size == 0` and admits every value `>= 1`.
`int` is 32-bit two's complement, so `size`'s declared domain is `INT_MIN..INT_MAX`.
After line 3, `alloc_size`'s residual range is `[1, SIZE_MAX]`; after line 5, `ret` is non-NULL before the line-6 store.
`TfLiteIntArrayGetSizeInBytes` returns the byte size for `size` elements (name-implied contract); its body and exact output-domain are not visible in the fragment.
limitations: Demoted: passing the unconstrained `int` `size` (full declared domain) into `TfLiteIntArrayGetSizeInBytes` at line 2 is an unvalidated-size flow, but the corrupting arithmetic is inside the unshown helper; the fragment's line-3 guard absorbs a `0` output and a huge `size_t` is absorbed by `malloc` failure plus line 5, so no security-relevant consequence is demonstrable from shown statements (no CWE).

Demoted: potential heap OOB write at `ret->size = size` (line 6) if `alloc_size` were smaller than the `size` member's placement; the excess cannot be computed because the struct layout and the helper output domain are not shown. Per the OOB standard, a boundary claim against a non-visible capacity is not a finding.

The line-3 guard, being an unsigned `<= 0` test, does not exclude huge `size_t` values produced by a signed negative helper return; those reach `malloc`, fail, and return NULL via line 5, which is benign in the shown code.
`malloc(SIZE_MAX)` failing is an environment/robustness concern (NULL is checked and returned), not an attacker-directed failing dereference.

verdict.summary: The functor indexes explicit_paddings[2..5] (lines 76-79) with no size check on the parameter, enabling an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) for any vector with fewer than 6 elements, and divides by unconstrained tensor-derived values (patch_depth / num_groups, lines 12, 20, 26) enabling divide-by-zero crashes (CWE-369).

evidence.reason: explicit_paddings (line 4) is a std::vector<int64_t> parameter whose size is never constrained by the shown code; its residual range includes vectors with 0-5 elements. On the path where padding == EXPLICIT (line 72, the only guard before the sink, which does not constrain vector size), std::vector::operator[] at indices 2-5 (lines 76-79) reads up to 8 bytes past the buffer end, an OOB read (CWE-125) with any short vector, e.g. explicit_paddings={}.

patch_depth = filter.dim_size(2) (line 11) and in_depth = input.dim_size(3) (line 10) are int64 values with no shown positivity bound; the full declared domain includes 0. If patch_depth == 0, the division at line 12 is integer division by zero (UB/SIGFPE). If patch_depth > in_depth >= 0, num_groups becomes 0 and the identical divisions at lines 20 and 26 divide by zero when post_shuffle/pre_shuffle run inside allocate_temp (lines 36-38, 44-46, 55-57), before any other guard executes. CWE-369.

num_groups is derived at line 12 as in_depth/patch_depth without a shown guard requiring patch_depth <= in_depth and non-zero; when in_depth < patch_depth (e.g. in_depth 0, patch_depth 1), num_groups == 0 and this pre_shuffle division divides by zero during the allocate_temp shape computations (lines 36-38, 44-46). CWE-369; the identical division is repeated at line 26 inside post_shuffle.

Same divide-by-zero sink as line 20: post_shuffle divides tensor.dim_size(3) by num_groups, which is 0 whenever in_depth < patch_depth (or in_depth is 0), a value reachable given the unconstrained dim_size inputs (lines 10-11) and the truncating division at line 12. Executed before the loop at lines 59-86, at the allocate_temp calls (lines 36-38, 44-46, 55-57). CWE-369.

assumptions: OP_REQUIRES_OK (lines 36-38, 44-46, 55-57) returns from the functor when ctx->allocate_temp fails, so allocation failures never reach the later sinks.

chip<0>(i) at lines 68-70 indexes tensors whose dim-0 was allocated as num_groups by post_shuffle (lines 24-27); the loop bound at line 59 (i < num_groups) therefore matches capacity, keeping the chips in bounds.

The Eigen shuffle assignments (lines 39-40, 47-48, 90-91) stay within source bounds because every destination element count is num_groups*N*H*W*(C/num_groups) <= N*H*W*C, by the shown division semantics.
limitations: NULL dereference of output: the pointer parameter is dereferenced without a check (lines 55-56, 90); a NULL value is only producible by an unshown caller, so it is treated as a robustness/framework-contract concern rather than a confirmed attacker-reachable finding.

Narrowing cast static_cast<int>(explicit_paddings[2..5]) (lines 76-79) truncates int64 values outside int32 range (confirmed CWE-681 mechanism for e.g. 2^40), but downstream impact inside the unseen SpatialConvolution callee determines severity; not added to the verdict CWE set.
row_stride/col_stride/row_dilation/col_dilation are forwarded without local validation (lines 75, 83); whether the hidden functor validates them is not shown, so no confirmed failure.

The fragment never checks in_depth % patch_depth == 0; non-divisible shapes yield truncated group counts and leave trailing output channels unwritten (lines 39-40, 90-91), a semantic correctness concern only - the shown byte arithmetic stays in bounds.
DCHECK(data_format == FORMAT_NHWC) (lines 6-8) is debug-only; release builds enforce nothing, but no subsequent statement consumes data_format.
Stride/dilation values with unusual magnitudes (e.g. negative ints) could matter only inside the hidden convolution implementation, which is outside the fragment.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the patched form of the einsum ParseEquation one-input out-of-bounds read. The short-circuit guard `num_inputs == 1 ||` at line 53 evaluates before the `(*input_label_counts)[1][label]` read at line 54, excluding the dangerous `num_inputs == 1` case; when line 54 evaluates, `input_label_counts` has at least 2 elements (resized to `num_inputs` at line 27), so index 1 is in bounds. All other label/count arrays are sized by the same derived `num_labels`/`num_inputs` values they are indexed with, and no other statement in the fragment produces an out-of-domain index.

assumptions: Non-ellipsis labels produced by MapToLabels are consecutive integers in [0, num_labels), per the fragment's own comment at lines 13-14 combined with `num_labels = label_mapping.size()` at line 26; all count arrays are sized `num_labels` at lines 30, 39, 49.

`input_labels`, `input_label_counts`, `output_label_counts`, `label_types`, `input_has_ellipsis`, and `output_has_ellipsis` are valid non-null out-parameters as implied by their dereference/use throughout.
`kEllipsisLabel` is a distinct sentinel value that the guards at lines 33, 42, and 51 route away from all count-array indexing.
limitations: OOB read of `(*input_label_counts)[0][label]` at line 53 in the `num_inputs == 0` case is not a finding: the degenerate empty-input value is not derived by any shown statement, and the sole producer of `input_str` (`ParseEinsumEquation`, line 11) is not shown to emit zero subscripts, so the witness is rejected under degenerate-input discipline.

Labels index `num_labels`-sized arrays at lines 34 and 43 without an explicit range check in this fragment; the in-range property rests on `MapToLabels`' visible consecutive-mapping contract (lines 13-14), and no shown statement diverges from it.

The `size_t`→`int` narrowing at lines 16 and 26 (`num_inputs`, `num_labels`) could in principle wrap for values exceeding INT_MAX, but no shown statement can produce such magnitudes from the equation string; classified as robustness only, not a confirmed vulnerability.

The known upstream einsum OOB (`input_label_counts[1]` with a single input) is only reachable in the unpatched form; this fragment contains the protective clause at line 53, so that path cannot be demonstrated here.

verdict.summary: afra_box_read reads global_entry_count (line 35) from untrusted file bytes as a u32 and uses it directly as the bound of the allocation loop at lines 36-39 without any check tying it to the remaining box size; the analogous entry_count flow is guarded at line 14, but no such guard exists for global entries. An attacker-set count up to 2^32-1, with an overclaimed box size budget, drives up to that many per-iteration gf_malloc/gf_list_insert heap allocations, enabling memory/CPU exhaustion (CWE-400).

evidence.reason: Sink: loop bound and per-iteration heap allocation. Taint: global_entry_count is read at line 35 via gf_bs_read_u32 from bs (entry-point input) with residual range [0, 2^32-1]; the only count-vs-size guard, line 14, tests entry_count on the local-entry path and never executes for this value, and lines 33-34 (global_entries gate, 4-byte budget reserve) impose no count bound. Impact: each of up to 2^32-1 iterations allocates at line 37 (and inside gf_list_insert at line 39) before the in-loop ISOM_DECREASE_SIZE checks (lines 41-59) can stop it, and those checks bound iterations only by the attacker-controlled claimed box budget; the absent bound between line 35 and line 36 is the missing validation, producing attacker-scaled heap exhaustion (CWE-400).

assumptions: ptr->size is the remaining-box-byte budget, decremented by ISOM_DECREASE_SIZE, per its use at lines 6, 14, 22, 25, 28, 34, 41, 44, 48, 53, 57.
gf_bs_read_u32 returns the full 32-bit value range read from the stream (entry-point input).
gf_malloc and gf_list_insert perform heap allocation per call; sizeof(GF_GlobalAfraEntry) is a compile-time constant.
limitations: ptr->size's declared type (u32 vs u64) is not visible in the fragment; even a u32 box-size claim (~4 GB) yields ~2x10^8 global-entry iterations, while a 64-bit claim scales further.

The local-entry loop (line 17) is guarded by line 14, whose admitted set (entry_count <= floor(size/12) or floor(size/16)) passes every in-loop ISOM_DECREASE_SIZE, so no separate finding is raised there; a budget-scaled DoS remains possible only via the same overclaimed-box-size mechanism and is subsumed by the global finding.
The gf_list_insert return values (lines 20, 39) are discarded; no confirmed security-relevant status-handling flaw.
The malloc-failure return at line 38 only triggers after exhaustion is already underway, so it does not mitigate the resource-exhaustion claim.
Any framework-level validation outside this fragment that would cap ptr->size against the real file length is not shown and is not used in either direction (per scope rules).

verdict.summary: xml_parse_node's PI/comment/CDATA scan loops have no end-of-input guard: on truncated input such as '<?x', '<!--', or '<a><![CDATA[x', the loops can never reach their break condition and spin forever (CWE-835), advancing the cursor past the buffer and reading out of bounds; the same function also recurses on nested elements with no depth limit (not scored separately).

evidence.reason: The only loop exit is line 19's break, guarded by line 17 requiring '?' followed by '>'.
