The branch guard at line 12 admits any '<?'-prefixed input; for the concrete witness '<?x', line 16 scans to end-of-input without finding '?', line 17 is false, and line 21 advances the cursor by 1, so the loop never terminates (CWE-835). No EOF/end-of-buffer check exists between line 14 and line 23 (contrast the is_eof guard used at line 88), and after the cursor passes the buffer end the repeated *scanner->curptr / pj_scan_strcmp reads are out of bounds.

Same missing-EOF-guard defect as the PI loop. The guard at line 28 admits any '<!'-prefixed input; for the concrete witness '<!--' (no '>'), line 32 scans to end-of-input, line 33's strcmp is non-zero, and line 37 advances the cursor by 1 indefinitely, so the loop never reaches its break at line 35 (CWE-835), with out-of-bounds cursor reads once the cursor passes the buffer end.

The CDATA branch (lines 93-94) admits '<![CDATA['-prefixed input; for the concrete witness '<a><![CDATA[x' the sub-node loop is skipped (line 81 excludes '!') and the content scan is skipped (line 88, *curptr == '<'), so line 96 advances 9, line 97 scans for ']' to end-of-input, line 98's strcmp is non-zero, and line 101 advances the cursor by 1 with line 102 finding no further ']' — the loop condition never clears (CWE-835). No end-of-input check bounds this loop; after the cursor passes the buffer end, the strcmp reads are out of bounds.

assumptions: The XML bytes behind pj_scanner are entry-point, attacker-controlled input; the fragment imposes no constraint on the presence of '?>', '>', or ']]>' terminators.

The pj_scan_* helpers follow name-implied semantics (scan to delimiter or end, compare bytes at the cursor, advance the cursor) and none is shown to abort when a terminator is absent; the loops in the fragment contain the only termination logic.
limitations: Unbounded recursion at line 83 (and lines 24/40) is also present with no depth limit (CWE-674), but the stack-exhaustion witness is a range claim depending on unshown stack/input sizes, so it is not scored as an additional CWE.

Out-of-bounds reads once the cursor passes the buffer end in the spinning loops depend on the unshown scanner buffer layout/NUL termination, so they are consequences of the CWE-835 finding, not a separate CWE-125 entry.
attr->value.slen -= 2 (line 62) can yield a negative/underflowed length on unterminated quote input, but attr->value is not consumed within the fragment, so no downstream sink is confirmable.
Unchecked *(scanner->curptr+1) reads (lines 12, 80-81, 93) and scans at end-of-input (line 50) are OOB only if the buffer lacks NUL slack; that invariant is not visible in the fragment.
A possible hang in the attribute loop at lines 53-66 on XML with whitespace after the tag name depends on unshown pj_scan_get_until_chr semantics and was not confirmed.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability in the fragment. The key input is validated to exactly one element (L17, admitted set {1}, excluding empty and multi-element keys) before the copy at L23 and the call at L31, and the values loop (L26-L28) is bounded by values_tensor.size() with max index size()-1. The unvalidated indices_tensor passed to map->put at L31 is recorded as a limitation: the fragment forwards it unchanged and derives no index/size argument at the call site, so any consumption (and hence impact) would occur in the unshown callee and cannot be confirmed here.

assumptions: OP_REQUIRES_OK returns from the kernel on failure, so execution past L3/L11/L12/L13/L31 implies the preceding call succeeded (framework-standard macro semantics).
OpInputList::size() returns the tensor count and operator[] is valid for i in [0, size()) (standard container semantics).
L17 (NumElements() == 1) restricts the key tensor to exactly one element, which is the domain the shown key uses at L23 and L31.
limitations: indices_tensor (L12) is forwarded to map->put (L31) with no shown validation of element count, dtype, shape, or value range. If the callee consumed it as an index array, a count mismatched with the tuple or an out-of-range index would be an OOB flow; this cannot be confirmed from the fragment because the callee body is not shown and the fragment derives no index/size argument at the call site (pure pass-through).
The key tensor's dtype is not validated (only NumElements), despite the int64 wording at L19; any downstream flat<int64>()/hash interpretation is outside the fragment.
No shown check ties values_tensor.size() to the op's declared dtypes attr or to indices_tensor.NumElements(); those invariants, if any, live in the op registration/framework, which is not shown.
Any vulnerability in the unshown StagingMap::put body (key hashing, tuple storage, indices use) is out of scope; only the argument derivations shown in this fragment were analyzed.

verdict.summary: digest_generic_verify takes len from digest_length(d) at line 4 with no validation and passes it as the allocation size to xmalloc (line 7) and as the read length to memcmp(md, tmp, len) (line 13). len retains the full int domain (no shown constraint), and md has no visible capacity bound; a negative len converts to a huge size_t (CWE-195) and len exceeding md's buffer causes an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). The only guard on the compare path, if (ret) goto end; (lines 10-11), checks digest_final's status, not the length, so it does not bound len or md.

evidence.reason: len (line 4, int) has residual range INT_MIN..INT_MAX because the fragment imposes no constraint on digest_length(d)'s return, and it flows unmodified into the length argument of memcmp at line 13. md has no visible capacity bound; a negative len is converted to a huge size_t (CWE-195) and any len above md's actual (unshown) buffer size reads out of bounds (CWE-125). The only guard on this path, if (ret) goto end; (lines 10-11), admits ret == 0 and tests only digest_final's status, so it does not validate len or md; the missing bound/validation check at the call site is the defect.

The same unvalidated int len from line 4 reaches xmalloc before any branch or check. Over the residual range (full int domain), a negative value converts to a near-SIZE_MAX size_t argument (CWE-195), yielding an oversized allocation/allocation failure; no statement between line 4 and line 7 constrains the size.

assumptions: tmp = xmalloc(len) (line 7) gives tmp a capacity of exactly len bytes for non-negative len — the only capacity visible in the fragment.
xmalloc and memcmp take size_t (non-negative) size/length parameters per their standard semantics, so an int argument is converted at the call site (call-site confirmation).
digest_final(d, tmp) (line 9) is expected to write len bytes on success, with the return checked at lines 10-11.
limitations: The exact magnitude digest_length(d) returns is not shown in the fragment; the finding rests on a residual-range claim (full int domain), not a demonstrated constant, which caps confidence at 0.6.
if (ret) goto end; (lines 10-11) correctly prevents comparing uninitialized/partial tmp after a failed digest_final — that error-handling issue is handled — but it does not validate len or md.
A NULL or short md buffer is not checked; whether callers guarantee md has at least len bytes is an invariant not derivable from the fragment and cannot demote the OOB claim.

tmp from xmalloc is used without a NULL check (lines 9, 13); under fail-on-OOM allocator semantics that is an environment-failure robustness concern, not an attacker-directed finding here — no CWE assigned.
memcmp is not a constant-time comparison; a timing side channel would require the computed digest in tmp to be secret (keyed MAC), an invariant the fragment does not establish — demoted.
digest_final's actual write amount relative to tmp's capacity and xmalloc's failure behavior are callee semantics not shown; demoted as unconfirmable.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. The SHA-256 digest write at line 11 is bounded by the fixed digest size into a buffer declared uint8_t[EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE] (line 2); the length consumed by EVP_DigestUpdate at line 16 is pinned to exactly SHA256_DIGEST_LENGTH by the equality RELEASE_ASSERT (lines 13-14) before the read; both list loops (lines 20-25, 27-32) pass each element's exact byte extent; and every crypto return code is asserted before further use.

assumptions: hash_buffer's capacity is EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE per its declaration (line 2), and SHA256_DIGEST_LENGTH is the SHA-256 digest size; the standard meaning of EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE (maximum digest size any EVP_MD can produce) gives EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE >= SHA256_DIGEST_LENGTH, so a fixed 32-byte write/read cannot exceed the buffer.

X509_digest's in/out length contract: on success it writes exactly EVP_MD_size(EVP_sha256()) = SHA256_DIGEST_LENGTH bytes and overwrites the length out-parameter with that value; the in-value only gates success/failure.

verify_certificate_hash_list_ and verify_certificate_spki_list_ are containers whose elements expose data()/size(); the shown length expression size()*sizeof(value_type) equals the exact byte extent of the object behind data() for any element type.
Zero-length EVP_DigestUpdate reads nothing and returns success, so an empty list element (data()==nullptr, size()==0) is safe.
limitations: Robustness concern (no CWE): with ca_cert_ != nullptr, a caller-supplied hash_length below SHA256_DIGEST_LENGTH makes X509_digest fail and RELEASE_ASSERT(rc == 1, ...) (line 12) abort. The fragment contains no statement that produces such a value (no shown producer; degenerate caller contract); the abort is the designed crypto-error path, the failure is not attacker-directed, and no security-relevant operation runs on the failure state.

The numeric values of EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE and SHA256_DIGEST_LENGTH are not printed in the fragment; the in-bounds conclusion for the fixed 32-byte digest write/read relies on the standard library relationship EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE >= SHA256_DIGEST_LENGTH implied by the constant's purpose and the line 2 array declaration.

The concrete element types of the two list containers are not shown; the analysis uses the shown expression, which computes the exact byte extent of each element, so correctness does not depend on the specific type.

fmt::format at line 14 uses a {} placeholder with an unsigned value; no format-string injection (CWE-134) is possible; RELEASE_ASSERT aborts are Envoy's designed error handling and are treated as robustness, not attacker-reachable crashes.

verdict.summary: The RTCP XR parser records pointers to report blocks (lines 31/34/37/40) without validating that the attacker-declared rb_len is large enough for the block type's fixed contents. On an admitted path (size=16, pkt_len=3, a single BT_RR_TIME block with rb_len=1 at byte 8), the loop exits and line 54 reads rb_rr_time->ntp_frac at bytes 16-19, a 4-byte heap out-of-bounds read past the 16-byte buffer (capacity=size, line 3); the stats and VoIP blocks overread further when flags set via header.specific are nonzero.

evidence.reason: Primary OOB read (CWE-125). rb_rr_time is recorded at line 31 from attacker-controlled block header fields (bt line 29, rb_len line 25) with no minimum-length check for BT_RR_TIME; guard line 19 admits pkt_len+1 == size/4 (equality) and loop line 23 admits the block start at word index pkt_len-1. With size=16 (capacity declared at line 3) and pkt_len=3, a BT_RR_TIME block with rb_len=1 at byte 8 passes line 28 and the switch; after loop exit, ntp_frac at byte 16 is read 4 bytes past the buffer.

Same missing per-type length validation (CWE-125): rb_dlrr recorded at line 34 from a block with attacker rb_len (minimum needed: 2 words); with the line-19 equality case and the block at word index pkt_len-1, the fixed 8 content bytes of the DLRR item extend past the buffer end (item.dlrr read at line 76 is 4 bytes past a 16-byte buffer).

Same block-type length gap (CWE-125): rb_stats recorded at line 37 with no minimum rb_len; attacker sets header.specific (line 139) so flags at lines 148-151 are all set and fields lost/dup/jitter_*/toh_* (lines 155-175) are read at offsets far beyond a minimal block and beyond the buffer end on the equality-boundary admitted path (line 19).

Same root cause (CWE-125): rb_voip_mtc recorded at line 40 without validating rb_len against the VoIP-metrics struct size; the unconditional field reads (lines 183-213) reach offsets (e.g., burst_dur at byte 16 with a block at byte 8 in a 16-byte packet) beyond the buffer admitted by guard line 19's equality case.

assumptions: pkt points to a received RTCP datagram of size bytes; size is the receiver-supplied length (the function's own entry-point parameter, constrained only by the word check at lines 19-20).

Standard layout implied by the member accesses: the RTCP common header is 2 words so rtcp_xr->buf starts at byte 8; each rb_header is 4 bytes with bt/specific/length, and the bt-specific structs place their named content fields after the 4-byte header (ntp_sec/ntp_frac at +4/+8, item.lrr/item.dlrr at +4/+8, etc.).
common.length is the RTCP length field (packet words minus one) converted via pj_ntohs at line 17; pkt_len is unsigned so pkt_len+1 cannot wrap.
limitations: sess is dereferenced without a NULL check (e.g., lines 53-54, 110-125), but NULL provenance is caller-side, not attacker-directed: robustness, not a confirmed finding.
TRACE_/PJ_LOG calls pass integer arguments to %p (lines 59-60, 96-99, 128-133); format/argument type mismatch is UB but the format strings are literals, so no injection is possible.
The DLRR delay arithmetic (lines 83, 89-93) deliberately wraps in 32-bit NTP space and the result is not used as an index, size, or length: no finding.

Pointer arithmetic at lines 46-47 can move the pointer past the end of the packet, but the loop exits before any dereference of the advanced pointer; the confirmed OOB is the post-loop content reads, not this arithmetic.

Sinks in the same family (DLRR item.dlrr read at line 76, stats begin_seq/end_seq at lines 144-145, dup at 159, jitter_* 163-167, toh_* 171-175, voip fields 184-213) share the confirmed root cause and are summarized; CWE-125 is reported once.

verdict.summary: Not vulnerable. Every copy sink (lines 57, 82, 92) is covered by a visible protective statement: rhs.IsInitialized() is enforced before any read (lines 9-11); the buffer-reuse path requires old_lhs.IsInitialized() and equal element counts (lines 44-45) so Copy targets a same-capacity buffer; and the fallback path allocates an initialized copy_tensor sized to rhs.shape() (lines 74-76) and replaces the ref before the unlocked copy (line 80). The CHECK at line 52 has no demonstrable failure input within the shown code (equal counts satisfy CopyFrom's standard precondition). No injection, integer, abort, or error-handling finding is confirmable from the fragment.

assumptions: Tensor::IsInitialized() (lines 10, 44) means the tensor has a non-null backing data buffer; an uninitialized Tensor has no buffer.

Tensor::CopyFrom(old_lhs, rhs.shape()) (line 52) succeeds when the source element count equals the new shape's element count; the guard at lines 44-45 establishes that equality and source initialization.
Copy writes exactly rhs.num_elements() elements into the destination buffer (elementwise device assignment in the AssignOp kernel, whose body is not shown).
OP_REQUIRES/OP_REQUIRES_OK abort Compute before any later statement when the predicate fails (lines 9-11, 27-34, 74-76).

context->mutable_input(0, /* lock_held */ false) (line 91) is the framework API called because the kernel does not hold the mutex; this fragment performs no unlocked mutation of the ref tensor itself.
limitations: The CHECK at line 52 would abort only if CopyFrom returned false; for inputs admitted by the guard at lines 44-45 (initialized source, equal element counts) no shown statement produces such a failure, and CopyFrom's internal preconditions are not shown, so a reachable-abort (CWE-617) verdict cannot be confirmed.
Dtype consistency between old_lhs and rhs is enforced by op-level typing outside the fragment and is not used to justify either direction of a verdict.
No loops exist in the fragment; iteration bounds inside the unshown Copy body are not analyzable here.
The fragment contains no command, SQL, format-string, log, HTTP, file-path, or crypto sinks; those vulnerability classes are out of scope.
The uninitialized-rhs read vector is excluded only by the shown OP_REQUIRES at lines 9-11, which executes before every sink in program order.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. The batch-index path is protected by shown guards: `splits_values(0) == 0` (line 27) forces batch_idx >= 1, and `splits_values(num_batches) == num_values` (line 30) forces batch_idx <= num_batches, so `splits_values(batch_idx)` (line 40) stays in-bounds and `per_batch_counts[batch_idx - 1]` (lines 46/48/50) stays within [0, num_batches-1]. `values_values(idx)` (line 43) is bounded by `idx < num_values` (line 39), and `weight_values(idx)` (line 48) is bounded by the weights/values shape equality (line 10). A residual unbounded size flow from attacker values through max_value to OutputSparse's size argument exists but its impact is not confirmable from the fragment (GetOutputSize/OutputSparse bodies not shown); it is recorded as a limitation, not a finding.

assumptions: Tensor::NumElements() returns the element count (int64 in TF) and is non-negative; `flat<T>()` views expose elements by index 0..NumElements()-1 (implied by the shown `flat`/`values_values(idx)` usage).

BatchedMap<W>(num_batches) is an associative container keyed by the value (per the name 'Map' and the `operator[]`-with-`value` usage at lines 46/48/50); associative insertion has no capacity that is violated by the admitted key range.
OP_REQUIRES failure aborts the invocation before the code below it runs (standard TF macro semantics); the guards at lines 24/27/30 therefore protect all following uses on the reachable path.
num_values/num_batches narrowing (lines 20-21) is exact for element counts that fit in int; all admitted in-fragment accesses are bounded by the narrowed quantities themselves.
limitations: Candidate A (OOB read of splits_values in the while loop) is demoted: the line 30 end-equality check `splits_values(num_batches) == num_values` combined with line 39 `idx < num_values` bounds batch_idx to <= num_batches on every path; no witness passes these guards.
Candidate B (unbounded `value` used as map key when maxlength_ <= 0) is demoted: no shown capacity or size consumer turns the associative key into an out-of-domain offset.

Candidate C (unbounded num_output_values from max_value reaching OutputSparse at line 59) is a missing-bound size flow but not a confirmed finding: GetOutputSize and OutputSparse are not shown, so clamping, allocation, and status handling cannot be verified from the fragment; impact is unconfirmable (potential CWE-400/CWE-770 at most).

Candidate D (int64 -> int narrowing of NumElements at lines 20-21) is demoted: demonstrating a truncating element count requires a >2^31-element tensor (resource boundary outside the fragment) and no shown downstream access is confirmed to be corrupted by the truncated value.
Templates T/W and attributes maxlength_/minlength_/binary_output_ are not shown; only their use at lines 44/46/48/50/58 constrains them. When maxlength_ <= 0, line 44 does not cap admitted values.

verdict.summary: flatpak_dir_ensure_bundle_remote feeds bundle-controlled strings (origin URL at L29, collection_id at L32, decomposed id/ref at L58/L65, filename basename at L60) into flatpak_dir_create_origin_remote at L61-L70 without any visible validation or escaping; CR/LF and GKeyFile-syntax characters survive to the persistent remote-config write, enabling config injection (CWE-74).

evidence.snippet:
remote = flatpak_dir_create_origin_remote (self,
                                                 origin,
                                                 id,
                                                 basename,
                                                 flatpak_decomposed_get_ref (ref),
                                                 gpg_data,
                                                 collection_id,
                                                 &created_remote,
                                                 cancellable,
                                                 error);
evidence.reason: origin and collection_id are parsed from the attacker-controlled bundle at L29/L32, and id/ref derive from the same metadata (L58/L65); basename comes from the untrusted bundle filename at L60. No shown statement between L27 and L70 validates, length-caps, escapes, or whitelists these values — g_file_get_basename at L60 only excludes '/', still admitting newline and GKeyFile-syntax characters — so their full char* domain reaches the sink L61-L70, which by name-implied semantics creates and persists a remote (URL=origin, collection-id, GPG keys) in the user's repository config. A payload such as origin="https://a\n[remote \"x\"]\nurl=https://a" passes every guard on the path (L24 success, L34 non-NULL metadata, L40 else branch with deploy_data==NULL for a not-yet-deployed ref; the L71 NULL check runs after the sink) and survives to the config write, yielding CWE-74 remote-config injection.

assumptions: file is an entry-point input: the path (and contents) of a user-supplied .flatpak bundle passed to the installer; bundle metadata parsed by flatpak_bundle_load (L27-L33) is therefore attacker-controlled and is unconstrained by any fragment statement.
flatpak_dir_create_origin_remote (L61-L70) persists a new remote (name, collection-id, GPG keys) and stores the origin URL in the repository config, by its name and use in the shown code.
g_file_get_basename (L60) excludes '/' from its result (POSIX path-component semantics) but not CR/LF or other config-significant characters.
deploy_data == NULL (L40 else path) is the ordinary state for a ref not yet installed, not a degenerate minimum.
limitations: The callee's exact config-write statements and any escaping inside flatpak_dir_create_origin_remote are not shown; if values are escaped by GKeyFile setters the injection materialization would be neutralized, capping confidence at 0.60.
Path traversal via basename was demoted: g_file_get_basename (L60) excludes '/'.
ostree_repo_copy_config (L49) has an unchecked return; NULL would reach flatpak_dir_modify_remote (L51), but the failure is not attacker-directed (robustness concern only).
remote can be NULL when flatpak_deploy_data_get_origin (L42) returns NULL, and basename can be NULL for a path without a basename component (L60->L64); no shown producer of those NULLs was confirmed.
NULL file/self would fault inside callees (L27/L60/L24), not in the fragment, so no NULL-dereference finding is confirmed.
The fragment contains no loops, memory copies, format strings, exec, or SQL sinks; memory-safety analysis is call-site-based only.

verdict.summary: Stack buffer overflow in check_attestation_fido_u2f: the fixed 200-byte buffer data_signed (line 9) receives rpid_hash, credential_id, cert_x, and cert_y via unvalidated size_t length parameters (credential_id_len, cert_x_len, cert_y_len, rpid_hash_len) with no capacity check anywhere in the fragment. The cumulative writes at lines 102-118 total 34 + rpid_hash_len + credential_id_len + cert_x_len + cert_y_len bytes, so any sum of lengths above 166 overflows indices 0..199, enabling stack memory corruption from attacker/protocol-supplied lengths.

evidence.reason: credential_id_len is a size_t parameter (line 1) with full declared domain; no guard in lines 12-107 constrains it. The destination data_signed has capacity 200 declared at line 9. By lines 102-106 the offset is already 33 + rpid_hash_len, so this memcpy writes up to credential_id_len bytes beyond capacity for any value where 33 + rpid_hash_len + credential_id_len > 200 (equivalently, sum of the four length parameters > 166). Missing bound (CWE-121) confirmed by byte-level accounting with the declared capacity.

rpid_hash_len is an unconstrained size_t parameter (line 1) with no shown validation; it is copied at offset 1 into the 200-byte data_signed (line 9). This is the first of the cascading unbounded memcpy sinks; any rpid_hash_len > 199 already overflows, and larger values corrupt regardless of the later writes.

data_signed_offset equals 33 + rpid_hash_len + credential_id_len at this point (lines 100-109), all attacker-supplied with no bound. When that offset exceeds 199, this single-byte store writes outside the 200-byte buffer declared at line 9, the same missing-capacity defect as the surrounding memcpy sinks.

cert_x_len is an unconstrained size_t parameter (line 1); offset here is 34 + rpid_hash_len + credential_id_len. The write of cert_x_len bytes must satisfy 34 + rpid_hash_len + credential_id_len + cert_x_len <= 200, which no shown statement enforces against the line 9 capacity of 200 bytes.

Final cascading sink: offset is 34 + rpid_hash_len + credential_id_len + cert_x_len and cert_y_len is unconstrained (line 1). The full chain writes 34 + rpid_hash_len + credential_id_len + cert_x_len + cert_y_len bytes; with lengths such as 32/96/32/32 the write reaches index 225, exceeding the capacity of data_signed[200] declared at line 9 by 26 bytes. No capacity check exists anywhere before this line.

assumptions: data_signed capacity of 200 bytes (line 9) is the binding destination capacity for the memcpy chain.
The four length parameters have the full size_t declared domain because the shown code imposes no constraint on them.
Standard semantics of memcpy/o_strlen/cbor size accessors are assumed.
limitations: The overflow witness is a range claim: length magnitudes (e.g., 32/96/32/32) are not constants derived in the shown code, so confidence is capped at 0.62; the range analysis itself is complete (capacity and all offsets are shown).

att_cert (line 52) is consumed as a bytestring at lines 53-54 with only array-size==1 validation (line 48); any type-confusion impact depends on cbor_bytestring_handle internals not shown, so it is not independently confirmed.
client_data is passed to o_strlen at line 87 without a shown NUL-termination or length bound; a potential OOB read depends on unshown caller contract and was demoted.
gnutls_pubkey_verify_data2 (line 127) treats negative GnuTLS errors as 'Invalid signature'; this is fail-closed and not a security finding.

No separate CWE is attached to the cascading write at line 105 because client_data_hash_len is fixed at 32 (line 10) and is in-range for the admitted length combinations that keep earlier offsets valid.

verdict.summary: nbFields is decoded directly from the bitstream at L20 (gf_bs_read_int(bs, NbBits) with NbBits up to 31) and never capped, so values up to 0x7FFFFFFF flow into the allocation count at L29, the QP length setter at L25, and both loop bounds at L32/L40 — attacker-controlled resource exhaustion.

evidence.reason: nbFields has residual range [0, 0x7FFFFFFF] (only the 31-bit read width at L20 bounds it; no cap exists between L20 and L29). Witness: 5-bit field 31 → NbBits=31, then 31 all-ones bits → nbFields=0x7FFFFFFF, passing L22/L28 and reaching L29, where an allocator whose third argument is an element count receives 2,147,483,647 with no visible limit — attacker-scaled allocation (CWE-770).

The same unconstrained nbFields ([0, 0x7FFFFFFF] from L20) is forwarded as a length count when codec->ActiveQP is set; the L22 guard does not bound nbFields, so a huge admitted value is consumed here as a length — same missing-bound root cause (CWE-770).

Loop bound i < nbFields admits up to 2^31-1 iterations (nbFields residual [0, 0x7FFFFFFF] from L20, no shown cap) on the non-MFNODE path; each iteration performs gf_sg_vrml_mf_get_item/dec_sf_field work, so CPU and memory work scale with attacker-chosen count (CWE-770).

MFNODE branch loop bound likewise admits up to 0x7FFFFFFF iterations with per-item gf_bifs_dec_node and node-list registration/adds; the same unbounded nbFields flows here with no visible cap (CWE-770).

assumptions: gf_bs_read_int(bs, N) returns an unsigned value in [0, 2^N - 1]; NbBits = gf_bs_read_int(bs, 5) therefore lies in [0,31].
gf_sg_vrml_mf_alloc's third parameter is an element count that controls allocation size (name/role-implied semantics); its body is not shown.
No capacity for the allocated field is visible in the fragment, so per the missing-bound standard the out-of-domain count flow is the finding without needing the backing allocation.
limitations: Integer overflow inside gf_sg_vrml_mf_alloc (count * element size) is not visible and is not confirmed; no secondary CWE assigned.
Actual OOB read/write inside gf_sg_vrml_mf_alloc / gf_sg_vrml_mf_get_item depends on callee internals; demoted in favor of the missing-bound flow.
If gf_bs_read_int returns 0 on bitstream exhaustion, nbFields becomes 0 and the loops are no-ops; treated as benign robustness, not a finding.
codec->ActiveQP / pCurrentProto / force_keep_qp states are framework-provided and unvalidated; L25's sink is reachable only when ActiveQP is set, but that guard does not bound nbFields.
The qp_local == 2 branch is commented-out dead code; not a vulnerability.

verdict.summary: `qeh` (a pointer-typed parameter, line 1) is dereferenced unconditionally at line 6 (`qeh->qeh_flags`) and at lines 8, 16, 19, 26-28, 32-33 with no NULL check and no shown statement establishing a non-NULL bound; NULL is a member of its full declared domain, so a caller-supplied NULL reaches the dereference and crashes the process (NULL-pointer dereference/DoS, CWE-476). The other dangerous-looking operations (TSU capacity at line 16, dyn-table minimum clamp at lines 17-18, unvalidated `max_table_size`/`max_risked_streams` forwarded to `lsqpack_enc_init` at lines 19-21) are either protected by shown statements or demoted as thin-wrapper forwards with no in-fragment derivation.

evidence.reason: `qeh` (struct qpack_enc_hdl *, line 1) has declared domain {NULL, valid pointer} and the fragment imposes no constraint on it: there is no NULL check, comparison, or initialization of `qeh` anywhere before this line, so its residual range is the full declared domain (internal-helper parameter, Phase 1). This statement dereferences `qeh->qeh_flags` unconditionally and is the first executable statement of the body, so the witness qeh=NULL passes every (absent) guard on the path and triggers a NULL-pointer dereference (CWE-476), a process-crash/availability failure. The protective statements at lines 16 and 17-18 bound only `qeh->qeh_tsu_sz` and `dyn_table_size` respectively and do not constrain `qeh`; subsequent unconditional dereferences at lines 8, 16, 19, 26-28, and 32-33 are equally unguarded.

assumptions: sizeof(qeh->qeh_tsu_buf) (line 16) is the compile-time capacity of the TSU buffer and equals the capacity handed to lsqpack_enc_init.
lsqpack_enc_init follows the standard capacity-in/used-out convention for (qeh->qeh_tsu_buf, &qeh->qeh_tsu_sz).
QENC_MIN_DYN_TABLE_SIZE is a positive constant, making {0} ∪ [QENC_MIN_DYN_TABLE_SIZE, UINT_MAX] the admitted set for dyn_table_size at lines 17-18.
qeh->qeh_tsu_sz is size_t, matching the %zu format at line 26.
limitations: CWE-476 verdict assumes a caller passes NULL for qeh; the concrete NULL producer is not shown, but the rubric's pointer-parameter rule treats the absence of the NULL check as the defect itself (no shown NULL producer is required).

`max_table_size` and `max_risked_streams` (and `dyn_table_size` values >= QENC_MIN_DYN_TABLE_SIZE) flow to lsqpack_enc_init (lines 19-21) with residual range up to UINT_MAX and no visible upper bound; demoted under the thin-wrapper rule because the shown code forwards them unchanged with no in-fragment derivation of an out-of-domain value, and any callee-side allocation failure/internal error is unshown (would be at most a CWE-770/CWE-20 range claim below the evidence bar).
`assert(qeh->qeh_flags & QEH_INITIALIZED)` (line 6) is not a confirmed reachable abort: no shown path produces an uninitialized qeh; it is an internal precondition and debug-build behavior.
TSU buffer safety relies on the callee respecting the line-16 capacity; an overflow inside lsqpack_enc_init would be callee behavior outside the fragment.
Log-format candidates (lines 10, 23, 26, 30-31) use constant format strings with matching argument types and integer-only payloads; no injection.
No loops are present in the fragment, so no loop-bound analysis applies.

verdict.summary: BiasAndClamp applies per-element bias/clamp using untrusted array_size/bias_size parameters with no runtime validation: the only guard, TFLITE_DCHECK_EQ((array_size % bias_size), 0) (line 9), is a debug-only assertion that neither protects release builds nor rejects non-positive sizes. With non-dividing sizes (e.g. array_size=5, bias_size=2) the reference loop writes array_data[5] past the array_size=5 capacity at lines 60-61, and the NEON path writes past array_ptr+array_size (lines 15, 52-53); negative/zero bias_size additionally yields non-termination (lines 15, 57-58) and division by zero (line 9).

evidence.snippet:
array_data[array_offset + i] = ActivationFunctionWithMinMax(
          array_data[array_offset + i] + bias_data[i], clamp_min, clamp_max);
evidence.reason: array_size=5, bias_size=2: line 57 admits offsets 0,2,4; last chunk offset=4 with i=1 writes array_data[5], but the visible capacity is array_size=5 elements (valid indices 0..4, derived from the line 57 bound and line 12 end pointer), so index 5 is a 1-element out-of-bounds write. bias_size/array_size retain their full int domain: line 9 is a debug-only assertion (TFLITE_DCHECK, no runtime effect in release, and even when active it checks only divisibility and admits negatives). CWE-787 OOB write via unvalidated size-derived index.

NEON path with array_size=4, bias_size=3: line 9 is inert in release builds; line 15 admits a second chunk at array_ptr = array_data+3 (3 != 4), and the tail loop (lines 51-54) writes array_ptr[1] and array_ptr[2], i.e. indices 4 and 5, exceeding the visible capacity array_size=4 established by array_end_ptr = array_ptr + array_size (line 12). OOB write of 2 elements; same CWE-787 mechanism from unvalidated bias_size/array_size.

assumptions: array_data's capacity is array_size elements, derived from the loop bound at line 57 (array_offset < array_size) and the end pointer at line 12 (array_end_ptr = array_ptr + array_size).

bias_size and array_size are internal-helper parameters whose declared int domain is unconstrained by any shown runtime check; the line-9 modulo assertion, even taken as active, restricts neither sign nor zero.
limitations: TFLITE_DCHECK_EQ is read as a debug-only assertion (name/standard semantics), since its macro definition is not in the fragment; if it were an active runtime check, the positive-mismatch witnesses would abort at execution time; however, negative sizes admitted by '% == 0' (array_size=-8, bias_size=4; bias_size=-4, array_size=4) still pass it and break the loops, so the function remains unsafe under the strongest reading.
The NEON-path claims apply only when USE_NEON is defined; the reference (#else) path is analyzed independently and is also OOB-capable.

Non-termination (CWE-835) is additionally confirmed: bias_size==0 freezes array_offset in the reference loop (lines 57-58), and bias_size<0 walks array_ptr away from array_end_ptr forever (line 15); recorded here, not as a second CWE, because it shares the missing-size-validation root cause.
Line 9 performs integer division by zero (UB) when bias_size==0 if the macro evaluates its argument; crash-class, not the primary finding.
bias_data and array_data are dereferenced with no NULL check on any non-empty execution (lines 18-22, 52, 60-61); robustness concern, not the primary finding.

Extreme magnitudes (bias_size=INT_MIN at lines 17/43 'bias_size - 16'/'bias_size - 4', and pointer arithmetic before the object at lines 12/15 with negative sizes) are UB; not used as a demonstrated witness.

verdict.summary: restore_index (int, line 3) receives no bounds or negativity check and is used as a flat-array index into tensor_name_t (line 16) and into context->input(2) (line 53); nothing shown links either tensor's element count to restore_index, so an attacker-chosen index performs an out-of-bounds read of tstring objects from heap storage (CWE-125).

evidence.reason: restore_index is declared int at line 3 and no shown statement constrains it before this sink; the only earlier guard (line 8, size == 1) applies to file_pattern_t, not to restore_index or to tensor_name_t's element count, which the fragment never derives. With a 1-element tensor_name_t and restore_index = 2 (or any value outside [0, NumElements)), the flat<tstring>() element fetch reads past the array end, and a negative index reads before it — a missing-bound out-of-bounds read, CWE-125.

Same unvalidated restore_index (line 3, full int domain) indexes context->input(2)'s flat tstring array on the restore_slice == true path admitted by line 51; the guard at line 51 constrains only restore_slice, and the shape_spec.empty() guard at line 54 executes after this OOB fetch (sink at line 53 precedes it). No shown statement bounds restore_index against input(2)'s element count, so this is the same missing-bound OOB read, CWE-125.

assumptions: flat<tstring>() yields one element per tensor element, with capacity equal to the tensor's element count via NumElements() semantics, as evidenced by the NumElements() call at line 6 and the size == 1 guard at line 8.
The line 8 guard admits exactly one element for file_pattern_t, so the line 13 index 0 is in-bounds.
allocate_output success (lines 70-71) guarantees non-null t.
ParseShapeAndSlice output is validated against saved_shape by IsSameSize (lines 59-65), and a zero-element output_shape returns early at line 73 before CopySliceData.
limitations: restore_index is also forwarded to context->expected_output_dtype(restore_index) (line 42) and context->allocate_output(restore_index, ...) (line 71); their out-of-range semantics live in framework code not shown, so they are noted as the same root cause but not independently confirmed.

tensor_name (obtained from the OOB read or the checkpoint) is interpolated into error status strings (lines 39-40, 46) without sanitization, but the fragment contains no log/message sink, so no injection CWE is confirmed.
preferred_shard is passed unvalidated to GetReader (line 24) and TensorSliceReader (line 28), but no consuming sink is visible in the fragment.
CHECK_NOTNULL(reader) (line 32) and new TensorSliceReader (line 28) can fail only on environment conditions (OOM), not on an attacker-directed failure, and no failure state is consumed.

The witness for the OOB read fixes the tensor element count (1) from an unconstrained domain; the index value itself is a full-domain member, and the fragment shows no capacity to be exceeded relative to a shown bound, so the confirmation rests on the missing-bound flow and is calibrated at 0.75.
No loops appear in the fragment, so no loop-termination or parser-position analysis applies.

verdict.summary: Chunk-offset bounds checks at lines 94 and 184 compute `offsets[i] + k` in unsigned 64-bit arithmetic before comparing to `size`, so an element equal to `2^64-20` (tiled) or `2^64-8` (scanline) wraps the sum to 0, the guard admits the path for any buffer size, and the subsequent `memcpy` calls read from `head + ~2^64`, an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) enabled by the wraparound (CWE-190).

evidence.reason: offsets[tile_idx] is a tinyexr_uint64 parameter element with unconstrained residual domain [0, 2^64-1]. The guard at line 94 (`offsets[tile_idx] + sizeof(int) * 5 > size`) adds 20 in uint64 arithmetic, so for offsets[tile_idx] = 2^64-20 the sum wraps to 0, `0 > size` is false for every size, and the path is admitted with no check between line 94 and this read. data_ptr (line 103) is head + 2^64-20, ~2^64 bytes beyond the size-byte buffer, and this 16-byte copy performs an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125); the unsigned wraparound corrupting the guard result is the independently confirmed secondary root cause (CWE-190).

Same admitted path as the line 106 sink: with offsets[tile_idx] = 2^64-20 the line 94 guard wraps to 0 and admits the path, data_ptr (line 103) points ~2^64 bytes past the buffer, and this 4-byte read at data_ptr+16 is out of bounds (CWE-125, secondary CWE-190). The later `data_len` checks at line 125 execute after this read and cannot protect it.

The scanline guard at line 184 (`offsets[y_idx] + sizeof(int) * 2 > size`) adds 8 in uint64 arithmetic, so offsets[y_idx] = 2^64-8 wraps the sum to 0, `0 > size` is false for every size, and the else branch is taken. data_ptr (line 192) is head + 2^64-8, ~2^64 bytes beyond the buffer, and this 4-byte read is out of bounds (CWE-125, primary in this branch, with secondary CWE-190 from the wrapping addition). All later guards (201, 204, 208, 219, 237) execute after this read.

Same admitted path as the line 195 sink: with offsets[y_idx] = 2^64-8 the line 184 guard wraps to 0 and admits the else branch, data_ptr (line 192) is ~2^64 bytes past the buffer, and this 4-byte read at data_ptr+4 is out of bounds (CWE-125, secondary CWE-190).

assumptions: tinyexr_uint64 is an unsigned 64-bit integer, so `offsets[i] + k` wraps modulo 2^64; this is the declared type of the vector elements at line 2.
head/size describe a buffer of exactly `size` bytes, and any real object is far smaller than 2^64 bytes, so `head + (2^64-20)` is out of bounds by construction.
Loop indices tile_idx (0..num_tiles-1) and y_idx (0..num_blocks-1) are in-bounds of `offsets` because num_tiles/num_blocks are taken from `offsets.size()` (lines 44, 80).
`sizeof(int)` is 4 bytes, matching the `sizeof(int) * 5 = 20` and `sizeof(int) * 2 = 8` header/offset arithmetic in the shown code.
limitations: Unchecked `calloc` (82-83) and `AllocateImage` (87-89, 174-176) with NULL then dereferenced (85/87, 240): the failure requires an allocator failure on attacker-scaled sizes; environment-dependent, no concrete witness, so not confirmed.

Signed-overflow UB in `data_window` arithmetic (16-17, and `data_window[3] + 1` at 215): under the strongest protective reading the wrapped/negative results are caught by the `data_height < 0` (19) and `num_lines <= 0` (219) checks, so no out-of-domain sink was demonstrated.
`DecodeTiledPixelData` return value at lines 135-147 is discarded; this is an error-handling robustness concern with no demonstrated memory-safety impact.

The `2 << 20` (2^21) line_no cap at line 204 admits slightly larger values than the 2^20 heuristic in the comment; the admitted values are still bounded by the window checks, so no security-relevant consumer was found.
The write loop at lines 269-270 (`exr_header->pixel_types[c]`) has no visible capacity for `pixel_types` in the fragment, so an OOB claim cannot be anchored.

verdict.summary: Remote out-of-bounds read in pjmedia_rtcp_fb_parse_rpsi: line 25 computes rpsi_bit_len = rpsi_len*8 - 16 - padlen in unsigned arithmetic, and for the guard-admitted packet hdr->length==2 (rpsi_len==0) with any padlen 0..255 the value wraps to a huge positive number, so line 26 passes a length of ~536,870,910 bytes to pj_strset for a string that has only 6 valid bytes remaining in the 12-byte buffer, causing an OOB read (CWE-125) from a root-cause unsigned underflow (CWE-190) when the recorded RPSI string is consumed.

evidence.reason: The length argument (rpsi->rpsi_bit_len + 7)/8 is derived from packet data with no visible bound. Entry-point fields: hdr->length (pj_uint16_t at line 18) and padlen (pj_uint8_t at line 23, full 0..255 domain, never constrained). The guard at line 19 ('if (length < rpsi_len + 12) return PJ_ETOOSMALL;') admits rpsi_len == 0 whenever length >= 12 (e.g., length==12 with hdr->length==2). Line 25 then computes rpsi_len*8 - 16 - padlen entirely in unsigned arithmetic: 0 - 16 - 0 wraps to 4294967280 (32-bit) / 2^64-16 (64-bit), making the line-26 length argument ~536,870,910 while only 6 bytes (offset 6..11) of the admitted 12-byte buffer remain past p. The line-19 guard certifies only length >= rpsi_len+12 and bounds the non-wrapping case (string end <= rpsi_len+4 < rpsi_len+12); it does not constrain padlen or the sign of rpsi_bit_len, so the wrapped length is an out-of-domain size for the pj_strset string-length parameter, producing an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) whose root cause is the unsigned underflow (CWE-190).

assumptions: pj_size_t is unsigned (declared in the fragment at line 9), so rpsi_len*8 - 16 - padlen at line 25 uses unsigned arithmetic and wraps modulo the unsigned width.

The RTCP common header (pjmedia_rtcp_common) is 4 bytes (u16 length + u8 pt + u8 count), so padlen/pt reads at offsets 4 and 5 are covered by the line-19 bound and the RPSI payload starts at offset 6; the OOB finding does not depend on this exact offset since the derived length is orders of magnitude larger than any buffer.
pj_strset's third parameter is a string length consumed as such (it records ptr/slen on rpsi->rpsi), per its name and use in the shown code.
PJ_ASSERT_RETURN performs its runtime check (returns the status on failure).
rpsi->rpsi_bit_len is at least 32 bits wide; whether it is 32- or 64-bit, the wrapped value yields a huge length at line 26.
limitations: The downstream consumer of rpsi->rpsi is not shown; the OOB read is realized by any consumer that copies or scans the recorded huge length (unvalidated-size/missing-bound flow confirmed by the shown arithmetic alone).
hdr->length values 0 and 1 make rpsi_len wrap to a huge unsigned, but the line-19 guard then rejects the packet ('length < huge + 12'), so that path is not a separate finding.
The cast of buf to pjmedia_rtcp_common* may raise alignment/strict-aliasing concerns, but no security consequence can be confirmed from the fragment.
If rpsi_bit_len were signed, the stored negative value would still convert to a huge pj_size_t length at the line-26 call, so the finding is robust to the unshown field type.

verdict.summary: Unconditional write through node->sgprivate at line 27 without a NULL check. node is derived from the attacker-controlled bitstream via gf_bifs_dec_node (line 6); the fragment constrains only node (line 7) and its tag (line 16), never the sgprivate pointer field, which retains NULL in its residual range. A decoded QuantizationParameter node with sgprivate == NULL reaches the dereference on the lines 6->7->10->13->14->16->22->23->24->27 path and crashes the process (NULL pointer dereference, CWE-476).

evidence.reason: Sink is an unconditional write through node->sgprivate. node is the entry-point-derived return of gf_bifs_dec_node (line 6) parsing bitstream bs; the fragment's only guards are line 7 (node != NULL) and line 16 (tag == TAG_MPEG4_QuantizationParameter), and neither constrains the sgprivate pointer field extracted from the decoded payload. Since no shown statement checks or initializes node->sgprivate, NULL remains in its residual range and the guard admitted sets (non-NULL QP-tagged node) intersect the failure set (sgprivate == NULL); the dereference at line 27 then faults. NULL pointer dereference, CWE-476, reachable on every path where the caller supplies a bitstream decoding to a QP node lacking sgprivate; the fragment demonstrates the missing NULL check.

assumptions: Line 7 guarantees node != NULL on all continuing paths; only NULL nodes are excluded.
Line 16 guarantees gf_node_get_tag(node) == TAG_MPEG4_QuantizationParameter on the path to lines 22-27, which also makes the cast at line 22 type-consistent.
node is produced by gf_bifs_dec_node (line 6) from the entry-point bitstream bs, making node and its fields attacker-influenced data.
limitations: The NULL producer for node->sgprivate resides inside gf_bifs_dec_node, whose body is not shown, so the witness is a residual-range witness rather than a fully traced concrete bitstream; this caps confidence at 0.62.

Unchecked returns of gf_sg_command_new (line 29) and gf_sg_command_field_new (line 30), dereferenced at lines 30-33, can only be NULL on allocation failure of fixed-size requests with no attacker-scaled argument; treated as robustness, not a CWE finding.
Dereferences of codec->scenegraph (lines 10, 14, 24) and codec->current_graph (line 29) rely on context invariants not visible in the fragment and carry no attacker-scaled values; no CWE assigned.
Discarded status of gf_node_unregister (lines 11, 17) and gf_list_add (line 34) has no security-relevant operation running on a failure state in the shown code.

verdict.summary: The size expression passed to o_malloc at line 98 sums four unconstrained size_t parameters (rpid_hash_len, credential_id_len, cert_x_len, cert_y_len) plus constants; unsigned arithmetic wraps modulo 2^64, so e.g. rpid_hash_len = SIZE_MAX yields a 33-byte allocation, and the memcpy at line 108 then copies rpid_hash_len (SIZE_MAX) bytes into it, causing a heap out-of-bounds write. No statement constrains any of the four lengths.

evidence.reason: CWE-787 OOB write sink: rpid_hash_len is a size_t parameter (line 1) with residual range [0, SIZE_MAX] and no constraint anywhere in the fragment. The allocation at line 98 is o_malloc(rpid_hash_len+32+credential_id_len+cert_x_len+cert_y_len+2); with rpid_hash_len = SIZE_MAX and the other lengths 0, the unsigned sum wraps to 33, so o_malloc(33) is admitted by the line-98 NULL-only guard. Line 108 then copies SIZE_MAX bytes into data_signed+1 (a 33-byte heap object), overflowing by ~2^64 bytes.

CWE-190 root cause: the allocation size sums four unconstrained size_t parameters with client_data_hash_len=32 (line 10) and 2, all in unsigned 64-bit arithmetic. For rpid_hash_len = 2^64-1 (SIZE_MAX) and the other lengths 0, the expression evaluates to 33 mod 2^64, which is consumed as the allocation size; the guard only tests for NULL, so the wrapped size is admitted, and the subsequent line-108 memcpy performs the overflow.

Standard name-implied semantics of the unshown helpers are used only where the fragment itself passes arguments: `skip_bits_long(gb, off)` advances by `off` bits, `get_bits(gb, 1)` reads one bit, `avpriv_mpeg4audio_get_config2` returns a bit count or a negative error sentinel (only the sign is material to the shown code).

No claim is made about caller-provided bounds on `size` (e.g., the demuxer's extradata size), since the callers are not shown; the not-vulnerable verdict stands on the fragment's own protective statements (lines 10-11, 17, 21, 25/29/33), not on any external invariant.

params.axis and params.batch_dims are integer index-valued fields copied verbatim into tflite::GatherParams; their exact declared width is not visible in the fragment, but any integer width leaves the residual range far larger than [0, rank(input)).
No constraining statement exists anywhere in the fragment (no comparison, clamp, equality check, or sanitization); the flow from lines 4-5 and 7-8 to lines 6-9 is unconditional.
limitations: The concrete input rank and axis-dimension sizes are not visible in the fragment, so the axis/positions defects are confirmed as a complete residual-range (missing-bound) analysis rather than a single demonstrated value; confidence is capped accordingly.
The out-of-range positions claim depends on the standard name-implied semantics of Gather consuming positions as indices at this call site; the values themselves are not parsed inside the fragment.

No statement on the path (zero-defaults at 164/182, max-merge at 155-158, %.20g formatting at 196-197) clamps or rejects the value; the delegate receives a page of magnitude ~1e19 x 1e19, enabling attacker-directed resource exhaustion.
