verdict.summary: Loop 2 (line 46) iterates over function->args_count, an unvalidated internal count with its full declared domain, and uses it to index the newly laid-out value array (p = native->arguments at line 43, advanced at line 51), dereferencing p at line 47 and conditionally writing at line 48. Same unvalidated flow as the line 47 read: when njs_is_valid(p) is false, this statement writes to the same offset p in the value array whose capacity is not visible in the fragment. It is reachable for every n admitted by the line 46 loop bound (function->args_count unconstrained) and constitutes the write side of the same missing-bound flow (not tagged CWE-787 because the target capacity is unshown).

assumptions: end - start == value_count is assumed from the name-implied semantics of njs_function_frame_values/njs_function_frame_value_count for the in-bounds assessment of loop 1; loop 1 is otherwise bounded by the shown start < end condition (line 36).

The OOB verdict relies on the missing-bound doctrine (no visible destination capacity) and is therefore a range claim rather than a demonstrated concrete witness.

verdict.summary: qftf_list is assigned from the user-supplied 'quickfixtextfunc' callback's return value (rettv.vval.v_list at line 34) and dereferenced unconditionally at qftf_list->lv_refcount++ (line 35). assumptions: A VAR_LIST-typed typval's vval.v_list pointer is unconstrained by any shown statement, so NULL remains in its residual range (Vim's empty-list representation).

limitations: qfl is dereferenced at lines 9 and 22 without a NULL check; demoted because NULL qfl cannot be produced by any shown path (caller-provided invariant, robustness class), no CWE attached.

verdict.summary: The state machine bounds every *p read and every in-place write with the entry guard (if (p == pe) goto _test_eof; at L16-17) and a per-state guard (if (++p == pe) goto _test_eofN;) before each case's read, so all accesses stay within [buffer+off, buffer+len). Every (ptr,len) slice passed to the parser callbacks derives from in-bounds marks with lengths in [0, len-off-1], and header_done gets p+1 <= pe with count >= 0. All loops advance p by 1 per iteration and terminate at p == pe. No reachable OOB, injection, logic, or termination flaw is demonstrated by the shown code.

assumptions: MARK/PTR_TO/LEN follow standard Ragel semantics: MARK stores the current position, PTR_TO yields a pointer into buffer, LEN computes p - mark (a non-negative in-buffer length). This is consistent with the visible asserts comparing parser->mark and parser->field_len against len.
The parser state cs takes values from the generated set 0..46; every state 1..46 is represented in the switch, and 0 has no case.
The buffer is treated as writable by the in-place snake_upcase_char normalization (the const cast), matching the callers' read-buffer usage; writes are in-bounds.
The function-pointer callbacks consume (ptr, len) slices of buffer; their internal behavior is outside the fragment.
limitations: The preconditions off <= len and pointer-distance identity (L5, L11) are asserts only; under NDEBUG a caller violating them could drive undefined behavior. This is a caller-contract robustness concern, not an attacker-reachable flaw through the shown data flow.
snake_upcase_char((char *)p) (L306, L310) casts away const and mutates the caller's buffer in place; it requires a writable buffer but is not an out-of-bounds access.

A cs value with no matching case (notably 0) falls through into the _test_eof2 label, which sets cs = 2; whether the epilogue's puma_parser_has_error logic (not shown) preserves the error state cannot be fully confirmed, but no OOB or incorrect continuation is demonstrated.
parser->nread accumulates unboundedly across calls (its type is not shown); overflow would require a session of ~2^64 bytes and is not attacker-scalable within the fragment.
No finding was confirmed, so no CWE is assigned; confidence reflects the decisive visible per-state bounds guards.

verdict.summary: The signed `step` parameter is never validated. With `step < 0`, `from += step` (line 13) moves the read pointer below the start of the source region and the dereferences at lines 14/11/20 read out of bounds past the object defined by `[from, end)`; with `step = 0`, the loops at lines 10 and 20-21 never terminate. No protective statement in the fragment bounds `step`, so the out-of-domain stride flows directly into pointer arithmetic and dereferences (CWE-125; same root also yields CWE-835 non-termination).

evidence.reason: Primary sink. `step` (line 1) is a signed int with no shown constraint, so its residual range includes every negative value. For `step = -1`, line 13 sets `from = from_initial - 1`; the line-14 guard `from >= end` is false (pointer moved downward) and `data != *from` dereferences `from_initial - 1`, outside the object region `[from, end)` established by the fragment. No statement bounds `step` or checks a base address; lines 10/14/20 bound only the upper edge. Confirmed out-of-bounds read, CWE-125, recurring every outer-loop iteration.

Same unvalidated-stride root: on every iteration after the first with `step < 0`, `from` has been decremented below `from_initial`, and the line-10 guard `from < end` still admits it, so this unconditional dereference reads outside the source region `[from, end)`. Missing bound on `step` (line 1) is the defect; CWE-125.

Non-termination with the same admitted input: with `step = 0` (member of the unconstrained int residual range) and any non-empty input, `from += step` at line 21 never advances `from`, so the condition `from < end && *from == data` stays true forever, and the outer loop at line 10 also never terminates. Same root cause (missing `step > 0` validation) as the primary CWE-125 finding; noted here rather than as a separate CWE.

assumptions: `byte` is treated as an unsigned 8-bit type and `gp_file` as an output-stream handle, consistent with usage in the fragment (`data >= 0xc0`, `gp_fputc(ch, file)`), though their definitions are not in the fragment.
The fragment defines the readable object as the parameter region starting at `from` and ending at `end`; no statement in the fragment establishes storage at addresses below the initial `from`.
limitations: Integer overflow in `int max_run = step * MAX_RUN_COUNT` (line 8) for `step > INT_MAX/15` is demoted: it only skips the line-23 chunk loop and leaves the count byte at line 29 unbounded, corrupting PCX output; demonstrating it requires absurd magnitudes (|step| in the hundreds of millions and multi-GB runs) and no memory-safety impact is shown.
Division by zero at line 29 is unreachable as a separate fault: `step = 0` stalls the inner loop at lines 20-21 first.
`gp_fputc` return values are discarded at lines 16/24/25/29/31 and `file == NULL` is unchecked; these are non-attacker-directed robustness concerns, not confirmed findings.
`from == NULL` would dereference NULL at line 11 (pointer-parameter rule); not listed as an additional CWE because it is secondary to the primary unvalidated-`step` finding.

The verdict rests on the absence of any `step` constraint in the fragment; a caller-side contract guaranteeing `step > 0` is not visible in the shown code and, per the analysis rules, cannot shrink the parameter's residual range.
The non-termination manifestation (CWE-835) shares the same root cause as the OOB read, so it is not issued as an independent CWE.

verdict.summary: The image-header-derived catalog_size is capped by the guard at line 28 (admitted 0..INT_MAX/4, excluded larger values) before the x4 allocation (line 33), the x4 bdrv_pread (line 35), and the element-indexing loop (lines 40-41). Over the admitted range the 32-bit product never wraps (max 2,147,483,644) and every index stays within the catalog_size x 4-byte buffer, so no heap overflow, OOB access, or non-terminating loop is reachable; residual robustness concerns (g_malloc OOM abort, unvalidated nb_sectors/tracks) do not constitute confirmed findings.

assumptions: s->catalog_size is treated as a 32-bit unsigned value: it is assigned from le32_to_cpu(ph.catalog_entries) (line 27), and the INT_MAX/4 guard (line 28) is exactly the bound that prevents a 32-bit wrap of the x4 product.

bdrv_pread returns a negative status on failure/short read, and the checks at lines 12-14 and 36-38 are the intended error handling.
limitations: g_malloc at line 33 can abort on OOM (size attacker-adjustable up to ~2 GB), but that requires an environment-level allocation failure not deterministically produced by any admitted input; robustness concern, no CWE assigned.

ph.nb_sectors -> bs->total_sectors (line 23) and ph.tracks -> s->tracks (line 25) are unvalidated, but neither reaches a security-relevant sink inside the fragment; validation, if required, is outside the shown scope.
A NULL bs->file or bs->opaque is not shown as producible or attacker-directed in the fragment, so no dereference finding is asserted.

If s->catalog_size were, contrary to the le32_to_cpu-derived 32-bit unsigned semantics, a signed int, an admitted near-INT_MAX value could overflow x4; the visible assignment and guard read as 32-bit unsigned, so this is not a demonstrated defect of the shown code.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. The cframe-chain unwind is protected against a NULL-cframe dereference by the explicit guard `if (cf == NULL) return 0;` (lines 12-13), which executes immediately after the only NULL-producing assignment inside the inner loop and before any re-entry to line 6, and by the outer guard `&& cf` (line 5) covering the remaining `cf = cframe_prev(cf)` sites (lines 21, 29, 37). All frame dereferences (lines 15, 28, 42) are bounded by `frame > bot` (line 5), which excludes frame at or below the stack base. This is the patched form of LuaJIT's finderrfunc; the previously-known NULL-cframe dereference path is cut by a visible protective statement, and candidate robustness issues (NULL lua_State at lines 3-4, reachable lua_assert in the default case at line 46) are not demonstrably reachable from the shown inputs.

assumptions: `tvref(L->stack)` (line 3) yields the address of the first slot of the stack array, so `frame > bot` (line 5) bounds every frame dereference to slots strictly above the array base; the minimal admitted frame is `bot+1`, and the `(frame-1)` read at line 28 then maps to the base slot, still in-bounds.
The cframe chain is acyclic and `cframe_prev` terminates at NULL; this is used only to support the termination argument for the inner loop, not to justify any guard.

On the executing error-handling path `L->base` is above the stack base so `L->base-1` is admitted by `frame > bot` on the first iteration; if it is not, the outer loop does not execute and the function returns 0 without dereferencing `frame`.
`restorestack(L, -cframe_nres(cf))` (line 7) is used solely in a comparison; its result is never dereferenced in the fragment.
limitations: NULL `lua_State` dereference at lines 3-4 is not reported as a finding: NULL cannot be derived from any statement shown in the fragment and would require the unshown VM error path to pass a NULL state; it is treated as a caller-contract robustness concern, not a demonstrated attacker-reachable NULL.

The `lua_assert(0)` in the `default` case (line 46) is reachable only for a `frame_typep(frame)` tag outside FRAME_LUA..FRAME_PCALLH; no shown statement can produce such a tag, so no CWE-617 finding is confirmed.

An extreme `-cframe_nres(cf)` (e.g., INT_MIN underflow) would require an adversarial `nres` field in a cframe record with no shown producer; the computed pointer is only compared at line 7, never dereferenced, so no memory-access flaw is confirmed.

The precise semantics of `cframe_raw`, `frame_prevl`, `frame_prevd`, `frame_typep`, `frame_ftsz`, `restorestack`, and `savestack` are not shown in the fragment; the not-vulnerable verdict is anchored on the visible guard structure (lines 5, 12-13) rather than on proving those macros' internal arithmetic.

The errfunc-selection interplay between the inner cframe loop (lines 6-14) and the FRAME_CP/FRAME_C cases (lines 20-39) could not be fully re-derived without the macro bodies; no flaw is asserted there.
An off-by-one or OOB claim on the upper side of the stack was not made because no capacity for the stack array is visible in the fragment.

verdict.summary: Missing NULL validation on both pointer parameters: `adapter` and `pfunction` are dereferenced unconditionally (line 11 for `adapter`; lines 12/20/21 for `pfunction`, where `interface_to_usbdev` reads `pfunction->dev`) with no NULL check anywhere in the fragment, so a NULL value from either pointer's full declared domain reaches the dereferences and causes a kernel NULL-pointer dereference (CWE-476). Error-path `status` handling is correct on all branches (lines 16/25/31), so the confirmed mechanism is solely the unchecked parameter dereference.

evidence.reason: `pfunction` (line 2) has an unconstrained residual range including NULL: no statement in the fragment validates it before this dereference; the only prior guard (line 8 `if (!rsi_dev)`) tests `rsi_dev`, not `pfunction`. `interface_to_usbdev` is the kernel macro `container_of(pinterface->dev.parent, ...)`, which dereferences `pfunction->dev`, so `pfunction == NULL` is a concrete witness that passes every intervening guard and faults here (and at lines 20-21). NULL-pointer dereference, primary CWE-476.

Second distinct dereference of the same unconstrained `pfunction` parameter: `usb_set_intfdata` writes `pfunction->dev`'s driver data, requiring a non-NULL `pfunction`. No shown guard (lines 8-9, 15, 24, 29) constrains `pfunction`, so `pfunction == NULL` is admitted and causes the same NULL-pointer dereference as the line 12 sink. CWE-476.

`adapter` (line 1) is dereferenced here with no NULL check in the fragment; its residual range is the full pointer domain including NULL, and the only guard executed before it (line 8 `if (!rsi_dev)`) does not constrain `adapter`. Witness `adapter == NULL` passes all checks and faults at this write, and later at lines 29, 36, 39-42, 46. Independent NULL-pointer-dereference sink, same CWE-476.

assumptions: `interface_to_usbdev` and `usb_set_intfdata` are the standard kernel macros that dereference the passed `usb_interface *` (via `pinterface->dev`).
`struct rsi_hw` and `struct rsi_91x_usbdev` fields accessed are members of those structs; the fragment provides no other layout constraints.
All allocations are fixed-size (`sizeof(*rsi_dev)` line 7, `2048` line 23) and their results are checked (lines 8, 24), so no allocation-size or uninitialized-allocation issue exists.
limitations: Dangling `adapter->rsi_dev` after the endpoint-failure path (`adapter->rsi_dev = rsi_dev;` line 11 followed by `kfree(rsi_dev);` line 56) is a potential use-after-free (CWE-416) only if the caller subsequently dereferences `adapter->rsi_dev`; that consuming statement is outside the fragment, so the UAF cannot be confirmed here.

The NULL-deref finding relies on the pointer parameters being NULL, which a well-behaved USB-core/`rsi_probe` caller would not pass; per the scoping rules that caller guarantee is not visible in the fragment and is not used to shrink the residual range.
`status` is verified initialized on every return path (lines 16, 25, 31 before line 58); an uninitialized-return flaw is not present.
`MAX_DEBUGFS_ENTRIES - 1` (line 46) would underflow only if the macro were 0, which is not derivable from the fragment; not a confirmed finding.
No loop, input-derived size, format-string, injection, crypto, file, or auth logic exists in the fragment, so no other vulnerability class applies.

verdict.summary: All dangerous operations are covered by visible guards. The outer condition `while (frame > bot && cf)` (line 5) bounds every frame/cf dereference: it admits only `frame >= bot+1`, so the visible `(frame-1)->u32.lo` read (line 28) and `savestack(L, frame-1)` (line 42) are in-bounds, and it excludes NULL `cf` before each case-based chain update. Inside the inner loop, `if (cf == NULL) return 0;` (lines 12-13) executes before the loop condition re-dereferences `cf` after `cf = cframe_prev(cf)` (line 11), preventing a NULL dereference at line 6. The remaining anomalies (signed negation overflow of `-cframe_nres(cf)` at line 7; reachable `lua_assert(0)` at line 45) are demoted to limitations because the corrupting values are VM-internal with no shown producer and are consumed only in comparisons, not in any security-relevant operation within the fragment.

assumptions: Line 5's `while (frame > bot && cf)` admits only `frame >= bot+1`, so `frame-1 >= bot` whenever the loop body executes; this covers `(frame-1)->u32.lo` (line 28) and `savestack(L, frame-1)` (line 42).

The `cf` chain originates from `L->cframe` (line 4) and `cframe_prev` (lines 11/21/29) and is terminated by NULL; the frame/cframe fields are VM-maintained and the fragment shows no attacker path that writes them.
`cframe_nres` returns a signed integer (implied by the `cframe_nres(...) < 0` comparison at line 6).
limitations: The negation `-cframe_nres(cf)` (line 7) overflows for the most-negative signed value of `nres`, but the finding is demoted: the fragment neither produces nor constrains such an `nres` (VM-internal state, no shown producer), and the wrapped stack offset is consumed only by the `>=` comparison at line 7 (no dereference of the computed pointer in the fragment), so the witness chain (part 2) and security impact (part 3) are not demonstrated.
`lua_assert(0)` (line 45) is reachable only for a frame type outside the enumerated `FRAME_*` cases, which relies on an unshown VM invariant; not confirmed as CWE-617.

The exact read offsets and delta signs of the unshown helpers (`frame_typep`, `frame_prevl`, `frame_prevd`, `frame_ftsz`) are not visible; termination of the frame walk and helper read bounds rest on standard VM frame semantics. No positive finding depends on them.
Returned values `cframe_errfunc(cf)` (lines 10/36) and `savestack(L, frame-1)` (line 42) propagate to a caller outside the fragment; no security-relevant internal sink for those values is visible.

verdict.summary: Not vulnerable. The only input-derived security-relevant flow is catalog_entries -> s->catalog_size, which is capped by the guard at line 33 (rejects values > INT_MAX/4 = 536870911). Over the admitted range [0, 536870911], catalog_size * 4 maxes at 2147483644 (no signed or unsigned 32-bit overflow), the g_malloc size (line 38) exactly equals the bdrv_pread length (line 40), and the loop (lines 45-46) indexes at most catalog_size-1 elements, in-bounds and terminating.

assumptions: s->catalog_size and the le32_to_cpu() results are 32-bit values; the guard at line 33 is analyzed at its strongest reading (admitted set [0, 536870911]).
bdrv_pread either reads the full requested size or returns ret < 0 (both calls' results are checked at lines 12 and 41), so ph is fully populated and the catalog read exactly fills the allocation.
sizeof(struct parallels_header) >= 16, so the memcmp(ph.magic, HEADER_MAGIC, 16) at line 16 reads within ph.
limitations: On the fail path before line 38, g_free(s->catalog_bitmap) (line 52) operates on framework-provided opaque state (bs->opaque field) that the fragment neither initializes nor shows producing a non-NULL garbage value; no NULL/garbage deref witness can be constructed from shown statements (real QEMU zeroes opaque outside this fragment).

catalog_entries == INT_MAX/4 admits a one-shot ~2 GiB g_malloc at line 38; g_malloc aborts on OOM rather than returning, the buffer is freed after the short-file read fails, and the volume does not compound — treated as a resource/robustness concern, not a confirmed finding.
bs->total_sectors (line 23) and s->tracks (line 25) are not range-validated beyond the tracks != 0 check, but neither value is consumed by any security-relevant sink in the shown fragment.

verdict.summary: ex_copy uses the unvalidated parameters line1 and n as line indices into the buffer's line array: ml_get(line1) at line 33 and ml_append(curwin->w_cursor.lnum, ...) at line 36. The only guard on the path, 'while (line1 <= line2)' (line 29), imposes a purely relative inequality and does not bound line1 to the valid line interval, so any member of the full linenr_T domain satisfying line1 <= line2 (e.g., 0, negative, or a value above the buffer's line count) reaches the indexed read as an out-of-domain argument — a missing-bound/unvalidated-index flow (CWE-125). The copy-loop non-termination class is protected by lines 40-41 and terminates for all inputs.

evidence.reason: line1 is declared linenr_T (line 1) and no statement in the fragment constrains it; the loop guard 'while (line1 <= line2)' (line 29) admits every pair with line1 <= line2, including values outside [1, ml_line_count] (0, negatives, or values above the buffer's line count), and it is the only guard before this read. ml_get consumes its argument as a line index into the memline array (name-implied), and the fragment shows no capacity (ml_line_count) or absolute bound for the target, so the out-of-domain argument is a confirmed missing-bound / unvalidated-index flow causing an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125).

n (linenr_T, line 1) is stored unvalidated into curwin->w_cursor.lnum (line 28) and passed as ml_append's insert-position/lines index here. The fragment contains no bound on n before the call, so any member of the full linenr_T domain (including values outside the buffer's line range) reaches this insert sink — the same missing-bound/unvalidated-index class (CWE-125).

assumptions: linenr_T is a signed integer type (Vim's typedef); the fragment defines no narrower bound for it, so its full declared domain is the residual-range starting point.

ml_get consumes its first argument as a 1-based line index into the buffer's line array, and ml_append consumes its first argument as the line number after which a line is inserted (name-implied semantics).
The buffer capacity ml_line_count is not visible in the fragment, so no absolute bound for the parameters can be derived from the shown code.
limitations: The fragment appears to be the fixed counterpart of the copy-range non-termination bug: lines 40-41 ('if (line1 == n) line1 = curwin->w_cursor.lnum;') provably keep line1 ahead of the cursor after the destination collides with the source range, so the loop terminates for every input (CWE-835 candidate demoted; no witness survives the strongest protective reading).
A negative/zero count can arise from line1 > line2 at line 6, but it flows only into marks/message (lines 10, 50, 52), which have no security-relevant consumer in the fragment.
n+1 (line 25) and n+count (line 10) can wrap only at LONG_MAX domain extremes and feed undo/mark internals with no visible security sink; not independently confirmed as a vulnerability.

The OOB magnitude for the secondary ml_append and u_save flows depends on the unshown buffer size and callee handling; the confirmed defect is the missing bound rather than a demonstrated specific offset, so these are reported as the same class, not separate CWEs.
vim_strsave NULL handling (line 34) and u_save FAIL handling (lines 25-26) are correct; malloc failure here is not attacker-scaled by the numeric parameters and is treated as a robustness concern.

verdict.summary: Heap buffer overflow in find_pattern_in_path: the unvalidated int parameter `len` feeds `pat = alloc(len + 5)` (line 60) and a `sprintf(..., "%.*s", len, ptr)` (line 63). With `len = -1` the allocation is 4 bytes and the negative precision of `%.*s` is treated as omitted, so the whole entry-supplied `ptr` string is copied into the undersized heap buffer, producing an unbounded heap write (CWE-122).

evidence.reason: The sink writes into `pat`, whose capacity is `alloc(len + 5)` at line 60 — 4 bytes for the admitted residual-range value `len = -1` (internal-helper int parameter; Phase 1 residual [INT_MIN, INT_MAX] because no shown statement constrains it). The precision argument `len` is negative, so printf treats the precision as omitted and copies the full entry-supplied `ptr` string plus NUL (>= 5 bytes) into the 4-byte buffer, overflowing it by >= 1 byte (e.g., ptr="abcd"). Guard 55-58 admits the path (type not CHECK_PATH/FIND_DEFINE, compl_status_sol()==0) and executes before the sink; the NULL check at 61-62 only excludes allocation failure. Unbounded copy over a visible heap size: CWE-122.

assumptions: C semantics of printf-family `%.*s`: a negative precision argument is treated as if the precision were omitted (C11 7.21.6.1), i.e., an unbounded copy of the string argument.
`alloc(4)` succeeds on the normal non-failure path (the finding is the subsequent overflow, not an allocation failure).

`compl_status_sol()` is an unconstrained call result whose domain includes 0; `type``s admitted set includes values other than the two named constants since the fragment excludes at most two int values.
`ptr` is arbitrary entry-supplied content of unshown length; any payload of at least 4 bytes is sufficient for the overflow.

verdict.summary: Out-of-bounds heap read in _inplace_src_spans: the line 9 guard (num_spans == 0) admits num_spans == 1, and the do/while body unconditionally dereferences spans[1] at line 15 (and spans[0] at line 92 after spans++ at line 89), reading one element past the single-element span array (CWE-125).

evidence.reason: num_spans (line 3) is unsigned and the only shown constraint is line 9's `num_spans == 0` early return, leaving the admitted range 1..UINT_MAX. spans (lines 2-3) is an array of exactly num_spans cairo_half_open_span_t elements. For the admitted value num_spans == 1 the loop body executes once (line 90: `--num_spans` -> 0, `0 > 1` false) and line 15 dereferences spans[1], i.e. index 1 of a 1-element array — a heap out-of-bounds read. No check between line 9 and line 15 re-bounds the count, so the CWE-125 over-read is reachable with the exact witness num_spans == 1.

On the same admitted path num_spans == 1, line 89 (`spans++;`) advances the pointer one element past the sole array element before the loop exits (line 90: 0 > 1 false), so line 92 unconditionally dereferences spans[0].x out of bounds — a second CWE-125 over-read from the same root cause (line 9 admits num_spans == 1 and no later guard bounds the pointer before this read).

assumptions: spans (lines 2-3) is a pointer to an array of exactly num_spans cairo_half_open_span_t elements, so spans[1] with num_spans == 1 is one element past the end.
num_spans is declared unsigned (line 3); the line 9 guard excludes only the value 0 and admits 1..UINT_MAX.
limitations: Mask writes at lines 83-86 (`*m++`, `memset (m, spans[0].coverage, --len)`) take their size from `len` (line 15), but the capacity of the mask image behind `base` (line 6) is not visible in the fragment, so an overrun beyond a visible capacity cannot be confirmed as a separate CWE.

`abstract_renderer` (line 5) and the return of `pixman_image_get_data` (line 6) are dereferenced without NULL checks; no attacker-directed NULL producer is shown, so these are demoted as robustness concerns.
Return values of all `pixman_image_composite32` calls (lines 19-114) are discarded; no security-relevant operation runs on a failure state, so no error/status-handling finding is confirmed.
The fragment shows no monotonicity check on span x-coordinates; a negative `len` would fail the line 84 (`len > 1`) guard and affect only render correctness, not a confirmed memory error.

verdict.summary: When num_spans == 1, the guard at lines 9-10 rejects only 0, so the do-while body (line 14) still executes once and reads spans[1] at line 15 — one element past a one-element span array (CWE-125). A secondary unvalidated-length write into r->_buf (lines 82-88) is also present but its memory-corruption impact depends on the unshown buffer capacity.

evidence.reason: num_spans has residual range [1, UINT_MAX] after the line 9-10 guard, which excludes only 0; num_spans == 1 is therefore admitted. spans has exactly num_spans == 1 visible elements (capacity from the spans/num_spans parameter pairing, lines 2-3). The do-while at line 14 executes its body unconditionally before line 90's post-test (--num_spans > 1), so on the first and only iteration line 15 dereferences spans[1] at index 1, exceeding the 1-element capacity by exactly one element — a one-element out-of-bounds read (CWE-125).

With the same admitted witness num_spans == 1, the loop body runs once, spans++ (line 89) advances the pointer to original element 1, and line 92 dereferences spans[0].x on a 1-element array — a second one-element out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) caused by the same missing num_spans >= 2 bound that fails to protect line 15.

assumptions: spans points to an array of exactly num_spans elements — the only length visible is the num_spans parameter paired with spans (lines 2-3).
The do-while loop (lines 14-90) executes its body at least once; the post-condition at line 90 is tested only after the body runs.
cairo_half_open_span_t.x is consumed into int (line 15) and its coverage is stored into uint8_t *m (line 83).
limitations: The buffer-write path (lines 82-88) forwards an input-derived length len into memset and *m++ against r->_buf, whose capacity is not visible in this fragment; this is a range-based unvalidated-length (missing-bound) flow with possible CWE-787 impact, omitted from the verdict's CWE array because its corruption impact requires the unshown _buf/run_length capacity.

Subtracting spans[1].x - spans[0].x in int (line 15) can overflow on widely separated x values (CWE-190/signed-overflow UB), but no downstream consumer effect is confirmable inside the fragment (composite widths target unshown destinations; the memset guard at line 84 excludes negative lengths), so it is not reported.

Caller-side invariants (e.g., that num_spans is always >= 2) were deliberately not assumed, since no such bound appears in the shown code.

verdict.summary: QPaintEngineEx::stroke() can loop forever: any element-type byte in path.elements() (line 84) that is not MoveToElement/LineToElement/CurveToElement falls into the switch default (lines 128-129 and 190-191), which breaks out of the switch without advancing points, types, or lastPoint, so the while loops at lines 108 and 164 (guarded only by 'points < lastPoint', line 88) never terminate, causing a render-thread hang / denial of service on attacker-supplied path content.

evidence.reason: In the non-cosmetic branch, the loop at line 108 ('while (points < lastPoint)') advances only inside the MoveTo/LineTo/CurveTo cases (lines 110-127). A byte from the types buffer (line 84, path.elements()) outside those three values hits this default, which performs no advancement of points/types, so the loop condition at line 108 stays true forever. The byte's residual range is the full uchar domain because the fragment imposes no validation on it; guard order is line 9 (isEmpty, admits elementCount>=1), line 74 (activeStroker), line 107 (types non-null), line 108 (points<lastPoint, unchanged). Primary CWE-835 (loop non-termination / DoS).

Same defect in the cosmetic branch: the loop at line 164 ('while (points < lastPoint)') advances only in the three element-type cases (lines 166-188); this default at lines 190-191 leaves points/types/lastPoint unchanged, so any non-advancing element-type byte from path.elements() (line 84) keeps the line 164 loop non-terminating. Guard order is line 9, line 74, line 163 (types non-null), line 164; all admit a path with elementCount()==1 and a byte such as 0xFF. Primary CWE-835.

assumptions: QVectorPath::isEmpty() returning true iff elementCount()==0 bounds pointCount below by 1 after the early return at lines 9-10 (no upper bound is shown).
QPainterPath::ElementType is a byte-backed enum; any byte other than MoveToElement/LineToElement/CurveToElement reaches the switch default.
The only points-buffer capacity derivable from the fragment is 2*pointCount qreals via lastPoint = points + (pointCount<<1) at line 88.
The default pen path reaches the vulnerable loops: lines 62-64 set activeStroker for Qt::SolidLine, and line 21's dash branch is skipped for SolidLine.
limitations: OOB read at lines 122-123 (and 181-183) if a CurveToElement type occurs with fewer than 6 qreals remaining is demoted: it requires the QVectorPath points/types arrays to be mutually inconsistent, an invariant not established by any shown statement.
Integer-overflow/UB candidates at lines 88 (pointCount<<1) and 13 (elementCount()+4) require elementCount near 2^30, a magnitude not derived by any shown statement.
C-style casts ((const QPointF *)points) at lines 167, 181-183, 195, 200, 204 alias a qreal buffer as QPointF (strict-aliasing UB): robustness concern without a demonstrated attacker-visible failure.
StrokeHandler internal array growth (lines 13, 90-91) and the dashed-path point counts are not visible in the fragment, so no size claim is made against them.

verdict.summary: get_visual_text() derives the selection length *lenp from the unvalidated visual columns VIsual.col/curwin->w_cursor.col (lines 24/29) and indexes the NUL-terminated line pointer *pp with *lenp - 1 (lines 38/39) without any shown bound tying *lenp to the line length. For a selection whose end column exceeds the line length (full declared domain of the entry-point columns is unconstrained), the indexed read lands past the terminating NUL, causing an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125).

evidence.reason: Primary sink (multibyte path). *lenp originates at lines 24/29 as end_col - start_col + 1 from the entry-point columns VIsual.col and curwin->w_cursor.col, whose declared domain is unconstrained by any shown statement; the only extent the fragment establishes for *pp is its terminating NUL (STRLEN/NUL checks at lines 17, 31, 39). The guard at line 33 admits [1, INT_MAX] and imposes no upper bound against the line length, so for an admitted selection with end_col > L the pointer *pp + (*lenp - 1) reads beyond the NUL (witness: L=2, VIsual.col=0, w_cursor.col=50, *lenp=51, index 50). Missing-bound out-of-bounds read (CWE-125).

Second sink (non-multibyte path). Index *lenp - 1 derives from the same unconstrained visual columns via lines 24/29, passes guard line 33 (*lenp in [1, INT_MAX]) with no bound relative to the line length, and reads (*pp)[*lenp - 1] ahead of the NUL check. With an admitted end column beyond the line length the byte read is past the terminating NUL (witness: L=2, *lenp=51, offset 50), i.e. out-of-bounds read (CWE-125).

assumptions: The line buffer pointed to by *pp is NUL-terminated; the fragment establishes its extent L as the index of the first NUL via STRLEN(*pp) at line 17 and the NUL checks at lines 31 and 39.

VIsual.col and curwin->w_cursor.col are entry-point visual/cursor columns whose declared integer domain is unconstrained by any statement in the fragment; per the analysis rules they retain their full domain.
The same-line guard at line 8 (VIsual.lnum != curwin->w_cursor.lnum → FAIL) admits only single-line selections and does not bound the column values.
cap is NULL-checked at line 10 before clearopbeep(cap->oap), so no cap-related dereference issue exists in the fragment.
limitations: The OOB-read witness is a range claim: the column magnitude (e.g. col=50 vs L=2) is chosen from the unconstrained declared domain, not produced by a shown statement, and no backing line allocation is visible; this caps confidence at 0.55.

If an unshown invariant (e.g. ml_get_pos clamping col to the line length, or the editor never placing the cursor past a line's NUL) held, the sinks would stay in bounds; no such statement appears in the fragment and per the rules it cannot be used to downgrade the finding.

The multibyte branch can leave the trailing NUL included in *lenp when the selection ends exactly at the line's NUL (mb_ptr2len on NUL returns 1); this is a correctness discrepancy with no shown security consumer of the returned length, so it is not reported.

Integer overflow of end_col - start_col + 1 (lines 24/29) or of *lenp += mb_ptr2len(...) - 1 (line 38) would require column endpoints near INT_MIN/INT_MAX; this is an unsubstantiated magnitude and is not reported as a secondary CWE.

NULL out-parameters pp/lenp are dereferenced unconditionally (lines 31, 38, 39), but a NULL can only arise from a caller contract violation, which no shown statement produces; recorded as a robustness concern only.
Negative *lenp values are excluded by the guard at line 33, and a selection starting at the NUL is collapsed to 0 at lines 31-32, so those degenerate cases are not findings.

verdict.summary: The capability parser validates that only 3 bytes remain (L13) but then unconditionally copies sizeof(struct capability) bytes from pnt+1 (L22) with no upper bound, so a record that leaves 3-4 bytes in the buffer reads past the end of the packet. The capability length check (L25) runs after the copy and is computed in bgp_size_t arithmetic; a crafted 16-bit cap.length of 65533-65535 wraps cap.length+3 to 0-2, so the check admits the record and the advance at L58 moves only 0-2 bytes, keeping the loop in the OOB window.

evidence.reason: cap.length and the afi/safi fields are packet-provided 16-bit values with no constraint placed on them by the fragment (only the unrelated 3-byte check at L13 precedes this copy). The admitted set of the guard contains end-pnt in [3, sizeof(struct capability)-1], and for those members the copy at L22 reads 1+sizeof(struct capability) bytes from a buffer of length `length`, exceeding `end` — CWE-125. The capability-length check at L25 executes after the copy, so it cannot protect it; no visible statement bounds the memcpy.

cap.length is a 16-bit packet field; on its full declared domain cap.length+3 wraps (65533->0, 65534->1, 65535->2), so the check admits those values (the check evaluates to false) and the loop proceeds with cap.length interpreted as ~0-2 bytes. The advance at L58 is packet-controlled and unbounded by any visible upper check, while the loop then re-runs the 3-byte guard at L12 and the struct copy at L22 inside an end-window of only 3-4 bytes — CWE-190 enables the admitted OOB-window set used by the read.

assumptions: sizeof(struct capability) exceeds 3 bytes (the struct contains cap.code and a 4-byte mpc union; any real layout is >= 6 bytes).
bgp_size_t is an unsigned 16-bit type for BGP messages (the same 0-2 byte window results from 32-bit arithmetic with a 16-bit cap.length).
peer, peer->bgp, peer->afc_* are valid peer context; no NULL producers are shown, so no NULL-deref is confirmed.
limitations: The afi/safi indexing into peer->afc_recv[afi][safi] is well-guarded by the L33 whitelist; out-of-range 16-bit values are excluded before the indexing expression, and the array's declared length is not visible, so no OOB write is confirmed there.
peer->bgp / peer->host / peer->flags dereferences have no NULL-producing call in the fragment; those are robustness concerns.

The exact maximum of the OOB read depends on sizeof(struct capability), which is not visible; the mechanism and the 3-byte hole are fully shown, so the finding is confirmed as a range with the copy-size as the conservative cap.
Loop termination: the loop always ends when the pnt+3 guard fails, so CWE-835 non-termination is not confirmed; the wrapped advance of 0-2 bytes is the OOB-enabling mechanism, not an infinite loop.

verdict.summary: OP_BLKPUSH and OP_ARGARY guard the environment stack length with `MRB_ENV_LEN(e) <= m1+r+m2+1`, admitting `L = m1+r+m2+2`. When the keyword-flag bit `kd` is set, the read index `m1+r+m2+kd` maps to `e->stack` index `m1+r+m2+2 = L`, one past the valid range `0..L-1` established by OP_GETUPVAR's `b < MRB_ENV_LEN(e)` guard, causing an out-of-bounds read of one `mrb_value` past the `REnv` stack.

The same index is also read at line 1180. Confirmed OOB read (CWE-125).

Guard at line 647 (`MRB_ENV_LEN(e) <= m1+r+m2+1`) admits `L >= m1+r+m2+2`; with `kd=1` the read at line 680, `stack[m1+r+m2+1]` = `e->stack[m1+r+m2+2]`, equals `L` at the minimal admitted length and is out of the valid `0..L-1` range (line 260 convention). OOB read of one `mrb_value` past the REnv stack (CWE-125).

assumptions: In-fragment validity convention for `e->stack`: index is valid iff index < `MRB_ENV_LEN(e)` (shown by OP_GETUPVAR line 260 `b < MRB_ENV_LEN(e)` before `e->stack[b]`).
Bytecode operands are treated as entry-point data (untrusted `.mrb`) because the fragment shows no validation of any operand.
`uvenv` may return NULL; the fragment checks it at lines 260, 272, 646, 1173.
The exact env length `L` is produced outside the fragment (closure/block creation); the fragment only constrains it via lines 647 and 1173-1174.
limitations: The witness's boundary value `L = m1+r+m2+2` requires an env whose length equals the minimal admitted value; env-length production is not shown, so this is a range/boundary claim (fragile boundary), capping confidence at 0.65.

Systemic missing capacity: virtually every `regs[]`, `pool[]`, `syms[]` access (e.g., OP_MOVE line 48, OP_ARYPUSH's `for (mrb_int i=0; i<b; i++)` pushing `regs[a+i+1]`, OP_HASH's `int lim = a+b*2`, OP_STRING/OP_SYMBOL `len = pool[b].tt >> 2`) has no visible capacity and depends on the compiler/loader `nregs` invariant outside the fragment; not reported as distinct findings.
OP_JMPUW main-path `pc = irep->iseq + a;` (line 330) lacks an `a < irep->ilen` check (assert at line 316 is restore-path/debug-only); demoted as same systemic missing-validation class.
OP_ENTER truncating store `mrb->c->ci->n = (uint8_t)len;` (line 816) has no shown security-relevant consumer for the truncated value.
No NULL-deref finding: `uvenv` results are checked on the analyzed paths.

verdict.summary: In drill_parse_T_code, tool_num parsed from the drill file at line 57 is used to index image->aperture at line 72 after the bounds check at line 63 only logs "Out of bounds drill number %d" and falls through without returning or clamping. A T-code such as T-1 (or any value < TOOL_MIN or >= TOOL_MAX) reaches the subscript with an out-of-range index, producing an OOB read (CWE-125); the same invalid index is also stored to at lines 126-127 and 184 when the OOB read yields NULL.

No capacity or bound for image->aperture is visible in the fragment; the missing bound is itself confirmed by the shown check flagging the value as out of bounds and then continuing to the sink.

TOOL_MIN/TOOL_MAX and the exact capacity of image->aperture are not declared in the fragment; the finding rests on the missing bound: the shown check at line 63 flags out-of-range values yet fails to exclude them from the line-72 subscript.
limitations: OOB writes at lines 126-127 and 184 execute only when the line-72 read returns NULL; the fragment cannot guarantee that heap content, so they are demoted (same root cause, CWE-125 primary).

get_line(fd++) at line 26 followed by fd->filename at line 30 dereferences the post-incremented local pointer (OOB struct read/UB); consequence is confined to the logged message and layout-dependent, so not reported.

dia = (double)(16 + 8 * tool_num) / 1000 at line 195 can overflow signed int for huge tool_num, but it is only reachable after the already-UB invalid store at line 184 (when the OOB read returns NULL), so no independent confirmed finding.
gerbv_stats_printf %s with file-derived strings (lines 30, 48) uses placeholders only (no format-string bug); CR/LF injection into an unshown log backend is not confirmed.

state->current_tool at line 71 and drill_stats_add_to_drill_list at lines 146-149 and 222-225 receive the unvalidated tool_num; downstream use is outside the fragment, so no independent CWE is assigned.
The EOF block at lines 168-176 is dead code ('\n'/'\r' can never equal EOF); no security impact identified.

verdict.summary: ex_copy consumes unvalidated line numbers: line1/line2/n retain their full linenr_T domain (no shown bound or capacity check), so ml_get(line1) at line 33 indexes the line array out of bounds for any admitted line1 exceeding the buffer's line count (missing bound, CWE-125), and count = line2 - line1 + 1 at line 6 wraps for in-domain extremes, corrupting the mark range and message count consumed at lines 10/50/54 (CWE-190).

line1 and line2 retain their full signed linenr_T domain (no shown constraint precedes line 6, which is the first statement). u_save returns OK on the analyzed paths; its FAIL outcome would return early at line 26 and is not forced by any shown input value.

limitations: Both confirmed findings are range claims: the decisive magnitudes (buffer line count B, linenr_T maximum) are not named in the fragment, so confidence is capped at 0.55.
The unbounded loop volume (lines 29-48, up to roughly line2-line1+1 appends for admitted ranges) is a resource-exhaustion aspect of the same missing bound and is not reported as a separate CWE.
n + 1 (lines 9, 25) and n + count (line 10) can also wrap for in-domain n; these are the same overflow family, lower severity, and are not listed separately.

ml_append position (line 36) derived from unvalidated n: the callee's boundary semantics are not visible, so no OOB-write claim is confirmed there.
NULL dereference of the vim_strsave result is prevented by the line-34 check before ml_append/vim_free; not a finding.
No injection, format-string, symlink, crypto, or authorization sinks are present in the fragment.

verdict.summary: Out-of-bounds read of the closure environment stack in OP_ARGARY (same defect in OP_BLKPUSH): the guard `MRB_ENV_LEN(e) <= m1+r+m2+1` (lines 639-640) admits an environment with exactly m1+r+m2+2 slots, and the kd branch then reads `stack[m1+r+m2+1]` == `e->stack[MRB_ENV_LEN(e)]` at line 672, one mrb_value past the last valid slot (capacity convention per OP_GETUPVAR guard at line 252). The kd bit of bytecode operand b and the admitted boundary value L = m1+r+m2+2 are both reachable from bytecode.

evidence.reason: OOB read (CWE-125). stack = e->stack + 1 (line 641) so stack[k] = e->stack[k+1]; the fragment's own capacity convention (OP_GETUPVAR guard at line 252 allows e->stack[b] only for b < MRB_ENV_LEN(e)) makes k valid only up to MRB_ENV_LEN(e)-2. verdict.summary: `rlen` can be negative and is passed as the length to `memcpy` at line 20; the negative int converts to a huge size_t, causing an out-of-bounds write into `buf` and out-of-bounds read from `dp->data`.

evidence.reason: The length argument `rlen` is set from `len` (line 12) or `remain` (line 17). `len` is an int parameter with no positivity check (its full int domain is admitted), and `remain` (line 10: `dp->logicalSize - dp->pos`) is unconstrained: guard line 14 excludes only `remain == 0`, and guard line 11 (`remain >= len`) admits negative `len` (e.g., `len = -1, remain = 10` -> `rlen = -1`) as well as the negative-remain path (`logicalSize = 10, pos = 20, len = 5` -> `remain = -10` -> `rlen = -10`). verdict.summary: ReadCINImage derives the per-row raster length from file-controlled columns (line 341) and bits_per_pixel (line 340) via GetBytesPerRow (lines 379/383) and passes it as the size argument of ReadBlobStream(image,length,pixels,&count) (line 395), writing into the per-row quantum buffer (GetQuantumPixels, line 386) whose capacity is never shown or validated. The guard at line 348 admits {columns*rows/8 <= blob size} and does not constrain depth or per-row length; with rows=1 and blob size large enough, depth in [33,255] yields length > 12*columns (the 32-bit RGB quantum row extent implied by SetQuantumQuantum(quantum_info,32) at line 374), so ReadBlobStream overflows the row buffer - heap buffer overflow via unvalidated input-derived size, CWE-787. The read-count check at line 396 only rejects short reads and does not protect the buffer.

These are the same missing-NULL-check family as the primary finding and would be fixed by the same style of small check; grouped with the primary CWE-476 rather than counted separately.

The witness's NULL precondition (tree->cdr == NULL) is not produced by any shown statement; it is justified only by the absence of a guard on tree->cdr, and by the task rule that unshown parser invariants cannot make the deref safe. Confidence is capped at 0.6 accordingly.

Codegen stack balance (pop_n/push/cursp consistency, gen_move semantics) is not confirmable from this fragment; no visible attacker-scalable memory-corruption sink was identified beyond the NULL deref.
's' (codegen_scope *) is dereferenced (lines 150, 160) with no visible NULL provenance; treated as framework-provided robustness concern, not a finding.
No injection, file, crypto, or log sinks exist in the fragment; 'codegen_error' uses constant format strings.

verdict.summary: bgp_capability_msg_parse over-reads the BGP OPEN message at line 49: the guard at line 41 (`(pnt + hdr->length + 3) > end`) proves only that hdr->length bytes follow the 3-byte header and imposes no lower bound on hdr->length, so an admitted hdr->length of 0..3 makes the fixed-size `memcpy(&mpc, pnt + 3, sizeof (struct capability_mp_data))` read past `end` (CWE-125, remote DoS). Independently, the `continue` statements at lines 59 and 66 skip the only loop advance `pnt += hdr->length + 3` (line 102), so an MP capability with invalid afi/safi (or with PEER_FLAG_OVERRIDE_CAPABILITY set) stalls the loop forever (CWE-835, remote DoS).

evidence.reason: hdr->length is an untrusted capability byte read at line 24 (pnt+2); its only constraint is the upper-bound guard at line 41, which admits hdr->length in [0, end-pnt-3] and enforces no minimum, while the sink copies sizeof(struct capability_mp_data) (>= 1 byte) starting at pnt+3 — in-message only if hdr->length >= sizeof(...), which no shown statement requires. Witness: a 3-byte message (length=3, end = pnt+3) with action=0, code=1, length=0 passes the guards at lines 17 (pnt+3 > end false), 27-28 (action whitelisted), and 41 (pnt+0+3 == end admitted by the `>` comparison), then line 49 reads from pnt+3 == end, i.e., every byte is past the message boundary derived at line 12 — OOB heap read, CWE-125.

The loop variable pnt is advanced only at line 102 (`pnt += hdr->length + 3;`). When bgp_afi_safi_valid_indices (line 61) rejects the message-derived afi/safi, this continue skips line 102, so pnt stays fixed while the loop condition at line 14 (`pnt < end`) remains true — non-termination. Witness: message [action=0x00, code=0x01, length=0x04, afi=0x0000, safi=0x01] (7 bytes) passes guards at lines 17, 27-28, 41 and the line 49 copy is in-bounds; line 61 rejects afi=0 reaching this continue; the loop spins forever — CWE-835 remote DoS.

Identical stall mechanism: when PEER_FLAG_OVERRIDE_CAPABILITY is set (line 58), any MP capability admitted by the guards at lines 17, 27-28, 41, 52 reaches this continue, which bypasses the sole pnt advance at line 102 and freezes the loop condition at line 14 — CWE-835.

assumptions: end = pnt + length (line 12) is the message boundary; bytes at or after end are out of bounds for the fragment.
sizeof(struct capability_mp_data) >= 1 is guaranteed for any C struct, so hdr->length = 0 always under-provisions the line 49 read.
bgp_afi_safi_valid_indices(afi, &safi) at line 61 is treated by its name and use as an afi/safi index validator; it therefore protects the array accesses at lines 79-89, which are not flagged.
CAPABILITY_ACTION_SET/UNSET and CAPABILITY_CODE_MP are small distinct constants (BGP action 0/1, MP code 1), consistent with the branch logic shown.
limitations: NULL dereference of peer (line 11) and pnt (line 23) is demoted: no shown statement can produce NULL for these context parameters, so it is a robustness concern, not a demonstrated finding.

The exact numeric value of sizeof(struct capability_mp_data) and any slack in the underlying receive buffer past end are not shown; the over-read is measured against the only visible capacity, the message bound end derived at line 12.
The override-capability non-termination path (lines 58-59) additionally requires PEER_FLAG_OVERRIDE_CAPABILITY to be configured; the invalid-afi/safi path (line 66) is purely message-triggered.
No log/SQL/command injection candidates: all zlog formats are literals and message-derived values are passed only as format arguments.
No CVE attribution is attempted; the verdict rests solely on the shown statements.

verdict.summary: Heap buffer overflow in do_put: the multiplication-overflow guards (lines 363-365 and 509) only cap large positive values of the unconstrained long parameter 'count' and never reject negative counts. A negative count (witness: -1) makes 'totlen' negative (e.g. -10), so 'alloc(totlen + oldlen + 1)' (line 372) under-allocates 'newp' (91 bytes for a 100-byte prefix), and the subsequent mch_memmove calls (lines 378 and 406-407; also line 536 on the MCHAR path) write up to (yanklen+spaces) bytes beyond the allocation, a heap out-of-bounds write.

evidence.reason: Heap OOB write (CWE-787). Sink copies bd.textcol (100 in the witness) bytes into newp, whose only visible capacity is the allocation at line 372, 'newp = alloc(totlen + oldlen + 1);' with totlen = count*(yanklen+spaces) + startspaces + endspaces. count (long, line 5) has no shown lower-bound constraint: guard line 363-365 compares 'count > (INT_MAX - ...)/(yanklen + spaces)' and therefore admits -1 (comparison false), leaving totlen = -10 and alloc(91) while the copy writes newp[0..99]; with bd.textcol == oldlen == 100 and startspaces/endspaces/delcount == 0 (from lines 316-345 and 326), the copy writes 9 bytes beyond the 91-byte allocation, and line 406-407 writes one more.

evidence.snippet:
mch_memmove(ptr, oldp + bd.textcol + delcount,
				(size_t)(oldlen - bd.textcol - delcount + 1));
evidence.reason: Same CWE-787 mechanism on the same witness (count = -1, yanklen+spaces = 10, oldlen = bd.textcol = 100, delcount = 0): ptr == newp+100, the final memmove writes newp[100], the 10th byte beyond the 91-byte allocation created at line 372 from the guard-admitted negative totlen = -10.

Independent sink for the same root cause on the MCHAR single-line path: with count = -1 the guard at line 509 ('count > INT_MAX / yanklen') admits -1 and the guard at line 504 rejects only count == 0, so totlen = count * yanklen (line 514) is negative; newp = alloc(totlen + oldlen + 1) (line 533) is under-sized, and this memmove using col (e.g. col = 50, oldlen = 100) followed by STRMOVE(ptr, oldp + col) at line 543 writes past the end of newp.

assumptions: count is declared 'long' (line 5); the fragment contains no statement that rejects or clamps negative counts; the only numeric bounds on it are the upper-side guards at lines 363-365 and 509.
y_size >= 1 and y_array != NULL on the main path are visible bounds, enforced by the guard at lines 182-187 before the first y_array[0] use at line 225.

The '=' register split loop (lines 91-119) produces identical y_size in both passes because pass 2 only NUL-replaces '\n' at positions located identically in pass 1; stores at line 98 stay within the ALLOC_MULT allocation at line 116.
Block-register lines are NUL-terminated as consumed by STRLEN at lines 225 and 348.
limitations: Reachability of count < 0 from a real caller is not demonstrated inside the fragment (the only shown use of count == -1, lines 59-60, is on the early-returning '.' path); per the analysis rules the unconstrained parameter retains its full declared domain, which is exactly the premise of the finding, and this unshown caller link caps confidence at 0.62.

Autocommand use-after-free protections appear present in this fragment (u_save before get_yank_register at lines 79/130 and the y_current_used consistency check at lines 685-692), so that attack class is treated as mitigated here.

OOB reads via col when col > oldlen at lines 536, 543 and 608 would additionally require violating the cursor-column invariant, which is not shown; the line buffer capacity is also not visible, so they are demoted per the OOB standard.
Signed overflow of yanklen + spaces (both near INT_MAX) defeating the guard requires ~2GB block lines and is theoretical.
Potential non-termination/resource exhaustion for huge positive count with yanklen + spaces == 0 (line 386) cannot be derived from a shown guaranteed minimum and is demoted.
Any NULL-deref via get_spec_reg('=')/get_yank_register('=') depends on unshown callee semantics and is demoted.

verdict.summary: NULL pointer dereference in eval7() case '(': after get_lambda_tv() returns OK, rettv->vval.v_partial is dereferenced (and pt_func->uf_ret_type immediately after) with no NULL check anywhere between the call and the dereference, so a crafted vim9 expression can crash Vim (CWE-476, denial of service).

evidence.reason: rettv->vval.v_partial is populated only by get_lambda_tv (line 161) and is an uninitialized union member otherwise (only v_type is set at line 21). On the path case '(' (line 158) with in_vim9script() true (line 159) and ret == OK && evaluate true (line 162), the pointer is dereferenced at line 164 with no NULL check and no shown statement establishing a non-NULL invariant, so NULL is a member of its residual range and reaches the sink (CWE-476). The guard at line 162 checks the return status, not the partial pointer.

ufunc is rettv->vval.v_partial->pt_func (line 164) with pt_func itself unchecked, and uf_ret_type's NULL-ness is unchecked; the dereference at line 169 executes on the same vim9/lambda path after get_lambda_tv returns OK and evaluate is true, with no protective statement between the call site (line 161) and this read, leaving NULL in the residual range of ufunc/uf_ret_type (CWE-476).

assumptions: *arg points to a NUL-terminated expression text, evidenced by **arg reads (line 51), (*arg)[1] (line 100), **arg != NUL (line 150) and get_name_len/STRNCMP usage.
evaluate is derived from evalarg at lines 7-8 (evalarg == NULL => 0, else eval_flags & EVAL_EVALUATE), and is TRUE on the deref path.
The recursion cap at line 44 (recurse == 1000) with ++recurse at line 49 and --recurse at line 281 bounds recursive descent to 1000 active frames on every incremented path.
limitations: A NULL v_partial/pt_func/uf_ret_type can be produced only by get_lambda_tv's unshown callee behavior; per the container-extraction NULL rule the missing check is the finding, but confidence is kept at 0.7 rather than the demonstrated-witness band.
One-past-NUL reads via *arg + 1 (lines 31, 181) cannot be confirmed as OOB reads because no backing capacity for *arg is visible in the fragment.
handle_subscript (line 273) with name_start == NULL and the get_name_len/alias length contract depend on unshown callee behavior that the fragment does not constrain.
semsg/emsg calls (lines 37, 46, 140) use constant _() formats with user text passed as data arguments, so format-string injection is not confirmed.
get_reg_contents (line 146) may return NULL; the fragment stores it as VAR_STRING without dereferencing it, so no NULL-deref finding is derivable there.
The sufficiency of the 1000-level recursion limit depends on platform stack size stated only in the comment (lines 42-43); treated as protective, not a finding.

verdict.summary: Neighbor indices read from the neighbors table (lines 45-46, 55) are used to index stl->neighbors_start in write paths (lines 61-62, 65-66, 73) with only a `!= -1` sentinel guard (lines 60, 64, 71). The guard excludes exactly {-1}, leaving any other out-of-range int (e.g. -2) admitted, so an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) is reachable via a missing bound on the neighbor index.

evidence.reason: neighbor1 is read at line 45 from stl->neighbors_start[facet].neighbor[edge1]; the only shown constraint is guard line 60 `if(neighbor1 != -1)`, whose admitted set is int\{-1}. No lower/upper bound or capacity for neighbors_start is declared, so admitted values such as -2 reach the indexed store at line 61 and write out of bounds (CWE-787, missing bound on the index).

Same outer index neighbor1, admitted only by the `!= -1` guard at line 60 (admitted set int\{-1}); the store to which_vertex_not at line 62 is out of bounds for any non-(-1) value outside the unshown capacity (CWE-787).

neighbor2 is read at line 46; guard line 64 `if(neighbor2 != -1)` admits int\{-1} before the indexed store at line 65, with no range check against any facet-count/capacity, so an out-of-range value (e.g. -2) writes out of bounds (CWE-787).
Same outer index neighbor2 admitted only by guard line 64 (int\{-1}); store at line 66 is out of bounds for any admitted value that is not a valid array index (CWE-787).

neighbor3 is read at line 55; guard line 71 `if(neighbor3 != -1)` admits int\{-1} before the indexed store at line 73. With no visible capacity/bound on neighbors_start, admitted non-(-1) values such as -2 produce an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787).

assumptions: The neighbor[]/which_vertex_not[] arrays are 3-element (edge constants {0,1,2} at lines 28-40 and the `% 3` arithmetic at 61-66, 73), but the fragment declares no capacity for facet_start or neighbors_start.

Values copied from the struct fields at lines 45-46 and 55-58 are container-extracted data; their full declared int domain is the residual range because the fragment constrains them only against -1 (neighbors) or not at all (vnots).
stl->error == 0 on the analyzed path (line 12) does not constrain the validity of facet or neighbor indices.
edge1/edge2/edge3 only ever hold 0, 1, or 2 (lines 28-40), so the inner edge-indexed reads at 45-46 and 55-58 are in-domain.
limitations: The concrete witness magnitude (e.g. neighbor1 = -2) is not produced by any statement in the fragment, so the OOB-write finding rests on complete residual-range analysis (admitted set int\{-1}) rather than a demonstrated value; confidence is capped at 0.62.

Negative which_vertex_not values (e.g. -2, yielding (-1)%3 == -1) would make the inner index `(vnotN + 1) % 3` negative at lines 61-62, 65-66, 73; no shown producer of negative vnot exists, and this is subsumed by the outer-index finding.

The facet parameter is never range-checked before subscripts at lines 14-17, 26-27, 31-32, 36-37, 45-46, 55-58 and before stl_remove_facet (lines 22, 69) - a missing-bound OOB-read flow (CWE-125) not included in the primary CWE list.
stl_update_connects_remove_1 calls at lines 49, 52, and 72 receive neighbor values excluded only from -1, and the callee bodies are not shown.
printf at line 20 uses a constant format string and memcmp return values are used only as booleans; no injection or status-handling flaw found.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability in the shown fragment. The only index/size path is pb_idx (line 9) bounded by pb_cnt = dp_packet_batch_size(pb) (line 5), and every batch packet is resolved exactly once (refill at lines 18/24 XOR delete at line 20, split at line 17). The EtherType guards (lines 10-14) admit only the two matching types to the fragment-handling path. Remaining concerns (NULL pointer parameters ipf/pb, post-delete batch-slot state, callee internals) depend on semantics not shown and are recorded in limitations.

assumptions: Line 5 `const size_t pb_cnt = dp_packet_batch_size(pb);` — pb_cnt is the batch's own element count at entry and is const thereafter.
Line 9 `DP_PACKET_BATCH_REFILL_FOR_EACH (pb_idx, pb_cnt, pkt, pb)` — name-implied refill-aware for-each binds pb_idx to [0, pb_cnt); the shown body never modifies pb_cnt or pb_idx.
Line 17 `if (!ipf_handle_frag(...))` — boolean return fully branched: false -> refill (18), true -> delete (20), with no conflation of outcomes.

Lines 10-14 admit only dl_type == htons(ETH_TYPE_IP) with v4-validator-true or dl_type == htons(ETH_TYPE_IPV6) with v6-validator-true to the handle path; all other packets take the else branch (line 24).
The dp_packet_batch object is presumed to hold exactly pb_cnt valid entries, as reported by dp_packet_batch_size at line 5.
limitations: NULL-deref of ipf (lines 16/22), pb (line 5) and pkt (passed at lines 11/14): pointer-typed parameters/macro-derived value dereferenced without a NULL check, but no shown statement on any reachable path can produce NULL and no shown input is attacker-directed at these pointers; demoted as a caller-invariant robustness concern.

Stale batch slot after dp_packet_delete(pkt) (line 20): whether the unshown DP_PACKET_BATCH_REFILL_FOR_EACH macro clears the extracted slot, and whether an unshown caller re-reads it, are not visible; no in-fragment use of pkt occurs after line 20, so any UAF is unconfirmable from the fragment.

Capacity of pb->packets (e.g., DP_PACKET_BATCH_SIZE) is not shown; no OOB write is derivable from the shown arithmetic (indices are confined to the batch's own reported count), so neither a capacity-bound safety claim nor an OOB claim is supportable.

Bodies of ipf_is_valid_v4_frag, ipf_is_valid_v6_frag, and ipf_handle_frag are not shown; any bounds they enforce (or lack) on packet headers cannot be assessed, and the shown call sites derive no out-of-domain index/size/length arguments.
The discarded return value of dp_packet_batch_refill (lines 18/24) is the displaced slot occupant managed by the loop contract; no security-relevant operation consumes it.
The int-vs-size_t comparison implied by the line-9 macro (pb_idx < pb_cnt) occurs inside unshown macro text, so no sign/narrowing claim is made.

verdict.summary: gdImageFillToBorder validates neither x against im->sx nor y against [0, im->sy-1] before the seek loops. For any admitted x >= im->sx (or y outside [0, im->sy-1]), the left seek loop indexes gdImageGetPixel/gdImageSetPixel out of bounds; the only horizontal capacity in the fragment, im->sx, is used solely as the right-loop bound at line 28 and never guards the left loop's i.

evidence.reason: Primary sink (CWE-787). i is derived from the unvalidated parameter x (residual range [0, INT_MAX]; no shown statement binds x < im->sx or y to [0, im->sy-1]). The tool's own capacity, i < im->sx at line 28, bounds only the right loop that executes after this statement; the left loop admits i = x >= im->sx (e.g., x = im->sx = 5 with image width 5), writing pixel row y at column 5, one past column capacity [0, im->sx-1]. The guard at line 13 (i >= 0) admits i = 5, and line 22's early return is not taken because a pixel is written first, so the write executes.

Second sink (CWE-125 variant of the same missing-bound defect). With x = im->sx (admitted by the i >= 0 guard at line 13, non-negative border passing line 8), gdImageGetPixel(im, im->sx, y) performs an unconditional out-of-bounds read before any pixel-content check; likewise row y is read unvalidated for any y outside [0, im->sy-1], whose capacity is visible only through the y < im->sy - 1 guard at line 62 that gates the separate below-scan.

assumptions: im->sx and im->sy are the image width and height: valid column indices are [0, im->sx-1] and valid row indices are [0, im->sy-1]. This is derivable from the fragment's own use at line 28 (i < im->sx) and line 62 (y < im->sy - 1).
gdImageGetPixel/gdImageSetPixel consume the x/y arguments as direct pixel-array indices (standard semantics, and consistent with the fragment's own bound usage).
limitations: The OOB write witness at line 19 additionally requires the OOB-read pixel value to differ from border; image content is unconstrained input, but no shown statement fixes that value, so the write rests on the complete residual-range analysis rather than an exact content value. The OOB read at line 15 is unconditional.

Recursion at lines 50/73 can reach depth proportional to the fill area (stack-exhaustion DoS shape), but a demonstrated stack overflow requires an unshown stack limit and image size; left as a robustness concern without a CWE.
If the library API contract guarantees in-bounds x/y at every call site, this defect is unreachable; that invariant is outside the fragment and was not used to adjust the verdict.
Signed overflow of x + 1 at line 28 for x = INT_MAX is subsumed by the primary out-of-bounds finding.
Negative x and negative border are handled correctly by the early returns at lines 22-25 and 8-12 respectively; they were not used as witnesses.

verdict.summary: In the FTPWHO upload block, the filename copy source address is computed as &name[sl - sizeof(shm_data_cur->filename) - 1U]. When the upload name has length exactly equal to sizeof(shm_data_cur->filename), the guard at line 149 (sl < sizeof(shm_data_cur->filename)) admits sl == C into the else branch and the size_t subtraction underflows to SIZE_MAX, so memcpy reads C bytes from an out-of-bounds address — OOB read of the name buffer causing remote denial of service or disclosure of adjacent memory into FTPWHO shared memory (CWE-125).

evidence.reason: The sink index at line 154 derives from sl = strlen(name) (line 141), where name is an entry-point FTP file name whose length the fragment never constrains (checknamesanity at line 33 imposes no length bound). The guard at line 149 (`if (sl < sizeof shm_data_cur->filename)`) admits the else branch for sl >= C (C = sizeof(shm_data_cur->filename)), including the boundary sl == C. At sl == C the size_t expression (sl - C) - 1U wraps to SIZE_MAX, forming &name[SIZE_MAX], and the memcpy at lines 153-155 performs an out-of-bounds read of C bytes from that address. The destination write (C bytes into filename[0..C-1]) is in bounds, so the confirmed mechanism is the OOB read caused by the guard's failure to exclude the equality boundary (CWE-125).

assumptions: C = sizeof(shm_data_cur->filename) is a positive size_t compile-time constant whose exact value is not shown; the witness is the boundary relation sl == C, not a numeric magnitude.
The FTPWHO block is compiled (#ifdef FTPWHO at line 139); the finding applies to builds with FTPWHO enabled.
strlen(name) at line 141 requires name to be a valid NUL-terminated string; its length domain is the full size_t range.
restartat used for lseek (line 95) and ftruncate (line 101) is clamped to [0, st.st_size] at lines 92-94, so the resume-offset arithmetic is in range.
limitations: NULL-deref of the name parameter: no NULL check is shown and the first dereference (line 29) precedes the analyzed region; no shown statement produces NULL, and the value is supplied by the unshown command dispatcher — treated as a generic robustness concern, not the fragment's defect.
FSTATFS(f, &statfsbuf) at line 179 runs after close(f) at line 173; the call fails on the closed descriptor and no security-relevant operation runs on a failure state, so it is robustness-only.

The exact value of sizeof(shm_data_cur->filename) is not visible; if a shown-statement buffer bound were required rather than the boundary relation, the finding would reduce to a range claim (calibrated: confidence 0.62).
Callee internals (checknamesanity, get_atomic_file, ul_init, ul_send, quota helpers) are not shown and were not analyzed.
time() return value at line 148 is discarded; a failure only leaves a stale timestamp — not security-relevant.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. Every dangerous operation is covered by a visible protective statement: the loop-top ga_grow(&ga, 120) (line 20) guarantees at least 120 free bytes before each fgets, so ga.ga_maxlen - ga.ga_len is always a valid in-capacity size; the full-buffer check (line 57) only continues after re-entering line 20 to grow; ga_grow(&ga, 1) with FAIL->break (lines 28-29) bounds the NUL write at line 31; the buflines index is bounded by line 24; and len >= 1 is guaranteed by every shown producer, so buf[len-1] never underflows the buffer.

assumptions: ga_grow(&ga, n) guarantees at least n free bytes (ga.ga_maxlen - ga.ga_len >= n) on success; this matches the function name and the in-fragment comment at line 19: "make room to read at least 120 (more) characters".
ga_init2(&ga, 1, 250) (line 13) sets the standard grow-array initial state ga_len = 0, ga_data = NULL, ga_maxlen = 0, with growsize 250.

ga_concat (line 26) appends a NUL-terminated string and grows the array to fit, consistent with the grow-array pattern and the immediately following ga_grow(&ga, 1) at line 28; a non-growing concat would contradict the name and surrounding usage.

Newly allocated grow-array memory is zero-initialized (Vim's alloc_clear), so STRLEN(buf + ga.ga_len) at line 40 in the source_from_buf branch reads 0; even absent that, the scanned region is in-bounds because line 20 guaranteed at least 120 free bytes.
limitations: sp == NULL, fp == NULL, or a NULL buflines element would fault, but no statement in the fragment can produce those values; they are caller-contract violations, not shown-path findings.

An integer overflow of len/ga_len for a single line exceeding INT_MAX (lines 40, 54, 57) is not demonstrated: it requires an assumed ~2GB magnitude with no shown bound on file size, and the unshown allocator would be expected to fail first, breaking via the checked ga_grow FAIL paths; confidence would fall below 0.5.

In source_from_buf mode, the exact-equality check at line 57 can, under specific internal growth arithmetic (capacity values not shown in the fragment), treat a complete line as buffer-full and merge it with the next bufline; this is a functional data-integrity concern, not a memory-safety flaw.

ga_concat's internal OOM path is not surfaced (it only reports); on internal failure the line content is silently dropped, a robustness/data-integrity issue with no memory-safety consequence given the line 20/28 bounds.

Repeated ga_grow copies (whole-array memmove per growth) yield super-linear work for very long lines; a potential resource-exhaustion/algorithmic-complexity concern that is not confirmed by the shown code.

verdict.summary: __bpf_ringbuf_reserve is the patched counterpart: the u64 size parameter is capped by the guard at lines 7-8 (RINGBUF_MAX_RECORD_SZ) before it reaches the u64-to-u32 length conversion (line 10) or the header length store (line 36), and the visible ring-bound checks (line 11 len <= mask+1; line 29 producer advance <= mask) bound all record writes to the ring capacity. No confirmed memory-safety or logic vulnerability is demonstrable from the shown statements; the only out-of-domain candidates depend on the unshown numeric value of RINGBUF_MAX_RECORD_SZ.

assumptions: Line 7-8 is the protective fix statement: it excludes all size > RINGBUF_MAX_RECORD_SZ and admits only [0, RINGBUF_MAX_RECORD_SZ]; the numeric value of that constant is not shown in the fragment.
rb->mask + 1 (line 11) represents the ring buffer data capacity in bytes, and the guard admits only len <= mask+1.

bpf_ringbuf_hdr.len is a 32-bit field storing the record length (the fragment's header store at line 36 and the u32-only header composition in the consumer protocol), and BPF_RINGBUF_HDR_SZ is 8 so that round_up(size + BPF_RINGBUF_HDR_SZ, 8) >= 8 for any size >= 0.
Consumer position is treated as monotonically advancing, which is used only to argue that a stale cons_pos read (line 14) makes the line 29 check more conservative, not less.
limitations: Truncation candidate C1 (line 10 u64->u32 len and line 36 hdr->len store of size) is not confirmable: a witness requires an admitted size >= 2^32 - 7, which in turn requires RINGBUF_MAX_RECORD_SZ >= 2^32 - 7; the constant's value is not derivable from the fragment, so the claim can be justified in neither direction.

rb NULL dereference (lines 14, 34, etc.) is not reported: rb is an internal-helper pointer parameter whose NULL cannot be produced by any value or statement shown in the fragment; it is a caller-contract robustness item.

The stale cons_pos read-before-lock (line 14 used at line 29) and the u64 wrap of new_prod_pos (line 24) both drive the line 29 unsigned-subtraction check toward rejection; no in-fragment hazard is demonstrated.

The multi-page wrap-around nature of the ring record layout is not fully shown in the fragment; however, for sizes admitted by the line 7 cap the index (prod_pos & rb->mask) and record length (len <= mask+1) stay within the ring capacity implied by rb->mask + 1.
A hostile consumer inflating consumer_pos would be a producer/consumer coherence issue requiring out-of-fragment consumer misbehavior and does not produce an out-of-bounds write in this function.

verdict.summary: dynamicGetbuf uses the unvalidated signed parameter len as a memcpy length: a negative len (full int domain is unconstrained by the shown code) passes the guard 'remain >= len' (line 11), setting rlen = len < 0 (line 12), and the implicit int-to-size_t conversion yields a huge copy length at the memcpy sink (line 20), causing an out-of-bounds read from dp->data and out-of-bounds write into buf. The 'remain <= 0' EOF check (line 14) executes only on the else path and never guards a negative len.

evidence.reason: len is an int-typed parameter whose residual range includes every negative value because no statement in the fragment constrains len > 0; the guard at line 11 ('remain >= len') admits negative len whenever remain >= len (witness len=-1, remain=0: 0 >= -1 is true), so rlen = len = -1 at line 12. The EOF guard at line 14 is confined to the else-arm and is not executed on the path 11 -> 12 -> 20, so it cannot protect the copy. At this sink, rlen=-1 is converted from int to size_t, producing 0xFFFFFFFF/0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF, so memcpy reads far beyond logicalSize (the only capacity derivable at line 10) and writes far beyond buf. Primary CWE-195: signed-to-unsigned conversion of a negative value into a huge size causing out-of-bounds read/write.

assumptions: len and rlen are declared int in the fragment, so the full signed int domain is the starting residual range and the int-to-size_t conversion at the memcpy call is standard C semantics.
memcpy's length parameter is size_t per the C standard; a negative int argument is converted to a huge unsigned value.
The struct fields logicalSize, pos, data exist as dynamicPtr members read at lines 10, 20, 21; their exact types are not redeclared in the fragment and are not needed for the negative-len finding.
limitations: NULL dereference of dp (via dctx->dp): no statement in the fragment produces a NULL dp, so this is a robustness concern, not a confirmed finding.
Signed overflow in 'remain = dp->logicalSize - dp->pos' (line 10): field types are unshown, and the EOF check (line 14) neutralizes negative results on the else path.
The capacity of buf is a caller contract not visible in the fragment; the confirmed defect is the missing validation of len as a copy length (residual-range flow), independent of buf's size.

Reachability of a negative len from real callers is not demonstrated within the fragment; per the analysis rules this caller-side constraint is not shown and therefore cannot demote the residual-range finding.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. The only file-controlled index reaching a memory sink is tool_num into image->aperture[] (lines 73, 127-128, 185), and it is protected by the bounds check at lines 63-69, which admits only [TOOL_MIN, TOOL_MAX-1] and explicitly rejects the boundary value TOOL_MAX (>=) and all values below TOOL_MIN, executing before every sink use on every path. Remaining suspicious constructs (fd++ at line 26, fd->ptr -= 4 at line 25, unescaped file line data in gerbv_stats_printf %s args, unchecked helper-parameter NULLs, constant-size allocation-failure aborts) cannot be confirmed from the shown fragment because each depends on a capacity, entry state, or callee behavior not visible in the code.
