assumptions: The guard at lines 63-69 (tool_num < TOOL_MIN || tool_num >= TOOL_MAX) defines the index domain: TOOL_MIN is a non-negative minimum and image->aperture has capacity >= TOOL_MAX, so the admitted range [TOOL_MIN, TOOL_MAX-1] stays in bounds. The array capacity itself is not visible in the fragment.
gerb_fgetint produces a value whose (int) cast at line 57 is the value the guard checks, so any truncation occurs before the guard and cannot admit an out-of-range index.
get_line returns a NUL-terminated string (g_free of the result at lines 31/49 is valid), and printf-family %s with NULL is non-fatal, so a NULL get_line result would not be a crash.

fd->ptr is advanced only by the parser's read path; the fragment's own fd->ptr -= 4 (line 25) keeps the position at or above zero when the entry position is >= 4, as implied by the caller having consumed the leading 'T' (comment lines 15-16).
limitations: get_line(fd++) at line 26 post-increments the fd parameter, so line 30 reads fd->filename from (fd+1); the branch is reachable via file content 'TCST...' with the line 22 guard satisfied, but the capacity of the object fd points to is not visible in the fragment, so the OOB-read boundary claim cannot be confirmed under the shown-capacity rule.

fd->ptr -= 4 (line 25) could underflow if the file position at entry were < 4; no shown statement can produce that state, and the entry position is outside the fragment, so no witness can be constructed from shown values.

File line content (tmps) is passed to gerbv_stats_printf %s sinks (lines 27-30, 45-48) with no shown sanitization; whether a CR/LF can be embedded depends on get_line's unshown behavior and no downstream log policy is shown.

Out-of-range or NaN drill sizes on the line 104 error path still flow into drill_stats_add_to_drill_list (lines 147-150); the statistics list has no shown memory/render sink, so impact is not confirmable.
(double)(16 + 8 * tool_num) at line 196 could overflow int only if TOOL_MAX exceeded about 2^28, which is not visible; the result is stored in a double (line 214), not consumed as an index/size.
Unchecked g_new0 failure leading to GERB_FATAL_ERROR (lines 129-131, 186-187) uses a constant-size allocation, so the failure is not attacker-directed (robustness only).
Helper parameters state/image/fd are dereferenced without NULL checks (lines 8, 22, 72-73); a NULL value is not producible by any shown statement.

Minor robustness issues noted but not security findings: dead EOF branch at lines 175-176 ('\n' == temp when temp == EOF), EOF error at 170-172 not setting done (loop still exits via default at 160-165), and the post-default gerb_fgetc at line 168 consuming the delimiter that default intended to put back.
If gerbv_stats_printf or drill_stats_add_to_drill_list interpret a NaN/huge size in a dangerous way internally, that callee behavior is not shown and is out of scope for this fragment.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the guarded ESP output-head implementation. Every dangerous operation has a protective statement executed before the sink on its path: the fast-path pskb_put is covered by tailen <= skb_tailroom(skb) (line 24, exact-fit boundary included); the page-frag fill index is covered by nr_frags < MAX_SKB_FRAGS (line 30, admits 0..MAX_SKB_FRAGS-1 only); the page-frag fill size and offset advance are covered by the skb_page_frag_refill() failure funnel (lines 42-45); and the cow-path put is covered by the skb_cow_data() error check (lines 80-81). No shown arithmetic produces a value that exceeds a visible capacity, so no confirmed vulnerability is demonstrable.

assumptions: MAX_SKB_FRAGS is the slot capacity the guard at line 30 targets: with nr_frags < MAX_SKB_FRAGS, the fill index at line 56 stays within 0..MAX_SKB_FRAGS-1, and the update at line 58 sets nr_frags <= MAX_SKB_FRAGS.

skb_page_frag_refill() succeeding (line 42) makes allocsize bytes available in pfrag, and its failure is funneled to cow (lines 42-45); skb_cow_data() succeeding (line 79) provides tailen tailroom in *trailer, and failure is propagated (lines 80-81) — name-implied contracts of standard kernel helpers, used as the visible guards.

pskb_put() (line 87) consumes exactly len bytes from the trailer's tailroom, so the line 24 guard (tailen <= skb_tailroom(skb)) exactly covers the fast path, including the boundary tailen == skb_tailroom(skb).
limitations: Negative tailen: esp->tailen is copied unmodified at line 8 (declared int, no shown lower-bound constraint), and the line 24 guard admits negatives into pskb_put (line 87). No statement in the fragment derives a negative magnitude, so no concrete witness is traceable to a shown statement; this is a range claim with an assumed magnitude and is demoted with no CWE. The caller-side computation of esp->tailen is outside the fragment.

The internal capacity of the page-frag buffer (allocsize <= pfrag->size) and of skb_cow_data expansion are not declared in the fragment; the safe reading relies on the name-implied contracts of those helpers. Under the shown caps (allocsize = ALIGN(tailen) <= allocsz <= ESP_SKB_FRAG_MAXSIZE when the line 20 guard passes) no shown arithmetic exceeds those contracts.

The u32+int sum at line 19 (skb->data_len + tailen) can wrap, which could defeat the allocsz cap on the cow-bypass decision; however every subsequently reached sink uses tailen, which is independently guarded (lines 24, 42, 80), so the wrapped guard value is inconsequential for the shown sinks — demoted (CWE-190 candidate, no confirmed mechanism).
x, skb, and esp are dereferenced with no NULL checks and no shown NULL producer; treated as environmental robustness, not a confirmed finding.
The pointer subtraction at line 77 uses esp->esph unvalidated, but the fragment contains no statement that can make esph NULL or invalid; demoted.

The frag path returns nr_frags+2 (nfrags++ at line 64) while only one frag was added (nr_frags+1); the sole internal consumer is return nfrags (line 90), whose downstream use is outside the fragment, so the discrepancy is not confirmable here.

verdict.summary: entry-point endpoint name is copied with an unbounded strcpy into the fixed-size sockaddr_un.sun_path buffer (line 15), overflowing the stack for any path longer than the platform capacity; the duplicate-check guard (line 5) admits all such paths because it imposes no length limit.

evidence.reason: pipePath (line 4, from entry-point endpoint.name()) retains its full string domain: no length bound is imposed by the only guard on the path, the duplicate check at line 5, whose admitted set is every not-yet-registered path. At the line-15 sink, strcpy writes pipePath.size()+1 bytes into the fixed-size sun_path member of the stack object declared at line 9 (sockaddr_un local;), so any admitted path longer than sun_path's capacity overflows adjacent stack memory. The missing length check/strncpy is the defect; primary mechanism is CWE-121 stack buffer overflow via unbounded copy, and the fix (a size comparison or bounded copy) is absent from the fragment.

assumptions: sockaddr_un.sun_path is a fixed-size member array whose exact capacity is defined by the platform type, not spelled in the fragment.
FATAL_FAIL (lines 12, 18, 21) is assumed to abort on failure based on its name; it affects only descriptor/syscall failures, not string lengths.
limitations: Exact overflow excess depends on the platform's sun_path capacity constant, which is not visible in the shown code; the overflow is nonetheless certain for any sufficiently long admitted path (range claim).

unlink(local.sun_path) and the bind path present a possible TOCTOU/symlink race (CWE-59-family), but a confirming attacker file-planting capability and race interleaving are not shown; demoted, not reported as a CWE.
The discarded return of ::listen(fd, 5) (line 19) is a robustness/error-handling concern, not a confirmed security-relevant flaw.
No other guards, loops, or sinks exist in the fragment; all other operations (mutex lock, socket/bind/chmod checks, map insert) were analyzed and do not introduce independent findings.

verdict.summary: do_put accepts negative `count` values: both multiplication-overflow guards (lines 363-365 and 507) only bound positive counts, so `count = -1` passes and makes `totlen` negative. `alloc(totlen + oldlen + 1)` then returns a buffer smaller than the region written by the tail copy, causing a heap out-of-bounds write at `STRMOVE` (line 541) and at the block-mode `mch_memmove` (lines 404-405).

evidence.reason: `count` (line 5, `long`) retains its full domain: line 502 rejects only `count == 0`, line 507 rejects only `count > INT_MAX / yanklen`, and neither rejects negatives; the fragment itself uses `count == -1` as a sentinel (lines 59-60). With `count = -1`, `yanklen = 1` (line 225/348; line 502 excludes only 0), `oldlen = 10` (line 515), `col = 0`, `VIsual_active` false: line 507 admits -1, line 512 sets `totlen = -1`, line 531 allocates `10` bytes, and line 536 copies nothing, so this STRMOVE writes `oldlen - col + 1 = 11` bytes into the 10-byte allocation at line 531 — a 1-byte heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787).

evidence.snippet:
mch_memmove(ptr, oldp + bd.textcol + delcount,
				(size_t)(oldlen - bd.textcol - delcount + 1));
evidence.reason: Same taint: `count = -1` passes the block-mode overflow guard (lines 363-365, which admits -1 since `-1 > (INT_MAX - start/end)/(yanklen+spaces)` is false), so line 371 yields `totlen = -2` and line 372 allocates `oldlen - 1` bytes (with `textcol = startspaces = endspaces = delcount = 0`, `PUT_BLOCK_INNER` keeping `spaces = 0`). This tail memmove then copies `oldlen + 1` bytes into the undersized allocation — a heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787), 2 bytes past capacity.

assumptions: Line 182 `if (y_size == 0 || y_array == NULL) ... goto end;` guarantees `y_size >= 1` and `y_array != NULL` on all post-check paths.
Line 502 `if (count == 0 || yanklen == 0)` excludes only zero values, so on the sink path `yanklen >= 1`.
`count == -1` is a value the fragment itself treats as meaningful for the '.' register (lines 59-60), confirming it is in the long domain.
The witness sets `VIsual_active` false and `col = 0`; nothing in the fragment constrains either, and no guard on the path is bypassed that would require a specific value.
limitations: Truncation to `int` of `STRLEN` results (lines 225, 317, 348, 515, 590) and int overflow of `totlen + oldlen + 1` (lines 372, 531) would require multi-gigabyte lines; no such capacity is visible in the fragment, so these are range-only hypotheses, not separate findings.

The `=`-register two-pass walk (lines 91-119) writes `y_array[y_size]` only on the second pass with an identical traversal; the count is bounds-consistent with the `ALLOC_MULT` (line 116), so no OOB is reported there.
`alloc` NULL returns are checked (lines 117, 153, 163, 373, 531, 592, 603); allocation failure is not the mechanism of any finding.
Miscellaneous unchecked return values (`getvcol`, `ml_append` in the line-split branch) are display/undo related and have no confirmed security-relevant consequence in the fragment.

verdict.summary: BM_ParseGlobalQuantizer releases the decoded node twice at lines 32-33: gf_node_unregister(node, NULL) is called back-to-back while the only acquisition shown is gf_bifs_dec_node at line 6, no gf_node_register appears anywhere (line 31's comment claims the node must be registered twice, but the code never does it), and lines 19-21 establish the fragment's own rule that a just-created node needs exactly one unregister. For any admitted node on this path (tag == TAG_MPEG4_QuantizationParameter per line 16, including USE nodes with num_instances >= 1 per lines 17-18), the first unregister can drop the count to zero and free the node; the second unregister then operates on freed memory (double free / UAF), and the dangling pointer is stored in inf->new_node (line 37), codec->ActiveQP (line 27) and scenegraph->global_qp (line 29) while GF_OK is returned at line 41, so the command/scenegraph later dereference freed memory (CWE-416).

evidence.reason: Two consecutive gf_node_unregister calls release the bitstream-derived node decoded at line 6 with no registration in between. Line 31's comment asserts the node is registered TWICE, but the shown code contains no gf_node_register, and lines 19-21 show a just-created node (num_instances == 0) is fully released by exactly one unregister after num_instances is forced to 1. For every admitted node reaching this sink (non-NULL per line 7, tag == TAG_MPEG4_QuantizationParameter per line 16, including USE nodes with num_instances >= 1 explicitly admitted at lines 17-18), the first unregister at line 32 drops the count to 0 and destroys the node, so the second unregister at line 33 re-releases and dereferences freed memory — double free / use-after-free (CWE-416 primary, double-free manifestation CWE-415). No guard between lines 32 and 33 constrains the reference count or adds a registration.

Executes after the double unregister at lines 32-33 and stores the now-dangling node pointer into the command field that is appended to com_list at line 40, while line 41 returns GF_OK. codec->ActiveQP (line 27) and scenegraph->global_qp (line 29) were already set to the same node before the releases, so the scenegraph and command processing consume freed memory — use-after-free (CWE-416) caused by the unbalanced release at lines 32-33.

assumptions: gf_node_unregister(node, NULL) releases one reference and destroys the node when its count reaches zero — consistent with its name and with the fragment's own release convention at lines 19-21 (a just-created node is fully released by one unregister after num_instances is set to 1).
The fragment admits both freshly created nodes (num_instances == 0, lines 17 and 19) and USE nodes (num_instances > 0, lines 17-18) as results of gf_bifs_dec_node at line 6.

node->sgprivate is non-NULL for a successfully decoded node (line 7 checks only node; line 19 dereferences node->sgprivate) — a framework invariant not shown in the fragment and not the basis of the finding.
limitations: The exact reference count of node at line 32 is not derivable from the fragment: a freshly created node still unregistered (num_instances == 0, per lines 17-19) would only underflow the counter under the two unregisters (leak/refcount corruption, no crash). The double-free/UAF verdict therefore rests on the admitted USE-node range (num_instances >= 1), so the witness is a range backed by the fragment's own admission at lines 17-18 rather than a single shown magnitude; confidence is capped at 0.62.

Downstream dereferences of the dangling ActiveQP/global_qp/inf->new_node pointers occur during scenegraph/command processing outside the fragment; the in-fragment anchors are the second unregister (line 33, double free) and the dangling store (line 37).

Returns of gf_sg_command_new (line 35) and gf_sg_command_field_new (line 36) are unchecked; dereferencing inf at line 37 would be a NULL dereference only if one of these helpers failed, which is not attacker-directed — robustness concern only.
The exact upstream CVE/commit identity cannot be established from this fragment alone.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. The attacker-controlled nlattr input is bounded at every security-relevant step: the nested parse (lines 9-10) is error-checked (11-12) and its maxtype NFTA_VERDICT_MAX cannot overflow the declared tb[NFTA_VERDICT_MAX + 1] (line 5); nla_get_be32 (line 16) is gated by the presence check (14-15); the u32 verdict code is validated by the switch (18-32) so arbitrary codes are rejected (25-26) and no code value is used as a size/index; jump/goto verdicts require exactly one chain selector (35-46) and the resulting chain pointer is IS_ERR-checked (42-43, 48-49) before every dereference and use (50, 53, 56-57).

assumptions: tb capacity statement 'struct nlattr *tb[NFTA_VERDICT_MAX + 1];' (line 5) combined with the parse maxtype argument NFTA_VERDICT_MAX (line 9) bounds all attribute-table writes; nla_parse_nested_deprecated never indexes past its maxtype.

nft_verdict_policy (line 10) is explicitly passed as the validation policy for the nested parse, providing attribute type/length validation for nla_get_be32 at line 16; its field definitions are outside the fragment.
nft_chain_lookup / nft_chain_lookup_byid signal failure via ERR_PTR, matching the repeated 'if (IS_ERR(chain)) return PTR_ERR(chain);' guards at lines 42-43 and 48-49.
limitations: The failure convention of nft_chain_lookup_byid (ERR_PTR vs NULL on not-found) is not visible in the fragment. If it returned NULL, the IS_ERR guards (42-43, 48-49) would not reject it and nft_is_base_chain(chain)/chain->flags at lines 50/53 would dereference NULL; since the fragment cannot show NULL as producible on any path, this is unconfirmable and carries no CWE.
The refcount increment 'chain->use++' (line 56) and the lifetime of data->verdict.chain beyond this function are not analyzed in the fragment; no attacker-scaled repetition or overflow is visible.
Caller-side state (size and initialization of *data, semantics of desc->flags/desc->len outside SETELEM) is not shown and was not relied on for the verdict.

verdict.summary: For any id not present in idInfoMap, the guard at L3 admits the miss and only logs via STFATAL; no shown statement terminates the branch, so execution falls through to `return it->second;` (L6), dereferencing the end() iterator (undefined behavior, typically a crash). The lookup result is dereferenced without an effective error-return.

evidence.reason: Input `id` (entry-point input, unconstrained at L1) reaches `idInfoMap.find(id)` at L2, which returns `end()` for any id not a map key. The guard at L3 admits exactly this miss, but its body (L4) contains only `STFATAL << "...";` with no visible return/abort/throw, so the shown sequence proceeds to L6 and dereferences `it` while `it == idInfoMap.end()` — an end-iterator dereference (undefined behavior, CWE-476 invalid-pointer/iterator dereference). The check at L3 does not exclude the failure value from the sink because no terminating statement covers the admitted path.

assumptions: idInfoMap is an associative container with std::map semantics where find() returns a valid element iterator or end() (name-implied by L2/L3 usage).
TerminalUserInfo is returned by value from the function.
limitations: STFATAL is a macro whose definition is outside the fragment; if it aborts/throws in the real build, the miss path terminates and the L6 dereference is unreachable. This verdict follows the rule that an invariant not shown in the fragment (STFATAL termination) cannot be used to declare the operation safe; the fall-through is the reading supported by the shown statements.

The concrete consequence of dereferencing map end() is implementation-defined UB (typically a crash, possibly reading a sentinel/garbage value); the precise runtime effect is not visible in the fragment.

Alternative classification as CWE-690 (unchecked return value to pointer dereference) or CWE-754 (improper check for unusual conditions) was considered; CWE-476 is reported as the single primary mechanism at the dereference sink.

The id's membership in idInfoMap depends on external registration state not shown here; that does not change the analysis, since the miss case is admitted by the shown guard and the fragment imposes no membership constraint.

verdict.summary: u64 size, admitted up to the unshown constant RINGBUF_MAX_RECORD_SZ by the line 7 guard, is rounded in 64-bit arithmetic and narrowed into u32 len at line 10. The shown guard does not demonstrably exclude sizes that push size + BPF_RINGBUF_HDR_SZ + 7 past 2^32, so an admitted size can wrap len, defeating the ring-capacity gate at line 26 and desynchronizing ring accounting (lines 21, 33) — leading to a kernel ring-buffer out-of-bounds write when the caller writes size bytes into the reserved area.

evidence.reason: Narrowing-store sink (CWE-190): size is the entry-point u64 argument whose residual range is [0, RINGBUF_MAX_RECORD_SZ] per the line 7 guard; the guard's cap value is unshown and cannot be shown to keep size + BPF_RINGBUF_HDR_SZ + 7 below 2^32, so the u64 rounded sum can exceed the visible u32 destination range of len and wrap. The wrapped len then feeds new_prod_pos at line 21 and the capacity gate at line 26, corrupting the size that gates ring admission — the primary integer-overflow mechanism.

Security-gating comparison consuming the truncated len: for an admitted size that wraps at line 10, new_prod_pos advances by the small wrapped len, so new_prod_pos - cons_pos can satisfy the mask limit even though the record's true size (stored at line 33 and written by the reserve caller) exceeds the ring data area. The check executes after the corruption (line 10 < line 26) and validates only the corrupted value, so it cannot protect the true record size.

assumptions: size is a u64 BPF-helper entry-point argument; the only shown constraint is line 7, admitting [0, RINGBUF_MAX_RECORD_SZ], and RINGBUF_MAX_RECORD_SZ's numeric value is outside the fragment.
BPF_RINGBUF_HDR_SZ and BPF_RINGBUF_BUSY_BIT are compile-time constants whose values are not shown.
rb->mask equals ringbuf data size minus one, supported by the visible comment at lines 23-25, so header addressing at line 31 stays inside the data area.
A successful reserve returns a pointer where the caller writes size bytes (standard reserve/output semantics); that copy call is outside the fragment.
Analysis assumes a 64-bit unsigned long for ring positions (x86-64), matching the u64 size arithmetic.
limitations: The truncation trigger is a range claim, not a demonstrated constant: it requires an admitted size >= ~2^32 - BPF_RINGBUF_HDR_SZ - 7, whose reachability depends on the unshown value of RINGBUF_MAX_RECORD_SZ; if that constant is below the threshold, line 7 fully protects and the fragment is the fixed counterpart. Confidence is capped at 0.55 for this reason.

The overwriting copy of size bytes after reserve is not in the fragment; the out-of-bounds-write impact is inferred from reserve-call semantics and the corrupted ring accounting, and is therefore not an independently confirmed secondary CWE.
hdr->len's field width and BPF_RINGBUF_BUSY_BIT's value are unshown, so the line 33 metadata store's own truncation/flag collision is not independently confirmable.

NULL rb dereference (lines 11, 13, 17, 20, 26, 31, 33, 37) is possible only in the declared pointer domain; no shown statement produces NULL and the object is framework-provided, so CWE-476 is demoted.
No loops exist in the fragment, so loop-termination analysis is not applicable.
The modular space check at line 26 is correct under the visible mask invariant; it is flagged only as a consumer of the corrupted length, not as an independent defect.

verdict.summary: An admitted TGA header with colormap_index==0 and colormap_length==0 makes image->colors==0; the decoder then subscripts image->colormap with a file-supplied byte (L308) through ConstrainColormapIndex with no in-fragment guarantee that colors >= 1, producing a heap out-of-bounds read (image->colormap[-1]) in the 8-bit colormap branch at L310-311.

evidence.reason: Heap OOB read (CWE-125): colormap_index and colormap_length are raw 16-bit file fields (L80-81) with no shown nonzero constraint, so L121-122 admits image->colors = 0+0 = 0 (PseudoClass requires only colormap_type != 0, L76-78, 119-122). The only protection candidate, L186-187, fires only when colors < colormap_index, which is false for (0,0), so colors stays 0 and AcquireImageColormap(image,0) (L188) yields a 0-entry colormap. The file-supplied pixel byte index in [0,255] (L308) is then used at L310-311 to read image->colormap[...] with no visible bound guaranteeing colors >= 1; the name-implied clamp to [0, colors-1] on the empty range returns (ssize_t)colors-1 == -1, i.e., image->colormap[-1] (or a NULL/zero-size access if allocation yields NULL), which is out of bounds for every possible callee result. Witness path passes every guard: TGAColormap (L69-75), colormap_type==1 (L76-78), bpp==8 (L91-93), ping==MagickFalse (L171), 1x1 image with SetImageExtent/QueueAuthenticPixels succeeding (L176, L274), skip==MagickFalse (L299), colormap_type != 0 (L309).

assumptions: ConstrainColormapIndex implements the name-implied clamp to [0, colors-1]; for colors==0 the range is empty, so no return value can be an in-bounds index of the 0-entry colormap — the OOB outcome is forced by the shown arithmetic (L122, L186-188) rather than by callee-specific behavior.

SetImageExtent (L176) and QueueAuthenticPixels (L274) succeed for the 1x1 crafted image, and AcquireImageColormap(image, 0) (L188) returns MagickTrue on the witness path; allocation failure there would be attacker-directed (the size 0 derives from file fields), and a per standard-operation basis for the other two.
EOFBlob checks (L89, L411) are satisfied by the crafted file, which carries the few header bytes plus one pixel byte.
limitations: Demoted: real=image->rows-real-1 (L273) cannot underflow — offset is initialized (L268), steps by 1/2 (L392-395), and the reset (L396-400) keeps offset and base below image->rows at every row start, so real stays in [0, rows-1].

Demoted: colormap fill writes (L191, L256) and the 15/16-bit colormap index (L345-347) are always within the image->colors-sized allocation; the 16-bit index only feeds SetPixelIndex (data write), not a pointer dereference.
Demoted: pixels[4] (L40) is written by checked reads of at most 4 bytes (L332-333, L355-356, L367-368); no overflow.
Demoted: RLE runlength is bounded to 0..127 (L293-295), decrements only when nonzero (L285), and loop progress is governed by x < columns (L277); no unbounded or non-terminating loop.

Secondary confirmed but lower-severity issue, not counted in the verdict: the ReadBlob return at L152 is discarded; on a truncated file uninitialized heap bytes inside comment[0..id_length-1] reach SetImageProperty (L154) via the NUL-termination at L153 (CWE-457/CWE-754, potential memory disclosure). No fragment-visible export of the property is shown, so impact is not demonstrated.
Zero width/height are not validated (L85-86) but lead either to SetImageExtent rejection or to loop bodies that execute zero times; no memory-safety consequence is demonstrated within the fragment.

verdict.summary: The loop bound `abbrev->count - 1` at line 6 underflows to SIZE_MAX when `abbrev->count` is 0, and the fragment imposes no check establishing count >= 1. The guard then admits every size_t index, so the loop writes `die->attr_values[i]` (memset, line 7) and reads `abbrev->defs[i]` (line 9) with an unvalidated index and no visible capacity — an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) caused by the unsigned underflow (CWE-190) on attacker-controlled DWARF input.

evidence.reason: abbrev->count is an entry-point-derived field with no shown constraint establishing count >= 1; with count == 0 the size_t expression `abbrev->count - 1` at line 6 underflows to SIZE_MAX (CWE-190), so the line-6 guard admits i = 0 (0 < SIZE_MAX) and every index up to SIZE_MAX-1. The memset at line 7 then writes through that input-derived index into die->attr_values[], whose capacity is never bounded in the fragment (missing-bound flow / CWE-787); the same admitted i drives the OOB read of abbrev->defs[i] at line 9. No protective statement between line 6 and line 7 constrains i.

assumptions: `abbrev->count` is an integer count field compared against `size_t i`, so the loop-bound arithmetic at line 6 is evaluated with unsigned (size_t) semantics; its declared domain therefore includes 0, and no shown statement derives a minimum.
`die->attr_values` and `abbrev->defs` are finite arrays; their sizes are not visible in the fragment, so the unvalidated-index (missing-bound) standard applies to the line 7 write and line 9 read.
`parse_attr_value` advances `buf` and returns the new read position; its error contract is not shown.
limitations: Unchecked `parse_attr_value` return (lines 9-10): if the callee returns NULL on malformed input, `buf_end - buf` (line 9) and `return buf` (line 38) would be UB/NULL-flow; the callee's NULL-on-error behavior is not visible in the fragment, so this is not confirmed (CWE-476/CWE-754 not attached).

`strdup(comp_dir)` at line 30 assumes `attribute->string.content` is NUL-terminated; that bound is established only inside the unshown `parse_attr_value`, so a length-dependent over-read is unconfirmed.

`info`, `die`, `abbrev`, and `hdr` are dereferenced without NULL checks (lines 7-32); no shown path produces NULL for them — caller-provided robustness concerns, not attacker-directed findings in this fragment.
`die->count` is incremented only `abbrev->count - 1` times (line 24); there is no visible consumer of `die->count`, so no security impact is demonstrable.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. Every input-derived size/index/length that reaches a sink is bounded by visible protective statements: the bpp whitelist (lines 91-93) admits only {2..16,24,32}; the post-header EOFBlob check (89-90) rejects truncated headers before field use; multi-byte and RLE reads are count-checked (293, 334, 357, 368); the comment buffer is allocated with length+MagickPathExtent under the ~length guard (149-151), so the write at 155 cannot exceed it; colormap colors are at most index+length <= 131070 or a guarded 1<<bpp (122, 129-130) and all writes stay within the colors-entry allocation (190-194); the row index real stays in [0, rows-1] because the size_t wrap at 396-399 uses >= (excludes offset==rows, which would underflow image->rows-real-1 at 275), and the pixel writes are bounded by the strict x<columns loop against the region fetched at 276.

assumptions: size_t is 64-bit on the analysis target (the bpp=32 `one << bits_per_pixel` path at line 129 then yields 2^32, which fails cleanly at the allocation-failure path 132-133).
ReadBlobLSBShort returns a 2-byte value in [0,65535] (shown uncast assignments at 80-81, 85-86), so colormap_index+colormap_length <= 131070 and width/height <= 65535.

ReadBlob returns the number of bytes transferred and never writes past the requested count; ReadBlobByte returns EOF without touching the buffer past the end; QueueAuthenticPixels fetches a region of exactly image->columns pixels x 1 row (name-implied standard contract); ConstrainColormapIndex clamps to the [0, image->colors-1] domain it indexes.
The offset<rows invariant at every loop top (lines 270-271, 393-399) is derivable from the shown statements: base counts prior wraps and is <= the iteration index, with rows maximal at 65535.
limitations: Line 154 discards the ReadBlob count for the comment; on a truncated file, bytes [count..id_length) of the freshly malloc'ed buffer are uninitialized and SetImageProperty (156) stores them into image metadata. This is a CWE-457/CWE-754-flavored single-shot leak of at most 255 bytes whose disclosure needs a downstream consumer of the property and is excluded as a finding by the single-shot-leak rule.

PseudoClass non-colormap path with bits_per_pixel==24/32 (line 129) requests a colormap of 2^24/2^32 entries on 64-bit; the overflow guard (130) is vacuous there, but the resulting allocation failure is explicitly converted to ThrowReaderException (132-133), so it is at most a handled resource-exhaustion attempt, not memory corruption.

A degenerate colormap with colormap_index=colormap_length=0 (both admitted 16-bit reads) makes image->colors==0 (122/188); whether AcquireImageColormap(0) succeeds and whether ConstrainColormapIndex(...,colors==0) clamps to a negative index at line 312 depends on unshown callee semantics, so no confirmed CWE-125 finding can be demonstrated.

On a hypothetical 32-bit size_t target, `one << tga_info.bits_per_pixel` (129) with bpp==32 is undefined behavior; this cannot be confirmed on the chosen target and no security-relevant consumption of a corrupted value is shown.

SetPixelIndex (380) may store an 8-bit value into a PseudoClass image whose colormap has fewer than 256 entries for bpp in 2..7; no shown statement indexes that colormap with the stored value, so any later over-read would occur in unshown downstream code.

verdict.summary: Out-of-bounds heap read (CWE-125) in issuerAndThisUpdateCheck: when the GSER issuer or thisUpdate value contains no closing double-quote, the scan loops at lines 65-77 / 107-111 exit with is->bv_len==x.bv_len / tu->bv_len==x.bv_len, so the unconditional advances at lines 78-79 / 112-113 move x.bv_val one byte past the end of the in berval and corrupt x.bv_len (unsigned wraparound at line 79). The post-branch space-eating loop at line 122 (and the comma check at line 130) then dereference x.bv_val[0], performing an out-of-bounds read of attacker-supplied input that can crash slapd (remote denial of service). The missing protective statement is a closing-quote terminator check after the value scans.

evidence.reason: Sink: first dereference of x.bv_val[0] after the cursor is corrupted. in (entry-point berval, residual range bv_len>=38 with bv_val[0]=='{' and bv_val[bv_len-1]=='}' per lines 19/21, interior unconstrained) flows via x into the issuer scan (lines 65-77), which exits with is->bv_len==x.bv_len when no closing quote exists (loop head line 65 admits that exit; no terminator check follows). Line 78 then sets x.bv_val = in->bv_val + in->bv_len (one byte past the 39-byte capacity implied by bv_len at lines 19/21) and line 79 makes x.bv_len wrap. Here the condition evaluates x.bv_val[0] before the length test, reading in->bv_val[bv_len] -- a 1-byte out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). Concrete witness: "{issuer rdnSequence:"AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA}" (39 bytes); after lines 55-60 x.bv_len==17 over 17 'A's, is->bv_len reaches 17, lines 78-79 advance the pointer to in+39, and this loop reads it.

Second sink on the same corrupted-cursor path from lines 78-79: with the witness "{issuer rdnSequence:"AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA}" (39 bytes, admitted by lines 19/21), x.bv_val points one byte past the berval and x.bv_len is wrapped, so this check reads in->bv_val[39] -- a further 1-byte out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) before returning LDAP_INVALID_SYNTAX. The thisUpdate variant reaches line 122 through lines 112-113 with the identical missing terminator check.

assumptions: The readable extent of the in berval is in->bv_val[0 .. in->bv_len-1], i.e., bv_len bytes, as implied by the length check (line 19) and the trailing-byte check (line 21).

ber_len_t (declared at line 145 for src/dst and used for all bv_len fields) is OpenLDAP's unsigned length type; under that reading x.bv_len -= is->bv_len+1 at line 79 wraps to a huge value. The OOB read at lines 122/130 is confirmed regardless of signedness because x.bv_val is advanced past the buffer by the shown arithmetic at line 78.
limitations: Continuation of the over-read beyond the first byte (if the heap byte at in->bv_val[bv_len] happens to be ' ' or ',') is heap-content-dependent and not attacker-directed.
The missing !x.bv_len guard at line 58 (present at line 100 for thisUpdate) is not itself exploitable: while the cursor invariant holds, the read lands on the in-bounds trailing '}' byte.
numdquotes is a signed int incremented per "" pair (line 72); overflowing it would require an input of roughly 2^32 bytes of quotes, which is impractical and not bounded by any shown cap.

Return values of ber_dupbv_x (line 142) and slap_sl_malloc (line 148) are unchecked; on allocation failure a NULL/empty berval is returned with success via *is=ni (line 158) and return 0 (line 160) -- allocation-failure robustness/DoS concern, not a deterministically confirmed defect.
No claim is made about the allocation size behind in->bv_val beyond the shown bv_len bytes.

verdict.summary: Heap-based buffer overflow in unix_expandpath(): dp->d_name from readdir() is copied into buf via STRCPY(s, dp->d_name) at line 150 with no length validation against buf's allocation STRLEN(path) + BASENAMELEN + 5 (line 32). d_name's length is unconstrained in the fragment, so a sufficiently long directory entry name (which the admission guard at lines 141-148 does not exclude) overflows the heap buffer; the same unvalidated length then drives the appends at lines 157-158 and 164.

evidence.reason: Sink of an unbounded NUL-terminated copy whose source dp->d_name (assigned at line 138 from readdir) retains its full declared domain because the fragment imposes no length cap on it (lines 141-144 only test characters; line 145-146 runs a regex; line 148 compares only e - s bytes, which is not a bound on the copy). The destination buf has the visible capacity STRLEN(path) + BASENAMELEN + 5 (line 32); with s - buf <= STRLEN(path) (scan-loop bound, lines 45-71), a d_name of length >= BASENAMELEN + 5/6 writes past the allocation. The admission guard at lines 141-148 executes before the sink but admits arbitrarily long names (a '*' pattern matches any length), so the failure set intersects the admitted set. Primary CWE-122: heap-based buffer overflow via unbounded copy over a visible allocation size.

assumptions: alloc() returns a heap buffer of exactly the requested size STRLEN(path) + BASENAMELEN + 5 (line 32); BASENAMELEN is a positive named constant.
STRCPY is an unbounded NUL-terminated string copy, in contrast to the bounded STRNCPY used at line 65 in the same fragment.
readdir()'s d_name is a NUL-terminated string; its maximum length is not established by any statement in the fragment.
The recursive calls at lines 125, 160, and 169 terminate: each consumes one path component and '**' recursion is capped by stardepth < 100 and didstar.
limitations: The overflow magnitude cannot be pinned to an exact value because BASENAMELEN's value and the OS maximum d_name length are not visible in the fragment; the finding is a sound residual-range claim (any d_name longer than the remaining capacity of buf), hence confidence 0.62.
NULL dereference of the gap and path parameters (lines 11, 32, 45) is not reachable: no shown statement produces a NULL value for them.
vim_regfree(regmatch.regprog) (line 204) can receive NULL when EW_NOTWILD is set and vim_regcomp failed (line 112); callee NULL-handling is not visible, so this is a robustness concern only.
Regex compilation/matching on the user-derived pattern (lines 107, 145) is a potential complexity concern but no resource bound or demonstrated algorithmic failure is established within the fragment.
The appends at lines 157-158 and 164 share the same root cause (unvalidated d_name length feeding len at line 151) and are not reported as independent findings.

verdict.summary: In the vim9script lambda branch of eval7, the typval payload `rettv->vval.v_partial` is dereferenced at line 154 with no NULL or type check. The guard at line 152 admits every `get_lambda_tv()` OK result in evaluating vim9script mode without constraining the result container, so an expression starting with '(' can drive an unguarded dereference that is not excluded by any shown statement, yielding a NULL/type-confusion crash (DoS) on attacker-supplied expression text.

evidence.reason: The sink dereferences `rettv->vval.v_partial`, a payload field of the result container produced by `get_lambda_tv()` (line 151), with no NULL or `v_type` check. Its residual range is unconstrained by the shown code: the guard at line 152 (`ret == OK && evaluate`) admits every OK result without inspecting the container, so the admitted set intersects the failure set (`v_partial` NULL / non-partial typval), and line 154 executes for the entire admitted set. The entry-point expression text (first byte '(' in vim9script, per `switch (**arg)` at line 41 and `in_vim9script()` at line 149) reaches this path with evaluate TRUE (lines 7-8), and no statement between lines 151 and 154 conditions the deref. Primary mechanism: CWE-476 NULL pointer dereference; no shown protective statement covers the operation.

assumptions: Line numbers are relative to the fragment as presented (line 1 = `eval7(`).
`in_vim9script()` is the framework mode flag that makes the `(`-lambda branch reachable, and `evaluate` reflects `evalarg->eval_flags & EVAL_EVALUATE` (lines 7-8).
`*arg` is a NUL-terminated C byte string; `char_u` is an 8-bit unsigned type.
The finding rests on the class standard that a payload-extracted pointer dereferenced with no NULL check is the defect; no shown NULL producer is required.
limitations: The NULL-producing `typval` state (get_lambda_tv returning OK without a valid `v_partial`) is callee-side and not visible in the fragment, which caps confidence at 0.65.

`@` register handling (lines 126-142): in legacy script mode the register byte passed to `get_reg_contents(**arg, ...)` (line 136) is unvalidated, but the callee's required domain is not shown, so an OOB on the register table cannot be confirmed.

Potential alias use-after-free: on the evaluate + curly-brace-name path, `name_start` aliases memory freed by `vim_free(alias)` (line 257) before `handle_subscript(arg, name_start, ...)` (line 263); no dereference of `name_start` after the free is visible in the fragment, so the UAF is unconfirmed.
`char_u *alias;` (line 14) is read at lines 198/257; whether every `get_name_len` path initializes `*alias` is not shown, so uninitialized use is unconfirmed.

The `@`-case error branches (lines 129-132) emit errors without setting `ret = FAIL`, then `eval7` continues to `handle_subscript` with `ret == OK` and a VAR_UNKNOWN `rettv`; the downstream effect is not visible and is recorded as a status-handling wart, not a confirmed finding.
`semsg`/`emsg` calls use fixed gettext format strings with `*arg` as a variadic argument; no format-string vulnerability is present.

verdict.summary: esp_output_head is the guarded version: every dangerous operation has a located protective bound. The frag-descriptor write at L51-52 is protected by L25 (`skb_shinfo(skb)->nr_frags < MAX_SKB_FRAGS`, admitting indices 0..MAX-1 before the index at L51); the linear tail growth and trailer fill at L81-82 are protected on the fast path by L19 (`tailen <= skb_tailroom(skb)` with trailer == skb at L21) and on the cow path by the checked `skb_cow_data` call at L74-76; the page-frag path routes refill failure to cow at L37-39 and never reaches pskb_put. No confirmed memory-safety, injection, crypto, or error-handling flaw is demonstrated from the shown code. Residual low-side concerns (negative `esp->tailen`, unbounded `esp->tfclen`/`esp->plen`, and the returned frag-count semantics) depend on magnitudes/consumers outside the fragment and are recorded as demoted limitations.

assumptions: `MAX_SKB_FRAGS` is the capacity of `skb_shinfo(skb)->frags[]`, and `nr_frags` counts its used entries; this is implied by L25 comparing `nr_frags` against `MAX_SKB_FRAGS` immediately before it is used as the descriptor index at L51 and stored back at L53.
`skb_tailroom(skb)` (L19) returns the writable linear tailroom in bytes, so `tailen <= skb_tailroom(skb)` bounds the L82 growth for the target `trailer == skb` (L21).
`skb_page_frag_refill(allocsize, pfrag, GFP_ATOMIC)` (L37) guarantees `allocsize` usable bytes at `pfrag->offset`, which covers the `tailen <= allocsize` bytes described at L51-52 and written at L47.
`skb_cow_data(skb, tailen, &trailer)` (L74) guarantees `tailen` bytes of tailroom in the returned `trailer`, and its failure is checked at L75-76 before `trailer`/`tail` are used at L77-82.
limitations: Negative `esp->tailen` would pass the L19 guard (`tailen <= skb_tailroom` excludes only the positive over-size) and reach `pskb_put(skb, trailer, tailen)` at L82 as a huge unsigned length, corrupting skb accounting / linear tail and making L81 fill run at a shifted tail; however, no shown statement produces or constrains a negative `tailen` (L8 merely copies `esp->tailen`, whose construction in `esp_output_alloc` is outside the fragment), so the witness is caller-magnitude-dependent — demoted under the reachability/degenerate-input discipline. A low-side (`tailen >= 0`) bound is not visible in the fragment.

`esp->tfclen` and `esp->plen` reach `esp_output_fill_trailer(tail, ..., esp->tfclen, esp->plen, ...)` at L47/L81 with no shown relation to `tailen` (the `tailen = tfclen + plen + auth/len` construction is outside the fragment); an over-write claim would need `tfclen + plen` to exceed the visible capacities (L19 tailroom / L33 allocsize) by arithmetic shown in the fragment, which cannot be demonstrated — range concern only, no CWE.

Return-value semantics of `nfrags` differ across paths (L20 = 1, L59 = nr_frags+2 after L53's `++nfrags`, L74 = `skb_cow_data` count), and the consumer is the unshown caller; any off-by-one in the returned fragment count cannot be confirmed as a security-relevant sink within the fragment.

`x`, `skb`, and `esp` are dereferenced without NULL checks (L11, L18, L25, L74), but the kernel XFRM path guarantees non-NULL objects and the fragment contains no NULL producer; a NULL-deref would be a robustness concern, not an attacker-directed finding.
`trailer` is not assigned on the page-frag path (L27-67) but is never read before `goto out` (L67), so no uninitialized use occurs.

`pfrag->offset + allocsize` (L55) and `page_address(page) + pfrag->offset` (L45) staying within the page relies on the `skb_page_frag_refill` contract named above; the fragment shows no explicit PAGE_SIZE check.

verdict.summary: The endpoint path (line 4) is copied into sockaddr_un::sun_path with strncpy bounded by sizeof(local.sun_path) but with no length check and no NUL-termination guard; a path of length >= sizeof(local.sun_path) leaves sun_path unterminated, and the subsequent unlink() (line 16) and chmod() (line 21) consume the buffer as a C string, reading past the S-byte array (CWE-125) and passing an attacker-shaped unterminated path to filesystem operations (CWE-170).

evidence.reason: pipePath (line 4, unconstrained std::string) is copied at line 15 with n = sizeof(local.sun_path) (the capacity of the array declared at line 9); for any admitted path of length >= sizeof(local.sun_path) no NUL byte is written into sun_path[0..S-1], so unlink's C-string scan reads at least one byte past the array and consumes an unbounded window of adjacent memory, while the FS argument is attacker-shaped. The only guard (line 5) admits first-time paths of this length; no shown statement checks the length or re-terminates the buffer. Primary CWE-170 (improper NUL termination followed by a length-dependent read), with the OOB read as its consequence.

On non-Win32 builds the same unterminated sun_path (produced by the bounded-but-unterminated strncpy at line 15 from the unconstrained pipePath of line 4) is passed to chmod, causing the same length-dependent read past the array declared at line 9 and applying permission changes to whatever path string results. Same missing length/NUL-termination guard as the line 16 sink; primary CWE-170.

assumptions: local.sun_path is an array whose size is exactly sizeof(local.sun_path) as used in the strncpy at line 15 (declared at line 9 via sockaddr_un local;).
std::string (line 4) admits lengths up to SIZE_MAX; the fragment imposes no length cap on pipePath.
unlink(2)/chmod(2) consume their path argument as a NUL-terminated C string (standard semantics).
The duplicate-path guard at line 5 admits any first-time path including lengths >= sizeof(local.sun_path).
limitations: Discarded return of ::listen(fd, 5) at line 19 is a status-handling weakness, but no shown data can trigger a listen failure on the freshly bound stream socket and no security-relevant operation on the failure state is demonstrated; demoted, no CWE.

TOCTOU/symlink race on the unlink (line 16) -> bind (line 18) -> chmod (line 21) pathname sequence requires an attacker interleaving between external syscalls that is not derivable from the fragment alone; demoted, no CWE.
An overlong pathname causing FATAL_FAIL(::bind(...)) at line 18 is a consequence of the same missing length validation as the primary finding, not an independent CWE.
No independent CWE-125 is reported because the out-of-bounds read is the direct consequence of the same CWE-170 root cause, not an independent mechanism.

verdict.summary: Unconditional NULL-pointer dereference of the `prog` parameter at line 4 (`prog->type`): the fragment imposes no check on `prog` before dereferencing it, so a NULL value (inside the pointer parameter's full declared domain) reaches the dereference on every path, causing a crash.

evidence.reason: The pointer-typed parameter `prog` is dereferenced unconditionally at line 4 with no NULL check anywhere between function entry (line 2) and the sink; the declared domain of `js_Ast *` includes NULL and no shown statement constrains it, so the residual range still contains NULL. The branch test itself is the dereference, so no guard can protect it, and the only other guard (line 10, `minify > 1`) executes after the sink on every path. A NULL `prog` triggers a segmentation fault, a CWE-476 NULL-pointer-dereference with DoS impact.

assumptions: `prog` is a pointer-typed parameter whose full declared domain includes NULL; the fragment contains no statement that initializes, checks, or derives a guaranteed non-NULL value for it.
`minify` is a module-level global assigned at line 3 from `dominify` and read at line 10; no other use is visible.
limitations: The witness value (NULL) is the degenerate case supplied by the parameter's declared domain rather than derived by a shown statement; per the NULL-dereference standard this is still the finding, but confidence is capped at 0.65.
Callers of `jsP_dumpsyntax` are not shown, so attacker reachability and the resulting severity (crash-only DoS, rated low) cannot be further confirmed.
`J` is unused in the shown code; `nl()` and `putchar` return values are discarded, but no security-relevant operation runs on their failure, so those are robustness concerns, not findings.
The bodies of `pstmlist` and `pstm` are not shown; the arguments `-1` and `0` are not derived quantities, so no out-of-domain call-site argument finding can be anchored.

verdict.summary: The not-found branch of the map lookup is guarded by an equality check (line 4) that routes to STFATAL (line 5), a fatal-severity log whose name-implied semantics terminate the process; consequently `return it->second;` (line 7) is only reached with a found, valid iterator. No tainted value reaches a security-relevant sink.

assumptions: `idInfoMap.find(id)` (line 3) returns `end()` exactly when `id` is not a key, and a found iterator refers to a valid element (standard `std::map` semantics inferred from the shown `find`, `end`, and `it->second` usage).
`STFATAL` is a fatal-severity logging stream whose name-implied semantics terminate the process, so control does not continue past line 5 on the not-found path.
`lock_guard` (line 2) holds `routerMutex` for the function scope, and no statement between the guard (lines 4-6) and the sink (line 7) mutates `idInfoMap`.
limitations: If `STFATAL` were implemented as a non-terminating log (e.g., a severity that logs and continues), an absent key would reach `return it->second;` at line 7 with `it == end()`, producing a past-the-end/NULL dereference (CWE-476/CWE-690); this cannot be confirmed because the macro's definition is outside the fragment, and its `FATAL` name-implied semantics are the deciding convention.

An attacker- or caller-supplied `id` that is not a key triggers the deliberate fatal abort at line 5 (reachable-abort/DoS reading, CWE-617); the fragment treats this as the intended protection for the dereference, and no caller contract or input validation is shown to make the abort an independent flaw.

The concrete type of `TerminalUserInfo` (the value read at line 7) and the map's backing allocation are not shown; only iterator validity is security-relevant here, and it is established by the guard.

verdict.summary: stl_remove_degenerate forwards the -1 sentinel neighbor index (as -1 index into stl->neighbors_start) via stl_update_connects_remove_1 at lines 49 and 52 whenever neighbor1 == -1 and neighbor2 == -1 (guards at lines 48/51 admit -1), yielding a negative-index heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) in the neighbor table; the argument is given no >= 0 or != -1 bound before the call.

evidence.reason: Sink for CWE-787: neighbor2 is read at line 46 (stl->neighbors_start[facet].neighbor[edge2]) with no range constraint, and the fragment's own guard at line 51 (neighbor2 == -1) proves -1 is in its admitted set. When line 48 admits neighbor1 == -1 and line 51 also admits neighbor2 == -1, this call passes -1 as the helper's facet index (facet_num); the helper consumes it as an index into stl->neighbors_start, and -1 is outside the 0-based index domain, so the helper performs a negative-index heap OOB write. No shown statement constrains the argument to >= 0 (guard at line 51 tests the other variable and executes after line 49's path is taken).

Sink for CWE-787: neighbor1 is read at line 45 (stl->neighbors_start[facet].neighbor[edge1]) with no range constraint, and the fragment's own guard at line 48 (neighbor1 == -1) proves -1 is in its admitted set. When line 51 admits neighbor2 == -1 and line 48 also admits neighbor1 == -1, this call passes -1 as the helper's facet index (facet_num); the helper consumes it as an index into stl->neighbors_start, so -1 selects before the start of the array and the helper performs a negative-index heap OOB write. No shown statement constrains the argument to >= 0 (guard at line 48 tests the other variable and is not a bound on neighbor1).

assumptions: neighbor[] and which_vertex_not[] are 3-slot arrays per facet, implied by the edge constants {0,1,2} (lines 28-40) and the (x+1)%3 index arithmetic (lines 62-67, 74).

stl_update_connects_remove_1(stl_file *, int facet_num) consumes its second parameter as a facet index into stl->neighbors_start, per its name/signature and the shown code's own identical access pattern (lines 45-59, 61-68).
facet_start and neighbors_start are 0-based C arrays; any negative index is out of bounds without needing a capacity.
Neighbor fields are read without any shown constraint or guaranteed minimum, so the sentinel -1 (explicitly tested at lines 48/51) is in the residual range for both neighbor1 and neighbor2.
limitations: Secondary confirmed flow (not a separate CWE): the parameter facet (int, full domain) reaches stl->facet_start[facet] (lines 14-17, 26-37) and stl->neighbors_start[facet] (lines 45-59) with no visible bounds check or capacity — an unvalidated-index / missing-bound OOB (CWE-125/787 class); line 12 only gates on stl->error.

The != -1 guards at lines 61/65/72 admit every int except -1, so the direct writes at lines 62/66/74 could also index out of range if a stored neighbor value is corrupted; same mechanism class as the primary, but those values are library-computed rather than directly file-parsed.
stl is dereferenced at line 12 with no NULL check (pointer-typed parameter) - classified here as a caller-caused robustness/DoS concern rather than the primary finding (CWE-476 class).

If the unshown callee stl_update_connects_remove_1 internally rejects -1 (e.g., an early return), the primary defect degrades to a robustness concern; per the call-site rule no such unshown check can be assumed, which caps confidence at 0.68.
(vnotN + 1) would overflow at INT_MAX (UB), but no shown producer yields such a value and the only consumer is (x+1)%3, which stays in 0..2.

verdict.summary: thread_call derives nparams = sq_gettop(v) (line 5) with no bound and copies stack slots 2..nparams to the target thread; the loop guard `i < nparams+1` admits i = nparams, which is one past the top of v's stack (valid indices 0..nparams-1), so every invocation performs an out-of-bounds stack read at line 8 and pushes the fetched value onto the target thread's stack as an argument to sq_call (line 9), enabling memory disclosure and stack-state corruption (CWE-125).

evidence.reason: nparams (residual range [2, SQInteger_MAX], unconstrained by any shown statement) is captured at line 5 as the stack count and drives the loop bound `i < nparams+1` at line 7, whose admitted set is i <= nparams inclusive. Since valid indices of v's stack are 0..nparams-1, the final iteration reads index nparams, one element past the top, at this sink line. Witness: thread.call with k=0 args gives nparams=2; line 7 admits i=2 (2<3); line 4 admits the OT_THREAD receiver; the read at index 2 exceeds max valid index 1 by exactly 1, and the same +1 excess occurs on the last iteration for every k. The retrieved object is then written onto the target thread's stack (this same sq_move) and consumed as part of sq_call's parameter layout (line 9), so the out-of-domain read propagates into the callee's stack state. Primary CWE-125 (out-of-bounds read); no protective statement bounds nparams or the index between line 5 and this sink.

assumptions: sq_gettop returns the VM stack element count, so valid indices are 0..nparams-1 (name-implied, standard semantics).
A native invocation guarantees stack slots 0 and 1 because stack_get(v,1) at line 3 is executed unguarded.

sq_move's parameter order follows the fragment's own use: line 8 copies v's slot i into the target thread's stack, and line 10 copies the target thread's top (index -1) back into v, followed by sq_pop(_thread(o),1) at line 11.
limitations: The target thread's stack capacity is not visible in the fragment, so the unchecked push volume (CWE-787) into _thread(o) cannot be independently confirmed; the confirmed out-of-domain derivation is the read index at line 8.

The concrete content of the over-read slot depends on prior stack state, which is not shown; the over-read itself is confirmed by the shown arithmetic (index nparams vs. max valid index nparams-1).

verdict.summary: thread_call passes sq_call a parameter count (nparams, from sq_gettop at L5) that is always one larger than the number of arguments actually staged on the target thread stack (nparams-1, pushed by L7-L9), so the call machinery reads one SQObjectPtr from a slot the shown code never initialized (out-of-bounds/uninitialized read), for every admissible call of a thread.

evidence.reason: The count argument nparams (L5, entry-point-derived via sq_gettop(v), residual range nparams >= 1 with no shown upper bound) is consumed at this sink as the parameter count, but the shown code staged only nparams-1 arguments on the thread stack: L7 pushes one callable entry and the L8-L9 loop (i in 2..nparams) pushes nparams-1 values, so the initialized region is indices 0..nparams-1. Passing nparams therefore overstates the staged parameters by exactly one for every admitted input (including nparams=1 with zero arguments); the callee must source an SQObjectPtr from slot nparams (reserved but never initialized by any shown push) or below the stack base, i.e. an out-of-bounds/uninitialized read (CWE-125) causing type confusion/crash. The L6 reservation nparams+3 covers the written indices but neither initializes the phantom slot nor protects below index 0, so no protective statement absorbs the mismatch.

sq_call's params argument has the name-implied, standard Squirrel API meaning of 'number of parameters' (the callable sits below them).
limitations: The exact byte-level failure mode inside the unshown sq_call (read of stack index -1 versus read of the reserved-but-uninitialized slot at index nparams) depends on the callee's stack layout; both are out-of-domain relative to the values the shown code initialized, which is what the confirmed excess (+1) demonstrates.

The discarded SQRETURN of sq_reservestack (L6) and of each sq_move (L9) is an unchecked-return robustness concern, not independently confirmed as a finding (no shown operation is demonstrated to run on a failed reservation state).
Integer overflow of nparams + 3 (L6) is not a finding: nparams would need to approach SQInteger max, which is not derivable from any shown constraint.
No log, command, SQL, XPath, format-string, or header injection sinks exist in the fragment; the L18 format string is static.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. Remaining candidates (buf->len narrowing on the merge path, ring_size==0 mask underflow, NULL derefs of page/i/pipe, size_t wrap in offset+bytes) are not confirmable from the shown statements.

Return values of `sanity(i)` (line 17) and `pipe_full(...)` (line 32) are fully consumed via early returns and the not-full gate executes before the slot stores (line 32 precedes lines 35-40).
On the install path, line 36 `buf->flags = 0;` always executes before the slot becomes visible at line 42, leaving `flags` with the single admitted value 0.
limitations: Merge path `buf->len += bytes` (line 25) narrows a `size_t` bytes residual [1, i->count] into `unsigned int`; a wrap requires a >= 2^32 count that no shown statement derives, the merge precondition (`offset == off && buf->page == page`) is not attacker-forgeable from the fragment alone, and the length consumer is outside the fragment — range claim only, no CWE.

`p_mask = pipe->ring_size - 1` (line 7) underflows to UINT_MAX only if ring_size == 0; the invariant ring_size >= 1 and the capacity of `pipe->bufs` are not visible in the fragment, so no OOB is confirmable in either direction.

NULL dereferences of `page`, `i`, and `i->pipe` (e.g., `get_page(page)` line 37): no shown statement can produce NULL, and validity of these framework pointers is an external invariant — robustness concern, not a confirmed finding.

The downstream consumer of `buf->flags` (the pipe write/merge path) is outside the fragment; the not-vulnerable verdict rests on the shown initialization at line 36 bounding flags to {0}.

verdict.summary: In ipf_extract_frags_from_batch, when ipf_handle_frag() returns true (the fragment is accepted, the packet is neither reinserted into the batch nor freed: the only refill calls (lines 18/22) execute only when the fragment is not handled or not a fragment, and no dp_packet_delete exists anywhere in the shown code. Every accepted IP/IPv6 fragment therefore leaks its dp_packet buffer, a per-packet leak whose rate tracks attacker-controlled fragment traffic and never decays, enabling memory-exhaustion DoS of the userspace datapath (CWE-401).

evidence.reason: pkt is an entry-point-derived batch element (line 9, dp_packet_batch_size at line 5 bounds the loop to [0, pb_cnt); no NULL/validity check is shown). The guards at lines 10-14 admit any valid IPv4/IPv6 fragment. When ipf_handle_frag returns true (normal acceptance), the false-only branch at line 18 is skipped and no statement in the fragment frees or returns pkt to the batch, so the packet's allocation is leaked once per accepted fragment (CWE-401); the leak rate equals the attacker's fragment rate and is unbounded over time, enabling resource-exhaustion DoS of vswitchd. The protective statement this path needs (else { dp_packet_delete(pkt); }) is absent.

assumptions: ipf_handle_frag stores a clone/keeps the fragment referenced internally and does not free the original packet passed from the batch; the caller (this function) owns the original dp_packet on the true path — the refill contract 'caller owns the packets that are not refilled' together with the absence of any free in the fragment makes the true-path packet a permanent leak.
pb_cnt = dp_packet_batch_size(pb) (line 5) is non-negative; loop index pb_idx stays within [0, pb_cnt).
limitations: Input validation performed inside ipf_is_valid_v4_frag / ipf_is_valid_v6_frag is not visible, so no OOB-read claim about short or malformed headers can be confirmed from this fragment.
No NULL-deref of pkt is confirmable: the fragment neither initializes nor derives a NULL packet pointer; NULL batch slots would have to come from an unshown producer.

The capacity of pb->packets[] and the exact DP_PACKET_BATCH_REFILL_FOR_EACH/refill macro internals are not in the fragment, so an OOB/batch-count claim on the loop cannot be demonstrated (reads stay within [0, pb_cnt) as shown).
Whether the batch leave stale entries for the caller after consumed packets is caller-side behavior and not analyzable here.

If ipf_handle_frag were instead assumed to free the original packet internally (a callee behavior not shown and contradicted by the module's refill-ownership contract), the failure would be a double-free rather than a leak; the fragment alone cannot distinguish these two callee implementations, and the leak interpretation is the one matching the shown ownership contract and the fix counterpart.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. The only dereference of the AST pointer prog (line 5) is fully guarded by the NULL check 'if (prog)' at line 4, which excludes NULL and admits only non-NULL pointers on the path to every use of prog (lines 5, 6, 8). Remaining calls receive constants or the guarded pointer, and dominify/minify only control emission of a newline; no memory, injection, crypto, or control-flow sink is reachable from unconstrained input in this fragment.
