The destination capacity of dir_ent.name for strcpy (line 107) is not shown; the source side is provably NUL-terminated within the line-5 buffer.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. The only attacker-influenced arithmetic sinks are the TrialStage ratios at L67 and L124; both are protected by explicit guards: L14 excludes numRecords <= 100 (admitting numRecords >= 101) before the sharded division, and L91 excludes numRecords == 0 and an unengaged bucketUnpacker before the time-series division. The divisions are floating-point, so even a zero denominator is not UB. plan_executor_factory::make's status is checked at L161-L163, and the bucketUnpacker and trialStage dereferences are covered by the guards at L91 and L168-L169. Remaining concerns (unguarded framework-handle dereferences, negative sampleSize/numRecords with no in-fragment sink, the unshown gTimeseriesBucketMaxCount value, and float precision loss in plan-choice heuristics) are demoted: none has a confirmable failure path within the shown code.

assumptions: The visible constants are kMaxSampleRatioForRandCursor = 0.05 (L12), kCoefficient = 0.01 (L27), kMaxPresampleSize = 100 (L59), kCoefficient = 0.02 and kMinBucketFullness = 0.25 (L121-L122); their values are in the fragment and back all ratio computations.
Both ratio expressions are floating-point (sampleSize and numRecords promote to double via the double constants), so division by zero yields IEEE infinity/NaN rather than undefined behavior.

boost::intrusive_ptr, CollectionPtr, and boost::optional are used at their standard semantics; the fragment contains no statement that assigns null to expCtx/coll or empties bucketUnpacker after its guard.
limitations: expCtx (L6, L10, L13, L43, L60, L84, L153) and coll (L10, L34, L43, L49, L138) are dereferenced without NULL checks; a null handle would require an unshown caller/lifecycle violation and is not attacker-directed by any shown statement, so it is a robustness concern, not a confirmed CWE-476 path.
CollectionShardingState::get(...)->getOwnershipFilter(...) (L48-L51) dereferences the lookup result unchecked; no in-fragment NULL producer exists and no attacker-directed failure is shown.

sampleSize and numRecords (long long, L3-L4) are never constrained to be non-negative; negative values would only affect the clamped ratios (L66-L67, L123-L125) and the unshown SampleFromTimeseriesBucket/UnpackTimeseriesBucket constructors (L126, L141), for which no out-of-domain argument can be confirmed from the fragment.

gTimeseriesBucketMaxCount is used at L28, L124, and L136 but is not defined in the fragment, so its value/positivity cannot be assumed in either direction; a 0/0 NaN case would require sampleSize == 0 combined with that unshown constant, and a zero denominator is absorbed by the std::min/std::max clamps at L123-L125.

Double-precision loss in the L14 and L28 comparisons for counts above 2^53 could marginally misclassify plan eligibility; the affected decision is a performance heuristic with no security-relevant consumer, so CWE-697 does not apply.
invariant() at L10 aborts only on an unshown framework precondition (collection lock in MODE_IS); failure is not derivable from attacker-controlled values in the fragment.

verdict.summary: do_mouse() indexes the global TabPageIdxs array with mouse_col (an int mouse-column global updated from mouse events) without bounding it to [0, Columns): the tab-line drag reads at lines 265 and 323 have no mouse_col check at all, and the click read at line 280 is guarded only by 'mouse_col < Columns' (line 277), which admits negative columns. A mouse event carrying an out-of-range column causes an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125), with the spilled value c1 then consumed by tabpage_move/goto_tabpage/find_tabpage.

evidence.reason: mouse_col (int global, mouse-input channel, residual range = full int domain, Phase 1) reaches the TabPageIdxs subscript on the drag path with no bound: the only guards before the sink are TabPageIdxs != NULL (256), mouse_row == 0 && firstwin->w_winrow > 0 (259), is_drag (261), in_tab_line (263); the code's own valid-index convention, the sibling guard 'mouse_col < Columns' (277), never executes on this path. A drag reaching line 265 with mouse_col == Columns (or any negative value) reads past/before the array — unvalidated-index out-of-bounds read (CWE-125).

The click path's protective statement 'mouse_col < Columns' (line 277) admits every int below Columns, including all negative values, so it bounds only the upper edge. With is_click and mouse_row == 0, mouse_col == -1 passes line 277 (-1 < Columns for positive Columns) and reads TabPageIdxs[-1] at line 280 — an out-of-bounds read below the array start (CWE-125); a lower-bound check (mouse_col >= 0) is missing.

Reached via 'else if (is_drag && in_tab_line)' (line 321) when line 259's mouse_row == 0 condition is false, after a prior tab-line click set in_tab_line (279). No statement constrains mouse_col on this path, so any int value outside the [0, Columns) range the code uses elsewhere (e.g., -1 or Columns) indexes out of bounds at line 323 — unvalidated-index out-of-bounds read (CWE-125).

assumptions: TabPageIdxs is the tab-page-index array for the tab line; its element count is not declared in the fragment, but the sibling guard 'mouse_col < Columns' (line 277) is the code's own convention that valid column indices are below Columns.

mouse_col/mouse_row are int globals holding mouse coordinates delivered by the input (terminal) layer; the fragment imposes no constraint on them, and it explicitly handles negative coordinates on the row axis ('if (is_drag && mouse_row < 0 && !in_status_line)').
The witnesses use mod_mask == 0 (no modifiers), which is in the declared int domain and satisfies the modifier-filter guards at lines 137-168 and 173.
limitations: The producer of mouse_col (terminal mouse-report decoding) is outside the fragment; per the analysis framework, framework/OS-provided data with no shown invariant retains its full declared int domain, so no clamp to [0, Columns) is assumed.

The exact upper capacity of TabPageIdxs is not declared in the fragment; the drag-path findings are therefore stated as missing-bound unvalidated-index OOB reads, while the negative-index read at line 280 is OOB before any array regardless of its size.

The downstream tabpage operations consuming the OOB-read value c1 (tabpage_move, goto_tabpage, find_tabpage, tabpage_close*) are consequences of the same confirmed OOB read and were not assigned a separate CWE.
The event-merging for(;;) loop (58-85) and the whitespace-skip while loop were examined for non-termination; each iteration consumes input or stops at VIM_ISWHITE(NUL)==false, so no CWE-835 finding.
All oap dereferences are NULL-guarded (lines 176-179, 188, and the operator-pending block), so no NULL-dereference finding.
No format-string, command, SQL, log, or other injection sink is present in the fragment; fixed-string and fixed-register arguments only.

verdict.summary: Stack out-of-bounds write in gopherToHTML: a gopher response line whose content totals TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1 bytes passes the size guard at line 75 (which only excludes llen >= TEMP_BUF_SIZE), and the NUL terminator at line 96 is written at line[llen+1] == line[TEMP_BUF_SIZE], one byte past the TEMP_BUF_SIZE-byte local array declared at line 6. The cap at line 77 reserves the NUL slot with -1, but the subsequent +1 in line 96 defeats it; both the capped and uncapped paths reach index TEMP_BUF_SIZE. Remotely triggerable memory corruption / DoS (CWE-787).

evidence.reason: llen is derived from attacker-supplied line data (lines 67-73) and can equal TEMP_BUF_SIZE - 1: with gopherState->len == 0 (established at line 92) the guard at line 75 only excludes llen >= TEMP_BUF_SIZE, so llen == TEMP_BUF_SIZE - 1 is admitted (and the cap at line 77 also yields TEMP_BUF_SIZE - 1 when it fires, restored to that value by line 91). The array `line` declared at line 6 as LOCAL_ARRAY(char, line, TEMP_BUF_SIZE) has valid indices 0..TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1, so the store at index llen+1 == TEMP_BUF_SIZE writes one byte past the end of the stack buffer (CWE-787). Witness: gopherState->len == 0; inbuf contains TEMP_BUF_SIZE-2 bytes then '\n' with len >= TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1; llen == lpos-pos == TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1 passes lines 75/79/87, copies in-bounds at line 94, and overruns at line 96.

assumptions: LOCAL_ARRAY(char, line, TEMP_BUF_SIZE) declares `line` as a stack array of exactly TEMP_BUF_SIZE chars (valid indices 0..TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1); TEMP_BUF_SIZE is a compile-time constant used in the comparisons and cap arithmetic at lines 16, 75, 77, 104, 246, 250.
gopherState->len is 0 at the start of a line-processing iteration (produced by line 92 and by first-call state); the overflow witness does not depend on the initial value.
limitations: gopherState->buf capacity is not shown; the memcpy calls at lines 83 and 89 rely on it being at least TEMP_BUF_SIZE, which cannot be verified from the fragment.

The outbuf.appendf at lines 235-236 (GOPHER_WWW branch) passes 3 arguments for 5 format specifiers (varargs mismatch, undefined behavior); no CWE from the scoped list cleanly matches (not a user-controlled format string), so it is recorded here rather than as a confirmed CWE.

host and port derived from the gopher response are inserted unescaped into HTML attribute values (lines 232-233, 219-225, 239-240); html_quote is applied only to name/result, so a crafted response can break out of the HREF attribute. This is a plausible secondary XSS-type concern (CWE-79), kept out of the primary verdict and cwe list to keep the focus on the confirmed memory-safety defect.

xstrdup at line 154 is dereferenced without a NULL check (lines 218, 239), but its only failure mode is allocation failure on a non-attacker-scaled size; per the analysis rules this is a robustness concern, not a confirmed finding.
strtok/atoi NULL paths (lines 262-294) are guarded: result non-NULL implies the token pointers it feeds to atoi are non-NULL, and `if (!result) break` precedes every atoi use.

verdict.summary: The recursion-data scan in get_recurse_data_length reads and advances its scan pointer using per-opcode argument bytes (cc[1] at lines 164/176, the branch offset gcGET(cc,1) at line 88) with no check that those argument bytes lie within [cc, ccend). The only guard, the L20 loop condition 'while (cc < ccend)', admits cc = ccend-1, where 'cc[1]' reads one code unit past ccend (CWE-125) and the advance pushes cc past ccend, guaranteeing the L199 'SLJIT_ASSERT(cc == ccend)' fails (reachable abort where asserts are active) or a wrong length/flag result is returned. The same missing bound affects the L89 dereference of 'alternative = cc + GET(cc, 1)'.

evidence.reason: Primary sink (OP_MARK/OP_COMMIT_ARG/OP_PRUNE_ARG/OP_THEN_ARG). cc[1] is a pattern code unit in the residual range [0, 2^width-1] with no visible bound check against ccend; the only prior guard is L20 'while (cc < ccend)', which admits cc = ccend-1. On that admitted value the read cc[1] targets address ccend (one code unit past the exclusive end of the scanned range [cc, ccend) defined by the ccend parameter), an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125), and the resulting advance cc += 1 + 2 + cc[1] >= ccend + 2 forces cc != ccend, tripping L199 'SLJIT_ASSERT(cc == ccend)' (reachable abort) or returning a wrong length. No statement between L20 and L164 bounds the argument byte against ccend; the missing bound is the defect.

Same missing-bound flow at the OP_SKIP_ARG sink. The unvalidated pattern byte cc[1] is read and used to advance cc with only the L20 'cc < ccend' guard on the path; an admitted cc = ccend-1 produces a one-code-unit out-of-bounds read of cc[1] at address ccend and an advance beyond ccend, violating the L199 equality assertion / poisoning the computed length. Confirmed OOB read (CWE-125) with identical provenance and absence of a per-opcode bounds check as the L164 sink.

Dereference of 'alternative' computed at L88 as 'cc + GET(cc, 1)', where GET(cc, 1) is a pattern-derived branch length with no visible bound. For an admitted OP_COND position at or near ccend (or a length field whose offset reaches past the end), alternative = cc + GET(cc,1) falls outside [cc, ccend) and the L89 read is out of bounds (CWE-125). The only guard before the read is L20 'cc < ccend', which does not bound the added offset; no sanitization or bound statement exists on the path.

Reachable-abort consequence of the missing-bound scans above: whenever an argument-bearing opcode is admitted at cc = ccend-1, cc is advanced to at least ccend+2, so this post-loop equality check fails on an attacker-chosen pattern value that passes every guard on the path (L20 strict < admits ccend-1; switch dispatch at L23 selects the OP_MARK/OP_SKIP_ARG/OP_COND cases). Where SLJIT_ASSERT is compiled in, this aborts; where it is a no-op, the function returns a corrupted length from L216. Same root cause (missing argument-bounds validation), reported as impact detail, not a separate CWE.

assumptions: ccend is the exclusive end pointer of the scanned compiled-code range [cc, ccend) (end-pointer semantics conveyed by the fragment's own loop 'while (cc < ccend)' and the final 'SLJIT_ASSERT(cc == ccend)').
PCRE2_SPTR points to unsigned code units, so cc[1] is non-negative with value domain 0..2^width-1 (width 8/16/32 per build configuration); the minimum advance of 1+2+cc[1] is therefore >= 3.

The OP_MARK/OP_COMMIT_ARG/OP_PRUNE_ARG/OP_THEN_ARG/OP_SKIP_ARG bytecode layout follows the constant advance '1 + 2 + cc[1]' used by the shown code itself, and OP_COND carries a GET(cc,1) branch offset.
limitations: The OOB-read witness requires an argument-carrying opcode to occupy the final position of the scanned range (a truncated/adversarial code range). The fragment neither derives nor forbids this state — the demonstrated defect is precisely the absence of a check — but the precondition is not produced by a shown statement, and the abort consequence depends on SLJIT_ASSERT build semantics (asserts may be compiled out in release builds, in which case the mis-scan silently returns a wrong length whose downstream allocation consequences are outside the fragment).

L194-195: if next_opcode(common, cc) returns NULL and SLJIT_ASSERT is a no-op, the next iteration dereferences NULL at L23 'switch(*cc)'; this depends on next_opcode's unshown behavior and the same malformed-pattern precondition, so it is not separately confirmed.

L73 'common->optimized_cbracket[GET2(cc, 1 + LINK_SIZE)]': the capture number is pattern-derived but the capacity of optimized_cbracket is not visible in the fragment; reported as a missing-bound candidate only, not a confirmed finding.

L42-48 'cc += PRIVATE_DATA(cc + 1)' and the unicode extra-length adjustments (L99/L108/L117) derive from compiler-internal state (PRIVATE_DATA table), not from attacker-visible values within the fragment; no finding is asserted for them.

The wrong 'length' value returned at L216 could under-allocate recursion data in the unshown caller, but that downstream memory impact is not visible in the fragment and therefore not part of the verdict.

verdict.summary: The int parameter `size` is passed unvalidated as the byte length to `qemu_send_packet(nc, buf, size)` (line 10) and `nc->info->receive(nc, buf, size)` (line 8). No statement in the fragment bounds or rejects it (residual range: full int domain, including negatives and values with no visible buffer capacity), so an admitted value supplies an out-of-domain length and drives an out-of-bounds read from `buf` in the emulator's network path (CWE-125), yielding a guest-triggerable host crash/DoS with possible memory disclosure.

evidence.reason: `size` (declared int at line 1) has residual range [INT_MIN, INT_MAX] because no statement between line 1 and line 10 constrains it; it is forwarded unchanged to qemu_send_packet's byte-length parameter. The length domain required is 0..capacity(buf), and capacity(buf) is not declared anywhere in the fragment (missing bound). A negative value such as -1 passes the only guard (line 7, a PHY-register branch that admits all sizes) and converts to a huge size_t in the callee, reading far past `buf` — out-of-bounds read, CWE-125.

On the loopback-admitted branch (line 7 true), the same unvalidated `size` (full int domain, no shown constraint) is consumed as the byte count of a receive from `buf`, whose capacity is not shown in the fragment. Any negative value (e.g., -1) or any positive value exceeding the undeclared buffer capacity supplies an out-of-domain length, causing an out-of-bounds read of `buf` in the receive path — CWE-125.

assumptions: `size` is declared `int` (line 1) and therefore spans [INT_MIN, INT_MAX].
The final argument of `qemu_send_packet` and of the `receive` callback is consumed as a byte length from `buf` (name- and use-implied standard semantics).
`buf` has no declared capacity anywhere in the fragment, so no positive upper bound is derivable from the shown code.
limitations: NULL dereference of `nc` from `qemu_get_queue(s->nic)` (line 6) is not a finding: no shown statement derives NULL, and the dereference would occur inside the library call.

`inc_tx_bcast_or_mcast_count(s, buf)` (line 12) performs a fixed-size read of `buf`; it shares the unshown-`buf`-capacity root cause and is subsumed by the primary `size` flow rather than reported as an independent sink.

`e1000x_increase_size_stats(s->mac_reg, PTCregs, size)` (line 13) is not a finding: `PTCregs` is a fixed 6-element array and no index derived from `size` is visible in the fragment; `size` is only compared.
The discarded return values of the send/receive calls run no security-relevant operation on failure; the post-send counter increments do not gate any security decision.

Confidence is capped at the range-analysis band (0.62) because the exploit magnitude (e.g., -1) is an arbitrary member of a fully unconstrained admitted set rather than a value produced by shown arithmetic.
A hypothetical caller-side 16-bit descriptor bound is excluded by the rules: it is not derivable from the shown code.

verdict.summary: parseDragons validates only `off >= size` (line 4) with non-negative size, so a negative `off` (full `int` domain, attacker-controlled from the parsed binary) passes every guard and is passed as the read offset at line 18 (`r_buf_read_at (buf, off, b, size)`) and as `off - 8` at line 55. No shown statement ever constrains `off >= 0`, producing an out-of-domain (negative) read offset over untrusted file data — an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) with attacker-controlled magnitude up to |INT_MIN|; the post-read `available != size` checks (lines 19/56) run after the attempt and cannot validate the offset.

evidence.snippet: int available = r_buf_read_at (buf, off, b, size);
evidence.reason: `off` is an `int` entry-point parameter whose residual range, after the only guard on the path (line 4 `if (off >= size)` with non-negative `r_buf_size`), is `[INT_MIN, size-1]` — every negative value admitted. A witness `off = -8` (buffer length 0x1000) passes lines 4, 8, 11, 15 (`size = 0x1008`, `malloc` succeeds) and reaches this sink with a negative source offset into `buf` (capacity quote: sparse declaration only, `RBuffer` length from line 3; valid offsets `[0, orig)`). The requested length `size = orig - off` also exceeds the valid tail, reading `|off|` bytes before the buffer start is out-of-domain. The post-read check `available != size` (line 19) executes after the attempt and cannot bound the offset; the missing `off >= 0` validation is the defect. Primary CWE-125 (out-of-bounds read).

Same taint source `off`; line 55 computes `off - 8`, which is negative not only for the already-admitted negative `off` but also for `off` in `[0,7]` (e.g., `off = 4`, `orig = 0x40` → `size = 0x3C` passes line 11; non-magic bytes at `b[0..3]`/`b[8..11]` make `magicCombo != 2` per lines 46–53), so the read offset (e.g., `-4`) is out of `buf`'s valid `[0, orig)` domain before the read; the destination `b` (capacity `size` from line 14) is written exactly `size` bytes, so the defect is the OOB/out-of-domain source read only. The `available != size` check on line 56 is post-hoc and cannot validate the offset. Primary CWE-125.

assumptions: `r_buf_size(buf)` returns the non-negative length of the buffer (its natural size-returning invariant); line 4's comparison thus admits all `off < size` including every negative `int`.
`r_buf_read_at` requires a non-negative in-bounds offset as its standard/name-implied contract; a negative offset argument is out of that required domain.
For the demonstrated witnesses the `malloc(size)` at line 14 succeeds (`size = 0x1008` / `0x3C`); failure is in any case handled by the NULL check at line 15.
limitations: Actual crash/info-leak manifestation depends on the unshown buffer-backend `read_at` behavior: a backend that bounds-checks returns a short/failed read which lines 19/56 turn into NULL, while a backend that reads from the negative offset performs an OOB read before the return check; the out-of-domain argument (missing `off >= 0` bound) is confirmed by the shown arithmetic alone.
The `st64`→`int` narrowing of `size` at `r_buf_read_at`'s length parameter cannot be confirmed because the callee signature is not visible in the fragment.

The invalid-magic `else` branch (lines 62–64) continues to `r_coresym_cache_element_new` with unchanged `off`; this is intentional per the surrounding comment and the callee's validation is not shown — no confirmable flaw.
`off -= 8`/`off + 16` `int` arithmetic can wrap only at `INT_MIN`/`INT_MAX` extremes, with no visible security-relevant consumer in the fragment.
No loops exist in the fragment, so no loop-termination or loop-index findings apply.

verdict.summary: In jetp3852_print_page, the guard `if (line_size > DATA_SIZE)` (line 22) admits line_size == DATA_SIZE (and the whole range [DATA_SIZE-6, DATA_SIZE]); when a scan line's final byte is nonzero, the trim at lines 33-34 leaves end_data at data+DATA_SIZE and `memset(end_data, 0, 7)` (line 45) writes 7 bytes past the DATA_SIZE-byte `data` array (line 10), a stack buffer overflow (CWE-787). The same guard also fails to exclude negative line_size, which leaves further out-of-bounds paths (recorded in limitations).

evidence.reason: line_size (line 19) is constrained only by `if (line_size > DATA_SIZE)` (line 22), whose admitted set includes exactly DATA_SIZE (line 3) and all values down to INT_MIN, so line_size == DATA_SIZE reaches the sink. For raster whose final byte is nonzero (copied at lines 30-31, per-byte domain 0..255; the trim at lines 33-34 decrements only while the trailing byte is 0), end_data stays at data + DATA_SIZE, `end_data == data` (line 35) is false, and the else-branch pad writes data[DATA_SIZE..DATA_SIZE+6] against the line-10 capacity byte data[DATA_SIZE] (indices 0..DATA_SIZE-1) — a 7-byte stack buffer overflow (CWE-787). The line-22 guard cannot protect this sink for any offset in [DATA_SIZE-6, DATA_SIZE]; line_size == DATA_SIZE with a nonzero final byte is the demonstrated witness.

assumptions: Line 10 declares `byte data[DATA_SIZE]`; with `#define DATA_SIZE (LINE_SIZE * 8)` (line 3), valid indices are 0..DATA_SIZE-1.
Line 11 declares `byte plane_data[LINE_SIZE * 3]`; the transpose writes (lines 66-68) reach index (LINE_SIZE-1) + 2*LINE_SIZE = 3*LINE_SIZE-1, i.e. the last element, in bounds.
Lines 30-31 fill the first line_size bytes of data with raster bytes whose values are unconstrained (0..255), which governs the trim at lines 33-34.
The only shown constraint on line_size is line 22 (`> DATA_SIZE` rejected); negative values and the boundary value DATA_SIZE remain in the residual range.
limitations: Negative line_size is not excluded by line 22; a negative library return would make `data + line_size` (line 29) and `memset(end_data,0,7)` (line 45) target memory before data, and lines 87-88 would compute line_size_color_plane ≈ 0x55555555, driving the loop at lines 103-105 and gp_fwrite (lines 107-108) far past plane_data. No shown statement produces a specific negative value (range claim over the int domain), so this class is recorded here rather than as a second verdict.

The primary witness requires the copied scan line's final byte to be nonzero; if it is 0 the trim at lines 33-34 takes the safe path. Nonzero is inside the per-byte residual range but the byte value is not traced to a shown statement, which caps confidence at 0.78.

Return values of gp_fputs/gp_fprintf/gp_fputc/gp_fwrite (lines 14, 74, 78, 93-95, 107-108, 115) and gdev_prn_copy_scan_lines (lines 30-31) are ignored; unchecked printer-I/O or partial-copy failure is a robustness concern, not an attacker-directed failure in this fragment.
Control bytes written to prn_stream are the printer's own command channel by design; no injection boundary (log/header/command/SQL) is demonstrated.
LINE_SIZE is not shown in the fragment; capacities scale with the line-3 macro, and the analysis holds for any positive LINE_SIZE whose compile-time products do not overflow.

verdict.summary: Unconditional NULL-pointer dereferences (CWE-476): cfg_trans is a pointer-typed parameter dereferenced at line 13 (cfg_trans->gen2) with no NULL check anywhere in the fragment, and its base_params member is dereferenced at line 38 with no validation either. NULL in either unconstrained residual range crashes the kernel during iwl_trans_pcie_alloc.

evidence.reason: cfg_trans (declared line 3) is a pointer-typed parameter whose residual range remains its full declared domain because no check or validation statement in the fragment constrains it prior to this first unconditional dereference; the only earlier guard (line 10, if (ret)) constrains ret, not cfg_trans. A NULL caller value, a member of the unconstrained domain, reaches cfg_trans->gen2 at line 13 and dereferences NULL — a confirmed CWE-476 null-pointer dereference; the missing NULL check on the parameter is the defect.

Even when cfg_trans is non-NULL so line 13 passes, the member pointer cfg_trans->base_params is dereferenced at line 38 with no NULL check; no shown statement assigns or validates base_params, so NULL remains in its residual range. NULL base_params is not excluded by any guard between line 13 and line 38 and reaches the dereference — a second confirmed CWE-476 null-pointer dereference sink.

assumptions: trans is non-NULL on every path after the guard at line 20, so IWL_TRANS_GET_PCIE_TRANS(trans) at line 23 and the trans_pcie dereferences operate on a valid object.
snprintf at lines 137-138 is bounded by the explicit capacity sizeof(trans->hw_id_str) and by the fixed 22-character format output, so the PCI-ID write cannot overflow.

Every goto out_no_pci/out_free_ict occurs after the tso_hdr_page allocation at line 31; the alloc-failure path leaves tso_hdr_page NULL, and free_percpu(NULL) is a no-op, so free_percpu at line 179 performs no double-free on any shown path.
limitations: alloc_workqueue at line 165 is unchecked, but within the fragment the returned pointer is only stored and never dereferenced or passed to a security-relevant sink (INIT_WORK at line 166 uses rba.rx_alloc); demoted as a robustness concern.

pcim_iomap_table(pdev)[0] at line 86 could only return NULL through a non-attacker-scaled devres/WARN environment failure, and the [0] element is checked at line 87; demoted under the environment-failure standard.

Line 136 ((pdev->device << 16) + pdev->subsystem_device): for device = 0xffff the promoted-int shift exceeds INT_MAX (undefined/implementation-defined wrap), but the resulting hw_id has no security-relevant consumer in the fragment, so no CWE is attached.

trans_pcie->msix_enabled read at line 145 is not assigned in the fragment; it is plausibly initialized by iwl_pcie_set_interrupt_capa (line 135) or by zeroing in the unshown allocator, so an uninitialized-use verdict is unconfirmable.

pdev is also a pointer-typed parameter dereferenced without a NULL check (line 9); it is treated as OS/framework-provided probe input and is not reported as a separate evidence item to keep the verdict focused on the config-data derefs.

verdict.summary: Copied scan-line bytes in data[0..line_size-1] (populated at lines 34-35) keep their full unsigned-char domain 0..255: the memset (line 15) only zeroes bytes at/after line_size, and the line_size check (line 26) only caps line_size. Any copied byte >= 8 reaches the transpose loop (lines 48-69) and is used as an index into the 8-entry static tables spr40/spr8/spr2 (declared lines 53-55) at lines 58-65, causing an out-of-bounds read of up to 247 bytes past a table (CWE-125).

evidence.reason: Sink is the table index spr40[dp[0]]. dp[0] = data[0 + i]; data bytes below line_size are set by gdev_prn_copy_scan_lines (lines 34-35) and retain the full unsigned-char domain 0..255 because the memset (line 15) covers only bytes >= line_size and the check at line 26 caps only line_size (10 <= DATA_SIZE is admitted). A copied byte of 8 (or up to 255) passes the guards on the path (lines 26, 37-39, 48) and indexes spr40 declared with capacity 8 at line 53, reading at least one element past the table — out-of-bounds read, primary CWE-125. The sibling indexes at lines 59-65 (spr40[dp[1]], spr8[dp[3]], spr2[dp[6]], ...) fail identically with the same unconstrained dp[x].

assumptions: LINE_SIZE is a positive compile-time constant, so DATA_SIZE = LINE_SIZE*8 (line 3) and plane_data has LINE_SIZE*3 bytes (line 11); all capacity arithmetic in the walk is relative to it.
The guard at line 26 admits line_size <= DATA_SIZE, which bounds the copy at lines 34-35 and the data reads in the transpose loop.
limitations: The uninitialized-tail OOB (bytes >= line_size read in the transpose) is neutralized by the memset at line 15 and is not reported.

A hypothetical negative line_size (which would make line_size_color_plane negative and gp_fwrite's length a huge size_t at lines 107-108) has no producing statement in the fragment and is treated as a robustness concern, not a finding.

A device-depth invariant that 'scan bytes are always <= 7' is not visible in the fragment and therefore cannot be used to neutralize the byte-arriving index; per the analysis rules, the residual range stays 0..255.

The return status of gdev_prn_copy_scan_lines (lines 34-35) is discarded; proceeding on a failed copy would consume stale/partial data. This is a robustness/error-handling concern subordinate to the confirmed OOB and is not a separate CWE.

verdict.summary: sug_filltree walks the case-folded trie with an unbounded `depth` that indexes the fixed-size stack arrays `arridx`, `curi`, `tword`, `wordcount` (declarations at lines 6-8 and 13, capacity MAXWLEN). No shown statement caps `depth`; a crafted spell-file trie shaped as a chain of more than MAXWLEN nodes (each descent driven by `byts[n] != 0` at line 56 and `arridx[depth] = idxs[n]` at line 89) drives `depth` past MAXWLEN and causes out-of-bounds stack writes at lines 88-91 (CWE-787) with attacker-controlled bytes/indices. Independently, the byte read `c = byts[n]` at line 56 is never checked against `slang->sl_fbyts_len` (the only visible byts bound, used solely in the NUL-skip loop at line 79), enabling out-of-bounds reads (CWE-125).

evidence.reason: `depth` (started at 0, line 36) is the post-incremented subscript into `tword` declared `char_u tword[MAXWLEN];` (line 8, valid indices 0..MAXWLEN-1). The descent branch is entered for every nonzero `c = byts[n]` (line 56) while line 39 admits `curi <= byts[arridx[depth]]` (count byte chosen as 1). There is no `depth < MAXWLEN` cap between line 36 and this write: line 37 only tests `depth >= 0`. A crafted byts/idxs chain with more than MAXWLEN nodes (each node: count 1 at byts[K], 'a' at byts[K+1], child at idxs[K+1]) makes `old depth == MAXWLEN` at this line, writing `tword[MAXWLEN]` one element past the declared capacity — CWE-787 stack out-of-bounds write with attacker-chosen byte `c`.

On the same descent, `depth` is MAXWLEN+1 when this line stores the file-supplied `idxs[n]` into `arridx` declared `idx_T arridx[MAXWLEN];` (line 6, valid indices 0..MAXWLEN-1). No depth bound exists anywhere before this sink (line 37 checks only `depth >= 0`; line 39's curi-vs-count test is indifferent to depth), so the write at index MAXWLEN+1 is out of bounds — CWE-787.

Same unbounded `depth` (== MAXWLEN+1 on the overflow descent) used to index `curi` declared `int curi[MAXWLEN];` (line 7). The 1 is written past the array's valid index range 0..MAXWLEN-1 — CWE-787, same root cause as line 88.

Same unbounded `depth` (== MAXWLEN+1 on the overflow descent) used to index `wordcount` declared `int wordcount[MAXWLEN];` (line 13). Write at index MAXWLEN+1 exceeds the array's capacity — CWE-787, same root cause as line 88.

`n = arridx[depth] + curi[depth]` (line 53) is derived entirely from trie bytes/indices in `slang` (node count `byts[arridx[depth]] = 0xFF`, `arridx[depth] = sl_fbyts_len - 10` via `idxs[parent]`, `curi = 30`, all admitted by line 39 since `30 <= 255`), giving `n = sl_fbyts_len + 20`. The only visible `byts` length bound is `slang->sl_fbyts_len`, used solely inside the NUL-skip loop at line 79, which does not execute before this read on the descent path. Line 56 therefore reads `byts[n]` past the array's valid range [0, sl_fbyts_len-1] — CWE-125 out-of-bounds read (missing `n < sl_fbyts_len` validation).

assumptions: MAXWLEN is the compile-time size of the stack arrays declared at lines 6-9 and 13; indexing any of them at index MAXWLEN or beyond is out of bounds for any positive MAXWLEN value.
slang->sl_fbyts_len is the valid-length bound of sl_fbyts in the shown code: line 79 reads `n + 1 < slang->sl_fbyts_len` with the comment 'don't go over the end.'
sl_fbyts/sl_fidxs contents (node counts, bytes, child indices) are validated nowhere in the fragment beyond the non-NULL check at lines 29-30, so the trie shape is attacker-chosen.
limitations: NULL dereference of `spin` (line 16) or `slang` (line 27) is not reported: both are internal-helper parameters and no shown statement can produce a NULL value for them.

The return value of `spell_soundfold` (line 61) is discarded, and `tsalword` could be uninitialized if it fails before `tree_add_word` consumes it; the callee contract is not visible in the fragment, so this is not confirmed.

Missing bounds on `idxs` accesses (read at line 89, write at line 42) show the same missing-bound shape but no capacity for `idxs` is visible in the fragment; kept in limitations rather than given its own CWE.
The OOB read via `byts[arridx[depth]]` at line 39 follows the same missing-bound pattern as line 56 but is not given a separate evidence item.
`words_done` is unsigned and passed to a `%d` format at line 96; a format mismatch with no demonstrated security impact.
An empty trie (`byts[0] == 0`) exits cleanly through the ascent at lines 39-46 (`depth` goes to -1), so the degenerate empty-trie input is not a finding.

verdict.summary: Stack buffer overflow in sug_filltree: the case-folded trie is traversed with no bound on depth. File-controlled bytes (byts) and child indexes (idxs) drive 'depth' past MAXWLEN, so lines 87-89 then 86 write arridx/curi/wordcount/tword at index >= MAXWLEN (first OOB index exactly MAXWLEN, capacity declared at lines 6-8 and 13), corrupting stack memory of a malicious spell file. Additionally, file-derived child indexes are dereferenced into byts without a range check (lines 37/54), giving an OOB read against sl_fbyts_len.

evidence.reason: First OOB write of the depth-overflow: after M descents on a file-defined chain of M non-NUL bytes, tword[depth++] sets depth = M = MAXWLEN and this statement writes arridx[M] against the capacity declared at line 6 (idx_T arridx[MAXWLEN], valid 0..MAXWLEN-1). Guards on the path (line 35 depth>=0, line 37 curi[depth] <= byts[arridx[depth]], line 55 c!=0) all admit the witness; no statement bounds depth by MAXWLEN, so index M exceeds the capacity by 1 and grows further with deeper chains. CWE-787 stack OOB write.

tword overflow in the same unbounded-depth walk: a word of at least MAXWLEN+1 file-supplied non-NUL bytes reaches this statement with depth == MAXWLEN, writing tword[MAXWLEN] against char_u tword[MAXWLEN] (line 8), and incrementing depth further (next iterations write indexes MAXWLEN+1, ...). No depth cap exists between the file-controlled flow (lines 54, 87) and this sink. CWE-787.

Same first-overflow iteration as line 87: curi[MAXWLEN] is written when depth reaches MAXWLEN after MAXWLEN non-NUL descents; capacity int curi[MAXWLEN] is declared at line 7. The write is out of bounds by 1 and repeats as depth grows. CWE-787.

Same first-overflow iteration: wordcount[MAXWLEN] is written against int wordcount[MAXWLEN] (capacity line 13) once depth reaches MAXWLEN through the file-controlled chain; index MAXWLEN is out of the valid 0..MAXWLEN-1 range. CWE-787.

Unvalidated file-derived index read: n = arridx[depth] + curi[depth] (line 51), where arridx[depth] for depth>=1 comes from the file value idxs[n] (line 87). A malformed spell file supplies a child index such that n >= slang->sl_fbyts_len (the byte-array length shown by the bound at line 77), and this read then indexes byts past its end; line 37 (byts[arridx[depth]]) has the identical flow. No range check precedes either access in the fragment, so the missing bound on entry-point data is the confirmed defect. CWE-125 OOB read.

assumptions: MAXWLEN is the element count of arridx (line 6), curi (line 7), tword (line 8), tsalword (line 9), and wordcount (line 13); valid indices are 0..MAXWLEN-1.
slang->sl_fbyts has length slang->sl_fbyts_len, as evidenced by the upper bound used at line 77.
The trie layout implied by the code (byts[arridx[depth]] is a child count; child bytes at byts[arridx[depth]+1..]; idxs holds child indexes) is used only to build the witness path.
limitations: OOB accesses to idxs itself (idxs[n] at line 87, idxs[arridx[depth]] at line 40) are not reported because no capacity for slang->sl_fidxs is visible in the fragment (missing-capacity write discipline).
NULL dereference of slang/byts/idxs (lines 27-28, no NULL checks) is a caller-invariant robustness concern, not an attacker-directed finding.
smsg(_("Total number of words: %d"), words_done) (line 94) mismatches %d with an unsigned value; benign and not security-relevant.

The bound at line 77 (n + 1 < slang->sl_fbyts_len) protects only the NUL-skip loop's reads; if this fragment is the patched counterpart of that OOB-read bug, that specific bug is neutralized, but the depth overflow and the unvalidated-index read remain.
Non-termination on a cyclic trie (idxs[n] pointing at an ancestor) is subsumed by the depth-overflow finding and not reported separately (CWE-835).

The depth-overflow witness is a range claim (any word chain of >= MAXWLEN non-NUL bytes), so confidence is calibrated to 0.65; the mechanism and missing guard are fully demonstrated within the fragment.

verdict.summary: Heap buffer overflow in the legacy .gpb pattern path of the brush loader (CWE-787, root cause CWE-190): the sanitizer at lines 47-51 bounds only the 64-bit product (G_MAXSIZE/w/h/b) and by the unshown constant GIMP_MAX_IMAGE_SIZE, while the allocation at line 164 and the loop at lines 166-176 multiply the 32-bit guint32 width/height directly, so admitted dimensions with width*height >= 2^30 wrap 4*width*height to a small/zero allocation and the loop writes up to 4*width*height-1 bytes past it. Independently, temp (line 97) is filled with attacker bytes and never NUL-terminated, yet line 109 passes length -1 (NUL-terminated semantics) to gimp_any_to_utf8, causing a heap OOB read (CWE-170/CWE-125).

evidence.reason: bh.width/bh.height are file-controlled guint32 fields whose only shown upper bound is the unshown constant GIMP_MAX_IMAGE_SIZE (lines 47-48); the line-51 check (G_MAXSIZE / bh.width / bh.height / bh.bytes < 1) bounds only the 64-bit product, so it cannot exclude width*height >= 2^30. The size argument 4 * bh.width * bh.height is computed in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic and wraps to 0 for width*height = 2^30 (e.g., 32768x32768, admissible whenever GIMP_MAX_IMAGE_SIZE >= 32768). The loop at line 166 then writes up to byte offset 4*(width*height)-1 via lines 168/176 into that wrapped-size allocation, a heap-buffer-overflow write (CWE-787) caused by the integer overflow of the allocation-size derivation (CWE-190); no shown statement casts to gsize or bounds width*height below 2^30 between the guard and this sink.

Sink write of the same wrapped-capacity vector: with ph.width == bh.width and ph.height == bh.height (lines 155-156), the loop bound is width*height and the last iteration writes i*4+3 = 4*(width*height)-1 against a brush_buf allocated at line 164 with capacity (4*width*height) mod 2^32, which is 0 (or otherwise < 4*width*height) for width*height >= 2^30. The index/size derivation is attacker-controlled via the header fields and is not bounded by any shown statement (CWE-787; CWE-190 secondary).

temp is allocated with exactly bn_size bytes (line 97, bn_size = header_size - sizeof(BrushHeader), admitted range [1, 2^31-1] by line 95) and filled by read() with attacker-chosen bytes (line 99); no statement appends a NUL terminator (g_new does not zero). The length argument -1 requests NUL-terminated-string semantics (glib convention, e.g. strlen-based scanning in the callee), so on any NUL-free bn_size-byte payload the callee reads past the allocation until a heap zero byte: heap OOB read (CWE-170, improper NUL termination followed by a length-dependent read; equivalently CWE-125). Reachable, e.g., with version=2, magic=GBRUSH_MAGIC, header_size = sizeof(BrushHeader)+1, width=1, height=1, bytes=1, and a 1-byte non-NUL name payload, all passing lines 47-51, 85-86, 95, 99.

assumptions: BrushHeader fields (header_size, version, width, height, bytes, magic_number) are 32-bit unsigned: the fragment normalizes them with g_ntohl (lines 38-44) and prints them via (unsigned long int) casts (lines 56-57); the multiplications at lines 121 and 164 are therefore 32-bit unsigned arithmetic.

GIMP_MAX_IMAGE_SIZE (lines 47-48) is a positive constant whose numeric value is not shown in the fragment; the analysis keeps the width/height admitted range as [1, GIMP_MAX_IMAGE_SIZE] and does not assume a value in either direction.
gimp_any_to_utf8's second parameter is a byte length with -1 meaning NUL-terminated input (glib convention for such *_to_utf8 helpers), so the callee scans up to the first NUL.
G_MAXSIZE is the maximum value of gsize (at least 2^32-1), so line 51 accepts any value whose 64-bit product w*h*bytes is <= G_MAXSIZE and does not bound the 32-bit multiplications at lines 121/164.
The Finding-B witness is fully symbolic (header_size = sizeof(BrushHeader)+1), so the numeric value of sizeof(BrushHeader) is not required; it only requires the sanitizer to admit width=height=1.
limitations: The primary heap-write finding (lines 164/168/176) is a range claim rather than an exact demonstrated witness: the boundary width=height=32768 (width*height = 2^30) is admissible only if the unshown GIMP_MAX_IMAGE_SIZE is >= 32768, and reaching the pattern branch requires the file to supply 1 GiB of brush data plus 3 bytes per pattern pixel (about 4 GiB total). The 32-bit wrap mechanism itself is unambiguous and confirmed by the shown arithmetic.

The same root cause (line 121 wrap for bytes=4) makes the later gimp_pixel_rgn_set_rect call (lines 261-262) read 4*width*height bytes from an undersized brush_buf (CWE-125); it shares the same unshown-constant dependence and is folded into the primary finding's mechanism rather than reported separately.
The case-2 half-float loop (lines 189-205) would also overflow if width*height >= 2^31 (requiring GIMP_MAX_IMAGE_SIZE >= 65536); not confirmable from the fragment, so not reported.

bn_size can reach 2^31-1 (lines 95-97), so g_new can request ~2 GiB on attacker-chosen header_size; allocation failure aborts the process (g_malloc semantics). Reported as a resource/robustness concern, not a separate CWE.

gimp_drawable_get (line 256) is dereferenced at line 258 (drawable->width) without a NULL check; a NULL here would require gimp_layer_new to fail on attacker-scaled dimensions, which depends on library behavior not shown, so it is noted as a robustness concern only.
The discarded lseek() return at line 67 (version-1 rewind) can only misalign subsequent reads, which are themselves checked (lines 99/124/168), so it is not a vulnerability.

verdict.summary: check_termcode writes a NUL via 'tp[len] = NUL;' at index exactly *buflen (or tb_off+tb_len), one byte past the input data it accounts for, and no shown statement bounds *buflen against the buffer capacity parameter 'bufsize' — an unvalidated-size (missing-bound) out-of-bounds write reachable on any matching termleader byte.

evidence.reason: The write index is derived from the helper parameter *buflen: line 54 'len = *buflen - offset;' with line 53 'tp = buf + offset;' makes tp[len] == buf[*buflen], and on the typebuf path lines 46-47 make it typebuf.tb_buf[tb_off + tb_len]. *buflen/tb_len have residual range [1, INT_MAX] (line 51 / line 44 breaks only force len >= 1; no upper bound), and 'bufsize' (line 4) is never compared against *buflen anywhere in the fragment. Lines 61, 75 and 82 are bypassed for an ESC first byte, so line 85 executes, writing one byte past the last data byte the fragment itself manages (buf[0..*buflen-1]) whenever the caller's buffer capacity is <= *buflen — the missing capacity bound is the confirmed defect (unvalidated-size flow, CWE-787).

assumptions: termcodes[], termleader, tc_len, p_cpo, p_ek, State, gui.in_use, T_RBG/T_RFG, check_for_codes, rcs_status are static/global configuration whose len/modlen fields bound termcodes[idx].code[...] reads to the constant table; they are not attacker-controlled in the fragment.
The write at line 85 is required by the fragment's own downstream scans (atoi, getdigits, STRNCMP) which rely on a NUL at tp[len]; the write index itself is never validated against any capacity.
bufsize (line 4) is the only visible capacity-like parameter and is used solely as an argument passed to handle_csi and put_string_in_typebuf; it never appears in any comparison in the fragment.
limitations: The positive verdict is a range claim: the fragment shows the write index equals *buflen exactly but shows no capacity; the overflow materializes for any buffer with capacity <= *buflen, which the fragment neither establishes nor rules out.

string[new_slen++] and mb_char2bytes(string + new_slen) writes: index originates from modifiers2keycode()/mb_char2bytes() whose bodies and return bounds are not shown; 'string' capacity is MAX_KEY_CODE_LEN + 1 (line 19) but the constant's value is not visible — unconfirmable.

GUI scrollbar loops (KS_VER_SCROLLBAR / KS_HOR_SCROLLBAR) read tp[j], tp[j+1], tp[j+2] without a bound against len; they are reachable only in FEAT_GUI builds on GUI-generated event bytes and depend on get_bytes_from_buf/get_long_from_buf semantics not shown — demoted.
atoi((char *)modifiers_start) and getdigits(&nr) reads are bounded by the NUL the fragment itself writes at tp[len]; no additional defect confirmed.
Return expression 'len + new_slen - slen + offset' could overflow int only for *buflen/max_offset near INT_MAX with no attacker-scalable allocation shown — not a finding.

Bodies of handle_csi, handle_osc, handle_dcs, put_string_in_typebuf, check_termcode_mouse are not shown; the arguments this fragment derives (len, argp, offset, bufsize, buflen) are in-domain for the checks present, so their internals cannot be verified.

verdict.summary: squashfs_opendir contains explicit protective guards that bound the two attacker-influenced length/count values before their consuming sinks: dir_count is capped at SQUASHFS_DIR_COUNT (line 64) before the inner entry loop, and dire->size is capped below SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN (line 81) before the name memcpy and NUL write. The destination buffer is deliberately declared one element larger (char buffer[sizeof(squashfs_dir_entry_2) + SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN + 1], line 5), so the maximum admitted copy (SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN bytes) plus the explicit NUL at index SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN fits exactly within capacity. check_name (line 91) further vets name content before the log sink and the strcpy. Residual concerns (reads from directory_table crossing the logical size bound, unchecked read_inode return, strcpy destination capacity) depend on capacities and callee semantics not visible in the fragment and are not confirmable findings.

assumptions: buffer at line 5 is the backing object for dire->name (alias at line 7); dire->name is the trailing member of squashfs_dir_entry_2, giving it at least SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN + 1 bytes of capacity within buffer.
SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN is the same constant used both in the line-5 buffer declaration and the line-81 guard, and SQUASHFS_DIR_COUNT bounds the per-header entry count admitted at line 64.
lookup_entry returns -1 on failure (lines 43-45) and non-negative byte offsets otherwise.

struct dir_ent is assumed to hold names of at least SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN + 1 bytes (its definition is not in the fragment); the strcpy source is bounded to at most SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN+1 bytes including NUL by guards 81 and 88.
limitations: Reads from directory_table at lines 53, 56, 72, 76, and 86 may cross the logical inode-data bound size (line 48) by up to sizeof(dirh)-2 or dire->size bytes, because the bound is only re-tested at the top of the outer loop; whether this is memory-safety relevant depends on the unshown allocation size of directory_table, so the OOB claim cannot be confirmed and is demoted.
The return of read_inode (line 17) is dereferenced without a NULL check (lines 25-29, 32, 41, 47-48); read_inode's failure behavior is outside the fragment, so a NULL-deref cannot be confirmed.

strcpy at line 107 writes into dir->dirs[dir->dir_count].name whose capacity is not visible; the source and index are bounded by shown statements (lines 81-88 and 99-106), so no out-of-domain value is derived at the call site.

malloc/realloc failures at lines 20-21 and 102-104 trigger EXIT_UNSQUASH; these are environment failures not directed by attacker-controlled magnitudes at practical scale and no security operation runs on the failure state.

The int arithmetic on bytes/size (lines 47-48) and the realloc size (lines 100-101) cannot wrap on the entering path because the loop only runs while size <= INT_MAX and terminates when bytes reaches size; a 2GB-scale prerequisite would be required and is not demonstrated.
Potential log injection via TRACE %s at lines 96-98 is neutralized by the check_name gate at line 91, whose exact rejection set is not shown; no injection mechanism is confirmable.

verdict.summary: check_termcode() reads past the available input when a GUI special-key code (CSI <KS_EXTRA> <KE_X1MOUSE> etc.) is matched: the only length guard is `if (len < 3) return -1;`, which admits len == 3, yet `get_bytes_from_buf(tp + slen, bytes, 4)` then reads 4 bytes at tp+3, i.e., up to 4 bytes beyond tp+len. The same missing `len - slen >= count` bound affects the KS_MENU/KS_TABLINE/KS_TABMENU and scrollbar read call sites, all yielding out-of-bounds reads (CWE-125).

evidence.reason: Entry-point terminal input at tp with len admitted as low as 3 (guard `if (len < 3) return -1;` at line 97 admits len==3) reaches the sink with slen=3 (line 99). get_bytes_from_buf reads 4 bytes at tp+3; the available span is tp[0..len-1] established by `tp = buf + offset; len = *buflen - offset;` (lines 53-54) and `if (offset >= *buflen) break;` (line 51). For len==3 the read extends 4 bytes past tp+len. No `len >= slen + 4` bound exists on the path — missing-bound out-of-bounds read, CWE-125. The `num_bytes == -1` check at line 363 fires only after the out-of-range bytes were already read.

KS_MENU branch reads a 4-byte long at tp+slen with only the line-97 guard admitting len==3 (slen==3). get_long_from_buf consumes 4 bytes from tp+3, up to 4 bytes past the declared tp+len span (lines 53-54, 51). No `len - slen >= 4` bound precedes the call — OOB read, CWE-125.

KS_TABLINE branch reads 1 byte at tp+slen; the same line-97 guard admits len==3 == slen, so the byte consumed lies at tp+len and beyond. No `len > slen` bound precedes the call — 1-byte OOB read, CWE-125.

KS_TABMENU branch reads 2 bytes at tp+slen under the same len==3-admitting guard (line 97), consuming bytes at tp+len and tp+len+1. No `len - slen >= 2` bound precedes the call — 2-byte OOB read, CWE-125.

evidence.snippet:
for (i = 0; tp[j] == CSI && tp[j + 1] == KS_VER_SCROLLBAR
						     && tp[j + 2] != NUL; ++i)
evidence.reason: KS_VER_SCROLLBAR loop condition dereferences tp[j+1] and tp[j+2] with no j+2 < len bound; j grows by at least 3 per iteration (j += 3 plus byte counts), so once j reaches len-2 the condition reads past tp+len. The body additionally calls get_long_from_buf(tp + j, &val) (line 491) with no `len - j >= 4` guarantee — OOB reads in the loop condition and body, CWE-125. The identical KS_HOR_SCROLLBAR loop (lines 508-509, 512) shares the defect.

assumptions: *buflen / typebuf.tb_len denote the number of valid input bytes; the fragment itself establishes the in-bounds span as tp..tp+len-1 via `tp = buf + offset; len = *buflen - offset;` (lines 53-54) and `if (offset >= *buflen) break;` (line 51).

get_bytes_from_buf / get_long_from_buf are read helpers with no length parameter, so they cannot themselves enforce a bound visible in the fragment (name-implied semantics: consume count bytes / one long from the given pointer).
termleader contains the first byte of each termcode (e.g., CSI) so the termleader membership check (lines 73-76) is satisfiable on the witness path.
The GUI blocks are compiled in (they are shown verbatim) and `gui.in_use` is true for the GUI path (line 90, line 350).
limitations: Stack-buffer `string[MAX_KEY_CODE_LEN + 1]` writes via `new_slen` (lines 567, 576-591) cannot be confirmed: the write bound of `modifiers2keycode` is not shown, so the headroom after its return is unknowable.

`put_string_in_typebuf(offset, slen, string, new_slen, ...)` (lines 593-594) can receive slen > remaining len on the GUI path (slen 7 vs len 3), but the callee body is not shown and its argument semantics cannot be confirmed.

Negative or oversized `termcodes[idx].len` flowing into STRNCMP (lines 121-122) would require corrupted global table data; on every demonstrated path a first-block STRNCMP match forces break/return before any unsafe read, so no witness passes all guards.
`atoi(modifiers_start)` (line 251) is safe: the digit scan (lines 239-245) limits the numeric run to tp[0..len-1] with the `if (len < j) return -1;` guard at line 243.

`current_menu = (vimmenu_T *)val;` (line 431) casts input-derived bytes to a pointer, but `check_menu_pointer(root_menu, current_menu)` (line 436) validates before use and the callee is not shown; not confirmable as a defect.
`check_termcode_mouse(tp, &slen, ...)` (lines 399-400) receives no length argument and may share the missing-bound family, but its read extent is not shown, so no sink extrapolation is confirmable.
LOG_TR calls (lines 312, 600) use constant format strings only; no log-injection surface is present.
Candidate boundary `len == slen` for the mouse/scrollbar reads is not fragile: any len in [3,6] triggers the confirmed excess, not a single degenerate value.

verdict.summary: e1000_send_packet passes the unvalidated int parameter `size` (declared at line 1, residual range [INT_MIN, INT_MAX] — no check or cap appears in the fragment) as the byte-count argument of qemu_receive_packet/qemu_send_packet at lines 8 and 10, and passes the unvalidated `buf` pointer to inc_tx_bcast_or_mcast_count at line 12. A negative or oversized `size` (e.g. -1, admitted since the only guard at line 7 constrains only s->phy_reg) is out of domain for a byte length and causes an out-of-bounds read of `buf` (CWE-125); `buf` is dereferenced with no NULL check (CWE-476). No protective statement exists between the taint origin and the sinks.

evidence.reason: `size` (line 1, `int`) has residual range [INT_MIN, INT_MAX]: no statement in the fragment constrains it, and the only guard (line 7 `if (s->phy_reg[PHY_CTRL] & MII_CR_LOOPBACK)`) tests only s->phy_reg. Witness `size = -1` passes every guard and reaches this sink as a byte-count argument, which is out of the required domain [0, capacity]. No capacity for `buf` and no lower bound on `size` are visible, so the negative value widens to a huge unsigned length in the callee and reads past the buffer — confirmed missing-bound / unvalidated-size OOB read, CWE-125.

Identical unvalidated-size sink on the loopback branch: the same tainted `size` (residual range [INT_MIN, INT_MAX], unconstrained by any shown check) is forwarded as the byte length of `buf`. A negative member such as -1 is admitted by the guard at line 7 (which depends only on s->phy_reg) and produces an out-of-bounds read of `buf`, CWE-125.

Pointer-typed parameter `buf` is passed here with no NULL or length check anywhere in the fragment (lines 1-14 contain none) and is dereferenced/read by the callee to classify the packet header. `buf == NULL` is a member of the unconstrained residual range and passes every guard on the path (line 7 is independent of `buf`), so a NULL dereference is reachable — independent root cause CWE-476.

assumptions: `size` is declared `int` at line 1, so its full domain is [INT_MIN, INT_MAX] absent any shown constraint.
qemu_receive_packet/qemu_send_packet consume their third argument as the byte length of the buffer, with negative values widening to huge unsigned lengths (standard C int-to-size_t semantics).
PTCregs is declared with exactly 6 elements at lines 3-4; no sentinel element is visible in the fragment.
The only branch guard in the fragment, line 7, constrains only s->phy_reg and admits both arms for any `size`/`buf`.
limitations: No backing capacity for `buf` is visible in the fragment, so the exact read excess cannot be quantified for positive oversized `size`; the primary finding is anchored on the negative-length, missing-bound mechanism.

e1000x_increase_size_stats (line 13) behavior — including whether it walks PTCregs beyond its 6 visible elements looking for a sentinel — is in a callee whose body is not shown; no confirmed finding is derived from it.

Absent NULL checks on `s` (dereferenced at lines 6, 7, 13) and `nc` (line 6) are robustness concerns in the shown fragment; no attacker-directed NULL producer is visible, so they are not reported as findings.
The discarded return statuses of qemu_receive_packet/qemu_send_packet (lines 8, 10) are not consumed by any downstream security-relevant operation in the fragment, so the discards are not findings.
The downstream heap-overflow chain in the loopback receive path (e1000_receive_iov) is outside the fragment and is not asserted as a confirmed mechanism here.

verdict.summary: The Ctrl-U handler (case Ctrl_U, lines 484-498) subtracts the unvalidated global cursor position from the command-line length and then uses the result as an array index: 'ccline.cmdlen -= j' (487) followed by 'ccline.cmdbuff[ccline.cmdlen] = NUL' (492) and the copy loop at 489-490. ccline.cmdpos/ccline.cmdlen are unconstrained on this path (the only relative bounds, at lines 544/566/576, live in other switch branches and never run before the sink), so cmdpos > cmdlen yields a negative index (heap underflow write, CWE-787) via a wrapping signed subtraction (CWE-190), or an unbounded loop/copy whose length has no visible capacity check.

evidence.reason: The loop bound is the value of ccline.cmdlen just recomputed at line 487 as 'ccline.cmdlen -= j' with j = ccline.cmdpos (line 486); neither ccline.cmdpos nor ccline.cmdlen has any shown constraint on the Ctrl-U path (no guard executes between the case entry at 484 and this sink; the relative guards at 544/566/576 belong to other switch branches). Residual range of both is the full int domain, so the bound N = cmdlen - cmdpos can be large positive with negative j start (out-of-bounds reads via cmdbuff[j++] and writes via cmdbuff[i++]) while no capacity for cmdbuff is visible in the fragment — a missing-bound (unvalidated-size) OOB flow, CWE-787 on the write side.

The write index is ccline.cmdlen after the unguarded subtraction at line 487 ('ccline.cmdlen -= j', j = ccline.cmdpos from line 486). ccline.cmdpos and ccline.cmdlen retain their full int residual range on this path: for cmdpos > cmdlen (e.g., L=5, P=100), line 487 yields -95 and this line writes ccline.cmdbuff[-95], a negative-offset (before-buffer) write; the signed subtraction can also wrap (CWE-190). No statement between the case entry (484) and this sink constrains the relationship, so the protective statements at 544/566/576 do not apply here. Confirmed missing-bound OOB write, CWE-787.

assumptions: ccline.cmdlen and ccline.cmdpos are int (per their uses at lines 486-488, 544, 695, 704).
ccline.cmdbuff is non-NULL on the editing-loop path because init_ccline (line 68) either succeeds or exits via 'goto theend' (line 69, comment 'out of memory').

The fragment treats index ccline.cmdlen as a valid NUL-terminator slot (it writes it at line 492), so the K_RIGHT condition read at line 558 (at most index cmdlen) and the Ex-mode read at line 395 (cmdlen-1, guarded by cmdpos > 0 at 394) are in-bounds under that convention; K_LEFT/K_RIGHT reads are otherwise guarded by lines 544, 566 and 576.
safe_vgetc() returns key codes (int); mb_ptr2len/mb_head_off follow their standard name-implied bounded semantics.
limitations: The negative-index precondition (cmdpos > cmdlen) has no producer inside the fragment — it depends on unshown editing helpers (put_on_cmdline, cmdline_erase_chars, cmdline_paste, bracketed_paste, cmdline_browse_history) retaining out-of-range state, so the finding is a residual-range claim rather than an exact shown-code witness; confidence is capped accordingly (0.55).
wim_flags[wim_index] accesses at lines 432 and 437 are demoted: wim_index is modified only inside the unshown cmdline_wildchar_complete (line 419), and the capacity of wim_flags is not visible.

draw_cmdline(ccline.cmdpos, ccline.cmdlen - ccline.cmdpos) at lines 798-799 can receive a negative length for the same unvalidated state, but the consumer semantics are unshown and it is the same root cause, so it is not a separate finding.

A stale-byte/strlen over-read after Ctrl-U is neutralized for the visible consumers (add_to_history at 953, vim_strsave at 958) by the NUL placed at line 492; that line's own index is the vulnerable operation and is reported above.
K_RIGHT (guards at 544 and 558 in-bounds terminator read), K_LEFT (guards at 566 and 576), and the recursion guard (line 71) are protective and not findings.
The K_IGNORE/K_NOP retry loop (224-228) could spin only if the input channel delivers exclusively those keys; not confirmed attacker-scalable in the shown code (no evidence item).
Return values of trigger_cmd_autocmd (151, 909, 980) and bracketed_paste (832) are discarded with no visible security-relevant consequence in the fragment.
IObuff size (876-882) and get_special_key_name's buffer (870) are unshown but the sizes written are helper-bounded (mb_char2bytes contract), not attacker-scaled, so no finding is asserted.

verdict.summary: No confirmed security vulnerability: the only entry-point input c is stored unmodified into the global VIsual_mode (line 8) with no in-fragment consumer, and the single guarded operation coladvance(curwin->w_virtcol) (line 18) consumes editor state refreshed by validate_virtcol() (line 17) immediately before it. The fragment contains no loops, allocations, index/size arithmetic, injection sinks, crypto, or file operations.

assumptions: Ctrl_V, TAB, VE_BLOCK, INVERTED, NUL, and TRUE are compile-time constants; their values do not affect any arithmetic, index, or capacity in the fragment.

Globals (VIsual_mode, VIsual, curwin fields, p_smd, msg_silent, redraw_cmdline, clip_star) are editor state maintained outside the fragment; the fragment only reads or writes them without deriving sizes or capacities.
validate_virtcol() (line 17) is given its strongest reading: it refreshes curwin->w_virtcol for the current cursor before that value is consumed at line 18.
limitations: Parameter c is not validated against an allowed mode set before the store VIsual_mode = c; (line 8); its only in-fragment consumer is the equality test at line 15. Any downstream array/index use of VIsual_mode is outside the fragment, so no sink or impact can be confirmed (no CWE attached).

coladvance(curwin->w_virtcol) (line 18) consumes framework state with no shown capacity bound and no shown derivation of an out-of-domain value; the stale-value concern is addressed by the validate-then-use ordering at lines 17-18.

Unconditional curwin dereferences (lines 4, 18, 20, 42, 44-45) assume the editor window invariant that the current-window pointer is always valid; a NULL here is not attacker-directed within the fragment (robustness concern only).
Returns of validate_virtcol() and coladvance() carry no shown failure semantics, and no operation consumes a failure state, so no error/status-handling flaw is demonstrable.
No loops, size expressions, or pointer arithmetic exist in the fragment, so overflow, OOB-by-index, off-by-one, and non-termination classes are inapplicable.

verdict.summary: In reverse search mode (forward=false, unconstrained in the fragment), the found path at lines 42-43 builds the returned post string as base ptr+size with length count + (size - 1). Because count at 'found' equals the match position p in reverse mode (the loop decrements count per position scanned from the end), the derived region [p+size, 2(p+size)-2] exceeds the haystack extent r_size(op1) whenever p+size >= 2. Exact witness: haystack "ab" (L=2), needle "b" (size=1), match at p=1 -> tail of 1 byte at offset 2, one byte past the end; the returned substring is then read by the interpreter, an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) from attacker-controlled PostScript strings.

evidence.reason: Sink: the tail length is derived from entry-point inputs size (line 5) and count (line 18) plus the unconstrained helper parameter forward (line 1). With forward=false, breakdown of the do/while accounting (lines 26-31) shows count at 'found' equals the reverse match position p, so the length is p+size-1 with base ptr+size at line 42. The visible capacity is the haystack length r_size(op1) = L (lines 14, 18). For the admitted-guard witness L=2, size=1, p=1 (haystack "ab", needle "b", reverse), line 14 admits size<=L, line 20 admits size!=0, line 27 admits the match; the described region is base[2..2], one byte past base[0..1]. Any consumer reading the returned substring performs an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125); line 43's size is the confirmed out-of-domain derivation.

assumptions: The haystack string's extent (capacity for bounds purposes) is r_size(op1) = L, visible at lines 14 and 18; valid bytes are base[0..L-1].
The needle's extent is r_size(op) = size (line 5), so pat[0] (line 25) and memcmp(ptr, pat, size) (line 27) read within the needle.
r_size and r_set_size manipulate the string length field of the ref; the returned descriptor is consumed by the interpreter as a string with that length.
limitations: A second trigger of the same sink: size==0 with forward=false and count==0 (empty haystack admitted by line 14) makes size-1 wrap to 0xFFFFFFFF (uint, line 43), producing a ~4 GiB tail descriptor via unsigned wrap; this is the same CWE-125 mechanism, not a separate CWE.
The scan loop itself is in bounds (forward last position base+count reads to base+L-1; reverse descends only to base; no dereference of ptr after loop exit on the no-match path).
The forward-mode tail length (count = L-size-p at found) is correct and in bounds; the flaw is specific to reverse mode.
The return status of push(2) (line 39) and check_read_type (lines 12-13) are not security decisions visible in the fragment; operand-stack overflow handling is outside the shown code.

The actual out-of-bounds read occurs when the returned post substring is consumed by later string operations; that consumer is not in the fragment, but the out-of-domain size derivation is fully confirmed by the shown arithmetic at lines 42-43.

verdict.summary: add_mtab writes the entry-point strings devname, mountpoint, and fstype verbatim into the privileged mtab file via addmntent (line 87) with no validation or sanitization in the fragment; embedded newlines or whitespace terminate/corrupt the record and inject forged mtab entries into a file parsed with trust by other privileged tools (CWE-74).

evidence.reason: Injection sink: struct mntent fields are assigned verbatim from unconstrained entry-point inputs at lines 59-61 (mnt_fsname=devname, mnt_dir=mountpoint, mnt_type=fstype) and written to the privileged file opened at line 51 (setmntent(MOUNTED, "a+")). No shown statement between lines 1 and 87 validates, sanitizes, escapes, or caps these strings, so their residual range is the full C-string domain. A witness such as devname="tmp\n/tmp fake ext2 defaults 0 0" is a member of every guard's admitted set on the normal success path (rc checks at 21/28/34/40/45, non-NULL checks at 52/63 all pass) and reaches the sink, where the embedded newline terminates the legitimate record and injects a forged mtab entry consumed with trust by downstream mount/umount tooling — CWE-74 improper neutralization of special elements in output used by a downstream component.

assumptions: addmntent writes the mntent fields verbatim as a whitespace-separated, newline-terminated record without escaping (standard <mntent.h> semantics implied by the call name and struct type).
MTAB_OPTIONS_LEN is an opaque positive size; strlcat (lines 65-82) bounds every write into mnt_opts regardless of its value, so the options buffer is not an overflow sink.

The function executes in a privileged context (setreuid to effective uid at line 20, toggle_dac_capability at line 39, append-write to MOUNTED at line 51), making the mtab content a privileged, security-sensitive output.
limitations: calloc failure at line 62 would pass a NULL mnt_opts into addmntent at line 87; failure of a fixed-size small allocation is not attacker-directed and no security-relevant operation is shown running on that failure state — robustness concern, not a finding (no CWE).

atexit(unlock_mtab) at line 43 is registered before lock_mtab() at line 44; on the lock-failure path (lines 45-49) the exit handler may run on a never-acquired lock, but the effect depends on the unshown unlock_mtab implementation — no demonstrated security impact (no CWE).
Unchecked endmntent (line 92) and mask-restore sigprocmask (line 97) are cleanup calls with no security-relevant operation on their failure states (no CWE).
strlcat of a long username (lines 80-82) can only truncate within MTAB_OPTIONS_LEN; newline/whitespace inside getusername output was not relied on for the primary finding.

The exploit leverage of a forged mtab entry on downstream consumers (e.g., mount -a/umount behavior) is outside the fragment; only the injection write itself is confirmed here, which is why severity is capped at medium.

verdict.summary: Header index u flows into fm->hdf[u] (line 6) and fm->hd[u] (lines 8, 11) with no bounds check against any visible capacity, so the entire unsigned domain 0..4294967295 is admitted and any u at or beyond the array sizes triggers an out-of-bounds read (missing-bound/unvalidated-index flow, CWE-125). The line-9 NULL guard protects only strchr's result and the line-12 guard only f, and the line-6 guard tests a flag bit, not an index bound.

evidence.reason: u is an unsigned parameter (line 1) with residual range 0..4294967295: no comparison, cast, or capacity check in the fragment constrains it, and no capacity for fm->hdf is declared or derived in the shown code. The guard tests the HDF_FILTER bit and does not bound u, so reading fm->hdf[u] is an out-of-bounds read for any u at or beyond the array's (unshown) size; this is the missing bound on an input-derived index (CWE-125).

The same unconstrained u from line 1 indexes fm->hd[u].b, producing an out-of-bounds read of the hd array before the value is scanned by strchr (sink). The line-9 guard (e == NULL) executes after this read and only excludes a NULL strchr result; it cannot bound the index that produced the read. An index value of any magnitude in 0..4294967295 passes every guard on the path (lines 6, 9, 12) since none of them tests u against a capacity, confirming the out-of-bounds read (CWE-125).

assumptions: fm->hdf and fm->hd are array members indexed by u (the [] syntax in the fragment implies this), and no capacity for either is visible in the fragment.
HDF_FILTER is a bit flag constant; the exact flag arithmetic is not security-relevant to this finding.
The fragment is analyzed as the complete function body for the missing-bound standard; capacities or caller-side checks outside the fragment are excluded by the analysis rules.
limitations: The finding is a missing-bound flow: the exact array sizes of hdf/hd are not shown, so the witness is a range claim (any u >= actual array size) rather than a single demonstrated boundary; confidence is calibrated to 0.62 accordingly.

Dereferencing fm at line 6 without a NULL check is a separate NULL-deref candidate (CWE-476) under the pointer-parameter rule, but it is a caller-contract robustness concern and is not counted as a second CWE.
strchr overrunning fm->hd[u].b would require the .b string to be unterminated, which cannot be confirmed from the fragment (no termination invariant or capacity visible); not reported.
The internals of http_hdr_flags are not shown; its arguments at the call site (line 11) are both derived from fm->hd[u].b and therefore in-domain with respect to each other.

verdict.summary: add_mtab is the patched variant: every dangerous operation is covered by a visible protective statement that executes before the sink. mountent.mnt_opts is allocated with capacity MTAB_OPTIONS_LEN (line 79) and every strlcat (lines 82-99) passes the identical MTAB_OPTIONS_LEN size and sits inside the `if (mountent.mnt_opts)` guard (line 80), excluding the NULL calloc result; mount_user is null-guarded (line 96). fileno() is checked before fstat/ftruncate (line 60), setmntent() NULL before addmntent (line 52), fstat() failure before statbuf use (line 68), and all security-relevant status returns are checked. No confirmed vulnerability.

assumptions: MTAB_OPTIONS_LEN is used identically as the calloc allocation size (line 79) and as every strlcat destination-size argument (lines 82-99), so the destination capacity exactly equals the size bound each strlcat enforces; the constant's numeric value need not be shown.
MOUNTED, EX_FILEIO, and the MS_* flags are external constants/symbols; only their identities and bit-test semantics are relied on.
getusername() returns either NULL or a NUL-terminated username string; the fragment relies only on nullness at line 96.
limitations: devname/mountpoint/fstype flow unsanitized into addmntent (line 104); the fragment's sink inventory does not classify structured-file record writes (mtab) as an injection sink and no downstream consumer is shown, so this is a demoted hypothesis without a CWE.

If calloc (line 79) fails, mnt_opts stays NULL for addmntent; the failure is not attacker-directed (constant size) and glibc-style addmntent handling of NULL mnt_opts is assumed, so this is a robustness concern only.
ftruncate's return is ignored (line 107); it is best-effort rollback and no security-relevant operation runs on its failure.

atexit(unlock_mtab) (line 43) combined with the explicit unlock_mtab (line 115 / error paths) can double-unlock at process exit; the lock is advisory and the sequence is not attacker-controlled, so it is a robustness concern only.

If getusername(uid) returned a string containing newline/space/comma, that content would reach the mtab record; strlcat (lines 98-99) still bounds the memory write, and the residual effect falls under the demoted injection class above.

verdict.summary: Not vulnerable. The only input-derived dangerous length, snprintf's would-be length mflen (line 42, residual range [0, INT_MAX]), is capped at the sink by the ternary clamp at line 65 to sizeof(mfn)-1 = MAXPATHLEN-1, which never exceeds the char mfn[MAXPATHLEN] buffer declared at line 34; every admitted value produces an in-bounds estrndup copy. Other concerns (efree of the stack buffer at line 59, mlen overflow, loop progress in unshown set_text_binary) are not reachable or not confirmable from the shown code.

assumptions: char mfn[MAXPATHLEN] at line 34 is the capacity of mfn, so sizeof(mfn) == MAXPATHLEN.
snprintf returns the would-be length excluding the NUL and NUL-terminates the destination when size > 0 (C standard), so strlen(mfn) <= MAXPATHLEN-1.
estrndup copies at most n bytes and appends a NUL (standard PHP/Zend helper semantics).
php_stream_readdir fills d.d_name as a NUL-terminated entry name and returns NULL at end of directory (library invariant).
Coalescing/parsing helpers load_1, set_text_binary, coalesce_entries, magic_entry_free, set_last_default behave per their standard names; their bodies are not shown.
limitations: Line 59 calls efree() on the STACK array mfn (declared line 34) — an invalid free — but it is reachable only when erealloc at lines 56-57 returns NULL (environmental OOM), which the shown code cannot deterministically produce; no concrete witness, no CWE assigned.
maxfiles/mlen arithmetic at lines 54-55 can overflow only after roughly 2^63 growth steps (an unrealizable number of directory entries); not a confirmed integer-overflow finding.
qsort with files == 0 and filearr == NULL at line 68 (empty directory) has nmemb == 0, so no elements are compared; not a confirmed issue.

Potential NULL dereferences of ms (line 16) or of a NULL result from estrndup stored at line 65 and passed to load_1 at line 70 require OOM or an API-contract violation and depend on unshown load_1; robustness concern only.
Non-termination of the loop at lines 81-86 cannot be confirmed because it depends on progress guarantees of the unshown set_text_binary and on mset[j].count populated by the unshown load_1.
NUL-termination of fn (line 42/75) and d.d_name (line 42) is assumed from caller/library contracts not visible in the fragment.
The FIXME comment at lines 30-31 about non-deterministic sort order is a determinism note, not a security finding.

verdict.summary: OOB read of the directory table: the inode field (*i)->data (unvalidated, entry-point data decoded from the archive) sets size at line 48, and the parse loop reads directory_table + bytes (lines 53/56/72/76/86) for any bytes < size with no visible bound tying size or bytes to the actual directory_table allocation; a crafted image with a large data field drives reads up to ~2^31-1 past the advertised region. The classic dire->name write overflow is separately guarded by the line 81 size check plus the line 5 +1 capacity.

evidence.reason: Read sink: source index `bytes` is advanced from `lookup_entry` (42) plus unvalidated `(*i)->offset` (47), and the sweep endpoint is `size = (*i)->data + bytes` (48) where `(*i)->data` is decoded from the attacker-controlled archive and never validated.
