Guard 21 ('argv[arg_start][0] == ':'') guarantees argv[arg_start] has length >= 1, keeping 'argv[arg_start] + 1' (line 24) inside the token or at its NUL.
limitations: The CWE-190 witness is a range claim: strings of length >= 2^31 - 2 are not produced by any shown statement; any real-world message-size cap lives outside the fragment, which caps confidence at 0.52. Within the fragment the corrupted length bounds both the malloc size and the snprintf limit, so no overflow write is demonstrated.

Unchecked use of the return of irc_msgbuffer_get_target_buffer (lines 79-80) as the target of weechat_printf_date_tags (line 78) could be a NULL dereference, but a NULL result is not shown to be attacker-directed (arguments are constants plus the framework 'server'), so it is a robustness concern, not a confirmed finding.

'argv[arg_start + 1] + 1' (line 30) would be a one-past-end read only if that token were empty; the fragment contains no statement deriving an empty token (the tokenizer is outside the fragment), so the degenerate witness is rejected.

Log/terminal-format injection through the %s arguments of weechat_printf_date_tags (lines 97-101) would require CR/LF or control bytes inside IRC message tokens; the CR/LF-free framing invariant is not visible in the fragment, so it is not confirmable.

All argv/argv_eol index guards (lines 20, 24, 25, 30, 31) and NULL checks (lines 36-37, 40, 44, 53, 60-61, 62, 64, 76) were audited and admit no out-of-bounds index or known NULL dereference on any path.

verdict.summary: btrfs_rm_device computes `num_devices - 1` (line 14) from the unconstrained u64 return of btrfs_num_devices (line 12) with no zero/minimum check. When the count is 0 the subtraction wraps to 18446744073709551615 and is passed as the remaining-device count to btrfs_check_raid_min_devices, corrupting the RAID minimum-device validation gate (CWE-190: unsigned underflow feeding a count/validation sink). The `if (ret)` guard at line 15 executes after the helper call, checks the helper's return status, and cannot constrain the wrapped argument, so no protective statement covers the subtraction. Gating return statuses are checked in the fragment: btrfs_check_raid_min_devices (line 15), btrfs_shrink_device (line 60), btrfs_rm_dev_item (line 67); discarded statuses (btrfs_scrub_cancel_dev line 71, btrfs_assign_next_active_device line 93, btrfs_sysfs_remove_device line 98, btrfs_scratch_superblocks line 109, btrfs_close_bdev line 112) are not followed in the fragment by an operation running on a failure state.

`num_devices = btrfs_super_num_devices(fs_info->super_copy) - 1` (line 101) can equally wrap to 18446744073709551615 and be stored by btrfs_set_super_num_devices (line 102), but that store requires a completed device removal while the superblock count is 0 — a degenerate value not established by any shown statement; demoted (same missing-bound class, weaker reachability).

The fragment contains no loop constructs, so the Loop phase is vacuous; no iteration-bound or termination claim is made.

verdict.summary: Not vulnerable. The guard at lines 77-81 caps every assembled line at TEMP_BUF_SIZE - 1 data bytes (admitted set 1..TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1, excluded >= TEMP_BUF_SIZE), and the LOCAL_ARRAY declarations at lines 6-7 reserve one extra element for the terminator, so the write `line[llen + 1] = '\0'` at line 99 reaches at most index TEMP_BUF_SIZE, which is inside the array. All other dangerous-looking operations (memcpy into gopherState->buf, atoi(strtok(...)), snprintf into tmpbuf) are covered by visible bounds or by the `if (!result) break;` guards at lines 276-277 and 302-303.

This boundary is absorbed only by the +1 capacity; if semantic knowledge of LOCAL_ARRAY is excluded, that path is an off-by-one finding.

The gopherState->buf allocation size is not shown; the write at line 86 is reported safe only because the guard at lines 77-81 supplies a visible TEMP_BUF_SIZE bound (a missing-bound flow would require NO visible bound).

host and port are inserted raw into href attributes at lines 229-234, 241-242 and 248-249 (no html_quote/rfc1738 escaping), so a malicious gopher response could break out of the attribute (CWE-79 mechanism); demoted because the page origin is the gopher server the client chose to browse, which already fully controls that origin's content, so no additional security boundary is crossed.
atoi(strtok(...)) NULL dereference (lines 279, 281, 305) is not reachable: if s_code/s_recno is NULL, result is necessarily NULL and `if (!result) break;` at lines 276-277 / 302-303 executes first.

verdict.summary: SparseFillEmptyRowsOpImpl validates only tensor shape-types and that dense_shape_t has at least one element (lines 19-41), leaving the coordinate values of indices_t, the dimension values of dense_shape_t, and the rank/count relationships between indices, values, and dense_shape completely unconstrained. These entry-point tensors are passed unmodified into the SparseFillEmptyRows functor (lines 44-47), which by name and signature writes values into a dense output sized from dense_shape at positions given by indices; an admitted input such as dense_shape={1}, indices={{7}} yields an out-of-bounds write. The TODO at lines 37-38 confirms the missing cross-validation.

evidence.snippet:
OP_REQUIRES_OK_ASYNC(context,
                       FunctorType()(context, default_value_t, indices_t,
                                     values_t, dense_shape_t, done),
                       done);
evidence.reason: The sink receives indices_t and dense_shape_t whose element payloads are entry-point inputs with unconstrained residual ranges: the guard at lines 24-27 admits any [N, rank] matrix with arbitrary coordinates (full Tindex domain), the guard at lines 19-23 admits any rank-1 dense_shape, and the guard at lines 39-41 only requires the vector length to be non-zero (it does not bound any dimension value). No shown statement bounds a coordinate to [0, dim) of the matching dense dimension, nor ties indices columns to dense rank or values count to index rows, as the TODO at lines 37-38 acknowledges. A witness passing every prior guard (lines 19-41) - dense_shape={1}, indices={{7}} - delivers an index coordinate of 7 to a functor that, by its name and arguments, writes into a dense output of shape dense_shape (1 element), producing an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) via the missing-bound/unvalidated-size flow.

assumptions: context->input(k) at lines 14-17 returns operator-supplied tensors whose element values are externally controllable (entry-point class); the fragment itself places no constraint on those values.
FunctorType() (lines 43-47), by its name 'SparseFillEmptyRows' and its parameters, consumes indices_t as coordinates and dense_shape_t as the shape of a dense output it writes into.
dense_shape_t.NumElements() at line 39 is the vector length (rank), not the product of the dimensions; the check only excludes rank 0.
The guards at lines 19-41 execute before the sink at lines 44-47 on every path (ordering verified).
limitations: The exact out-of-bounds arithmetic and the failing memory operation occur inside the unshown functor body; the write direction is inferred from name-implied fill semantics, which caps confidence at 0.62.
The witness coordinate (e.g. 7 for dense_shape={1}) is a residual-range value (any Tindex >= the dimension is admitted), not a constant whose magnitude is derived from a shown statement.
The rank-mismatch (indices columns vs dense_shape length) and count-mismatch (values length vs indices rows) gaps are part of the same missing-validation flow and are not assigned a separate CWE.
A claim that the functor is safe because it validates internally would rely on an unshown protective statement and is therefore excluded from the verdict.

The missing rank-consistency and dtype checks acknowledged by the TODO at lines 43-44 are real validation gaps, but their failure occurs inside the unshown functor body and cannot be confirmed from this fragment.

verdict.summary: SampleInterleavedLSScan::ParseMCU writes into the fixed-size local arrays `struct Line *line[4]` (line 4) and `LONG *lp[4]` (line 24) using `m_ucCount` (UBYTE, residual range 0..255) as the loop bound; the only guard is the debug-only `assert(m_ucCount < 4)` at line 15, which does not exist in release (NDEBUG) builds. `m_ucCount = 5` passes the loop guard `cx < m_ucCount` at cx = 4 and overwrites `line[4]`/`lp[4]`, which are then dereferenced at lines 26/55/79, producing a stack out-of-bounds write (CWE-787).

evidence.reason: `cx` is UBYTE (0..255) and the loop at line 18 admits `cx < m_ucCount` with `m_ucCount` residual 0..255 (the only shown guard, `assert(m_ucCount < 4)` at line 15, is a debug-only macro and is absent in NDEBUG builds). With `m_ucCount = 5`, iteration cx = 4 is admitted (4 < 5) and writes `line[4]`, past the 4-element array declared at line 4 (`struct Line *line[4]`, capacity indices 0..3). This is a stack out-of-bounds write; the overwritten slot is subsequently dereferenced at line 26 (`lp[cx] = line[cx]->m_pData;`) and at the write sinks lines 45/55/79 (`*lp[cx]++`).

Same admitted index as evidence 1: for `m_ucCount = 5`, cx = 4 writes `lp[4]`, past `LONG *lp[4]` declared at line 24 (capacity indices 0..3); the clobbered entry is dereferenced by `*lp[cx]++` at lines 45/55/79, turning the stack overflow into an out-of-bounds write through a corrupted pointer (CWE-787).

Write sink inside `while (run)` (line 41): the iteration count `run` is the unreserved return of `DecodeRun(length, m_lRunIndex[0])` (line 39) and the fragment shows no statement bounding `run` against the line capacity, and no capacity for the `m_pData` buffers is visible; for any `run > length` (admitted residual range), the writes continue until `run == 0` while `length` underflows past -1 and the line-65 `break` fires only after all samples were written — unvalidated-size flow into the same sink. Additionally, with `m_ucCount >= 5` the index `cx` is already out of range for `lp[4]` per evidence 1/2. Confidence for the unanchored `run` magnitude is lower than for the m_ucCount overflow; the m_ucCount-driven overflow is the confirmed primary mechanism.

assumptions: `line` declared at line 4 as `struct Line *line[4]` and `lp` declared at line 24 as `LONG *lp[4]` have exactly 4 elements (indices 0..3).
`m_ucCount` is declared with the UBYTE domain 0..255; no runtime inequality other than the line 15 `assert` appears in the fragment.
`assert` uses standard C++ NDEBUG semantics (no effect in release builds).

`run` (line 39) is a decoded stream value; `DecodeRun`'s body and the `m_pData` buffer capacities are not part of the fragment, so the exact excess of the run-driven overflow cannot be computed from the shown code.
limitations: Candidate NULL dereference (CWE-476) on `line[cx]->m_pNext` (line 93) / `line[cx]->m_pData` (line 26) would require the line chain to hold fewer entries than `lines` (up to 8, including the DNL branch at line 9 when `m_ulRemaining[0] == 0`); no chain capacity/length statement is shown in the fragment, so the NULL producer is not derivable from the shown code — placed in limitations.

Candidate `preshift` shift overflow (`rx << preshift`, lines 45/55/79 with `preshift = m_ucLowBit + FractionalColorBitsOf()` at line 4) is possible only for total bit depth >= 32, whose reachability is not shown in the fragment — not confirmed.

Candidate begin-read error handling (`BeginReadMCU` returning false, line 28): no security-relevant sink was shown to consume the failure state (the code only skips the decode block and still advances lines), so it is a robustness concern, not a confirmed flaw.

The exact magnitude of the run-driven overflow (evidence 3) cannot be anchored without `DecodeRun`'s body or the line-buffer capacity; the confirmed, fully anchored mechanism is the `m_ucCount`-indexed overflow of `line[4]`/`lp[4]`.

verdict.summary: The ELF parser maps an attacker-controlled file as exactly st.st_size bytes (line 23) and then dereferences unvalidated, file-supplied offsets, indices, and counts. shdr[e_shstrndx] (line 177) can read ~2.6 MB past the mapping (e_shstrndx=0xFFFF, small file); unvalidated sh_name/sh_offset pointers feed unbounded strlen/printf %s/strcmp reads (253/321/334/362); uninitialized dynamic/dynstr (329-330) index shdr (344); and the unvalidated sh_size-derived dyn loop (345/349/352) reads past the mapping. All result in out-of-bounds reads (CWE-125), with the uninitialized index as an independent root cause (CWE-457).

evidence.reason: e_shstrndx (Elf32_Half, 0..65535) and e_shoff (Elf32_Off, 0..2^32-1) are attacker-controlled file fields with no constraint in the fragment; the only capacity is the mapping of st.st_size bytes (line 23). Witness: 52-byte ELFCLASS32 file, e_shoff=0, e_shstrndx=65535; shdr=(Elf32_Shdr *)elf_map (line 175) makes shdr[65535] read the 40 bytes at byte 2,621,400, beyond the 52-byte map, because no check e_shstrndx < e_shnum (or any offset/size check) executes before line 177. Guards at lines 13, 18, 24 and the MODE branch at line 30 all admit the input. Confirmed OOB read, CWE-125.

ehdr = (Elf32_Ehdr *)elf_map (line 33) is dereferenced without any check that st.st_size >= sizeof(Elf32_Ehdr). st.st_size (fstat, lines 18-21) retains its full positive domain (0 is blocked only by mmap failing at 24). A file smaller than 18 bytes whose contents yield MODE==ELFCLASS32 (branch 30 admits ELFCLASS32 with no size link) reads e_type at byte 16 past the mapping end. Missing minimum-size validation; CWE-125 (range witness, not an exact value).

name is derived at line 182 as elf_map + shstrtab.sh_offset + shdr[i].sh_name with both addends unvalidated 32-bit attack data (shstrtab itself came from the unvalidated read at line 177); the pointer may land at or beyond the st.st_size-byte mapping (line 23). strlen(name) scans until NUL with no NUL guaranteed inside the map, so an attacker who places non-NUL bytes at the map end forces an unbounded OOB read; the same unvalidated pointer is consumed by printf(" %s", name) at 321, strcmp at 334, and snprintf(...,"Shared library: [%s]", name) at 362. CWE-125.

dynamic is declared at line 330 without initialization and is assigned only when the loop at 332-340 finds a section named ".dynamic" (line 337-339); dynstr (329) likewise only for ".dynstr" (334-336). If the attacker names sections so neither matches (e.g., ".text"), both variables stay indeterminate and shdr[dynamic] indexes the section table with that indeterminate value, producing a wild OOB read (and sh_size is then used at 345; shdr[dynstr] at 361). No check that the names were found precedes line 344. Uninitialized use, CWE-457, with OOB-read consequence.

count = shdr[dynamic].sh_size / sizeof(Elf32_Dyn) (line 345) derives from attacker-controlled sh_size (Elf32_Word, up to 2^32-1, i.e. up to 536,870,911 entries) and sh_offset is unvalidated; the loop at line 349 iterates i < count and dyn[i] reads 8 bytes at sh_offset + i*8 with no check that sh_offset + count*8 <= st.st_size (line 23). For a small map (e.g., 52 bytes) and sh_offset=0, indices >= 7 already read past the end and the loop continues far beyond the mapping. OOB read, CWE-125.

assumptions: ELF type widths and structure sizes follow from the declared types used in the fragment: Elf32_Half is 16-bit unsigned (0..65535), Elf32_Off/Word/Addr are 32-bit unsigned (0..2^32-1), Elf32_Ehdr=52 bytes, Elf32_Shdr=40 bytes, Elf32_Phdr=32 bytes, Elf32_Dyn=8 bytes.
The only visible capacity for all file-derived pointers is the mapping length st.st_size at line 23.
MODE is produced only by get_elf_class(elf) at line 10 and consumed only by the branch comparisons at lines 30 and 676; the fragment imposes no constraint linking MODE to file size.
limitations: Candidate B (header read without minimum-size check) is a residual-range claim because the exact minimum file size that yields MODE==ELFCLASS32 depends on the unshown get_elf_class; it is confirmed as a missing-bound flow but not as an exact-value witness.
The 64-bit branch (line 676 onward) duplicates every 32-bit sink at an approximate +646 line offset; evidence is anchored to the 32-bit occurrences only.

Integer wrap in shdr[j].sh_addr + shdr[j].sh_size and phdr[i].p_vaddr + phdr[i].p_memsz (line 319) can flip the guard, but its only downstream effect is printing the already-unvalidated name pointer; no independent security consequence, so it is not a confirmed finding.

The machine-type switch at line 62 reads ehdr->e_type instead of e_machine (display-only logic bug), and default branches of the sh_type/p_type switches leave tmp stale (output spoofing only); neither is a security finding.

strcpy(&name[15-6], "[...]") at line 254 is bounded by the strlen(name) > 15 guard (writes 6 bytes within the first 16 bytes of a writable mapping) and strcpy(flag, "   ") at line 256 exactly fills flag[4]; they are not independent write findings - the flaw is the upstream strlen read of an unvalidated pointer.
No cryptographic, command-injection, format-string (all formats are literals), or temp-file sinks exist in the fragment.

verdict.summary: Unvalidated signed tensor index is converted to std::size_t at line 7; any negative int becomes a huge size_t value that is passed to buf->Peek at line 9 with no range check, enabling an out-of-bounds read of the staged buffer (signed-to-unsigned conversion / missing index bound).

evidence.reason: The index argument originates from entry-point input ctx->input(0).scalar<int>()() (line 7), declared int with full domain [-2^31, 2^31-1] and no shown constraint. Storing it into std::size_t flips signedness: e.g. -1 becomes 2^64-1, so the residual range reaching this call is [0,2^31-1] union [2^64-2^31, 2^64-1]. No guard between line 7 and line 9 validates sign or upper bound; the OP_REQUIRES_OK at line 9 only checks Peek's return status after the call and cannot prevent an out-of-bounds read inside Peek when the huge index is consumed as a buffer index. Witness: scalar -1 -> index = 2^64-1 -> Peek(2^64-1, &tuple) executes at line 9. Primary CWE-195: signed-to-unsigned conversion of a negative value into a huge index consumed by a security-relevant index sink.

assumptions: size_t is 64-bit on the target platform, so (size_t)(-1) == 2^64-1.
Buffer::Peek's first parameter is consumed as an index into the staged buffer (name-implied semantics and the shown call site).
Buffer::Tuple::size() returns the number of tensors in the peeked entry and num_outputs() is the framework-provided output count.
limitations: Buffer::Peek's body is not shown; if it bounds-checks index internally it would return an error and the OP_REQUIRES_OK at line 9 would abort the op. The finding rests on the fact that the shown code itself provides no bound for index (missing-bound flow).

The loop at lines 16-18 is safe: the equality guard at line 12 admits only tuple.size() == num_outputs(), and i < tuple.size() keeps both tuple[i] and set_output(i, ...) in-domain; no CWE is attached to it.
Validation that input(0) is a scalar tensor (shape check before scalar<int>()) is not shown in the fragment and was not used in the verdict.

verdict.summary: The `publish` fragment builds a segment view with `topic.substr(start, stop - start)` (line 6) using the unconstrained `size_t start` parameter. Nothing in the shown code bounds `start` against `topic.size()` (the loop guard at line 4 tests only `stop`), so for any admitted entry with `stop != npos` and `start > topic.size()`, `topic.find` returns `npos` and `substr` is called with `pos > size()`, creating a view far past the buffer that is later read by `iterator->children.find(segment)` at line 40 — a confirmed out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). Additionally, the `Topic *iterator` parameter is dereferenced at lines 20 and 50 with no NULL check (CWE-476).

evidence.reason: `start` is a `size_t` parameter (line 1) whose residual range is unconstrained: the only guard before this sink, `for (; stop != std::string::npos; ...)` at line 4, tests `stop` and never `start`. For the admitted input `stop = 0` with `start > topic.size()` (e.g., `start = S+1` for a topic of length `S`), `topic.find('/', start)` at line 5 returns `npos`, so `stop - start` becomes `npos - start` and `topic.substr` is invoked with `pos > size()`, violating the C++17 `std::string_view::substr` precondition. The resulting view `(data()+start, huge)` points beyond the buffer, and the lexicographic comparison inside `iterator->children.find(segment)` at line 40 reads out of bounds. The wildcard guard at line 13 admits only length-1 segments and does not fire for the huge length. This is an OOB read (CWE-125, primary), driven by the missing bound on `start`.

`iterator` is a `Topic *` parameter (line 1) dereferenced unconditionally here on the loop path (for any `stop != npos` admitted by line 4). No statement in the fragment NULL-checks `iterator` before this line or on the loop-skipped path leading to line 50. The full pointer parameter domain (including NULL) is the residual range, so `iterator = NULL` reaches this dereference — a confirmed NULL-pointer dereference (CWE-476, secondary).

When the initial `stop == std::string::npos`, the loop at line 4 is skipped and this statement dereferences the unvalidated `Topic *iterator` parameter directly; when the loop runs, the possibly-`NULL` parameter is dereferenced earlier at line 20, then reassigned only from the map at line 46. There is no NULL check anywhere in the fragment, and NULL is a member of the parameter's declared pointer domain, so this unconditional dereference confirms CWE-476 as a second sink statement.

assumptions: C++17 `std::string_view::substr(pos, count)` requires `pos <= size()`; a larger `pos` is undefined behavior and here would construct a view of `(data()+pos, ...)` with `data()+pos` beyond one-past-the-end (no throw is mandated for `string_view::substr`).
`std::string_view::find(c, pos)` returns `npos` whenever `pos >= size()` (no matching position exists).
The capacity of the topic buffer is its own length, carried by the `std::string_view` parameter; the fragment never bounds or caps it.
To enter the loop, the entry passes `stop != std::string::npos`; any other `size_t` value remains in the parameter's domain per the fragment.
limitations: Unbounded recursion / stack exhaustion via the line-37 `publish(iterator->wildcardChild, stop + 1, stop, ...)` call is not confirmed: recursion height equals the `wildcardChild` chain depth in the trie, and the presence/capping of such chains is not shown in the fragment.

`messageId`, `numTriggeredTopics`, `triggeredTopics`, and `drain()` are not declared in the fragment; the bounds of `messages[messageId]` and `triggeredTopics[...]` and the reset behavior of `drain()` cannot be confirmed, and none of these indices is derived from the fragment's inputs.

The line-6 OOB read requires the entry to pass `start > topic.size()`; a conforming caller that always passes `start <= topic.size()` would avoid it, but the fragment itself provides no such guarantee, which is the demonstrated defect.

The CWE-476 dereference requires the entry call to supply a NULL `iterator`; the fragment's own recursion passes a NULL-checked `wildcardChild` (line 36), but the unvalidated entry parameter is the residual-range source per the analysis rules.

verdict.summary: gopherToHTML writes a NUL terminator one byte past the stack buffer `line` (declared TEMP_BUF_SIZE at L6): the clamp at L77 caps the combined line length at exactly TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1, after which L97 'line[llen + 1] = '\0';' writes index TEMP_BUF_SIZE (CWE-787), reachable from unconstrained gopher-server data (len/inbuf). Independently, attacker-controlled `host` is interpolated unescaped into generated HTML at L244-245 (CWE-79), allowing attribute breakout and script injection.

evidence.reason: OOB write (CWE-787): `line` has capacity TEMP_BUF_SIZE (L6, L16). llen is derived from entry-point data (memchr at L68 -> L71/L73) with no cap on len, and both the clamp path (L75 true -> L77 => llen = TEMP_BUF_SIZE - gopherState->len - 1, then L92 => llen = TEMP_BUF_SIZE - 1) and the non-clamp boundary (gopherState->len + llen == TEMP_BUF_SIZE - 1) make L97 write index llen+1 == TEMP_BUF_SIZE, exactly 1 byte past the buffer. The L75 guard's admitted set includes every value it clamps to TEMP_BUF_SIZE - 1, which is precisely the failure value; no shown statement bounds llen to TEMP_BUF_SIZE - 2.

evidence.snippet: outbuf.appendf(" %s\n", icon_url, host, gtype, escaped_selector, html_quote(name));
evidence.reason: HTML injection (CWE-79): `host` from the attacker-controlled gopher line (L123, split at L126-L127) is passed raw as a %s into an HTML attribute without HTML escaping (only `name` is html_quote'd). A host value like 'x"><script>alert(1)</script>' closes the HREF attribute into HTML markup served to the client, yielding script execution in the proxy-served page. Reachable on the standard-link branch: selector/host/port non-NULL (L120/L125/L130), gtype e.g. GOPHER_FILE, selector not starting with "GET /".

assumptions: TEMP_BUF_SIZE is a compile-time constant and `line` holds exactly TEMP_BUF_SIZE bytes (L6, L16); all index/capacity arithmetic in the finding uses the same symbol, so its numeric value is immaterial.
gopherState->len is confined to [0, TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1] by the shown clamp (L77) and the shown writer (L84-L85).
inbuf/len are network-supplied gopher/CSO data (entry-point inputs); the fragment imposes no length cap or content validation on them.

memcpy at L84 into gopherState->buf cannot be confirmed as OOB: gopherState->buf's capacity is not visible in the fragment, though the copy size is clamped to <= TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1.
NULL dereference of gopherState/gopherState->entry is not attacker-directed and NULL cannot be produced on any shown path; treated as robustness only.

The GOPHER_WWW appendf at L240-241 has 5 format specifiers but only 3 arguments, reading unspecified variadic values (garbage content / possible crash); not attacker-controlled content and not a confirmed finding.
xstrdup (L155) returning NULL is not handled before use; would require an unshown allocation failure, robustness only.

verdict.summary: SparseDenseBinaryOpShared::Compute reads the sparse indices matrix with an `int` loop counter bounded only by the unconstrained int64 `nnz` (line 66, no shown cap). For `nnz >= 2^31` the guard `i < nnz` admits `i = 2^31-1`, then `i++` overflows signed int and the loop continues at `i = -2^31`, so line 94 performs an out-of-bounds heap read of the indices matrix (CWE-125, root cause signed overflow CWE-190). The later `indices_valid` check (lines 99-102) runs after this read and does not protect it. Reachability requires tensors of >= 2^31 rows and successful ~tens-of-GiB allocations (lines 67-71), so the witness is a range claim with a machine-memory precondition.

evidence.reason: `indices_mat` is an `nnz` x `ndims` matrix where `nnz = indices_t->dim_size(0)` (line 66) is an int64 value with no upper bound enforced by any shown validation (lines 9, 26, 31, 36, 57 only check shape validity and cross-tensor equality). The row position `i` is an `int` loop counter (line 92); the guard `i < nnz` admits `i = 2^31-1` when `nnz = 2^31` (a member of the admitted residual domain), and `i++` then overflows signed int (CWE-190), wrapping to `-2^31` with the guard still true. The inner loop at line 94 then reads row `-2^31` of a matrix with rows [0, 2^31-1], i.e. an out-of-bounds read 2^31 rows before the buffer (CWE-125). The `indices_valid` OP_REQUIRES at lines 99-102 executes after this read and only gates the write at line 103, so it does not mitigate this sink.

assumptions: OP_REQUIRES/OP_REQUIRES_OK call CtxFailure and return from Compute on failure (standard TensorFlow macro semantics, not defined inside the fragment).
FastBoundsCheck (line 95) is the standard two-sided bounds check `0 <= v < limit` (bounds_check.h semantics assumed by name; not defined in the fragment).
indices_t/values_t/shape_t/dense_t are op inputs (entry-point class), so `nnz = indices_t->dim_size(0)` starts at the full int64 domain since no shown statement caps it.
limitations: The witness requires allocations at lines 67-71 to succeed for tensors of >= 2^31 elements (~tens of GiB); success is the shown-code precondition (OP_REQUIRES_OK) but its availability depends on machine memory, so confidence is capped.

The OOB write at line 103 (dense_gathered_flat(-2^31), potential CWE-787) is gated by OP_REQUIRES(indices_valid) (lines 99-102), which requires every garbage idx value read at line 94 to pass FastBoundsCheck; garbage values cannot be specified deterministically, so the write is not a confirmed witness.
The sticky `indices_valid` flag (line 91) is not exploitable in this fragment: the OP_REQUIRES at lines 99-102 returns on the first invalid row, so no later row runs with a stale flag.
A rank-0 (scalar) dense input could make `b.y_reshape()` size differ from NDIM and trip an assertion in `Tensor::shaped`, but BCast internals are not shown, so this is unconfirmable.
If FastBoundsCheck were only an upper-bound test, negative `idx[d]` would bypass it; this is not assumed because the standard macro is two-sided.

verdict.summary: In publish(), the trigger queue is drained only once per call at entry when numTriggeredTopics == 64 (line 3), while the queue stores at lines 29 and 53 (triggeredTopics[numTriggeredTopics++]) are unguarded and fire once per matched segment plus once for the exact match. An attacker-chosen topic with enough segments (e.g., entry count 62 with three '#'-subscribed nodes → line-29 stores at indices 62, 63, 64; or entry count 63 with a '#'-child plus the exact-match tail → line-53 store at index 64) writes past the 64-entry triggeredTopics array: out-of-bounds write, CWE-787.

evidence.reason: The store index is numTriggeredTopics, whose entry value is admitted by the line-3 guard ('== 64' excludes only the value 64; 62 and 0 pass) and which is incremented once per loop iteration. Iterations are driven by the entry-point publish topic (line 1), whose length/count is unconstrained in the fragment, so a single call can perform arbitrarily many stores. Witness: numTriggeredTopics=62 at entry, topic 's1/s2/s3' with terminating-wildcard ('#') children at the root, node s1, and node s2; lines 17-18 admit segments 's1','s2','s3'; line 29 stores land at indices 62, 63, then 64, exceeding the 64-entry triggeredTopics capacity evidenced by the line-2 comment and the line-3 threshold — out-of-bounds write (CWE-787).

Same unguarded store as line 29, executed after the loop for the exact-match node. Witness: numTriggeredTopics=63 at entry (63 != 64 passes the line-3 guard), root has a terminating-wildcard child T and children['a']=A, topic 'a'; the line-29 store consumes index 63 (count→64), then this tail store executes at index 64 with no draining check between line 3 and line 53, writing past the 64-entry triggeredTopics array — out-of-bounds write (CWE-787).

assumptions: triggeredTopics holds exactly 64 Topic* entries — evidenced by the comment at line 2 ('64 triggered topics') and the drain threshold numTriggeredTopics == 64 at line 3.
drain() processes and clears the queued triggers (resetting numTriggeredTopics), as implied by its role as the ==64 safety valve; the finding holds even without this assumption.

Topic trie node pointers on shown paths are non-NULL: wildcard children are dereferenced only after the null checks at lines 24/35, and the line 45 value it->second would require an unshown NULL producer in the map.

When run exceeds the per-line sample budget length (line 33), the writes pass the end of the line, if (length) (line 80) admits the resulting negative length and adds one more write per component (line 106), and do { ... } while(--length) (line 152) keeps looping across negative values until 32-bit wrap-around, producing an unbounded out-of-bounds write / near-non-termination on crafted input (CWE-787).

evidence.reason: CWE-787 out-of-bounds write. The write count is run, the unconstrained return of DecodeRun (line 63; full LONG residual range, no comparison/clamp/cast shown after the call). while(run) (line 66) and run--,length-- (line 74) never check run against the visible per-line budget length = m_ulWidth[0] (line 33) or any capacity of lp[cx] = line[cx]->m_pData (line 38) — the target capacity is not shown, so this is a confirmed missing-bound/unvalidated-size flow. Witness range: run = length+1 (e.g., length=8, run=9), with m_ucCount=1 (passes line 23), isrun=true (line 62); after the loop length is -1, the guard if (length) (line 80) admits negative values, and while(--length) (line 152) continues until 32-bit wrap, amplifying the overflow.

CWE-787 out-of-bounds write (same root cause). After an over-long run makes length negative, the guard if (length) (line 80) admits the negative value, so this interruption-path write executes one additional time per component, writing beyond the sample budget already exceeded by the run loop at line 72.

Arrays line[4] (line 6), lp[4] (line 34), and a[4]/b[4]/c[4]/d[4]/d1[4]/d2[4]/d3[4] (lines 45-46) are declared with capacity 4.

limitations: m_ucCount (line 23) is guarded only by assert(m_ucCount < 4); if compiled out, m_ucCount >= 5 overflows the 4-element arrays (CWE-787), and if active it becomes a reachable abort (CWE-617) — the build mode is not shown in the fragment, so this is not confirmed.

The concrete overflow magnitude depends on DecodeRun's return value (a range, run in [length+1, LONG_MAX], rather than a single demonstrated constant), which caps confidence at 0.62.

verdict.summary: Null pointer dereference: after a successful find_site_by_name() at line 26, the out-parameter 'local' is dereferenced at line 31 (local->local = 1) with no NULL check. On the admitted path where the lookup returns non-zero (guard 26 condition false), control reaches line 31 unconditionally past line 26 with no intervening NULL check, and 'local->local = 1' dereferences a possibly-NULL pointer, crashing the daemon (availability/DoS).

verdict.summary: Examples::Initialize reads example_labels(example_id) at line 65 with an index derived from example_weights.size() (num_examples) while never validating that the example_labels tensor has at least num_examples elements; an attacker-supplied labels tensor smaller than the weights tensor causes an out-of-bounds heap read (missing bound / unvalidated-size flow). evidence.reason: Index example_id ∈ [0, num_examples-1] derives from example_weights.size() (line 46, admitted < INT_MAX by the line 39 guard), but example_labels (loaded line 49) has no size constraint anywhere in the fragment; with weights size 2 and labels size 1, the loop at line 60 admits example_id = 1 (1 < 2), so line 65 reads example_labels(1) one element past the 1-element labels buffer — CWE-125 OOB read via unvalidated index. No protective statement covers this sink; the line 39 guard only bounds example_weights before the cast at line 46.

Tensor element counts from flat views (lines 37, 49) are size_t-sized and can differ between the example_weights and example_labels op inputs, since no shown statement relates them.
All TF_RETURN_IF_ERROR statuses are checked and early-returned; no status-handling flaw is visible.

Line 63 `resize(num_dense_features)` with a negative value converts to a huge size_t and throws length_error/bad_alloc: an op-failure/robustness concern (framework-handled exception), not memory corruption; no attacker-directed failing operation on a failure state is shown.

Line 67-68 dereferences context->device()->tensorflow_cpu_worker_threads() without a null check; treated as a framework-invariant robustness concern with no exhibited NULL producer.
The example_labels OOB is the only confirmed finding; all other candidates lack a demonstrated security-relevant sink or corrupting operation.

verdict.summary: Integer truncation in the thousand-separator size math bypasses the overflow guard and undersizes the output buffer: line 62 checks the term only in size_t arithmetic, so the value admitted at line 67 (e.g. 102 * 42,107,523 = 4,294,967,346) then narrows into int integral, making reslen (line 70) and the String resstr allocation (line 88) far smaller than the bytes the copy loop writes (lines 124-129). This yields an attacker-reachable heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787; root cause CWE-190).

evidence.reason: Primary sink: thousand_sep.size() is the unconstrained String length (only line 61's non-empty check guards it). The overflow check at line 62 compares in size_t and admits terms above INT_MAX (e.g. 102 * 42,107,523), then line 67 narrows the term into int integral so that line 70 sets reslen = 359 instead of the required 4,294,967,655 bytes; the 359-byte allocation at line 88 (String resstr(reslen, ReserveString)) is therefore far smaller than the memcpy's 42,107,523 bytes of out-of-bounds writes near resbuf - 42,107,167, repeated 102 times. Heap OOB write, CWE-787.

Secondary sink on the same path: after each oversized separator memcpy at lines 126-128, t is advanced ~42,107,523 bytes below resbuf, so the next digit writes at *t-- land outside the 359-byte allocation derived from the truncated reslen; the write target is the same corrupted-size chain (lines 62-92), confirming heap OOB write, CWE-787 with CWE-190 root cause.

assumptions: String::size() returns size_t, and ReserveString(N) provides N characters plus a terminating NUL as stated by the visible comment at lines 20-21; the exploited undersized allocation is String resstr(reslen, ReserveString) at line 88.

The witness relies on the standard snprintf behavior of '%.*F' (309-digit integer part for d=1e308, return value = would-be length) and on the mainstream ABI semantics that narrowing an out-of-range size_t to int yields low bits (here 359); even without that exact wrap, any int result is below the 4,294,967,655 bytes actually written.
thousand_sep of length 42,107,523 and d = 1e308 are members of the parameters' residual ranges, since the fragment imposes no length cap on the separator and no other bound on d.
limitations: The same mixed-int/size_t arithmetic affects reslen += dec (line 73) and reslen += dec_point.size() (line 80); those variants were not given separate CWEs because the huge-dec path additionally depends on snprintf succeeding for a multi-GB precision.

A dec near INT_MAX would also drive a multi-GB String(tmplen, ReserveString) allocation at line 35 (resource-exhaustion concern); not independently confirmed because it depends on libc behavior for enormous '%.*F' precision.

If ReserveString(N) reserved only N total bytes (contradicting the visible comment at lines 20-21), the first snprintf at line 24 would be a one-byte overflow; that reading was not adopted because the comment states the 63+NUL invariant.
Line 37's tmplen + 1 would wrap only at tmplen == INT_MAX, which requires the same huge-precision environment; not confirmed.
The tmpbuf == nullptr checks at lines 29 and 39 are dead given mutableData()'s contract; not findings.
dp-missing/declen-vs-dec mismatches are only reachable through truncated snprintf output, which the redirect at lines 33-43 prevents for shown inputs; not confirmed.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the fixed btrfs_rm_device: the swapfile guard at lines 29-35 (if (btrfs_pinned_by_swapfile(fs_info, device)) { ret = -ETXTBSY; goto out; }) executes before every destructive use of the device and excludes exactly the devices backing an active swapfile, so the sinks btrfs_scratch_superblocks (121-122), btrfs_close_bdev (124), and btrfs_free_device (126) are unreachable for a swap-pinned device, preventing the known use-after-free class. Entry-point inputs device_path and devid flow only into the lookup (18) and strcmp (22), never into a sink; residual candidates (u64 count underflows at 14 and 111, NULL dereferences of device/device->name, log injection, counter underflows) lack any witness constructible from the shown statements.

assumptions: Line 20's IS_ERR(device) together with lines 21-25 (PTR_ERR(device) == -ENOENT, ret = PTR_ERR(device)) shows the lookup's error convention is ERR_PTR, so the continuation set after line 27 contains only valid btrfs_device pointers; NULL is not produced on any shown path.

Line 29's btrfs_pinned_by_swapfile(fs_info, device) reports whether device backs an active swapfile; no statement between lines 29 and 126 can create or destroy such a pin (the intermediate operations are locks, counter/list updates, and the shown btrfs_* calls).

The device found at line 18 is already a member of the counted sets decremented at lines 51, 94-95, 98, 101, 106 (WRITEABLE implies rw_devices membership, MISSING implies missing_devices membership, device->bdev non-NULL implies open_devices membership), so those decrements cannot underflow on the shown path.
device->name is populated when the device is registered and is used at lines 32 and 122; no shown statement sets it to NULL.
limitations: TOCTOU window: uuid_mutex is released at line 55 and re-acquired at line 59 around btrfs_shrink_device; if swap activation could pin device in that window via concurrent code outside the fragment, the line 29 check would be stale and lines 121-126 would free a device still in swap use. The activation path is not shown, so no witness can be constructed from the fragment; this class is the one the fragment's swapfile guard is the known fix for.

u64 underflow at line 14 (num_devices - 1) and line 111 (btrfs_super_num_devices(...) - 1) require a zero count that no shown statement derives; the continuation path also requires a successful lookup at line 18, contradicting num_devices == 0, and the line 112 store is a plain u64 in-memory superblock value with no shown memory-safety consumer.
NULL-dereference candidates for device (after IS_ERR at line 20) and device->name (lines 32, 122) have no NULL producer on any shown path.
Log injection via %s of device->name at lines 30-32 is not reachable from the fragment's entry-point string device_path, which is consumed only at lines 18 and 22.

Counter-underflow and free_fs_devices edge cases (lines 94-95, 101, 106, 128-132) depend on accounting invariants and on the RAID-profile minimum enforced by btrfs_check_raid_min_devices at line 14, whose numeric minimum is not shown.

btrfs_reada_undo_remove_dev at line 139 runs after a btrfs_shrink_device failure even though btrfs_reada_remove_dev (line 58) was skipped; this is an undo-safe absent-entry removal, not a security-relevant operation on a failure state.

Residual concerns (get_name's internal write bound vs. the name_len+4 capacity, int narrowing of *parsed_len, unchecked pj_pool_alloc) cannot be confirmed from the shown code and are recorded in limitations; no confirmed vulnerability.

The capacity of q->name.ptr is name_len+4 as allocated at line 15; q->type and q->dnsclass are 2-byte fields (read via 2-byte pj_memcpy).
The status of get_name_len (line 10) and get_name (line 19) is checked before their outputs are used (lines 11-12 and 20-21).
limitations: get_name (line 19) writes into q->name.ptr whose only visible capacity is name_len+4 (line 15); whether get_name can write more than that is not determinable from the shown code, and no shown arithmetic produces a size exceeding the visible capacity, so no confirmed write-side finding exists.

*parsed_len = (int)(p - start) (line 39) narrows a ptrdiff_t to int; truncation would require a packet span exceeding INT_MAX bytes, a magnitude no shown statement establishes, so it remains an unconfirmed range claim with no CWE.

The pj_pool_alloc return (line 15) is unchecked; a NULL result would require an allocation failure whose magnitude is not demonstrated by any shown statement, so it is treated as a robustness concern only.

q and parsed_len are dereferenced without NULL checks (lines 15-16, 19, 30, 35, 39), but NULL cannot be produced on any shown path since they are caller-supplied output pointers; classified as robustness, not a finding.

Had the line 26-27 check been absent, pj_memcpy at lines 30/35 would be an OOB read; the check is present and sufficient, so this is contextual only, not a finding.

verdict.summary: Heap OOB read in SparseCountSparseOutputShapeFn: line 2 calls c->Dim(c->input(0), 1) without validating that input(0) has rank >= 2. A crafted graph binding the 'indices' input to a scalar or rank-1 int64 tensor (R = 0 or 1, both in the unconstrained residual range) reaches the sink unconditionally, and the constant index 1 exceeds the shape's dim storage, causing an out-of-bounds read (or an abort) inside shape inference. The fix is an added rank check (e.g., WithRankAtLeast(c->input(0), 2, ...)) before the Dim call.

evidence.reason: CWE-125: c->input(0) is a graph-supplied ShapeHandle whose rank R is never constrained by any statement in the fragment (no WithRankAtLeast/WithRank check exists), so R retains the full domain {0,1,2,...} including 0 and 1. The constant index 1 is consumed unconditionally at this sink before any other statement; for R=1 (e.g., input shape [7]) the valid index set is {0} and index 1 exceeds the dims storage by 1, and for R=0 (scalar []) it indexes an empty dim list. Dim is an index-consuming helper, and the shown code derives no bound proving the argument in-domain (R >= 2), so the missing rank bound is the confirmed defect; the out-of-bounds read occurs inside the shape's dimension storage.

assumptions: c->input(0) yields the ShapeHandle of the op's first input, and its rank is unconstrained because the fragment contains no rank-validation statement (the op-contract invariant that indices is [N, rank] is not visible in the fragment and cannot be used).
InferenceContext::Dim(shape, index) consumes index as a dimension index into the shape's stored dims, per its name and its use in the shown code.
limitations: The exact internal behavior of InferenceContext::Dim for an out-of-range index is not shown; if it internally bounds-checked and returned an unknown dim, no read would occur, but no such protective statement is visible in the fragment, so the out-of-domain derivation (missing bound) stands as the finding.

The unvalidated 'rank' also flows into c->Matrix(nvals, rank) and c->Vector(rank) at lines 4 and 6 (output sizing); this is reported only as part of the line-2 mechanism, not as an independent finding.
No branches or loops exist in the fragment, so branch-order and loop-bound analyses are vacuous; the fragment contains no other guards that could exclude the witness.

verdict.summary: Integer overflow corrupts the allocation size in xQueueGenericCreate: a length/item-size pair admitted by the multiplication-overflow check (e.g., uxQueueLength=0xFFFFFFFF, uxItemSize=1) makes xQueueSizeInBytes=0xFFFFFFFF, and the size_t addition sizeof(Queue_t)+xQueueSizeInBytes wraps to sizeof(Queue_t)-1 at line 28, so pvPortMalloc returns an undersized heap block that queue initialization and storage later overflow.

evidence.snippet: pxNewQueue = ( Queue_t * ) pvPortMalloc( sizeof( Queue_t ) + xQueueSizeInBytes ); /*lint !e9087 !e9079 see comment above. */
evidence.reason: uxQueueLength/uxItemSize (UBaseType_t, internal-helper parameters) are constrained only by the configASSERT guards at lines 9 and 17. The line-17 guard admits non-wrapping products only, and L=0xFFFFFFFF, S=1 is admitted: line 14 yields xQueueSizeInBytes=0xFFFFFFFF (no wrap) and 0xFFFFFFFF/1==0xFFFFFFFF passes line 17. At line 28 the size_t sum sizeof(Queue_t)+0xFFFFFFFF wraps modulo 2^32 to sizeof(Queue_t)-1 (standard ports with equal UBaseType_t/size_t width), so pvPortMalloc is called with an undersized size while line 46 forwards the full length/item size and a storage pointer past the end of the block — CWE-190 integer overflow corrupting the allocation size, leading to heap overflow.

evidence.snippet: prvInitialiseNewQueue( uxQueueLength, uxItemSize, pucQueueStorage, ucQueueType, pxNewQueue );
evidence.reason: On the admitted path (uxQueueLength=0xFFFFFFFF, uxItemSize=1) the heap block from line 28 is only sizeof(Queue_t)-1 bytes, yet this call supplies uxQueueLength=0xFFFFFFFF, uxItemSize=1, and pucQueueStorage (line 35: base + sizeof(Queue_t), already 1+ bytes past the end of the block) to prvInitialiseNewQueue; the length/size arguments are out of domain for the actual allocation, so the callee initializes a queue whose storage requirement (0xFFFFFFFF bytes) exceeds the allocated block — the missing-bound flow of the shown arguments under the CWE-190 root cause.

assumptions: configASSERT was credited at its strongest protective reading (assertions enabled; a false condition halts execution); the reported witness still passes both guards, so the verdict does not depend on asserts being disabled.

pvPortMalloc is assumed to succeed for the small wrapped size (sizeof(Queue_t)-1), entering the NULL-checked success branch at line 30; on allocation failure the function returns NULL without dereferencing.
sizeof( Queue_t ) >= 1, so (sizeof( Queue_t ) - 1) mod 2^32 is strictly below the required allocation size.
limitations: The primary witness assumes the standard FreeRTOS port invariant sizeof(size_t) == sizeof(UBaseType_t) (32-bit on common targets); the fragment does not show these widths, which affects the arithmetic at line 28.

If configASSERT is compiled out (asserts disabled), line 17 imposes no runtime constraint and the line-14 multiplication wraps unchecked (e.g., 0x10001*0x10001 -> 0x00020001), producing the same undersized-allocation class; this configuration-dependent path is not reported as a separate CWE.

The heap-overflow write itself happens inside prvInitialiseNewQueue / queue enqueue, which is not shown, so CWE-787 is not listed as an independently confirmed CWE; the shown sink is the corrupted allocation size at line 28.
The configASSERT abort paths (lines 9, 17) are treated as intended fail-closed assertions, not CWE-617.
No injection, crypto, file-handling, or authn/authz sinks exist in this fragment; NULL dereference is guarded at line 30.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. session_state is null-checked (L4-L6) before its only dereference at L7; AddTensor and allocate_output statuses are honored via OP_REQUIRES_OK (L9, L12); the output is a rank-0 tensor from TensorShape({}) with exactly one element, and both write paths (L19, L22) write exactly one element. The unchecked ctx->tensor_store() dereference at L9 and the dtype assumption in the else branch are framework-level robustness concerns with no attacker-directed failure path derivable from the shown code.

assumptions: TensorShape({}) at L12 produces a rank-0 tensor whose num_elements() is exactly 1 (empty product), fixing the output capacity that the L19 and L22 single-element writes target.
OP_REQUIRES and OP_REQUIRES_OK abort Compute with an error status when their condition/status fails, so no statement after a failed check executes.
handle->scalar<ResourceHandle>()() writes one element (index 0) and handle->flat<tstring>() yields a 1-element view whose setConstant fills exactly one element.
name() and requested_device() are node attributes supplied by the graph/framework.
limitations: ctx->tensor_store() at L9 is dereferenced without a null check; a null store can only arise from framework context construction (no shown producer, no attacker-directed argument), so it is recorded as a robustness concern, not a confirmed NULL-deref (no CWE).

The else branch (L20-L22) writes a tstring without re-verifying the output dtype; a non-DT_STRING/non-DT_RESOURCE expected_output_dtype would be a type-confused write, but producing such a value requires violating the op type-signature/type-inference invariant outside the fragment, so the candidate is demoted.
ctx and ctx->input(0) are assumed non-null and valid per framework callback semantics; no null path for them is derivable from shown statements.
The string from tk.GetHandle(name()) is stored as plain data at L16/L22; no format-string, path, URL, query, command, or log sink appears in the fragment, so no injection candidate exists.

The loop condition p < pend (line 10) bounds every dereference in the loop body.
pgpDigParamsFree is NULL-safe by convention (used at line 51 without a NULL guard).

limitations: A zero or negative packet advance (line 41: (pkt->body - pkt->head) + pkt->blen) would stall the loop (CWE-835), but whether decodePkt admits such a packet is not shown, so no concrete witness can be constructed; recorded as a limitation.
