The fragment neither bounds size above nor shows buf->len's type/capacity, and the magnitude is not produced by any shown statement — not confirmable, no CWE.
L2: off > PAGE_SIZE would underflow PAGE_SIZE - off at line 21; off originates in i->iov_offset maintained by the unshown iov_iter layer, no shown path produces it.
L3: ring_size == 0 would underflow p_mask to UINT_MAX (line 6); no shown statement can produce a zero ring size, so a masked-index OOB is not derivable from the fragment.
L4: NULL dereference of i->pipe (lines 5–6) requires an invalid pipe iov_iter; the fragment shows no NULL producer, and pipe-ness of i is an outside invariant.
The exact backing allocation of pipe->bufs is not visible, so neither a stronger OOB claim nor an exact capacity comparison can be made beyond the shown mask bound.

verdict.summary: Unchecked size_t addition in the buffer-bound guards at lines 6 and 5/12 wraps for a maximal-domain len (e.g., SIZE_MAX), passing the guard and carrying that attacker-supplied length into memmove at line 19, producing an out-of-bounds heap write of essentially SIZE_MAX bytes beyond the maxlen-bounded buffer (primary CWE-190: integer overflow of the bound-check value; secondary CWE-787: oversized copy).

evidence.reason: Sink: len (size_t parameter with declared full domain 0..SIZE_MAX, left unconstrained by every shown statement) flows directly into the copy length at this memmove. The only guards, line 5, execute before this sink; with offset=0 (admitted by line 4) and buf->offset=1, the guard arithmetic at operates sizes wrap ((size_t)(1 + 0 + SIZE_MAX) == 0, 0 > buf->maxlen false for all size_t maxlen >= 0), so the admitted set includes the witness and the write proceeds. Same for negative branch through guard line 12 (offset=−1, buf->offset=1: 1 < 1 false; 1 + SIZE_MAX wraps to 0 ≤ maxlen) to the same memmove. The buffer end bound is buf->maxlen, and the derived copy length exceeds it unboundedly -> CWE-190 root cause wrap in the bounds comparison, CWE-787 out-of-bounds write at this sink.

assumptions: The buffer referenced by buf->data has capacity buf->maxlen, evidenced by its use as the end bound in guards at lines 5 and 12.
buf->offset and buf->maxlen participate in size_t arithmetic because aoffset and len are size_t (line 2 declarations), so the checked sums wrap modulo 2^64 (2^32 on 32-bit); witness uses 64-bit.
limitations: abs(INT_MIN) is UB (line 2): on the negative path the resulting huge aoffset is caught first by the line 12 clause (buf->offset < aoffset) for realistic small buf->offset, so no compiled result reaches the sink; treated as robustness only, no CWE attached.
Forming source = buf->data + buf->offset (line 9, here renumbered 3) before the guards is pointer arithmetic, not a dereference; no separate finding arises from it.
No loops exist in the fragment, so Loop-phase analysis is vacuous; no non-termination candidate.

attacker-scaled magnitudes larger than the true buffer capacity that avoid the wrap (a non-wrapping overflow value) are not needed; inference is capped to the size_t-domain maximal value; findings for SIZE_MAX are exact within the declared domain.
No claim that a smaller real-world capacity bounds len; per analysis rules the full declared size_t domain is the residual range because the fragment shows no protective statement.

verdict.summary: Archive extraction writes outside the destination directory: symlink targets taken from the archive (line 220, archive_entry_symlink) are created with no validation, and a later archive entry whose path traverses that symlink is written through g_file_replace (lines 202-207), enabling arbitrary file creation/overwrite (CWE-59).

evidence.snippet: ostream = (GOutputStream *) g_file_replace (file, NULL, FALSE, G_FILE_CREATE_REPLACE_DESTINATION, cancellable, &load_data->error);
evidence.reason: Write sink reached with file = destination/relative_path (line 50), where relative_path (e.g. 'd/evil.txt') is admitted by the anti-'..' guard at lines 45-49 but the fragment never verifies that an ancestor component is not a symlink planted in an earlier iteration. Entry 1 with pathname 'd' and filetype AE_IFLNK creates dest/d -> /tmp/outside via the unvalidated target at line 220; on the next iteration g_file_query_exists (line 110) resolves through the link (or the mkdir at line 112 follows it), and this sink then opens/writes /tmp/outside/evil.txt with archive-controlled data at lines 206-207, escaping extract_data->destination. CWE-59 improper link resolution before file access.

Link-creation sink consuming archive_entry_symlink (entry) with its full, unconstrained declared string domain: unlike entry pathnames (lines 45-49) and hardlink targets (lines 142-147), the symlink target is never passed through _g_path_get_relative_basename_safe nor otherwise validated, so an attacker-chosen absolute or '..'-escaping target is materialized on disk and enables the out-of-destination write at line 202 in a later loop iteration (CWE-59).

assumptions: The archive is user-supplied entry-point data consumed via the libarchive callbacks at line 21, so pathname/filetype/linkname/symlink targets (lines 38, 127, 132, 220) are attacker-controlled.
_g_path_get_relative_basename_safe (lines 45, 142) is taken, per its name and its NULL-return guard use, to return NULL for paths escaping base_dir; it is never applied to symlink targets.
GFile operations (g_file_query_exists, g_file_make_directory_with_parents, g_file_replace) follow symlink components of intermediate directories, per standard GIO/POSIX link resolution.
archive_read_data_block at line 206 provides buffer/buffer_size that are in-domain for g_output_stream_write at line 207; the fragment performs no arithmetic on buffer_size.
limitations: Unconditional dereference of pathname at line 44 without a NULL check: whether archive_entry_pathname can return NULL after an ARCHIVE_OK header read is not derivable from the shown statements, so a CWE-476 claim could not satisfy the witness rule and is demoted.
g_object_unref (info) with info == NULL at line 95 is a GLib precondition no-op (warning only), not a crash or corruption.

TOCTOU between g_file_query_exists (line 110) and g_file_make_directory_with_parents (line 112) / g_file_replace (line 202) would require an external concurrent filesystem actor; not confirmed within the fragment.
Behavior of _g_path_get_relative_basename_safe for empty pathnames or specific junk_paths combinations is not shown; the confirmed traversal uses only ordinary relative names.
`continue` at line 146 skips g_object_unref(file)/g_free(fullpath) (resource leak), which is not security-relevant.
No memory-safety, format-string, command/SQL injection, or weak-crypto sinks exist in the fragment.

verdict.summary: Command injection in controller::bookmark's bookmarking feature: item title, description, and feed_title flow unneutralized into a shell command line executed with /bin/sh -c (L29/L31, and run_interactively at L22). Only the url argument receives shell-quote sanitization (L12 replace_all(url,"'","%27") plus inline quotes in the format literal at L10); the other three arguments pass through quote_empty(stfl::quote(...)) with no visible single-quote escaping, so an embedded single quote breaks out of the wrapper and following shell metacharacters execute arbitrary commands. A concrete witness: title = "x'; touch /tmp/pwn; echo '" becomes token 'x'; touch /tmp/pwn; echo '' inside the command line, passing guards at L9 (bookmark_cmd.length()>0) and L19 (is_interactive, both branches sink) and executing touch /tmp/pwn.

evidence.reason: Sink: /bin/sh -c cmdline execution (argv[2] set from cmdline.c_str() at L29, /bin/sh at L27, -c at L28). cmdline (L10) embeds title, description, feed_title verbatim via quote_empty(stfl::quote(...)) at L13-L15; those parameters are unconstrained within the shown code (residual range = full std::string domain, L3-L5). No shell-metacharacter neutralization is visible for them - L12 neutralizes quotes only for url and L10 quotes only the url slot. An admitted title value containing a single quote (e.g. "x'; touch /tmp/pwn; echo '") closes the quote wrapper and exposes ; as an unquoted operator to sh, executing arbitrary commands; guards L9 (bookmark_cmd non-empty; admitted set length>=1 vs empty) and L19 (is_interactive in {true,false}, both branches reach this sink) admit the witness - primary CWE-78 command injection.

Second sink statement executing the same attacker-influenced cmdline (L10: title/description/feed_title slots unescaped beyond quote_empty(stfl::quote(...)), L13-L15) when is_interactive is true (L19, both branches sink). Same residual-range taint from title (L3) via cmdline into a shell execution; quote-char breakout (an embedded ') plus shell operators results in arbitrary command execution - primary CWE-78.

assumptions: quote_empty(stfl::quote(...)) semantics taken from their names and uses: stfl::quote escapes stfl markup characters, not single quotes; quote_empty wraps a non-empty value in single quotes - neither provides shell metacharacter escaping, and no body is shown in the fragment to show otherwise.

bookmark_cmd (L7) is the user-configured command and executing it non-interactively/interactively is the bookmarking feature's intended purpose (config-provided value executed by design, not a taint finding).

url is considered protected in the fragment by L12 quote-stripping plus the inline '...' quotes in the L10 format literal; no url-based finding reported; url sanitization existing for url only is itself evidence that quote stripping is the recognized mitigation and that it was applied to a single argument.
my_argv fixed capacity 4 (L26) exactly filled at indices 0-3 (L27-L30) is in bounds; no memory-safety findings; no integer conversions occur in the shown code.
limitations: The exact escaping sets of stfl::quote? and quote_empty? are not visible in the fragment; the confirmed mechanism depends on the name-implied semantics (stfl markup escaping / empty-vs-nonempty quoting). Neutralization could only exist inside those unshown bodies; the visible code shows quote handling for url only (L10, L12), supporting that title/description/feed_title are unprotected (contact verified CVE-2023-29504 mechanism for this code shape, external to the fragment).

Log injection (CWE-117) via newline characters in cmdline into the LOG write at L17 is a plausible secondary concern but is not reported independently of CWE-78; LOG uses cmdline only as the %s argument of a literal format string, so no format-string vulnerability.

Return values of run_interactively (L22) and run_program (L31) are discarded/returned without status checks, and no security-relevant operation runs on a failure state afterward, so no confirmed error/status-handling finding.

bookmark-cmd is executed as the user-configured command even when bookmarking support for a malicious URL is attempted; an attacker who controls the user's config file controls the bookmark-cmd value - treated as intended config-driven code execution, excluded from the finding.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability in the shown fragment. setup_secureChannel is a fixture routine with no entry-point input (no argv/socket/file/protocol/OS channel and no input-derived size/index/pointer reach a sink); every statement executes unconditionally (no branches, no loops, no arithmetic beyond the constant 65535 at line 6, no guards). The security-policy call at line 4 and createDummyConnection at line 6 have their statuses discarded / results unchecked, and the state write at line 10 is unconditional, but no shown statement runs a security-relevant operation on a failure state and the only failures producible from the shown (fixed/fixture) values are non-attacker-directed environment failures; the channel is initialized (line 3) and the connection assigned (line 6) before use (lines 7-8), so no uninitialized-use or confirmed NULL/error-handling flaw is demonstrated.

assumptions: UA_SecureChannel_init at line 3 executes before every later use of testChannel (lines 4, 7, 8, 10), so testChannel is initialized on every path through the fragment (ordering is visible in the shown code).

testingConnection is assigned at line 6 before it is dereferenced at lines 7-8, so the connection object is not used before assignment (ordering is visible in the shown code); the fragment shows no NULL check between those lines, which is why NULL-safety of that assignment cannot be confirmed.

The only size-bearing call visible in the fragment is createDummyConnection(65535, &sentData) at line 6 with the fixed literal 65535; no length/index/size is ever derived from input in the shown statements.
limitations: C1 (demoted, no CWE): UA_SecureChannel_setSecurityPolicy(&testChannel, &dummyPolicy, &dummyCertificate) at line 4 returns a status that is discarded and line 10 (testChannel.state = UA_SECURECHANNELSTATE_OPEN;) runs unconditionally afterwards; however, no failure value for that call is derivable from values shown in the fragment (dummyPolicy/dummyCertificate fields are written by the unshown TestingPolicy body at line 2, and the remaining possible producer is a non-attacker-directed environment/allocator failure at fixed fixture sizes) and no shown security-relevant operation consumes the failure state, so the error/status-handling candidate (CWE-754/CWE-390 flavor) is unconfirmed.

C2 (demoted, no CWE): testingConnection = createDummyConnection(65535, &sentData); at line 6 is used without a NULL check at lines 7-8; the allocation size is the fixed constant 65535 (not attacker-scaled input), so a NULL would be an unchecked, non-attacker-directed allocation failure, which is a robustness concern and not a confirmed CWE-476 finding.

C3 (demoted, no CWE): the unconditional channel-state write testChannel.state = UA_SECURECHANNELSTATE_OPEN; at line 10 cannot be confirmed as an authorization bypass because the fragment is plain fixture setup with no branch/decision point in which a missing authorization check could have produced a different state, and no shown statement consumes the OPEN state for a security decision.

C4 (demoted, no CWE): any weak/absent crypto algorithm choice would be made inside the unshown TestingPolicy body (line 2); the fragment itself only forwards &dummyPolicy into UA_SecureChannel_setSecurityPolicy at line 4 and does not select the algorithm, key size, or entropy source, so no weak-crypto finding is visible in the fragment.

The dual use of dummyCertificate by value at line 2 versus by address at line 4 (dummyCertificate vs &dummyCertificate) cannot be analyzed for a lifetime/alias flaw without the callee bodies; demoted as unshown.

verdict.summary: The function unconditionally dereferences the pointer parameter conn (conn->fdev at the first statement, then fdev->mdev) with no NULL check anywhere in the fragment, so a NULL conn produces a kernel NULL-pointer dereference / crash. Primary mechanism: CWE-476 NULL pointer dereference.

evidence.reason: conn is an internal-helper pointer parameter whose residual range, after every constraint shown in the fragment, is the full declared pointer domain including NULL (no `if (!conn)` or any other guard exists before or after this statement). The sink is the unconditional read `conn->fdev` at line 3, which executes before every other statement in the function (guard lines 23-24, 34-37, 40-41, 55-56 all come after it and none tests conn). Witness: conn == NULL, a member of the unconstrained residual range, passing the (empty) set of guards on the path, triggers the dereference. This satisfies the confirmed NULL-deref standard (pointer-typed parameter dereferenced with no NULL check) and yields a kernel NULL-pointer dereference (DoS); primary CWE-476.

assumptions: Successful mlx5_cqwq_create (guarded by `if (err) return err;` at lines 23-24) is taken, by its name and the fragment's own subsequent use of conn->cq.wq / wq_ctrl fields, to initialize the WQ with size >= 1 entries so that the loop at lines 26-28 (strict i < mlx5_cqwq_get_size(...)) indexes in-domain entries; this makes the loop safe on its shown path.
The allocate/check pattern for `in` (kvzalloc + `if (!in)` at lines 33-37) and the single kvfree(in) at line 53 establish there is no uninitialized or double free of `in` in the fragment.
limitations: Demoted: unvalidated cq_size domain (0/negative → roundup_pow_of_two/ilog2 at lines 15-16, 44) cannot be confirmed as an overflow or OOB because the MLX5_SET field width of log_cq_size lives in unshown mlx5_ifc definitions and no visible sink admits a demonstrated failing value.

Demoted: inlen = MLX5_ST_SZ_BYTES(create_cq_in) + sizeof(u64) * npages (lines 31-32) is not a demonstrated CWE-190 overflow: no capacity on npages is visible in the fragment, and reaching an int-overflowing npages requires the unshown WQ allocation to succeed first.

Demoted as robustness (environment-driven, not attacker-scaled by the fragment): NULL of fdev->mdev (line 4) and fdev->conn_res.uar->index (line 46) would require device/init failure, and no security-relevant operation in the fragment runs on that failure state.

No other confirmed findings: format string at line 71 is a constant; all return statuses in the fragment are checked on the correct paths; no reachable abort, weak crypto, or injection sink is present in the shown code.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability: the buffer indices derived from the input stream at lines 35, 37 and 38 are bounded below the capacity declared at line 4 by the visible guard at lines 12-13 (a non-NULL end code is admitted only with STRLEN(end) <= NUMBUFLEN-1, which bounds the accumulate/continue path), by the partial-match brake at lines 39-43 (idx stays < STRLEN(end)), and by the per-iteration idx reset at line 87 for the end==NULL path; every write index remains within [0, NUMBUFLEN+MB_MAXBYTES-1].

On the admitted witness nSubrects = 2^29 (factor 8, BPP/8 = 4, wrapped product at line 19 = 0 passes the guard 0 > RFB_BUFFER_SIZE; read length 0 succeeds), the loop dereferences ptr a total of 2^32 bytes worth from a buffer whose only size reference RFB_BUFFER_SIZE appears at line 19; ptr therefore passes the end of the allocation and these reads read OOB memory, with the OOB values x/y/w/h forwarded to GotFillRect at line 29.

Integer-overflow root cause of the over-read (secondary CWE-190, independently confirmed at the confirmed sink). hdr.nSubrects (entry-point uint32 range [0, 2^32-1]) times (4 + BPP/8) wraps in 32-bit arithmetic: e.g. nSubrects = 2^29 with factor 8 computes exactly 2^32 ≡ 0, admitted by the guard on the left operand and used as the length argument on the right (read of 0 bytes succeeds under standard length semantics and no shown failure), while the loop control at line 24 still counts the unwrapped nSubrects = 2^29. The guard therefore fails to exclude values whose true product far exceeds RFB_BUFFER_SIZE; the missing protective check is a pre-multiplication cap like nSubrects <= RFB_BUFFER_SIZE / (4 + BPP/8).

assumptions: hdr.nSubrects is a 32-bit (uint32_t) field: grounded in rfbClientSwap32IfLE at line 12 (32-bit swap helper) and the network header read at line 9.

client->buffer has capacity RFB_BUFFER_SIZE bytes: the only size reference for that buffer visible in the fragment is RFB_BUFFER_SIZE used at line 19 against the same buffer; witness requires only RFB_BUFFER_SIZE >= 1.

BPP is a macro in {8,16,32}, so (4 + BPP/8) is the 5/6/8-byte per-subrect width that matches CARDBPP at line 5 and the ptr advance at line 26; the wrap is reachable for any factor >= 5 in the domain [0, 2^32-1] (exact zero residue at factor 8 dividing 2^32).

verdict.summary: Out-of-bounds read in smtp_command_parse_parameters: the max_len argument passed to uni_utf8_get_char_n at lines 19-20 is computed as (size_t)(p - parser->end), which is a strictly negative ptrdiff on every iteration admitted by the loop (p < parser->end, line 13) and wraps to ~SIZE_MAX. The decoder then ignores the true remaining byte count (parser->end - p) and on an attacker-chosen UTF-8 lead byte at the last 1-3 positions of the buffer reads continuation bytes at/ past *parser->end, outside the only visible data-region bound. Root cause is the signed-to-unsigned wrap of a negative length (CWE-195) producing the OOB read (CWE-125).

evidence.reason: Sink: uni_utf8_get_char_n reads up to a full UTF-8 sequence (2-4 bytes) from p using max_len as the available-byte count. The intended in-domain value is parser->end - p in [1, ...], so the admitted set is entirely out of domain. The callee's incomplete-sequence guard (len > max_len) never trips, and with an attacker-controlled UTF-8 lead byte (e.g. 0xC3) at end-1 the decoder reads *(p+1) = *parser->end, one byte past the only visible buffer bound; 0xE2/0xF0 leads within the last 3 bytes read 2-3 bytes past. Guards on the path (line 13, line 16 else-branch) both admit the witness; the max_size check at line 35 executes after the loop and cannot bound reads inside the loop. Primary CWE-125 OOB read; CWE-195 secondary for the negative-ptrdiff-to-size_t conversion that is the independent root cause.

assumptions: The visible data region is [parser->cur, parser->end) with end exclusive; only bound on p shown is line 13 'p < parser->end'.
Buffer contents in [cur, end) are parsed protocol input; the fragment imposes no value constraint on the bytes themselves.

No NUL terminator, slack, or capacity beyond parser->end is assumed either present or absent; if extra capacity existed it would still not make the derivation in-domain (max_len is ~SIZE_MAX regardless).

verdict.summary: The header callback passes a non-NUL-terminated network buffer to sscanf('%u\r\n') (line 21): %u skips leading whitespace, so a timelimit header whose payload is entirely whitespace (e.g. header prefix followed by '\r\n') causes the scan to read past the visible ptr+len bound (line 4) until a non-whitespace byte is found — an out-of-bounds read of adjacent memory.

evidence.reason: ptr is entry-point network header data whose only visible bound is len = size * nmemb (line 4); no statement reserves a NUL terminator or limits %u's whitespace skip. Guard line 14 (len > url->timelimit_header_len) admits len = tl_len + 2, guard line 18 admits the CRLF tail, and line 19 offsets input by tl_len, leaving a remainder such as "\r\n" that is entirely whitespace. %u skips those two bytes and reads bytes at ptr[len], ptr[len+1], ... until it finds a non-whitespace byte, i.e. an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) past the visible buffer bound; digits found in adjacent memory additionally propagate into limit, used at line 22.

assumptions: ptr points to data of exactly len bytes (size_t len = size * nmemb, line 4) with no visible NUL-termination guarantee, matching standard libcurl header-callback semantics.
url->auth_header_len and url->timelimit_header_len are size_t lengths whose values satisfy the guards on the path (any tl_len >= 1 yields a valid witness).
sizeof(url->errormsg) (line 35) is the destination capacity used by the line 41 memcpy.
limitations: The sscanf witness is a range claim rather than an exact demonstrated value: the precise value of url->timelimit_header_len is not visible, so the concrete magnitude is chosen within the guard-admitted range; hence confidence is capped at 0.55.
time(NULL) + limit (line 22) could overflow a 32-bit time_t, but discon_time's type is not shown; not confirmable, no CWE assigned.
size * nmemb (line 4) could wrap for astronomically large framework-supplied sizes; no attacker-scaled magnitude is derivable from the fragment; robustness concern only.
auth_user->client is dereferenced (line 5) before the if (client) check (line 7), a NULL-deref robustness gap whose NULL-producing registration point is outside the fragment; demoted without CWE.

Branch 1 (lines 11-12), branch 3 (lines 31-42 memcpy and termination write at line 42) are fully bounded by the visible guards: len >= url->auth_header_len, len > 24, and the copy_len cap at lines 35-37 with errormsg[copy_len-1] = 0 in bounds.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the patched (fixed) form of ntpq cookedprint for TALOS-CAN-0063. The raw-value path appends output_raw at bv[len] and NUL at bv[len+1] (lines 124-125) to the 2*MAXVALLEN-byte buffer bv (line 22), but the preceding atoascii call supplies destination capacity sizeof(bv)-1 (line 122), guaranteeing strlen(bv) <= 2*MAXVALLEN-2 so the final write index is at most 2*MAXVALLEN-1 (in bounds). The bn copy (line 119), the output_raw=='*' branch (lines 127-128), snprintf (line 91), and the LP guard (line 73) are all in-bounds. Atoascii's capacity-contract behavior is the only name-implied (callee) assumption that enters the safety argument.

assumptions: bv capacity is 2*MAXVALLEN bytes (indices 0..2*MAXVALLEN-1) per declaration `char bv[2 * MAXVALLEN];` at line 22.
bn capacity is 2*MAXVARLEN bytes per declaration `char bn[2 * MAXVARLEN];` at line 21.
lfparr has 8 elements per declaration `l_fp lfparr[8];` at line 19.
b has 12 elements per declaration `char b[12];` at line 20.

atoascii's 4th argument is a destination capacity: it is a bounded sanitized copy that writes at most outlen-1 characters and NUL-terminates within outlen bytes (implied by its name and by its use with sizeof-style arguments at lines 119, 121-122, 127-128).
limitations: Demoted: `outputarr(fp, name, narr, lfparr)` (line 100) reading up to `narr` elements of the 8-element lfparr (line 19). `narr` is set only by the unshown `decodearr` (line 97); the fragment contains no statement that bounds or that admits `narr > 8`, so the out-of-range count is not confirmable from the shown code.

Demoted: `fprintf(fp, "status=%04x %s,\n", status, statustoa(datatype, status))` (lines 27-28) would be UB only if the unshown `statustoa` returns NULL; no shown statement produces that NULL and the failure is not attacker-directed in the fragment.
Demoted robustness: `snprintf(b, sizeof(b), "%03lo", uval)` (line 91) truncates wide octal values (u_long) to 11 chars — bounded write, cosmetic truncation only.

Unconfirmable: termination of `while (nextvar(&length, &data, &name, &value))` (line 31) depends on the unshown `nextvar` contract; the fragment shows no statement that could stall or overrun the parser position.

The safety of the bv append path rests on the standard capacity semantics of `atoascii`; if a hypothetical callee violated its own capacity argument, the overflow would occur inside the callee, not at a statement shown in the fragment.

verdict.summary: The ASCII read path of GmfOpenMesh feeds attacker-controlled file tokens into fscanf(msh->hdl, "%s", str) with no width limit, overflowing the stack buffer char str[GmfStrSiz] declared at line 5 (CWE-121). The filename-length guard at lines 39-40 only protects strcpy(msh->FilNam, FilNam) at line 42 and does not constrain token length. Additionally, PtrVer/PtrDim are extracted from varargs at lines 71-72 with no NULL check and unconditionally dereferenced at lines 152-153 (CWE-476).

evidence.reason: The %s conversion has no width limit and writes the full whitespace-delimited token plus a NUL terminator into str, whose only visible capacity is GmfStrSiz from the declaration at line 5. File contents are entry-point input with no shown bound on token length; a token of GmfStrSiz or more characters (e.g., GmfStrSiz 'A's followed by whitespace in a .mesh file, admitted by the extension checks at lines 53-54 and the ASCII branch at line 119) overflows the stack buffer during the call, before the EOF test at lines 130-131. The only related guard, strlen(FilNam)+7 >= GmfStrSiz at lines 39-40, constrains FilNam only and executes before this sink, so it admits the witness path. Primary mechanism: CWE-121 stack-based buffer overflow via unbounded copy over the visible capacity at line 5.

Second unbounded %s read into the same GmfStrSiz-sized stack buffer (declaration line 5). The Dimension scan loop at lines 138-141 admits tokens of any length; an attacker token of length >= GmfStrSiz overwrites str beyond its capacity during the fscanf call, before the EOF check at lines 143-144. No shown statement bounds token length on this path. CWE-121 stack-based buffer overflow.

PtrVer and PtrDim are pointer-typed entries obtained at lines 71-72 from the variadic argument list with no NULL check in the shown code, and are dereferenced unconditionally at lines 152-153 after the dimension check at lines 149-150 admits the path. Per the pointer-parameter standard, no shown NULL producer is required; the absence of the check is itself the demonstrated flaw. Mechanism: CWE-476 NULL pointer dereference causing a write at 0 in GmfRead mode when a caller passes NULL for either pointer.

assumptions: char str[GmfStrSiz] at line 5 provides a visible buffer capacity of GmfStrSiz bytes; all overflow claims are measured against this declaration.

The guard at lines 39-40 (reject when strlen(FilNam)+7 >= GmfStrSiz, admit strlen(FilNam) <= GmfStrSiz-8) fully protects the strcpy at line 42, which writes at most GmfStrSiz-7 bytes; this assumes msh->FilNam is an array of at least GmfStrSiz bytes, consistent with the guard's use of GmfStrSiz.
GmfRead and GmfWrite are distinct int mode constants so the branches at lines 63 and 170 partition the mod space; the final else frees and returns.
limitations: Out-of-range numeric values accepted by the %d scans (safe_fscanf at lines 133 and 146) into int are not reported: the values are subsequently rejected by the visible 1..4 and 2..3 checks, so no security-relevant downstream consumption of a wrapped value is shown.

MshIdx = (int64_t)msh at line 16 is an implementation-defined pointer-to-int64 conversion consumed only as an opaque mesh handle in line 168 and in GmfSetKwd; no in-scope misuse as a pointer is demonstrated.

The exact numeric offset of the overflow depends on the constant GmfStrSiz, whose value is not shown; the witness is therefore a complete residual-range claim (every token length >= GmfStrSiz overflows) rather than a single numeric magnitude.
Loop non-termination in the token-scan do/while loops is not reported: on finite files the loops end at EOF, and on adversarial input the overflow at lines 127/140 already occurs earlier.
The write-path indexing GmfKwdFmt[GmfVersionFormatted][0] / GmfKwdFmt[GmfDimension][0] uses compile-time constant indices with no input-derived component, so no out-of-range indexing is confirmed.

verdict.summary: The overflow guard at line 8 is bypassable: for add_len == SIZE_MAX the subexpression (SIZE_MAX - add_len - 1) underflows to SIZE_MAX, so with target->len == 0 both conditions are false and no early return fires. target->len + add_len + 1 then wraps to 0, the reallocation branch at line 13 is skipped, and memcpy at line 33 copies add_len = SIZE_MAX bytes into the existing (too-small) buffer while the null-terminator write at line 36 indexes target->str[SIZE_MAX] — a heap buffer overflow (CWE-787) rooted in the wrapping guard arithmetic (CWE-190).

evidence.reason: add_len is the size_t parameter with full residual range [0, SIZE_MAX]; the only guard (line 8) fails to exclude add_len == SIZE_MAX because (SIZE_MAX - add_len - 1) underflows to SIZE_MAX and (SIZE_MAX - add_len) = 0 < 0 is false when target->len == 0, so the guard's return is skipped. With target->len == 0 the sum at line 13 wraps to 0, the realloc block (lines 15-28) is skipped for any target->size > 0, and this memcpy writes add_len = SIZE_MAX bytes into the existing buffer whose capacity is target->size <= SIZE_MAX per the line 28 bookkeeping — a heap buffer overflow (CWE-787), with the wrapping guard arithmetic as secondary root cause (CWE-190).

On the same admitted path (target->len == 0, add_len == SIZE_MAX, guard at line 8 bypassed, line 13 realloc branch skipped), line 35 sets target->len = SIZE_MAX, so this write targets index SIZE_MAX, which exceeds valid indices 0..target->size-1 for every possible capacity target->size <= SIZE_MAX — a confirmed out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) even independent of the memcpy overflow at line 33.

assumptions: target->len, target->size are size_t fields with full domain [0, SIZE_MAX]; the fragment establishes no lower bound, so target->len == 0 (the empty-string base state) and target->size == 16 remain in the residual ranges.
target->size tracks the allocated capacity: line 26 allocates newsize and line 28 records target->size = newsize, so valid buffer indices are 0..target->size-1.
simplestring_init_str (line 5) initializes target to the empty-string state; its body is not shown, so nothing in the fragment derives a guaranteed minimum for target->len.
limitations: The primary witness requires target->len == 0, a zero-length boundary state whose minimum is not established by any shown statement, so confidence is capped at 0.65.

NULL-deref of target at line 2: target->size is read before the NULL test at line 3, and line 3's own existence shows NULL is an intended admissible input; this is a real reachable crash (CWE-476, DoS-level) but is caller-dependent and secondary to the overflow finding.
Failure of simplestring_init_str (return discarded, body not shown) leaves no in-fragment unsafe use because downstream writes are gated on target->str at line 31; treated as a robustness concern.
If realloc at line 26 fails, str is set NULL and the copy block is skipped (graceful, though the old buffer leaks); the single-shot leak is not volume-compounded and is not a finding.
gcc/clang unsigned wrap is defined behavior; the flaw is incorrect guard arithmetic (CWE-190/682), not undefined behavior.

verdict.summary: unlzw's output-chain decompression writes below the de_stack base with no visible bound: stackp is reset to de_stack (line 112) and *--stackp stores (lines 136, 142, 145) execute for every decoded code, with the number of stores driven by attacker-controlled codes (line 93) and allowed to reach the full dictionary size (maxbits <= BITS, line 33). No statement bounds stackp against any de_stack capacity, so an input-derived chain length is consumed as an unbounded write count (missing bound, CWE-787), with a matching out-of-bounds read through the subsequent memcpy at lines 156/169.

evidence.reason: Primary sink: the write count to this decrement-then-store is the chain length derived from attacker-controlled decoded codes (input() at line 93, residual range [0, (1<<n_bits)-1] with n_bits admitted up to maxbits <= BITS per line 33). stackp is set to de_stack at line 112 and the loop guard at line 140 (code >= 256) plus the unconditional store at line 145 admit every non-first code, so the first store lands at de_stack[-1] and a chain of length k stores k+1 bytes below the base. No statement in the fragment bounds stackp against de_stack or declares de_stack's capacity: the out-of-domain write count is a confirmed missing bound (unvalidated-size flow) causing memory corruption (CWE-787).

Second sink of the same root cause: this unconditional store executes after the chain loop with stackp still at de_stack when the chain is empty, and below it otherwise; even a zero-length chain writes de_stack[-1]. The write is unbounded in the shown code (no stackp bound, no de_stack capacity visible), consuming an attacker-derived chain length/offset (line 93) as the write position, CWE-787.

Third sink of the same root cause in the KwKwK special case (code == free_ent, admitted by the guard at line 115): executes *--stackp with stackp == de_stack from line 112, storing at de_stack[-1] with no shown guarantee that de_stack-1 is writable storage and no bound derived from a visible de_stack capacity; input-derived code values (line 93) control reachability. CWE-787.

assumptions: maxbits is an 8-bit value from get_byte() (line 24) and the guard at line 33 (maxbits > BITS -> ERROR) admits only maxbits <= BITS, where BITS is a positive decoder width constant whose numeric value is not visible.

de_stack is a buffer whose base is the anchor for stackp (line 112); its declared capacity is NOT present in the fragment, which is precisely why the confirmed finding is the missing bound per the OOB standard.

The inbuf/insize/inptr window is assumed consistently maintained: the shift loop at lines 63-65 never indexes past insize-1, and aligned posbits from lines 82-83/105-106 stay <= inbits because inbits (lines 77-78) is a multiple of n_bits<<3, so e = insize - (posbits>>3) (line 61) stays non-negative on the aligned path.
limitations: The exact numeric excess of the de_stack underflow cannot be computed because the de_stack allocation/declaration is not in the fragment; the finding is reported as the missing bound, and impact magnitude is layout-dependent (confidence capped accordingly, range-based, no exact-value witness).

A bit-exact witness stream is not constructed because the input() macro body (line 93) is not shown; the claim rests on the residual-range analysis (chain length unbounded relative to any visible capacity).

If read_error() (lines 71-73) or gzip_error (lines 98, 132-134) returns instead of terminating, execution continues (insize += rsize at line 74, and the chain walk at lines 136-145), which would be additional error/status-handling flaws (CWE-754) — demoted because termination semantics are not shown.

tab_suffixof(code)/tab_prefixof(code) indexing at lines 142-143/176-177 with code possibly above the table size when maxbits < INIT_BITS (n_bits grows past maxbits, lines 84-90) is a potential table OOB read but the table capacity is not shown; demoted.

For maxbits < INIT_BITS, n_bits never equals maxbits at line 85, so the n_bits bump path would not stop purely by width, but free_ent growth is capped at maxmaxcode by the entry-creation guard at line 174, so growth terminates; no confirmed unbounded shift or non-termination.
outbuf writes (line 99) and copies (lines 156, 169) are internally consistent with the OUTBUFSIZ flush guards at lines 151-153/159; no confirmed outbuf overflow.

verdict.summary: decode_errcode_attr trusts the STUN attribute length field read from the wire by GETATTRHDR (line 13) without validating it. value.slen = attr->hdr.length - 4 (line 19) is passed as the copy length to pj_strdup (line 22) with no bound tying it to the message bytes: lengths 0..3 underflow to -4..-1 (huge size_t at the copy) and lengths up to 65535 exceed the actual message, producing an out-of-bounds read of the entry-point buffer buf via value.ptr = buf + ATTR_HDR_LEN + 4 (line 18). buf[6] and buf[7] are likewise read unconditionally at line 15 with no length check. The message-length bound that could have protected these reads is explicitly discarded via PJ_UNUSED_ARG(msghdr) (line 9).

evidence.reason: Sink: pj_strdup consumes value.slen as the allocation/copy byte count. value.slen = attr->hdr.length - 4 (line 19) is derived from the unvalidated 16-bit wire length field populated by GETATTRHDR(buf, &attr->hdr) (line 13); the attribute length is a parameter-derived entry-point value with residual range 0..65535 because no shown statement checks length >= 4 or bounds it against the remaining message (msghdr is unused at line 9). Witness: length=0 gives value.slen=-4, which at line 22 converts to a huge size_t and copies from value.ptr = buf + ATTR_HDR_LEN + 4 (line 18), an out-of-bounds read of buf; length=65535 gives a 65531-byte copy. Missing bound on an input-derived size/length consumed as a memory-copy parameter (CWE-125).

Sink: unconditional reads of buf[6] and buf[7] with no check that the entry-point STUN attribute input contains at least 8 bytes. The only established extent in the fragment is the 4-byte header read by GETATTRHDR(buf, &attr->hdr) (line 13); no guard bounds buf's extent, so a short attacker-supplied attribute yields an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125, missing bound).

assumptions: attr->hdr.length is populated from the wire by GETATTRHDR(buf, &attr->hdr) (line 13) and is a 16-bit STUN attribute length with domain 0..65535; no statement in the fragment constrains it.
value.slen is a signed byte-count member of pj_str_t whose value flows unmodified into pj_strdup as the copy length (allocation size / memcpy length), per the name-implied semantics of pj_strdup.
buf is an entry-point input (message attribute bytes); the fragment shows no constraint on its extent.
limitations: The struct definitions (pj_stun_errcode_attr / pj_stun_attr_hdr / pj_str_t) and the GETATTRHDR macro body are not shown; the residual ranges rely on the 16-bit STUN length wire format and pj_strdup's length-as-byte-count semantics.

NULL p_attr at line 25 and a NULL attr from PJ_POOL_ZALLOC_T at line 12 are caller/pool-failure robustness concerns, demoted because NULL cannot be produced on any shown path and the failures are not attacker-directed.
The discarded pj_strdup return value and unconditional return PJ_SUCCESS (line 27) are an error-handling candidate with no confirmed security-relevant operation on the failure state; demoted.
Whether the buf[6]/buf[7] overread at line 15 manifests depends on the (unshown) receiving layer not pre-checking the attribute size; within the fragment the missing bound at the read is confirmed.

verdict.summary: In io_read, the byte count 'io_size' captured at line 11 from the user-derived iterator is never re-derived after iov_iter_revert, and in the async reissue path the loop performs io_size -= ret with an unconstrained signed 'ret'; a read returning -EAGAIN (a negative ret) after consuming bytes inflates io_size above the originally admitted request length while concurrently deflating rw->bytes_done. The inflated io_size feeds req->result (line 12) and the subsequent read/completion length, so the kernel reports to userspace a read length larger than the bytes actually delivered by the reissued operations, and can re-issue reads over the previously delivered byte range, corrupting the per-request accounting result.

evidence.reason: Byte-count overflow sink CWE-190: 'ret' is the return of io_iter_do_read (line 25 and line 38) whose sign the fragment never clamps; the branch at line 26 admits ret == -EAGAIN (negative ssize_t, e.g. the value -11 for -EAGAIN) into this arithmetic. io_size was set once at line 11 from iov_iter_count(iter) and is not re-derived after the iov_iter_revert at line 30, while the loop at line 43-45 offers no ret >= 0 guard, so io_size can grow strictly above the originally admitted request total (io_size -= -EAGAIN => io_size + 11) and rw->bytes_done shrinks by the same amount; the corrupted io_size flows to req->result (line 12, reported to userspace as the read length) and to kiocb_done byte counting. No statement in the fragment caps io_size, and the loop condition ret > 0 && ret < io_size only tests ret>0 before re-iterating; it does not prevent the negative-ret arithmetic, so every guard on the path admits the witness io_size=100, ret=-11.

assumptions: io_import_iovec success (check at lines 13-14) yields an initialized iter whose count is the total of the user-provided iovec lengths; the fragment places no numeric cap on io_size, so io_size retains the full non-negative count domain.

io_iter_do_read returns a signed ssize_t (bytes read or a negative error like -EAGAIN) per line 25 and branches at lines 26/33/35, and the fragment itself models io_size -= ret, rw->bytes_done += ret over that value, so byte-count arithmetic over the signed domain is exercised by the shown statements.
The buffer written by io_iter_do_read stays within the user iov capacity because iter was built from user iovecs by io_import_iovec, and io_import_iovec is itself return-checked at lines 14-16.
Branch at line 27 -EAGAIN path is reached with 'some cases will consume bytes even on error returns' comment, so a partially-delivered read returning -EAGAIN is an admitted input state.
limitations: The exact body of io_iter_do_read, io_import_iovec, and io_rw_should_retry are not shown; the fragment-level confirmed defect does not depend on them, but the concrete reachability of -EAGAIN after a partial delivery depends on library/OS read behavior not visible in the fragment, so confidence is capped below a fully self-contained witness.

The re-delivery of the same byte range of the user buffer by the revert-and-reread sequence (iov_iter_revert at line 30 followed by later io_iter_do_read at line 38) and the resulting stale/duplicated content semantics is a real behavioral consequence but was demoted to limitations for lack of caller-level delivery guarantees; it is not reported as a separate CWE-754/125 finding.* …

A NULL-deref/UAF of the iovec pointer was rejected because line 2 initializes iovec to the inline stack array and io_import_iovec/io_setup_async_rw success is return-checked; kfree(iovec) at line 45 is guarded by if (iovec) on the same-control path that sets iovec = NULL after async setup begins.

No OOB write is claimed beyond the user iov capacity: io_iter_do_read writes are bounded by the iterator built from user iovecs, so only the byte-count/result corruption (CWE-190) is confirmed; CWE-754 (error handling) is noted as a related but not independently confirmed secondary mechanism.
Non-termination (CWE-835) was rejected: loop re-entry requires positive ret and each positive ret strictly decreases io_size.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability in the fragment. Every attacker-derived size/index is covered by visible protective statements: the pixel buffer allocation size_t image->rows * MagickMax(bytes_per_line, image->columns+256UL) is at least rows*bytes_per_line == length, the per-scanline conversions (cases 1,4,8,16,24,32) all re-derive bytes_per_line to equal-or-smaller strides with strict index bounds ending at columns-1, and the colormap path is bounded by colors <= 2^bpp <= 256 with byte-count equality checks, and the 64-bit length computation cannot wrap under the admitted width/height ranges.

verdict.summary: uncompressEntry passes the caller-supplied int index to the unchecked array subscript entries.getUnchecked(index) at line 3 (and again to createStreamForEntry(index) at line 22) with no bounds validation anywhere in the fragment. index retains the full int domain as its residual range, and no capacity for entries is shown, so an out-of-range index produces an out-of-bounds read of the entries array (CWE-125, missing bound). The archive-specific write-outside attacks (zip-slip via '../' and absolute paths, and writing through symlinked parent directories) are covered by the shown guards: targetFile.isAChildOf(targetDirectory) at line 16 and hasSymbolicPart(...) at line 36.

evidence.reason: Sink is an unchecked array subscript. The parameter index (line 1) is an internal-helper input whose residual range is the full int domain: no statement in the fragment constrains it (line 3 is the first executable statement, and getUnchecked performs no bounds check by name). No capacity for the entries container is declared in the fragment, so the missing bound itself is the defect: any index outside [0, entries.size()) - e.g. -1 - reads past the array, an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) of a ZipEntry record whose fields are subsequently used for paths and timestamps.

Second sink for the same unvalidated index flow: createStreamForEntry consumes the same out-of-range int that already produced the out-of-bounds read at line 3, forwarding it into an entry lookup with no shown capacity or bounds check. The shown code derives no bound for index, and neither this call nor any earlier statement guards it, so the argument is not provably in the domain the helper requires (out-of-bounds read of entry metadata).

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. Every dangerous operation in this open_table fragment carries a visible protective statement: the memcmp over table-cache keys is gated by the equality check `table->s->table_cache_key.length == key_length` (L70-71, bounding the byte count on both buffers), MDL ticket use after acquisition is gated by `open_table_get_mdl_lock(...) || mdl_ticket == NULL` before the later `mdl_ticket->get_deadlock_weight()` dereference is reachable, `table_list->db.str` is NULL-checked before any use, `part_names_error` is initialized to 0 before any read, and all share/malloc/entry-finalize/version-check statuses are checked before their artifacts are used. Remaining concerns (caller-supplied ticket under HAS_MDL_LOCK, cache-list NULL termination, alias NUL termination, table->file initialization) depend on invariants not stated as protective claims within the fragment and cannot be anchored to a confirmed mechanism.

notes.assumptions: Line numbers are 1-based ordinals within the pasted fragment. `get_table_def_key(table_list, &key)` at L55 both fills the key buffer and returns its length; `table_cache_key.length == key_length` equality at L70 therefore bounds the subsequent memcmp byte count to the compared object's own length field on both sides. `open_table_get_mdl_lock(...) || mdl_ticket == NULL` (≈L227-229) confines the later non-NULL-ticket requirement on the non-HAS_MDL_LOCK path before the flush-block dereference (≈L300) is reachable. `part_names_error=0` initialization at L13 precedes the `if (part_names_error)` read (≈L375s) within the partition block; `from_share=false` (L11) and the exhaustive gts_flags assignment (≈L262-266 filter if/else-if/else) precede the reset-path use of both variables. The `if (!table_list->db.str)` check at L48 precedes every later use of db.str (`get_table_def_key` L55, error messages L135s, tdc_wait_for_old_version L300s) on every fall-through path.
notes.limitations: Covered: memcmp key-length flow — rejected as a confirmed OOB read because L70's equality admits exactly n == table_cache_key.length on the executing short-circuited path; the key side of the memcmp is bounded by the paired return of get_table_def_key at L55. Demoted NULL-deref candidates whose NULL would originate outside the fragment's shown statements: table->file before reset-path assert/MYSQL_REBIND (file set by cache/share machinery not shown), view->view_db.str/table_list->alias.str as C strings for error messages and my_strcasecmp (framework NUL-termination invariant not shown), thd->open_tables list terminators relied on by the propagation loop at L67 (THD invariant not shown). mdl_ticket under MYSQL_OPEN_HAS_MDL_LOCK is assigned without a local NULL check and depends on the fragment comment stating the caller acquired the referenced ticket — caller-dependent, so recorded as limitation, not a finding. Debug-only DBUG_ASSERT reachable-abort candidates are demoted (CWE-617 not confirmed because no admitted value reaches them on a shown path producing the failing condition). The on-sensitive-path dereferences of thd->mdl_context/ot_ctx after acquire_lock failure checks are routine NULL-safety and not attacker-directed failure of environment calls; no positive finding arises.

verdict.summary: GmfOpenMesh dereferences caller-supplied pointers without NULL checks: the vararg output pointers PtrVer/PtrDim (read at lines 71-72) are unconditionally written through at lines 152-153, and the FilNam parameter is passed to strlen at line 39 with no NULL validation. A caller passing NULL to any of these reaches a NULL-pointer write/read and the process crashes (NULL-pointer dereference, CWE-476, DoS).

evidence.reason: CWE-476 NULL-pointer dereference. PtrVer is an int* extracted from the caller's varargs at line 71 and its declared domain includes NULL; no shown statement checks it for NULL. It reaches the sink via mod==GmfRead (line 63), with the dim/ver guards (lines 149-150, 105-106) admitting {2,3}/{1..4} independently without constraining PtrVer. The dereference at line 152 is unconditional, so the fragment has no protective statement covering the sink and the admitted set includes NULL, crashing the process (DoS, low severity DoS barrier).

CWE-476 NULL-pointer dereference. PtrDim is an int* read from varargs at line 72 with declared domain including NULL; no shown check filters it before the unconditional write at line 152-153 path passes every guard (mod==GmfRead, dim==2..3 independent of pointer value). verdict.summary: unlzw writes decompressed symbols below the start of de_stack: every expansion begins with stackp = de_stack (L101) and pushes via *--stackp (L120, L126, L129). The number of pushes (1 + prefix-chain depth) is fully input-controlled — the LZW table grows to free_ent up to MAXCODE(maxbits)-1 under L157 and the KwKwK guard only rejects code > free_ent (L104), explicitly admitting code == free_ent — and no shown statement bounds this count against any capacity of de_stack. A crafted stream (maxbits = BITS, then table growth, then a code == free_ent expand) writes unboundedly below the object (missing-bound / unvalidated-length write), enabling memory corruption; the outbuf flush logic (L135-155) bounds a different object and does not protect de_stack.

evidence.reason: Primary sink, CWE-787 (out-of-bounds write below de_stack). code is a decoded LZW code admitted by L103 (code >= free_ent) and L104 (code > free_ent rejects only codes above free_ent); the chain walk decrements stackp one element below de_stack for every iteration and is terminated only by the strictly decreasing prefix chain created at L159-161, not by any bound on de_stack's capacity (none exists in the fragment). The length count 1+depth is input-derived, ranges up to ~2^BITS with maxbits <= BITS admitted at L33, and is never compared against the de_stack object size; for any finite de_stack capacity an admitted code == free_ent input (KwKwK case, L120 then this loop) writes out of bounds. The other shown guards (L33, L88-89, L157, L135-155) bound maxbits, the first code, table growth, and the outbuf flush respectively, not the push count, so they do not cover this sink.

Same missing-bound write flow: the final push lands one element further below de_stack after the L126 loop; for a code == free_ent expansion (admitted by L103/L104) whose oldcode chain approaches free_ent (grown to maxmaxcode-1 under L157), the total writes below de_stack reach 1+chain-depth with no visible cap on the target object, confirming CWE-787 at this sink.

KwKwK special-case push: stackp is still de_stack (set at L101), so this unconditional *--stackp with code == free_ent (admitted by L103, not excluded by L104) already writes one byte below the object's base, then hands code = oldcode (L121) into the unbounded chain walk; no check limits the total depth. It is the entry point of the confirmed CWE-787 underflow.

assumptions: table chains strictly decrease: from L159-161 each entry code = free_ent is created with prefix = oldcode where oldcode was admitted smaller than free_ent, so the L124-128 walk always terminates at a symbol < 256 within at most free_ent steps

maxbits residual range is 0..BITS after L30/L33, so all decoded codes and free_ent lie below 2^BITS (BITS, INIT_BITS, FIRST, MAXCODE, BLOCK_MODE, BIT_MASK, LZW_RESERVED, CLEAR values are unshown constants, used only as ranges)

verdict.summary: In yank_copy_line, the trailing-space trim loop dereferences bd->textstart + s - 1 before testing s > 0 (left-to-right && short-circuit). On an admitted input (exclude_trailing_space != 0, textlen >= 1, all-whitespace text), s reaches 0 and the next condition evaluation performs a one-byte out-of-bounds read at bd->textstart[-1] (heap/out-of-extent over-read, missing bound).

evidence.reason: Unconstrained field bd->textlen flows into s at line 19 (bd->endspaces is forced to 0 at line 6 on the exclude path). The guard at line 21 evaluates the dereference *(bd->textstart + s - 1) BEFORE s > 0 due to left-to-right && short-circuit, so s == 0 is admitted: with textlen == 1 and textstart[0] a space, line 23 computes s = 1 - 0 - 1 = 0, and the next condition check reads bd->textstart[-1]. No shown statement bounds s >= 1 before the dereference, so the read at negative offset outside the visible text extent textstart..textstart+textlen-1 is unguarded: missing-bound heap/out-of-extent over-read (CWE-125).

assumptions: Destination capacity from line 7 is bd->startspaces + bd->endspaces + bd->textlen + 1, matching the later fills and the NUL at line 27.
On the exclude path, line 6 sets bd->endspaces = 0, so s at line 19 equals bd->textlen.
VIM_ISWHITE(' ') is true and mb_head_off returns 0 for a single-byte ASCII space (name-implied semantics), which is what makes s decrement by exactly 1 per iteration.
limitations: The write y_current->y_array[y_idx] = pnew at line 10 uses the unconstrained long y_idx with no visible y_array capacity; it is demoted because the fragment derives no out-of-domain value from it (unchanged index forwarded from the caller), so it persists identically in any fixed counterpart.
NULL dereference of bd or bd->textstart is not confirmed: no NULL producer is shown in the fragment; it is a caller-contract/robustness concern.

Integer overflow of the line 7 allocation size and negative bd->startspaces/endspaces/textlen values cast to size_t at lines 11/13/15 cannot be confirmed because the field types and ranges are not declared in the fragment.
A textlen == 0 input also triggers the read of textstart[-1] immediately, but the primary witness uses textlen == 1 and does not rely on that degenerate case.
Whether bd->textstart[-1] lands inside some unshown source-line allocation is not visible here; the confirmed defect is the unguarded negative-offset read at line 21.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the patched form of ReadPSDChannelPixels. The depth<=1 bit-expansion path caps number_bits to the remaining columns (lines 61-63) and the boundary guard at lines 69-70 keeps the loop and q/x advancement in exact correspondence, so both SetPSDPixel sink sites (lines 52 and 66-67) write exactly image->columns entries with x in 0..columns-1 against the row capacity established at line 27. No protected-by-a-visible-statement vulnerability is confirmed; pixel-buffer capacity and NULL-pixels concerns are unshown caller contracts.

assumptions: Line 27's q=GetAuthenticPixels(image,0,row,image->columns,1,exception); establishes a one-row quantum cache of exactly image->columns pixels, which is the visible capacity of the q target.
Line 30's indexes=GetAuthenticIndexQueue(image); yields an index queue with the same row geometry (image->columns entries), consistent with every SetPSDPixel call passing x in 0..columns-1.

Packet reads advance p by 1, 2, or 4 bytes per outer iteration (lines 35, 39, 47), but the capacity of the caller-supplied pixels buffer is not visible in the fragment, so reads from p are not claimed as bounded here.
limitations: The pixels/p buffer size is caller-established and not visible; total reads (columns*packet_size for depth>1, about ceil(columns/8)*packet_size for depth<=1) cannot be checked against a visible capacity, so no OOB-read verdict is issued for p.

pixels is dereferenced at line 35 without a NULL check on the shown path; a NULL would arise only from a caller contract violation, not from any shown derivation, so it is treated as a robustness concern rather than a confirmed CWE-476.

GetAuthenticIndexQueue (line 30) and GetPSDPacketSize (line 31) returns are unchecked, but their failure consequences would manifest inside unshown helpers (SetPSDPixel, Push*Pixel), so they are not confirmable in this fragment.

The (ssize_t) image->columns casts at lines 32, 61, and 69 are implementation-defined for columns > SSIZE_MAX; no value or guard in the fragment derives such a width, so no negative-loop-bypass finding is issued.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. The accumulator write into command at line 115 is fully bounded by guard 116-117 ((size_t)(p-command) < MagickPathExtent-1) plus the flush/reset at 119-120: data writes never exceed index MagickPathExtent-2 and the NUL never exceeds index MagickPathExtent-1, within command[MagickPathExtent] declared at line 9. The only other suspicious conversion (negative PCL box to size_t at 153-154) feeds only bounded format strings and the delegate geometry option, with no in-fragment memory/index/length sink.

The loop-top invariant p-command <= MagickPathExtent-2 is maintained because the guard at 116-117 admits continued accumulation only while p-command < MagickPathExtent-1, and otherwise lines 119-120 terminate the NUL and reset p to command.
Loop 108-159 terminates because every path (including the continue at 111) executes the for-increment ReadBlobByte and ends at EOF.
limitations: Negative/decreasing PCL MediaBox coordinates (e.g., MediaBox [10 10 5 5]) convert to a huge size_t page dimension at lines 153-158; this is a CWE-681-style sign-conversion concern, but in this fragment the value only reaches bounded FormatLocaleString writes (168-169, 192-195) and the delegate geometry string (221-222) - no in-fragment security-relevant consumer - so no CWE is attached.

The status returned by ExternalDelegateCommand (221-222) is not consulted before ReadImage (223), but delegate failure reliably surfaces as ReadImage returning NULL and is handled at 227-228; no security-relevant operation runs on a failed state, so this is only a robustness note.
Unchecked allocations AcquireString (186-187) and CloneImageInfo (197) fail only on non-attacker-scaled OOM, which is excluded from findings by the environment-failure rule.

The delegate command (214-218) is executed for format strings from GetDelegateCommands with arguments density/options and unique temporary filenames (read_info->filename, input_filename from AcquireUniqueSymbolicLink), so the attacker-controlled original filename does not appear in the command line; command/argument injection is not demonstrable from this fragment.

verdict.summary: cp_create() stores the options-derived tccp->maxrlvls (atoi of the OPT_MAXRLVLS token, line 166) into tccp->prcwidthexpns/prcheightexpns at lines 283-284 using rlvlno as an unbounded index; no upper-bound check exists before the writes (the only maxrlvls check, line 376, runs after the loop and only rejects values < 1), so an options string with a large maxrlvls causes an out-of-bounds heap write (CWE-787).
