For any finite capacity C of prcwidthexpns/prcheightexpns (capacity not declared in the fragment), maxrlvls = C+1 passes the guard and writes index C — an out-of-domain index derivation consuming an input-derived size with no visible bound; heap OOB write into the jpc_enc_tccp_t embedded in the line-28 allocation, primary CWE-787.

image is a pointer-typed parameter whose residual range is the full pointer domain including NULL — no NULL check appears anywhere in the fragment before this unconditional dereference (repeated at lines 51-80, 244-245, 261-265, 272, 275). NULL reaching line 47 is an unconditional NULL-pointer dereference; secondary CWE-476.

assumptions: cp is heap-allocated at line 28 and tccp->prcwidthexpns/prcheightexpns are members of the embedded jpc_enc_tccp_t, so writes beyond their (unshown) capacity corrupt heap memory.
jpc_atoaf on success fills exactly numilyrrates double values, making the copy loop at lines 325-327 (bound i < numlyrs-1 == numilyrrates) in-bounds against the line 321-322 allocation.
jas_taginfo_nonull(...) is NULL-tolerant by its name, so dereferencing its result is not treated as a finding.
limitations: The capacity of tccp->prcwidthexpns/prcheightexpns is not declared in the fragment, so the OOB witness is a range claim (any maxrlvls greater than the unknown capacity); confidence capped at 0.55.
If uint_fast16_t is 16-bit and maxrlvls > 65535, rlvlno wraps 65535->0 and the loop at lines 282-285 fails to terminate (CWE-835); this is platform-dependent and not asserted.

Unsigned arithmetic (imgareatlx *= hsteplcm at 234/242, refgrdwidth sums at 244-245, tilegrdoffx+tilewidth at 305-306, numhtiles*numvtiles at 317) can wrap, but no security-relevant operation in the shown code consumes a wrapped value.

The jas_tvparser_next return status (ret, lines 106/218) is discarded after the loop, so a mid-parse failure continues with partially parsed options; no confirmed security impact is derivable from the shown code.
A very long OPT_ILYRRATES value list could drive a large allocation at lines 321-322 (possible resource exhaustion), but jpc_atoaf internals and any input-length bound are not shown.

verdict.summary: Tensor::FromProto derives the element count N = shape.num_elements() from the attacker-supplied tensor_shape and forwards it to Helper<T>::Decode(a, content, N) with no visible validation against the byte length of proto.tensor_content(). The only guards are N > 0 (line 8) and content non-empty (line 10), so an admitted input such as N=1 with DT_FLOAT and a 1-byte content makes Decode read 4 bytes from a 1-byte buffer, an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). The same unvalidated N is forwarded to FromProtoField<T>(a, proto, N) on the empty-content path.

evidence.reason: N (int64_t) is derived only from proto.tensor_shape() via shape.num_elements() (line 7) and is constrained only by N > 0 (line 8), leaving residual range [1, INT64_MAX]; content is constrained only by !empty() (line 10), leaving residual range >= 1 byte. No shown statement bounds N * sizeof(T) against content.size(). Witness: N=1, dtype=DT_FLOAT, content of size 1 byte passes lines 4, 5, 8, and 10, and reaches the sink, where decoding 1 element requires 4 bytes but only 1 is present, causing a 3-byte out-of-bounds read from content (CWE-125). The 1-byte capacity is the string's own size; the missing bound is the defect.

On the empty-tensor_content path the same input-derived count N (residual range [1, INT64_MAX], line 7, guarded only by N > 0 at line 8) is forwarded as the element count to FromProtoField<T>(a, proto, N). The fragment shows no statement relating N to the number of populated per-dtype *_val fields in proto, so a proto whose shape declares more elements than the fields carry drives the same unvalidated-size read (CWE-125). Confidence is slightly lower than the Decode sink because the callee receives the proto itself, but the call site still supplies an unvalidated count.

assumptions: Helper<T>::Decode(a, content, N) has the standard semantics implied by its name and arguments: it decodes N elements of type T from the byte string content, requiring sizeof(T) * N bytes.
proto.tensor_content() is a byte string whose size() is the number of bytes available to Decode.
proto.dtype() members other than DT_INVALID (e.g., DT_FLOAT, DT_UINT8) are in the enum's declared domain and admitted by line 5; sizeof(T) >= 1 for the dispatched types.
TensorShape::IsValid (line 4) validates the shape but, from the shown code, establishes no relationship between num_elements() and the byte payload.
limitations: CHECK_NOTNULL(a) at line 2 aborts on a NULL Allocator*, which is in the parameter's declared domain, but a is an internal-helper parameter; NULL here is a caller contract violation rather than a value the shown code derives from attack data, so it is treated as a robustness concern (demoted, no CWE).
Integer overflow of N * sizeof(T) or of num_elements() itself would occur only inside callees whose bodies are not shown; not assessed as a separate finding.

If a callee internally validates content.size() or the repeated-field sizes, the flaw would be neutralized, but no such protective statement appears anywhere in the fragment, and per the call-site standard the shown code must itself supply an in-domain argument.

The exact number of bytes over-read depends on the attacker-chosen content length; the demonstrated minimum over-read (3 bytes with N=1, DT_FLOAT, 1-byte content) is anchored to the minima the shown guards admit.

verdict.summary: Out-of-bounds heap write in FractionalAvgPool-style backprop: row_seq_tensor/col_seq_tensor values are read as int64 indices with no non-negativity (or range) validation. A negative in_row_start or in_col_start propagates into in_index, which is used as the column index in Eigen coeffRef on the heap-allocated in_backprop temp matrix (width = in_cols*in_rows*in_batch), writing before the buffer. Witness: orig shape [1,4,4,1], out dims [1,1,1,1], row_seq=[-100,2], col_seq=[0,2] yields in_index=-4 at the sink.

evidence.reason: CWE-787 heap out-of-bounds write. in_index is computed at line 115 as (b*in_rows + in_r)*in_cols + in_c, where in_r ranges from unvalidated in_row_start (line 98, full int64_t residual range; only the sequence element count is checked at line 38, never the values) to in_row_end, which line 101 clamps only from above. With in_rows=4, in_cols=4, in_batch=1, out dims all 1, overlapping_=true, row_seq=[-100,2], col_seq=[0,2], iteration b=0,r=0,c=0,in_r=-1,in_c=0,d=0 passes lines 24-26, 38, 44, 59-70, and 101/106 (clamps admit it) and reaches this coeffRef call with in_index=-4. The target matrix has rows=in_depth and cols=in_cols*in_rows*in_batch (lines 86-88) over the 16-element temp tensor allocated at lines 81-83, so storage offset d + in_index*in_depth = -4 writes before the buffer. No shown guard constrains in_row_start/in_col_start to be non-negative or within [0, in_max_*_index]; the missing lower-bound validation is the defect.

assumptions: Capacity of in_backprop temp is in_depth rows x (in_cols*in_rows*in_batch) columns, from lines 86-88, over the tensor allocated with in_shape at lines 81-83.
row_seq_tensor/col_seq_tensor element values are int64_t and only their element counts are constrained (lines 38-49); values retain the full int64_t domain.
out_batch/out_rows/out_cols/out_depth are non-negative int64_t dim_size values with no shown relation to the in_* dims.
Eigen Map coeffRef performs no release-mode bounds checking (standard Eigen behavior).
limitations: Additional but unconfirmed vectors to the same sink line 121: out_depth > in_depth (row index d out of the in_depth-row matrix) and out_batch > in_batch (in_index beyond in_batch*in_rows*in_cols), since no shown check ties out dims to in dims.

Negative in_* dims are admitted by the !=0 checks (lines 59-70) and flow into TensorShape::AddDim (line 76) and the matrix row/col counts; downstream behavior of negative tensor dims is indeterminate and not used for the verdict.
int64 overflow of product terms (lines 88, 91, 115) and non-termination for in_row_start = INT64_MIN are range claims requiring extreme magnitudes; same root cause as the primary finding.
Allocation failure of forward_input_or_allocate_temp/output is handled via OP_REQUIRES_OK and is not treated as a finding.

verdict.summary: The seccomp rule-installation error checks at lines 217 and 235 are inverted: `if (r < 0 && r == -EFAULT)` is logically equivalent to `r == -EFAULT`, so the only failure that aborts setup is -EFAULT — annotated in the same statement as the benign 'unknown syscall' case — while every other negative return from `seccomp_rule_add` is silently treated as success. A failed rule installation (e.g., -EINVAL/-ENOMEM, any negative errno except -EFAULT) therefore leaves the syscall unblocked, and the incomplete filter is still exported at line 266 and handed to the sandbox at line 271, a fail-open security boundary (CWE-754).

evidence.reason: r is the return status of `seccomp_rule_add` (lines 214/216) for the static syscall blocklist. The fragment itself establishes the negative-errno return convention by comparing r to -EEXIST at line 186 and to -EFAULT here. Since -EFAULT < 0, `r < 0 && r == -EFAULT` equals `r == -EFAULT`, and the comment identifies -EFAULT as the tolerated 'unknown syscall' case. The guard therefore admits every non-EFAULT failure (any r < 0, r != -EFAULT) into the success path: no early return at line 218, and the loop continues, after which `seccomp_export_bpf` (line 266) and `flatpak_bwrap_add_args_data_fd` (line 271) install a filter missing the failed deny-rule — an error-status-handling flaw (CWE-754) that fail-opens the seccomp sandbox boundary.

Identical inversion in the non-devel blocklist loop: r is the return of `seccomp_rule_add` (lines 231/233) blocking perf_event_open, personality (except `allowed_personality`), and ptrace. The guard admits every negative return other than -EFAULT as success, so a failed rule for ptrace/personality is silently dropped, and the incomplete filter is still exported (line 266) and installed (line 271), weakening the non-devel restriction fail-open — same CWE-754 mechanism.

assumptions: `G_N_ELEMENTS` bounds the three static arrays (`syscall_blocklist`, `syscall_nondevel_blocklist`, `socket_family_allowlist`) used as loop bounds at lines 206, 223, and 244; all three are fully visible and constant.

`seccomp_rule_add`/`seccomp_arch_add` return 0 on success and negative errno values on failure — this convention is visible in the shown code itself via the comparisons to -EEXIST (lines 186/194) and -EFAULT (lines 217/235).
`seccomp_x86_64_extra_arches`/`seccomp_aarch64_extra_arches` are 0-terminated as required by the loop condition `extra_arches[i] != 0` at line 191.
limitations: The triggering failure value (a negative return from `seccomp_rule_add` other than -EFAULT) is not a constant shown in the fragment; the finding rests on a complete residual-range analysis of r's negative-errno domain, so confidence is capped at 0.65 per the range-claim calibration.

`bwrap` (FlatpakBwrap*) is a pointer-typed helper parameter consumed at line 271 with no NULL check; its NULL cannot be produced on any shown path, so this is left as an unconfirmed robustness concern, not a CWE-476 finding.

The `seccomp_rule_add_exact` return values for socket-family rules (lines 256/261) are discarded, but the comment at lines 240-242 documents this as an intentional fail-open for e.g. i386; no verdict is based on it.
`lseek` at line 269 discards its return value; failure is not attacker-directed and no security-relevant operation in the shown code consumes the failure state, so it is a robustness concern only.
An unrecognized `arch` string simply leaves `arch_id == 0` (line 178) and installs the default native filter; no dangerous operation consumes the unknown string.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. The two in-fragment protective statements — the early return `if (bias_size == 0) return;` (line 4) and the divisibility equality check `TFLITE_DCHECK_EQ((array_size % bias_size), 0);` (line 10) — leave only pairs with bias_size != 0 and array_size % bias_size == 0 admitted. Over that admitted domain, both the NEON path (lines 16-56) and the scalar path (lines 58-64) write exactly elements [0, array_size) with every block-local index bounded by bias_size - 1, so no out-of-bounds access or non-termination is reachable from the shown statements.

assumptions: bias_data points to at least bias_size floats and array_data to at least array_size floats (implied by the parameter names and the indexing pattern; no capacity declaration exists in the fragment).

TFLITE_DCHECK_EQ((array_size % bias_size), 0) at line 10 is treated at its most protective reading — an active equality check enforcing array_size % bias_size == 0 — per the protective-reading discipline.
NEON intrinsics vld1q_f32/vst1q_f32 operate on exactly 4 floats, matching the +0/+4/+8/+12 index offsets.
ActivationFunctionWithMinMax is a purely elementwise bounded transformation (no sink behavior shown).
limitations: Line 10 is a debug-style assertion (name implies DCHECK); if it is compiled out in release builds, the divisibility invariant is unenforced at runtime and a non-multiple pair such as (bias_size=2, array_size=5) would let the NEON outer loop on line 16 step past array_end_ptr (line 13), causing out-of-bounds writes (lines 39-42, 50, 53) and non-termination, and an out-of-bounds write at index 5 in the scalar path (lines 61-62). This is not confirmable inside the fragment because the macro's runtime semantics are not shown.

Negative sizes that still satisfy both shown checks, e.g. (bias_size=-2, array_size=6), pass line 4 and line 10 (6 % -2 == 0) and cause unbounded non-termination of the line 16 / line 58 loops; this depends on treating negative cardinalities as admitted production inputs, which no shown statement derives and which external TFLite shape validation (not visible here) normally excludes — demoted, no CWE.
No NULL checks on bias_data or array_data; no NULL-producing statement is shown, so a NULL dereference would be an environment/contract violation, not a demonstrated finding.
Potential pointer/offset arithmetic overflow on `array_ptr + array_size` (line 13) is not demonstrated: the fragment exposes no capacity or magnitude bound against which a wrap could be shown.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. The protective statement is the guard at lines 38-39 (old_lhs.IsInitialized() && old_lhs.shape().num_elements() == rhs.shape().num_elements()), which executes before the dangerous CHECK(reshaped_old_lhs.CopyFrom(old_lhs, rhs.shape())) at line 46 and excludes every element-count mismatch that would make the reshape-copy fail and abort; every Copy sink (lines 51, 76, 86) targets a tensor whose element count equals rhs's by lines 39/44/47/69/74, so no out-of-bounds access is derivable from the shown code. Attacker-shape flows are fully bounded by the equality guard; the only residual concern is a dtype-mismatch abort whose witness is not expressible with values shown in the fragment (see limitations).

assumptions: Tensor::CopyFrom returns false on an element-count mismatch between the source and the requested reshape shape, so the guard at lines 38-39 cover the count-based failure of the CHECK at line 46; matching element counts make the reshape succeed on that axis.
num_elements() returns the number of elements (int64); the equality comparison at line 39 is exact and admits only equal counts.
allocate_temp at lines 68-70 allocates a buffer holding rhs.shape().num_elements() elements of old_lhs.dtype(); its failure is handled by OP_REQUIRES_OK.
context->replace_ref_input does not invalidate the local Tensor object's buffer (data is visible to the ref slot), matching the subsequent Copy at lines 51/76/86 operating on the same buffer.
limitations: A CHECK-fail at line 46 on a dtype mismatch between old_lhs and the default-constructed reshaped_old_lhs is not confirmed: the necessary dtype values are not present in the fragment, so no witness can be written with the shown code's own values; the op framework's dtype constraint (if any) is outside the fragment and cannot be used in either direction.

Type confusion between old_lhs.dtype() (line 69 allocate_temp) and rhs.dtype() (line 58 forward_input) was considered but requires a dtype mismatch not expressible in the fragment and depends on unshown Copy semantics; not confirmed.

forward_ref_input_to_ref_output at line 5 runs before shape validation at lines 21-28; on OP_REQUIRES failure the kernel returns an error and no consumer of the forwarded output is shown, so no error-status-handling flaw is confirmed.

The fall-through copy at lines 85-86 runs with lock_held=false when use_exclusive_lock_ is false; concurrent mutation safety is a caller-level contract not visible here and no racing operation is shown.
No loops, injection sinks, crypto/entropy use, or file/access-control logic exist in the fragment, so those classes are out of scope.

verdict.summary: Heap buffer overflow in Image::printIFDStructure: the allocation-size expression at line 68 (long long allocate = (long long)(size*count + pad+20)) is evaluated in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic before widening, so an attacker-chosen count wraps the product. The guard at line 69 then validates the already-wrapped value (e.g., 12) against io.size(), passes for any minimal file, and DataBuf buf(12) is allocated at line 72. bOffsetIsPointer (line 74) admits the wrapped product 0xFFFFFFF8, and line 79 executes io.read(buf.pData_, count*size) with a ~4 GB read length into the 12-byte buffer, overflowing the heap. Concrete witness: dirLength=1, type=LONG(4), count=0x3FFFFFFE, offset=0 in an 18-byte file; 4*count wraps to 0xFFFFFFF8, +20 wraps to 12; the read writes at least 18 bytes into 12. Root cause is the 32-bit wrap (CWE-190) corrupting the size consumed as the heap-write length (CWE-787).

evidence.reason: Heap buffer overflow write (CWE-787). count is a uint32_t decoded from file bytes at line 37 with residual range [0, 2^32-1] (no cap in the fragment; line 65's clamp is commented out). On the witness path type=4 (LONG, admitted by typeValid at line 41 and presupposed by the isLongType branch at line 97), so size=4 (line 60) and pad=0 (line 57). With count=0x3FFFFFFE, line 68 computes size*count+pad+20 in 32-bit arithmetic: 4*count=0xFFFFFFF8, +20 wraps to 12, so allocate=12 and the line 69 check (12 > io.size()) passes for any 18-byte file (2-byte IFD header + 12-byte entry + 4-byte next-IFD). DataBuf buf(12) at line 72 is 12 bytes; bOffsetIsPointer at line 74 admits the same wrapped product (0xFFFFFFF8 > 4); line 79 then reads min(0xFFFFFFF8, remaining) — at least the file's 18 bytes — into the 12-byte heap buffer, overflowing by >= 6 bytes and arbitrarily more for larger files. No statement between lines 69 and 79 bounds count*size against buf's capacity.

Integer-wraparound root cause (CWE-190) of the CWE-787 write. All operands (size, count, pad uint32_t) make the parenthesized expression 32-bit unsigned arithmetic; the (long long) cast applies only after the wrap. For size=4, count=0x3FFFFFFE (line 37), the product is 0xFFFFFFF8 and +pad+20 wraps to 12, which is then cast to 12. The downstream guard at line 69 compares this wrapped value to io.size() instead of the true 8*size*count-scale requirement, so the guard admits the undersized allocation and the oversized read length (0xFFFFFFF8) is later passed to io.read at line 79.

assumptions: typeValid(type) admits LONG (type 4) and the standard TIFF numeric types; the fragment's own print branches (isLongType line 97, isRationalType line 103) presuppose these are valid, so the line 41 gate does not exclude the witness.

BasicIo::read(buf, n) writes up to min(n, remaining file bytes) and io.size() returns the file length; a minimal one-directory file (header 2 + entry 12 + next-IFD 4 = 18 bytes) yields io.size()=18, satisfying the line 69 guard for the wrapped allocate=12.
Line numbers count the fragment verbatim, first line = 1.
limitations: Alternate manifestation of the same wrap: with an 8-byte type (RATIONAL) and count=0x40000000, allocate wraps to 20, bOffsetIsPointer is false, and the rational print loop (lines 103-109, kount=5) reads byteSwap4(buf, k*8+4) up to index 36 against a 20-byte buffer — heap out-of-bounds read (CWE-125); requires bPrint and a file of at least 20 bytes, and is not the primary finding.
Same-root-cause OOB write at line 159 (buf.pData_[count]=0) for count >= 2^32-21 on the XMP path; on every such path the line 79 read overflows first, so it is subsumed by the primary finding.

Unbounded do/while (lines 11-170) driven by attacker-controlled start (line 168) and unbounded recursion (lines 121, 151) with no depth/cycle limit allow infinite loops and stack exhaustion (CWE-835/CWE-674) via cyclic offsets; a separate DoS-only concern, excluded from the CWE list per output guidance.
All io.read/io.seek return values are discarded (lines 14, 34, 79, 128, 139, 144, 167) — a status-handling robustness issue, not independently exploitable here.
tooBig (line 17) is dead after the immediate throw at line 18; the if (tooBig) statements at lines 22 and 168 are unreachable — not a security issue by itself.

verdict.summary: Heap out-of-bounds read in jp2_decode: the CDEF loop at line 315 iterates dec->numchans (set at line 233 from the unvalidated CMAP box numchans or the codestream component count) and reads dec->cdef->data.cdef.ents[i] with no shown bound tying the CDEF box's entry count to dec->numchans; the guard at line 317 reads ents[i] before validating it, so a CDEF box declaring fewer channels than dec->numchans yields an out-of-bounds heap read (CWE-125). Independently, when a CMAP box is present but no CDEF box was parsed, line 268 unconditionally dereferences dec->cdef, which is NULL (only ever assigned at lines 84-87 under a CDEF-box check), causing a deterministic NULL-pointer dereference (CWE-476).

evidence.reason: dec->numchans (line 233: dec->numchans = dec->cmap ? dec->cmap->data.cmap.numchans : numcmpts) is an entry-point-derived count with no shown bound and drives loop index i at line 315; the read dec->cdef->data.cdef.ents[i] has no visible capacity bound linking the CDEF box's entry array to dec->numchans. The guard on this line loads ents[i].channo before any validation, so it cannot constrain i; any input where the CDEF box declares fewer channels than dec->numchans reads past the end of ents (unvalidated-size / missing-bound OOB read, CWE-125).

In the dec->cmap != NULL branch, dec->cdef is dereferenced unconditionally; dec->cdef is only assigned at lines 84-87 when a CDEF box is parsed, and the shown reconciling checks at lines 218-229 touch only cmap/pclr. An input containing a CMAP box but no CDEF box leaves dec->cdef == NULL (the shown `if (!dec->cdef)` assignment pattern depends on that NULL initial state), so &dec->cdef->data.cdef dereferences NULL and crashes deterministically before the loop at line 269 (CWE-476).

assumptions: dec->cdef is NULL when no CDEF box was parsed: the shown code assigns it only under the `if (!dec->cdef)` guard at lines 84-87 and lines 218-229 never touch it.
jas_image_numcmpts(dec->image) >= 1 on paths reaching the CDEF loop, enforced at lines 141-144 and 342-345.
On the CMAP-present palette path, dec->pclr is non-NULL because lines 218-222 destroy dec->cmap otherwise.
limitations: The CDEF ents capacity is not visible in the fragment, so the CWE-125 witness is a range claim (CDEF entry count < dec->numchans); this caps confidence at 0.65 per the missing-bound standard.
jas_cmprof_createfromiccprof (line 211) is only guarded by assert (line 212); a NULL cmprof_ abort/propagation depends on the unshown function's failure behavior and NDEBUG, so it is not reported.
jas_alloc2 at line 274 is unchecked; a NULL lutents after allocator failure (with attacker-scaled numlutents) would be dereferenced at line 276 — resource-exhaustion-dependent, demoted.
The lutdata read at line 276 is kept below the presumed numlutents*numchans product by the pcol guard at line 246, and the lutdata capacity is not visible; no confirmed finding.
Unsigned overflow of i * pclrd->numchans at line 276 would require attacker magnitudes not demonstrated in the shown code.

verdict.summary: win_redr_status() derives len = (int)STRLEN(NameBuff) from the buffer name filled by get_trans_bufname() with no visible length bound, then appends status markers without ever validating len against the MAXPATHL bound it relies on. For a buffer name of length >= MAXPATHL, the unconditional write at `*(p + len++) = ' '` (line 54) and `vim_snprintf((char *)p + len, MAXPATHL - len, ...)` (lines 57/63/73/78, where MAXPATHL - len goes negative and is sign-extended to a huge size_t) write past the end of the NameBuff region, an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) reachable via a crafted long file name.

evidence.reason: Sink write with no bound check. len comes from line 46 `len = (int)STRLEN(p)` where p = NameBuff (line 45) filled by get_trans_bufname(wp->w_buffer) (line 44); the fragment imposes no upper bound on this length, so its residual range is 0..INT_MAX. The fragment's own capacity model for p is MAXPATHL (used as the snprintf size at lines 57/63/73/78), but no statement clamps len before this write, which executes when the buffer is help/preview/changed/read-only (lines 48-53). For a translated buffer name of length len >= MAXPATHL (e.g., len == MAXPATHL), the ' ' write lands at index >= MAXPATHL, one past the fragment-implied capacity, and for len == MAXPATHL-1 it overwrites the NUL terminator. Guards at lines 13, 20, 25, 28, 34, 48-53 all admit this state and none constrains len. Primary mechanism: out-of-bounds write (CWE-787).

Sink whose destination pointer p + len and size MAXPATHL - len are both derived from the unbounded len of line 46. For len > MAXPATHL (in the residual range 0..INT_MAX because get_trans_bufname's output length is not bounded by any shown statement), the int expression MAXPATHL - len is negative and converts, at the size_t size parameter, to a huge value, so vim_snprintf copies "[Help]" plus NUL beyond the MAXPATHL-bounded NameBuff region — an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). Lines 63, 73, and 78 use the identical argument pattern. The strongest protective reading (snprintf truncation) protects only when len <= MAXPATHL, a precondition no shown statement establishes; line 57 executes before any later truncation logic (lines 82-116).

assumptions: MAXPATHL, referenced at lines 57, 63, 73, 78, and 122, is the fragment's own bound for the NameBuff region that p points to; the fragment uses it directly as the size limit for the same p.

The append phase on the analyzed path executes the else-block at line 40 with redrawing() true, pum not drawn over it, and no custom 'statusline' (lines 25-38); these are the conditions the guard analysis used, and they admit the witness.
limitations: The exact overflow magnitude (bytes past the end) depends on the true declared size of NameBuff, which is outside the fragment; the finding is therefore anchored as a missing-bound/unvalidated-size flow (CWE-787) rather than an exact-byte OOB demonstration, which caps confidence at 0.62.

The initial length of the name produced by get_trans_bufname() is not derivable from the fragment; the witness is a range claim (len >= MAXPATHL) over the unconstrained residual range, not a single exactly-shown value.
NULL dereference of wp is demoted: the shown code never produces a NULL wp on any path; it is an internal-caller invariant and a robustness concern, not a confirmed finding.

screen_fill()/screen_puts() calls at lines 118-120 and 124-125 may receive column arguments (len/this_ru_col-derived) outside the screen width, and the STRLEN(p + len) reads at lines 58/64/74/79 are post-overflow effects of the same root cause; both depend on unshown callee/screen internals and are not reported as separate findings.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability in the fragment. The early return `if (stack->top == 0) { return; }` (lines 10-11) runs before every `wddx_stack_top` pop (lines 19, 52, 121), leaving the residual range of stack->top as >= 1 at each pop site, so no stack underflow/OOB pop is reachable. The additional guard `if (ent2->type == ST_FIELD && Z_ISUNDEF(ent2->data)) { ... return; }` (line 55) executes before the dereference of ent2->data (line 61), excluding the non-existent-field path. Entry-point input `name` reaches only strcmp comparisons, and no attacker-derived value is used as an index, size, or length in the fragment.

assumptions: Relative line numbers 1-125 start at `static void php_wddx_pop_element(...)`.
`stack->top` is an integer counter compared with `== 0` / `> 1`; the fragment's only visible constraint is `top >= 1` after line 10.
`wddx_stack_top` pops element `top-1`; with the line 10 guard and the line 50/22 decrement conditions, every call site has `top >= 1`.
Stack entries (`st_entry`) and `stack->varname` are allocated by push-side handlers outside the fragment; their allocation and zval typing are not verified inside this function.
limitations: C1 (stack pop with top == 0) demoted: excluded by the line 10-11 early return on every path; admitted set is top >= 1.
C2 (dereference of undef field data) demoted: excluded by the line 55 guard before line 61.
C3 (NULL from php_base64_decode handed to ZVAL_STR at line 35) not confirmed: NULL behavior of the callee is not shown and the standard PHP 7 implementation returns an empty string on failure.

C4 (type confusion in the EL_BINARY branch, Z_STRVAL/Z_STRLEN at lines 32-33 on a non-string) not confirmed: whether a non-string entry can occupy the stack is determined by unshown push-side handlers.
C5 (EL_FIELD branch lines 119-123 frees the entry without destroying its data/varname) noted as a memory-accounting leak; no memory-safety sink and no demonstrated security impact.
C6 (possible NULL target_hash from HASH_OF at line 62, later used at lines 105/109) not confirmed: requires an unshown object class whose get_properties returns NULL.
C7 (uninitialized retval destroyed at line 47 after unchecked call_user_function_ex) not confirmed: standard zend_call_function initializes the return zval.

verdict.summary: Fragment is the patched bmexec_trans: the guard `if (len > size) return -1;` (lines 11-12) excludes every case where `kwset->mind` exceeds the text length, so `tp = text + len` (line 21) and the later reads `d1[U(tp[-1])]` (lines 71, 74) always stay within [text, text+size); the len==1 path is handled by a size-bounded memchr_kwset (lines 13-17), and the final loop's condition `d <= ep - tp` (line 72) provably keeps tp within the buffer. No confirmed vulnerability.

assumptions: Line 11 compares `int len` with `size_t size`, so after the guards the surviving path has 1 <= len <= size (len==0 excluded at line 9; len==1 handled at lines 13-17).
`tp = text + len` (line 21) with 2 <= len <= size places tp in [text+2, text+size], making every tp[-1] read fall in [text+1, text+size-1].
Line 26 (`size > 12 * len`) ensures `ep = text + size - 11 * len` (line 28) satisfies ep > text and ep < text+size when the big loop runs.
Line 72 (`while (d <= ep - tp)`) with ep = text + size (line 70) admits only advances that keep tp <= text+size, so the read at line 74 is in-bounds by the shown arithmetic.
`memchr_kwset (text, size, kwset)` (line 15) scans at most size bytes and its NULL result is handled at line 16.
limitations: The `kwset->delta` table contents are not shown; in-fragment the only visible bound on `d` is 0..255 (unsigned char to int). Whether the big-loop skip chain (lines 31-46) or the length `text + size - tp` at line 54 can leave the buffer depends on the unshown delta1 construction invariant, and `d` is not derived from the entry-point inputs text/size within the fragment, so no tainted OOB is confirmable.
`bm_delta2_search`'s body is not shown; loop progress after a d==0 hit relies on it advancing tp via &tp, so a delta-stall non-termination claim cannot be confirmed.

Integer overflow of `12 * len` / `11 * len` (lines 26, 28) for len near INT_MAX/12 is a C-UB robustness concern; on visible paths the wrapped comparison makes `size > 12*len` false and the big loop is skipped, so no security-relevant sink is demonstrably reached.

`text` is not NULL-checked; dereferences occur only when size >= len >= 1, so a NULL text with positive size would violate the buffer contract the fragment assumes (robustness, not a confirmed finding).
Capacity of `d1` (standard 256-entry delta table) is not visible; index `U(tp[-1])` is type-bounded to 0..255, so an OOB index into d1 cannot be confirmed or excluded from the fragment alone.

verdict.summary: Heap/stack out-of-bounds write in glob()'s GLOB_TILDE '~user' handling: the user_name buffer is allocated as end_name - dirname bytes (lines 471/474), but the no-unescape path copies end_name - dirname bytes and then writes a NUL one byte past the object (lines 507-508), and the unescape loop (lines 487-504) continues past end_name through the rest of dirname, writing up to strlen(suffix)+1 bytes past the end of the buffer. Both are reachable with an attacker-chosen pattern such as "~bob/rest/x" or "~bob\\x/rest/y" plus the GLOB_TILDE flag.

evidence.reason: CWE-787 OOB write. pattern (entry-point input, no length/content constraint in the fragment) reaches line 507 via the branch chain: line 315 (GLOB_TILDE set by attacker, admitted by the line 16 flag check), lines 317-319 false for dirname="~bob/rest", line 465 false, allocation line 471/474 sized L = end_name - dirname = 4. The sink then mempcpy's L bytes into indices 0..L-1 and writes the NUL at newp[L], exactly one byte past the L-byte object, for every admitted input with end_name != NULL (e.g. pattern "~bob/rest/x", flags=GLOB_TILDE, gl_offs=0). No shown statement adds the required -1 or +1 margin; the off-by-one is deterministic.

CWE-787 OOB write. With pattern "~bob\\x/rest/y" and GLOB_TILDE (NOESCAPE clear), line 463 sets unescape to the backslash at offset 4, buffer newp = malloc(end_name - dirname) = 6 bytes (line 474). Line 484-485 copies 3 bytes, then the loop (487-503) copies 'x','/','r' into indices 3..5 and 'e','s','t' into indices 6..8, and line 504 writes the NUL at index 9 — 4 bytes past the 6-byte object; the excess grows with the length of the dirname suffix after the '/' because the loop terminates on the string NUL, not at end_name. The guard at 491-498 only handles a trailing backslash and does not bound q.

assumptions: pattern is a NUL-terminated C string, as required by the shown strlen/strrchr/strchr/mempcpy usage (lines 24, 91, 129, 187, 206, 268).
GLOB_TILDE (and the other referenced GLOB_* flags) are members of __GLOB_FLAGS, so flags=GLOB_TILDE passes the validation at line 16.

The non-Windows build is the active compilation path (the vulnerable block is inside #ifndef WINDOWS32 at line 448; the #if defined __MSDOS__ || defined WINDOWS32 blocks at lines 189, 240, 272, 326, 448 are compiled out).
globfree treats gl_pathv == NULL as a no-op; the fragment explicitly sets dirs.gl_pathv = NULL at lines 217, 305, 818 before any goto no_matches.
Buffer capacities cited (lines 471/474, 263, 550/554, 604-605, 850) come from their declarations in the shown code.
limitations: Line 376 dereferences p->pw_dir when getpwnam_r returns success with p == NULL (login name absent from the passwd database); the failure is environment-driven, not directed by the attacker pattern, so it is treated as a robustness concern, not a confirmed finding.
assert at line 169 is not a confirmed reachable abort: the rest-walk at lines 119-126 already validated the same brace-expression sweep with next_brace_sub before the alternatives loop.

GLOB_BRACE expansion count/recursion is unbounded for adversarial patterns (potential resource exhaustion), but no concrete amplifying blow-up was demonstrated from the shown arithmetic, so it is not reported as a finding.
Callee bodies not shown (glob_in_dir, prefix_array, is_dir, __glob_pattern_type, next_brace_sub, glob_use_alloca) were analyzed only at their call sites; no finding is attributed to their internals.
The GLOB_MARK loop (846-860) and qsort (866-868) rely on capacity guarantees established by not-shown glob_in_dir/prefix_array; no OOB claim is made there.
Single-shot allocation/free paths (e.g. spurious GLOB_NOSPACE on zero-size malloc at line 97) are not attacker-scaled and are not findings.

verdict.summary: Heap out-of-bounds read in XM pattern decompression: `pc` advances without any bound against the buffer capacity `patdata` (allocated at L289), so a crafted XM file (e.g. patdata=1, rows=1, channum=1, first pattern byte 0x00) makes `memcpy(slot, buffer+pc, 5)` at L342 read 5 bytes from a 1-byte heap allocation, and the packed-data path reads `buffer[pc]` at L308 after `pc` has freely advanced past `patdata`, causing crash or information disclosure.

evidence.reason: Sink of the primary CWE-125 heap OOB read. `pc` is attacker-derived: initialized 0 (L301) and advanced by 5 per uncompressed cell (L343) or by 1+set-flags bits in the packed path (L310-L336), with rows/channum (file-controlled, L49/L264) bounding only the outer loops (L302-L303) and never compared against `patdata`. `buffer` capacity is `phead[y].patdata` bytes (L289), residual range [1,65535] (16-bit file field L265, guard L288 admits any nonzero value). Witness: ver=0x104, rows=1, channum=1, patdata=1, buffer[0]=0x00 -> else branch (L340) executes memcpy of 5 bytes from a 1-byte allocation, reading 4 bytes past the heap object. No statement between L289 and L342 bounds pc.

Same CWE-125 mechanism on the packed-data path. `buffer[pc]` is dereferenced with `pc` unbounded by the `patdata`-byte capacity from L289; the packed path then reads `buffer[pc]` again at L315/L320/L325/L330/L335. Witness: patdata=1, buffer[0]=0xFF (all five flag bits set) -> pc becomes 6 (L311 plus five increments), and the next cell's read at this line accesses buffer[6] on the 1-byte allocation. The guard at L288 only discriminates zero vs nonzero patdata and provides no index bound, so the residual range [1,65535] of patdata and full byte range of pattern data reach the sink unconstrained.

assumptions: mp_ubyte is 8-bit (file byte reads at L22-L26, L193 etc.); the 5-byte memcpy count is in bytes regardless, and even a wider mp_ubyte keeps the patdata=1 witness out of bounds for any element size < 5 bytes.
Allocations at L278/L289 succeed on the witness path (explicitly NULL-checked at L281/L292).

ver, hdrsize, channum, patnum, rows, patdata, instrument sizes and pattern bytes are entry-point file fields; constraints named are only those shown (L29-L32, L56-L59, L86-L87, L104-L105, L434-L435, L455-L459, L288).
limitations: smpReloc[nbu[sc]] OOB read (L229/L596) requires MP_MAXINSSAMPS < 256; that constant's value is not derivable from the fragment, so the index excess is unprovable here.
Fixed-amount envelope parsing from insData (L112-L162, L477-L528) can over-read the 230-byte insData only if MP_MAXINSSAMPS + 8*XM_ENVELOPENUMPOINTS + 19 > 230; those constants are not shown.

hdrsize < 4 wraps at L36 to >= 0xFFFFFFFC, driving a ~4GB `new` at L42 (attacker-directed resource-exhaustion candidate, CWE-770), plus a NULL-deref at L43 if allocation fails; demoted to a secondary DoS concern, not the primary evidence.
MODPLUG message path (L779-L784): len+1 wraps for len=0xFFFFFFFF, but confirmability of the consequent overflow depends on unshown allocateSongMessage and f.read clamping semantics.
Capacities of module->phead, module->smp and smp[s].sample are not visible, so patnum/sample-index-driven OOB writes and the stereo-conversion sample[i+samplen] reads cannot be sized.

rows*channum*6 (L278/L286) in 32-bit arithmetic would overflow to a huge/negative size for extreme file values (allocation failure), not a small-size wrap enabling OOB writes, so no CWE-787 is confirmable from the shown types.

verdict.summary: NULL pointer dereference of dec->cdef at jp2_decode line 268: an input containing a CMAP box (and its required PCLR box) but no CDEF box leaves dec->cdef NULL — no statement in the fragment requires a CDEF box — and 'cdefd = &dec->cdef->data.cdef;' applies '->' through the NULL pointer (CWE-476, crash/DoS on crafted JP2). Secondary confirmed finding: assert(dec->image->cmprof_) at line 212 is reachable with a NULL return from jas_cmprof_createfromiccprof on a crafted COLR-ICC profile, aborting the process (CWE-617).

evidence.reason: dec->cdef is assigned only when a JP2_BOX_CDEF box is parsed (lines 84-87) and no statement between lines 83 and 268 requires or verifies CDEF presence; the decoder's NULL default for dec->cdef is required by the shown 'if (!dec->cdef)' test at line 84 itself. On the admitting path (CMAP box at 95-99, PCLR box present so the guard at 218-221 and 225-229 pass, cmap sanity loop at 237-252 with cmptno/pcol in the admitted sets of guards 240 and 246, allocation at 255 succeeds, no CDEF box), the else-branch at 265 executes and line 268 dereferences NULL dec->cdef. No protective guard constrains dec->cdef before the sink; the only CDEF-conditional statement, line 306, executes after it. This is a NULL pointer dereference (CWE-476) with crash/DoS impact on untrusted input.

dec->image->cmprof_ is assigned the unchecked return of jas_cmprof_createfromiccprof at line 211; the shown code establishes the NULL-on-failure convention for this create-family by checking the sibling jas_iccprof_createfrombuf result at lines 204-207. For input with colr.method == JP2_COLR_ICC (line 201) whose profile (iccp/iccplen, attacker-controlled) is rejected by the cmprof builder, the return is NULL and assert(dec->image->cmprof_) at line 212 fails, aborting the process — a reachable assertion (CWE-617).

assumptions: The decoder's box fields (ihdr, bpcc, cdef, pclr, cmap, colr) start NULL after jp2_dec_create(); this is required by the fragment's own guarding style, e.g. 'if (!dec->cdef)' at line 84 and 'if (dec->cdef)' at line 306.
dec->chantocmptlut is allocated with dec->numchans entries at lines 255-256; that is the visible capacity used to validate all chantocmptlut reads/writes at lines 263, 272, 282, 314 and 321.

pclrd->lutdata and pclrd->bpc are assumed to be sized per the JP2 box format (numlutents*numchans and numchans entries respectively); their capacities are not visible in this fragment, so the lutdata/bpc accesses are judged only through the visible pcol < numchans guard at lines 246-250.
limitations: OOB claims for cmap->ents (line 270), cdef->ents (lines 307/309), bpcc->bpcs (line 182), and pclr->lutdata/bpc (lines 276/281) cannot be confirmed because the backing array capacities are not declared in the fragment (missing visible capacity); the bat data access at line 276 is within bounds by the shown guard's arithmetic and is not reported.

lutents = jas_alloc2(pclrd->numlutents, sizeof(int_fast32_t)) at line 274 is not NULL-checked before the write at line 276; this is a possible NULL dereference on allocation failure with an attacker-scaled size, but it depends on an environment OOM and is treated as a robustness concern, not a confirmed finding.

The runtime fault at line 268 is compiler-dependent: address-of-member through a NULL pointer is undefined behavior but commonly folds to pure address arithmetic, and all downstream uses of cdefd are disabled by the '#if 0' block at lines 284-294; the confirmed defect is the NULL dereference/UB itself.

The reachable-assert finding at line 212 depends on the unshown behavior of jas_cmprof_createfromiccprof returning NULL for some crafted ICC profile; the sibling NULL-check at lines 202-207 supports that convention, but no concrete failing profile can be constructed from the shown code, so this finding is a range claim at reduced confidence.

verdict.summary: Nullable parser state pointers are dereferenced without validation: in the slice-parsing path, `avc->s_info.sps` and `n_state.sps` are dereferenced at line 79 with no NULL check; the only protection visible is a debug-only `assert` at line 77 (compiled out under NDEBUG). A crafted bitstream of slice NALs that reference an SPS id never parsed makes both pointers NULL (propagated through the memcpys at lines 13/159), reaching line 79 and crashing the parser (NULL deref / reachable assert) — a remote denial-of-service (CWE-476).

evidence.reason: NULL-pointer dereference (CWE-476). `avc->s_info.sps` and `n_state.sps` have residual range including NULL: the fragment never initializes or validates them (the only prior mention is the `assert` at line 77, which is an abort — removed under NDEBUG — and cannot make the deref safe). `n_state.sps` is seeded from `avc->s_info.sps` at line 13 and may be repopulated by `avc_parse_slice` (line 54) from a bitstream-controlled SPS id with no shown constraint on the outcome; if the referenced SPS was never parsed, `n_state.sps` stays NULL and is stored back into `avc->s_info.sps` by the memcpy at line 159. Reachability: a first slice NAL (switch labels lines 47-51, `nal_hdr & 0x1F` at line 14) with unparsed SPS id passes `ret >= 0` (line 55) and stores NULL via line 159; a second slice NAL with matching `frame_num`/`field_pic_flag`/`nal_ref_idc` passes guards at lines 57-62 (previous type is now a slice type, so no break), 63, 68, and 72-73 in path order, then reaches line 79, dereferencing NULL. No shown guard excludes the NULL value from the sink's path.

assumptions: `avc->s_info` is cross-call parser state; its `sps` pointer is populated only by parsing helpers called at lines 29/54/114/119/123, and the shown code imposes no constraint on its value (line 13 merely copies the prior value).

The switch label sets at lines 47-51 and 20-22/26/43/113/118/122/126/131-132/135 define the admitted NAL-type sets; numeric values of `GF_AVC_NALU_*` are not visible in the fragment and are not needed for the verdict.
`gf_bs_read_ue` (line 127) returns u32; the `(s32)` cast wrap is caught by the `last_ps_idx < 0` check at line 128, which is why that site is not a finding.
limitations: The NULL production for `avc->s_info.sps`/`n_state.sps` ultimately depends on `avc_parse_slice` (callee body not shown) returning >= 0 while leaving `n_state.sps` NULL for an unparsed SPS id; if that helper instead errors out, line 55's early return would prevent reaching line 77. The witness is therefore a residual-range claim, not a fully line-traceable value, which caps confidence at 0.6.

`assert(avc->s_info.sps)` (line 77) is itself a reachable-abort sink (CWE-617) in debug builds; it is treated as the same missing-validation defect as the line-79 dereference, not an independent root cause.

The discarded return of `svc_parse_slice` (line 29) lets a stale/partial `n_state` reach `avc_compute_poc` (line 34) and the `memcpy` to `avc->s_info` (lines 37/40): an error/status-handling concern (CWE-754 family) with no demonstrable security-relevant sink in the fragment; not confirmed.

Memory-safety of callees (`SVC_ReadNal_header_extension`, `avc_parse_slice`, `avc_compute_poc`) and of `avc->last_ps_idx` consumption is not assessable: the callee bodies and the sizes of `n_state.NalHeader`/`avc->sps`/`avc->pps` are not shown.

There are no loops in the fragment, so no termination/index-overrun analysis was applicable; no numeric range for `GL_AVC_NALU_*` is visible, so range claims about the composite guard at lines 58-59 use the guard's structure only.

verdict.summary: User-influenced filp->f_flags flows into NFS_PROTO(dir)->open_context() as openflags with only partial sanitization: the fragment rejects nothing, silently remaps the invalid access mode 3 to O_RDWR at line 27, strips only O_CREAT|O_EXCL at line 30, and lacks a whitelist mask before the protocol-open call at line 47, so unvalidated access-mode and leftover flag bits reach the remote NFS OPEN.

evidence.reason: openflags originates at line 7 from filp->f_flags (entry-point data, full unsigned flag domain: no shown statement bounds it beyond the opaque nfs_check_flags call at line 22, the single-equality remap at lines 26-27 which converts invalid access mode 3 to 2 = O_RDWR instead of rejecting it, and the O_CREAT|O_EXCL clear at line 30). The residual domain, including O_TRUNC/O_APPEND/O_DIRECT/O_SYNC/O_NONBLOCK/O_NOATIME and access mode 3 remapped to read-write, is forwarded verbatim as the openflags argument of the NFS OPEN call at line 47 with no visible protocol flag whitelist or mask — the missing bound on an input-derived argument to a security-relevant sink (CWE-20, improper input validation).

assumptions: O_ACCMODE == 3 is implied by the literal `== 3` at line 26, and O_CREAT|O_EXCL are the flag bits cleared at line 30.
nfs_check_flags (line 22) has no visible body, so it is treated as transparent: it supplies no nameable bound and does not block the witness.
NFS_PROTO(dir)->open_context is a protocol open whose openflags argument is consumed as the open access/flags (call-site semantics implied by the parameter name and by the shown usage).
limitations: Real-world reachability of access mode 3 depends on the VFS open-syscall boundary, which is not shown; per the fragment analysis rules filp->f_flags retains its full declared domain, which is exactly what makes this a missing-validation finding rather than a caller-dependent one.

NULL-dereference candidates for inode (line 44), parent (line 33) and dir (lines 33/47) are robustness concerns: the fragment derives no NULL on any shown path and the guarantees come from an unshown VFS invariant.
The discarded filemap_write_and_wait return (line 44) means a failed writeback still proceeds to the open with ATTR_SIZE=0, but the failure is not attacker-directed in the shown code.
Severity is capped at low because, within the shown code, a user could equivalently request O_RDWR legitimately; no privilege boundary is demonstrably crossed.
No memory-safety, size/arithmetic, or loop structures exist in the fragment, so no OOB/overflow/loop-termination candidates arise.

verdict.summary: No confirmable vulnerability in the fragment. All attacker-shapeable magnitudes that flow to consuming operations are confined by visible bounds: the esil-backscan keeps addr >= esil_buf (line 38, reads stay within the strdup'd NUL-terminated buffer), and both sign branches reject frame_off outside [-8192, 8192] (lines 90-92 and 156-158) before get_stack_var/r_anal_function_set_var/r_anal_var_set_access execute; every pointer dereference is null-guarded. Remaining concerns (st64 wrap via R_ABS/casts, R_ROUND-by-zero, countdown-loop termination) cannot be demonstrated with values traced solely through shown statements.

assumptions: Line 9: R_ARRAY_SIZE(op->src) is the visible capacity bounding the source-operand scan (max index R_ARRAY_SIZE(op->src)-1).

Line 26: esil_buf is a NUL-terminated strdup result; because strstr finds the pattern at line 31, strlen(op_esil) >= strlen(esilexpr) >= 4, so the buffer has at least 5 bytes when the loop at line 38 runs, making reads esil_buf[0] and esil_buf[1] in-bounds.
Lines 4, 90, 156: maxstackframe = 8192 is a visible constant; the guards admit frame_off in [-8192, 8192] and exclude all other values on the paths to the var-access/set sinks.
Line 6: r_return_if_fail guarantees anal, fcn, op, reg are non-NULL.
limitations: R_ABS(op->src[i]->delta) with delta == INT64_MIN (line 14) is a wrap/UB corner, but the resulting INT64_MIN magnitude is rejected by the frame_off guards (90/156) unless fcn->stack/fcn->bp_off take unshown extreme values that cancel the wrap; no witness traceable to shown statements.
(st64)r_num_get casts (lines 59, 72) and R_ABS(op->ptr) (line 67) can flip large unsigned values negative, but reaching a sink again requires an unshown offset cancellation; demoted.

R_ROUND(sum_sz, bytes) (line 127) divides by zero when bytes == 0, i.e., (fcn->bits ? fcn->bits : anal->bits) in 0..7 (line 114) combined with an argument type of bit_sz 0 (lines 125-126); both operands are framework data unconstrained by the fragment and not attacker-directed by a shown statement; robustness concern only.

The reverse-argument countdown loop (lines 106-115) would wrap size_t i at 0 when cnt == 0 and to == 0; termination then rests on r_type_func_args_type returning NULL for out-of-range indices (lines 117-119), a callee property not shown in the fragment.
NULL/invalid returns from r_type_func_guess, r_anal_cc_arg, or fcn->name/cc are framework-robustness concerns, not attacker-directed failures.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability in the shown fragment. Every attacker-controlled field (width>0, height!=0, planes==1, bpp whitelist {1,4,8,16,24,32}, number_colors capped by GetBlobSize and by 2^bpp, compression restricted to RGB/RLE8/RLE4/BITFIELDS) is validated before use, and every memory sink is bounded by a visible capacity: the pixel buffer (rows*max(bytes_per_line,columns+256)) is always >= length=bytes_per_line*rows with max bytes_per_line*rows = 2^64-2^33 (no 64-bit wrap), ReadBlob returns are compared with == length / == packet_size*colors before proceeding, DecodeImage extent columns*rows <= buffer capacity, the colormap read fits the 4*colors allocation, and all scanline index writes stay within [0, columns-1]. Demoted non-findings: the length/8 blob-size comparison is 8x permissive but has no security-relevant consumer (count check and buffer sizing absorb it); shift-by-32 UB in the bit-mask loops only feeds color-scaling math; huge-dimension requests fail through checked allocation paths.

assumptions: size_t, ssize_t, and MagickOffsetType are 64-bit as declared (ReadBlobLSBSignedLong sign-extends the 32-bit field into ssize_t).
ReadBlob(image,n,ptr) writes at most n bytes and returns the number of bytes actually read; ReadBlobLSB* return the documented 16/32-bit little-endian values.

SetImageExtent, AcquireVirtualMemory, AcquireQuantumMemory, AcquireImageColormap, DecodeImage, SyncAuthenticPixels, and QueueAuthenticPixels report failure through the return values that the shown code checks before continuing.
Buffer capacity for the pixel cache is exactly image->rows * MagickMax(bytes_per_line, image->columns+256UL) per the shown AcquireVirtualMemory call.
limitations: The comparison `if (((MagickSizeType) length/8) > GetBlobSize(image))` is weaker than a plain `length > GetBlobSize` check, but it is not a confirmed finding: the allocation is always >= length and `if (count != (ssize_t) length)` rejects short reads, so no out-of-domain value reaches a memory sink; the over-permissive bound has no security-relevant consumer.

Left-shift-by-32 UB in the red/green/blue/opacity mask loops is reachable for mask 0xFFFFFFFF, but the resulting out-of-range quantum_bits value only gates color-scaling branches and is not consumed by a memory, size, or index operation.

Admitted dimensions up to columns=2^31-1 and rows=2^31 cause very large allocation requests (SetImageExtent/AcquireVirtualMemory); the shown code checks and converts allocation failure into exceptions, and length cannot wrap in 64-bit arithmetic (max 2^64-2^33), so no confirmed overflow or resource-exhaustion mechanism is demonstrable from the fragment.
AcquireImage/OpenBlob NULL-style environment failures are handled by the shown `status == MagickFalse` return and are not attacker-directed; not treated as findings.
The `if (x < (ssize_t) image->columns) break;` statement in the 4-bpp case is dead for every admitted column count (x reaches columns on both even and odd paths); harmless.

Behavior of unshown helpers (SetImageExtent pixel-cache limits, DecodeImage internal bounds) was not used to justify the verdict either direction; the argument relies only on the byte-level capacities derivable from the shown statements.

verdict.summary: The concat axis tensor is read with no value validation (line 44, DT_INT64 path retains the full int64 domain). The ternary at line 48 overflows int64 for the admitted boundary values: -concat_dim wraps at INT64_MIN and concat_dim + 1 wraps at INT64_MAX, producing min_rank = INT64_MIN. That corrupted value defeats the WithRankAtLeast rank validation at lines 54/67 and yields out-of-domain index arguments to Subshape/Dim at lines 55/56/60 and 68/69/73, with signed-overflow UB as the root cause (CWE-190).

evidence.reason: concat_dim originates at line 44 from flat<int64>()(0) with no shown bound, so INT64_MIN and INT64_MAX are in its residual range. For INT64_MIN, -concat_dim overflows int64 and wraps to INT64_MIN; for INT64_MAX, concat_dim + 1 wraps to INT64_MIN. The corrupted min_rank is consumed by the rank-validation checks at lines 54/67 and the corrupted coordinate values flow into lines 55/56/60 and 68/69/73; this signed-overflow of an unvalidated input value is the CWE-190 root cause.

min_rank can be INT64_MIN via the line 48 overflow on the unvalidated line 44 value; WithRankAtLeast then admits every possible input rank, so the intended validation (rank >= |concat_dim|) is bypassed before concat_dim is used as an index at lines 55/56/60 and 68/69/73. A comparison gating a security-relevant check consumes the wrapped value (CWE-190 consumption point).

concat_dim retains the full unvalidated int64 residual range from line 44 and is passed here as Subshape's end coordinate; with concat_dim = INT64_MIN (admitted by every guard on the path, including lines 6/41/45/48/54/57), the coordinate is vastly out of domain for any permitted shape rank, and no capacity or bound check is shown before the call (missing-bound flow under CWE-190).

For concat_dim = INT64_MAX the shown expression concat_dim + 1 overflows to INT64_MIN and is forwarded as Subshape's start coordinate; the guard at line 57 excludes only exactly -1, not the extreme values, so the out-of-domain argument is derived by the shown arithmetic with no bound check (CWE-190).

assumptions: Line 4 (c->WithRank(c->input(dim_index), 0, &unused)) establishes the concat-dim tensor is a scalar, so the element reads at lines 42/44 (index 0) are in-bounds.
Line 6 guarantees concat_dim_t is non-NULL before the dereferences at lines 42/44.
The DT_INT32 path (line 42) widens int32 to int64 value-preservingly; INT32_MIN does not overflow after widening, so only the DT_INT64 else-branch (line 44) admits INT64_MIN/INT64_MAX.

Negative concat_dim values other than -1 rely on relative-from-end semantics in Subshape/Dim, implied by the -1 special case at lines 57/70 and by concat's negative-axis support; those callee-side bounds are outside the fragment.
limitations: Memory-level impact (OOB read/write, CWE-125/787) of the out-of-domain Subshape/Dim coordinates is not demonstrable because the callees' bounds checks and capacities are not shown; if the callees bounds-check and return errors, the residual impact is the signed-overflow UB at line 48 plus the bypassed rank validation rather than memory corruption.

start_value_index/end_value_index/dim_index are unconstrained helper parameters; degenerate caller ranges (e.g., end_value_index <= start_value_index making line 53 read input(end-1), or start_value_index = INT_MIN making line 63's --i wrap) are caller-dependent and were not confirmed.
Possible int64 overflow inside c->Add (line 77) from attacker-crafted huge input dimensions is not confirmable because dimension magnitudes are not visible in the fragment.
A dtype other than DT_INT32/DT_INT64 reaching the else at line 44 would reinterpret the buffer as int64; the op definition normally constrains dtype, so it was not treated as a separate finding.

verdict.summary: Out-of-bounds heap read in mrb_vm_exec: the OP_ARGARY and OP_BLKPUSH environment-length guards (lines 644 and 1170-1171) admit MRB_ENV_LEN(e) == m1+r+m2+2, while the kd=1 paths dereference e->stack[m1+r+m2+2] at lines 677 and 1177/1181, one element past the last valid slot (len-1). The guard's +1 covers the non-kd read but lacks the kd term; a crafted instruction operand (kd=1, m1=r=m2=0, lv=1) with an environment of length m1+r+m2+2 passes every guard and reads one mrb_value out of bounds.

evidence.reason: OP_ARGARY kd-path OOB read. kd (line 628) can be 1 and m1=r=m2=0 per the bit masks at lines 625-629. The only env guard, line 644, rejects MRB_ENV_LEN(e) <= m1+r+m2+1, so its admitted set is [m1+r+m2+2, inf). Since stack = e->stack + 1 (line 646), this statement reads e->stack[m1+r+m2+2]; for an env of length m1+r+m2+2 the valid indices end at len-1 = m1+r+m2+1, so index m1+r+m2+2 is one past the end. The +1 term covers only the kd=0 read stack[m1+r+m2]; no kd term exists in the guard. Primary mechanism: heap OOB read (CWE-125).

OP_BLKPUSH kd-path OOB read. kd (line 1163) can be 1 and m1=r=m2=0 per the bit masks at lines 1160-1164. The guard at lines 1170-1171 rejects only MRB_ENV_LEN(e) <= m1+r+m2+1 (admitted set [m1+r+m2+2, inf)), and with stack = e->stack + 1 (line 1175) this dereference reads e->stack[m1+r+m2+kd+1]; for kd=1 and an env of length m1+r+m2+2 that index equals len, one past the last valid slot len-1. The +1 term lacks the kd term. Primary mechanism: heap OOB read (CWE-125).

assumptions: e->stack has exactly MRB_ENV_LEN(e) slots with valid indices 0..MRB_ENV_LEN(e)-1; OP_ARGARY/OP_BLKPUSH use stack = e->stack + 1 (lines 646 and 1175), skipping the self slot.
Bit-field decoding visible at lines 625-629 and 1160-1164 bounds m1<=63, r<=1, m2<=31, kd<=1, lv<=15.
The register stack capacity is irep->nregs as established by mrb_stack_extend at lines 482, 523, 618, and 938.
limitations: OP_JMPUW (line 330, pc = irep->iseq + a) has no main-path bounds check against irep->ilen; only an assert inside CHECKPOINT_RESTORE (line 316) that is compiled out in release builds — demoted as bytecode-trust/hardening with no demonstrated in-range guard failure.
Operand-driven regs[a] indexing with no visible nregs bound (e.g., lines 48, 257-264, 353, 382) is pervasive across every opcode and treated as compiler-trust; not reported as an independent finding.

OP_ENTER writes regs[blk_pos] (line 805) and regs[kw_pos] (line 809) and the narrowing store ci->n = (uint8_t)len (line 813) depend on MRB_ASPEC_* macro widths that are not shown, so the admitted operand domain cannot be bounded — demoted.
OP_LOADL bigint length bytes s[0]/s[1] (line 74) come from pool layout not validated in this fragment — demoted to hardening concern.

The witness's env length (MRB_ENV_LEN(e) == m1+r+m2+2) is a runtime value not produced by a shown statement, making the confirmed part a residual-range claim rather than a fully constant-instantiated witness; hence confidence 0.6.

verdict.summary: NULL pointer dereference (CWE-476) when parsing attacker-controlled ISO BMFF data: a top-level MOOF parsed without an MFHD child is dereferenced at line 365 (mov->moof->mfhd->sequence_number) in GF_ISOM_OPEN_KEEP_FRAGMENTS mode, and a MOOV track missing the Media/information/sampleTable chain is dereferenced at line 100. No shown statement validates either pointer chain, so both crashes are reachable from a crafted file.

evidence.reason: The parsed top-level box `a` (line 30, attacker-controlled file data) is stored at line 308 (mov->moof = (GF_MovieFragmentBox *) a;). `mov->moof->mfhd` is a child-box pointer populated from the file, and no shown statement validates it: the path to this sink (line 32 e>=0; line 292 case MOOF; line 312 non-debug; line 364 openMode==GF_ISOM_OPEN_KEEP_FRAGMENTS) contains no check on mfhd, so a MOOF whose children omit MFHD is admitted and NULL is dereferenced. Primary CWE-476 (NULL pointer dereference).

`trak` is retrieved from the file-derived trackList at line 99; the nested pointers Media, information, and sampleTable are populated from parsed file data and are dereferenced unconditionally at line 100 (and again at line 101) with no NULL checks between the MOOV assignment (line 57) and this statement. The only guards on the path (line 76 requires mvhd; line 98 bounds the list index) do not constrain the trak field chain, so a track lacking mdia/stbl causes a NULL member dereference. CWE-476.

assumptions: gf_isom_parse_root_box (line 30) stores a valid box into `a` whenever it returns e >= 0; the switch dereference at line 49 relies on this success contract.

gf_list_count/gf_list_get (lines 88-99, 316-356) are consistent so index k in [0, count-1] is valid and list elements are non-NULL; the confirmed findings concern nested payload fields, not the list element itself.
box->dataSize==4 (line 399) guarantees 4 readable bytes at box->data, protecting the JP 4CC check at line 399.
mov->moov->mvhd->timeScale (line 476) is safe because lines 76-79 unconditionally require mvhd before any path that sets mov->moov (line 57).
limitations: assert(totSize >= mov->bytes_removed) (line 15): reachable-abort (debug) / u64-underflow (NDEBUG) candidate, but the bytes_removed vs current_top_box_start relationship is not derivable from shown statements; not confirmed.
Unchecked gf_list_add returns at lines 153 and 327: discarded status would only cause missed tracking/leak; single-shot, not attacker-scaled.
GF_LOG format `%d` with u64 position (line 27): constant format string, so no format-string injection; type mismatch is UB/robustness only.
Outer while loop (line 23) termination depends on gf_isom_parse_root_box advancing the bitstream; callee not shown, so CWE-835 non-termination is unconfirmable.
u32 wrap of sequence_number+1 (line 365) has no shown security-relevant consumer.
Potential dangling mov->moof after gf_isom_box_del(a) at line 371 is not dereferenced within this fragment (MergeFragment may clear it); demoted.

verdict.summary: networkstatus_parse_vote_from_string dereferences the result of find_by_keyword(tokens, K_VALID_AFTER) at line 110 without a NULL check; an attacker-controlled networkstatus document that omits the required 'valid-after' line passes every shown guard (tokenize at L29, asserts at L41/L67, type match at L79) and crashes the parsing process via a NULL-pointer dereference, enabling remote denial of service. The same unchecked-lookup pattern repeats for K_PUBLISHED (L86), K_FRESH_UNTIL (L114), and K_VALID_UNTIL (L118).

evidence.reason: Entry-point input s (full declared domain, unconstrained by the fragment) supplies the token set; find_by_keyword at L109 returns NULL when the document omits 'valid-after' (absence is shown to be possible by the fragment's own tor_assert(tok) pattern at L41 and by find_opt_by_keyword usage at L90/L98/L148/L151/L170/L276/L360/L367). No shown statement between L108 and L110 checks tok, so line 110 dereferences a NULL lookup result (CWE-476). Prior guards L22, L29, L41, L51, L67, L79 all admit a well-formed consensus that merely omits the valid-after line, so the crash is reachable on attacker-chosen input.

Same unchecked-lookup NULL dereference as the primary finding: find_by_keyword at L113 can return NULL on a document without 'fresh-until', and L114 dereferences tok->args[0] with no NULL check and no shown guard between L113 and L114 (CWE-476), extending the remote crash to this sibling sink.

assumptions: find_by_keyword returns NULL when the requested keyword is absent; the fragment itself demonstrates this by asserting its first result at L41 and by asserting n_args for other lookups at L67/L122/L203/L249/L397.

The tokenizer (tokenize_string and the referenced token tables at L29/L341) does not enforce keyword presence or minimal argument counts; the parser performs those checks itself via find_by_keyword/asserts.
directory_token_t args are valid for indices [0, n_args), so loops bounded by tok->n_args (L92/L158/L174/L370) index in-domain.
tor_parse_long range arguments ([0, INT_MAX] L124/L128, [0,65535] L233/L238, [INT32_MIN, INT32_MAX] L181/L378) make the subsequent int/uint16_t casts non-truncating for admitted values.
limitations: find_by_keyword's body is not shown; if it internally aborts on missing tokens (as real Tor does), the effect is a reachable abort (CWE-617) rather than NULL propagation, though the fragment's own explicit tor_assert(tok) at L41 indicates callers are expected to guard NULL.
Reachability assumes tokenize_string accepts a document missing a keyword; if the unshown token tables rejected such documents, the NULL path would be unreachable.
Unasserted token-argument derefs at L149/L152/L246/L278 share the same root class but are not reported as separate CWEs.

The explicit tor_assert(tok->n_args) and tor_assert(tok) sites (L41/L67/L122/L203/L249/L397) are reachable aborts on malformed input (CWE-617 class); treated as the same missing-validation root cause, not independent findings.

end_of_header from find_start_of_next_routerstatus (L28) is used at L29/L295/L298 without a NULL check, and termination of the L298 while-loop depends on the unshown routerstatus_parse_entry_from_string advancing s; the callee contracts are not visible, so no loop/OOB verdict is possible from the fragment alone.
tor_memdup at L479 is protectively bounded by L415-417 (object_size excluded outside [128,512]) and was analyzed as safe.
Unchecked allocations (memarea_new L27, tor_malloc_zero L37/L207/L300/L434) are not attacker-directed and are not findings.

verdict.summary: Heap buffer overflow in GetEXIFProperty: in all-mode ('exif:*') the key buffer is allocated as AcquireString(property) — exactly strlen(property)+1 bytes, minimum 7 — but FormatLocaleString(key,MaxTextExtent,"%s",description) then writes the static tag description (up to 35 bytes) with a MaxTextExtent-sized destination argument. A crafted EXIF entry whose tag maps to a long description (e.g., 0x0112 -> "exif:Orientation", 16 bytes) overflows the 7-byte key by up to 28 bytes, corrupting heap memory.

evidence.reason: Heap OOB write (CWE-787). Destination key is allocated at line 761 as key=AcquireString(property) with capacity strlen(property)+1; property's residual range is any string with strlen>=6 (line 447 admits 'exif:*', 7 bytes incl. NUL) and no shown statement reallocates key before this call. Description (lines 769-779) comes from the static EXIFTag table selected by attacker-controlled tag_value read from the EXIF entry at line 612, and can be up to 35 bytes ('exif:ThumbnailPrimaryChromaticities'); the size argument MaxTextExtent (~4096) exceeds the 7-byte capacity, so the full description+NUL is written past the allocation. Witness: property='exif:*' (passes line 447), all=1 via case '*' (lines 453-458), valid 28-byte EXIF profile passing checks at lines 550/556-566/590/610, first entry tag=0x0112, format=3, components=1 passing lines 617-627 and 652, then case 1 (line 764) selects description 'exif:Orientation' (16 bytes with NUL), overflowing the 7-byte key by 9 bytes; overflow reaches 28 bytes for the longest table description.

assumptions: AcquireString(property) allocates strlen(property)+1 bytes and copies the string (standard string-duplication semantics of the named helper; this yields the key capacity used in the finding).

MaxTextExtent is the standard large ImageMagick text-buffer constant (4096); the fragment's own usage — char buffer[MaxTextExtent] (line 650) and the clamp to MaxTextExtent-1 (lines 40-41/66-67) — confirms it is far larger than the 7-byte key allocation and larger than every table description.

EXIF profile bytes returned by GetImageProfile/GetStringInfoDatum are the image's exif metadata and are attacker-influenced (consistent with the fragment treating them as untrusted protocol data via the many validation checks).
limitations: Demoted: EXIFMultipleValues/EXIFMultipleFractions buffer writes are protected by the truncation clamp (lines 40-41/66-67) and the guarded buffer[length-2] assignment (lines 44-45/70-71); no buffer overrun was found there.

Demoted: number_bytes = components*tag_bytes[format] cannot wrap in 64-bit arithmetic because components is a signed 32-bit read (line 621, max 2^31-1); the overflow guard at line 625 and the region checks at lines 638-642 are consistent and effective.
Demoted: pointers read in the value-format switch are confined to [exif, exif+length) by lines 627/638-644 (offset case) or q+12 <= exif+length (inline case), verified by lines 652 and 731.
Demoted: directory_stack indexing is bounded by the level < MaxDirectoryStack-2 guards at lines 826 and 855 (max index written 14 < 16).
Demoted: case-2 FormatLocaleString calls (lines 792-799) write at most 6 bytes into a key of at least 7 bytes; safe.

Robustness only (no CWE attached): unaligned dereferences *(float*)p1 / *(double*)p1 in macro arguments may be undefined behavior on strict-alignment targets, and large components can trigger allocation proportional to the input profile size (no amplification).
Malloc/allocation failure inside the value builders would skip the key block; the demonstrated witness relies on the tiny value allocation succeeding, which is the ordinary non-failing case.

verdict.summary: In the USB_DT_OTG branch of composite_setup, config is taken from cdev->configs with list_first_entry (L112-114) and the subsequent 'if (!config) goto done;' (L115-116) is dead: list_first_entry cannot return NULL, so on an empty cdev->configs list config is a non-NULL container_of(&cdev->configs,...) bogus pointer. The guard admits it, and memcpy(req->buf, config->descriptors[0], value) (L127, value = min_t(int, w_length, otg_desc_len) in [1,26], L126) dereferences a wild kernel pointer populated from attacker-controlled USB control input (GET_DESCRIPTOR/OTG, w_length capped to [0, USB_COMP_EP0_BUFSIZ] at L14-24), causing a kernel crash/KASAN fault or disclosure of up to 26 bytes of kernel memory (queued to the host at L402/L405). The one-statement fix is list_first_entry_or_null at L112.

evidence.reason: Attacker-controlled entry-point input ctrl (USB control request) selects this sink: bRequest=USB_REQ_GET_DESCRIPTOR with w_value>>8==USB_DT_OTG (L46/L49/L104) and w_length (L10, residual range [0, USB_COMP_EP0_BUFSIZ] per the L14-24 cap) feeds value = min_t(int, w_length, otg_desc_len) at L126 (otg_desc_len in {20,26} per L118-124, so value in [1,26] for w_length>=1). The memcpy source config->descriptors[0] is derived from cdev->configs by list_first_entry at L112-114; on an empty list the macro returns container_of(&cdev->configs, struct usb_configuration, list), which is provably non-NULL, so the intended protector 'if (!config) goto done;' (L115-116) admits it (dead guard). The memcpy then reads up to 26 bytes through a wild kernel pointer populated from a bogus offset inside cdev (line 127), yielding a kernel Oops/KASAN fault or an out-of-bounds kernel-memory read that is transmitted to the host via req->length=value and composite_ep0_queue (L402/L405). Primary CWE-125 out-of-bounds read via the unvalidated list-extraction pointer; fix is list_first_entry_or_null at L112.

assumptions: w_length residual range [0, USB_COMP_EP0_BUFSIZ] on all IN paths derives from the shown cap at L14-24.
otg_desc_len is 20 (usb_otg_descriptor) or 26 (usb_otg20_descriptor) per L118-124, so value at L126 is at most 26.
list_first_entry semantics (container_of((head)->next, ...)) make NULL impossible, even on an empty list; hence the L115-116 check is dead.

limitations: The empty cdev->configs precondition is external gadget state (unbind teardown race with an in-flight control transfer, or a driver marking is_otg before adding configs), not derived inside the fragment; upstream commit f8f680609c2b3 ('usb: gadget: composite: fix dead empty check in the USB_DT_OTG handler') corroborates it with a KASAN reproducer, but the shown code does not itself derive the degenerate list, capping confidence at 0.62.

USB_DT_BOS: a negative return from bos_desc (L100) would be swallowed by the (u16) cast so min(w_length, (u16)value) yields w_length and queues stale buffer contents (info-leak class); bos_desc internals are not shown and upstream never returns negative, so not confirmed.

verdict.summary: In gen_hash, the hash-pair counter `len` is incremented once per key/value entry (line 33) and is only ever capped by the loop-tail flush at lines 36-48, whose guard `if (val && cursp() >= slimit)` explicitly excludes `val == 0`. For `val == 0` (a member of the parameter's unconstrained int domain), `len` is unbounded by any shown statement and flows into the kw-rest branch sinks `pop_n(len*2)` (line 11) and `genop_2(s, OP_HASH, cursp(), len)` / `genop_2(s, OP_HASHADD, cursp(), len)` (lines 13, 17).
