evidence.reason: Sink consumes the input-derived pair count `len` as the OP_HASH operand. `len` originates from `len++` (line 33) over the attacker-supplied `tree` list and is capped only by the flush at lines 36-48, whose guard `if (val && cursp() >= slimit)` (line 36) excludes `val == 0`; with `val == 0` no shown statement bounds `len` above. The kw-rest path admits `len > 0` (line 10) with no upper bound, so e.g. `len = 40000` (> the fragment's own INT16_MAX ceiling at line 4) is issued as the instruction operand, causing operand truncation and execution-time OOB access on the VM stack (CWE-787, missing bound on an input-derived size/count).

Second distinct sink on the same path: the stack-pop count `len*2` is derived from the unbounded, input-driven `len` on the `val == 0` path (flush at line 36 is val-gated and never runs). For 40000 pairs preceded by `**rest`, `pop_n(80000)` is issued with no visible capacity bound on the codegen stack, so the pop count is out-of-domain relative to the fragment's own INT16_MAX ceiling (line 4) and to the stack contents the fragment tracks (2 values per pair).

Same missing-bound flow as line 13, reached on a second `**rest` entry after `update` became TRUE: `len` (pairs accumulated since the last reset at line 28) is again unbounded when `val == 0` and is encoded as the OP_HASHADD pair-count operand, exceeding the 16-bit count domain evidenced by INT16_MAX at line 4 and corrupting generated code/VM stack accounting (CWE-787).

assumptions: INT16_MAX = 32767 (standard constant).
The shown `len*2`/`pop_n(len*2)` accounting implies one stack value pushed per key and per value by `codegen`; this invariant is stated by the fragment's own arithmetic.
`GEN_VAL_STACK_MAX` and `GEN_LIT_ARY_MAX` are positive constants whose numeric values are not shown; only their relational use at lines 3-4 is considered.
Line numbers are 1-based as presented in the fragment block.
limitations: The bodies of `genop_2`, `pop_n`, `cursp`, and `codegen` are outside the fragment; the 16-bit operand/count domain is inferred from the fragment's own `slimit = INT16_MAX` ceiling (line 4). If the operand domain were >= int width, the confirmed damage would be miscompilation rather than memory unsafety.

`val == 0` reachability is analyzed per the internal-helper full-declared-domain rule; no call site is shown. If every real caller passes a nonzero `val`, the flush (lines 36-48) bounds `len` to <= ~slimit/2 + 1 and the fragment is safe on that path.

The polarity of line 4 (raising the flush ceiling exactly when `cursp()` is already >= GEN_LIT_ARY_MAX) cannot be adjudicated without the values of GEN_LIT_ARY_MAX/GEN_VAL_STACK_MAX and is not used for the verdict.

The three-level dereference at line 9 (`tree->car->car->car`) has no shown NULL checks on intermediate links; demoted because no shown statement can derive a NULL link and AST shape is parser-enforced outside the fragment.

The final `pop_n(len*2+1)`/`genop_2(OP_HASHADD, ...)` at lines 52-53 is not a sink for the `val == 0` witness because line 51 gates it on `val`, and on the `val != 0` path `len` is already bounded by the flush.
The `return -1` (line 56) and `return len` (line 58) values flow to unshown callers; any operand emission for the no-kw-rest `val == 0` case happens in that unshown caller.
Loops terminate only given an acyclic `tree` list; a cyclic-list non-termination witness cannot be constructed from shown statements.
The `limit` parameter is declared but never used.

verdict.summary: Stack buffer overflow in suggest_trie_walk: tword[] (capacity MAXWLEN, line 7) is written as tword[sp->ts_twordlen++] = c in STATE_PLAIN (line 700) and STATE_INS (line 931) with no shown check that ts_twordlen < MAXWLEN, while the bad-word length driving ts_twordlen (fword/su->su_badlen) is never capped in the fragment; a bad word and matching trie path of at least MAXWLEN+1 bytes writes one or more bytes past tword[MAXWLEN-1] on the stack.

evidence.reason: CWE-787: tword has visible capacity MAXWLEN (line 7, valid indices 0..MAXWLEN-1). The index sp->ts_twordlen is incremented once per admitted trie byte on this path and no statement in the fragment compares it to MAXWLEN; the only MAXWLEN-indexed guard, 'if (depth < MAXWLEN - 1' (line 126), sits in the PFD_PREFIXTREE branch that breaks at line 157 and never runs on this path. Entry-point input fword/su->su_badlen is uncapped here (no length check anywhere in the fragment), so a bad word of length >= MAXWLEN+1 whose first bytes match a trie path drives ts_twordlen to MAXWLEN, and this write lands at tword[MAXWLEN], one byte past the line-7 array (stack overflow). The guards on the path (lines 674-675, 679-683, 698-699) admit every score-0 matching byte and never bound ts_twordlen; TRY_DEEPER's expansion is not shown and cannot supply a demonstrated bound. Witness is a range claim (badlen >= MAXWLEN+1 with matching dictionary bytes), hence calibrated confidence 0.55.

CWE-787: same unbounded write into tword[MAXWLEN] (line 7) from the STATE_INS path. The insert guard 'if (c != fword[sp->ts_fidx] && TRY_DEEPER(...))' (lines 920-921) admits an insert byte at the (possibly NUL) current fword position without any check on sp->ts_twordlen; each insert increments ts_twordlen at line 931, so repeated inserts (or inserts following MAXWLEN accepted bytes) reach index MAXWLEN and overflow the line-7 array. limitations: Reachability to the boundary index is a range claim, not a single demonstrated value: it requires a bad word of length >= MAXWLEN+1 and a dictionary path matching/inserting that many bytes; dictionary word-length limits and TRY_DEEPER's expansion (which in the real code bounds depth) are not shown, which caps confidence at 0.55.

compflags[sp->ts_complen] writes (lines 270-271, 481-482) show the same unbounded-index shape, but their boundary is additionally governed by can_be_compound() and compmax/compsylmax semantics that are not visible in the fragment; demoted.

Non-termination of the main loop (line 98) is not demonstrated: depth increments are gated by the unshown TRY_DEEPER macro, which the fragment neither shows failing nor succeeding.

verdict.summary: Attacker-controlled MP4 box data reaches unguarded multi-level pointer dereferences. In the MOOV branch (line 101) each track-list element is dereferenced as trak->Media->information->sampleTable with no NULL check on trak/Media/information/sampleTable, and in the KEEP_FRAGMENTS MOOF branch (line 366) mov->moof->mfhd is dereferenced with no NULL check. evidence.reason: CONFIRMED NULL-DEREF (CWE-476). Taint: file-parsed box `a` (line 30) is stored as `mov->moov` (line 58), and `trak` is fetched from `mov->moov->trackList` (lines 99-100) with the residual range of its fields unconstrained. The only guards before the sink are the mvhd check (lines 77-80) and the loop-index bound (line 99); neither constrains `trak`, `Media`, `information`, or `sampleTable`, and no NULL check exists between lines 100 and 101. Witness by simulation: a MOOV containing mvhd (passing line 77) plus a trak without the 'mdia' child leaves `Media==NULL`; the path line 30 -> 50 -> 52 -> 58 -> 72 -> 77 (admitted) -> 87 (admitted) -> 99 (admitted) -> 101 dereferences NULL, crashing the process (DoS).

CONFIRMED NULL-DEREF (CWE-476). Taint: a file-parsed MOOF box becomes `mov->moof` (line 309); `mfhd` is a parsed child-box field whose residual range includes NULL because the fragment assigns and validates it nowhere. Sink: line 366 dereferences `mov->moof->mfhd->sequence_number` on the `openMode==GF_ISOM_OPEN_KEEP_FRAGMENTS` path (line 365) with the debug flag clear (line 326). Witness: a MOOF box without an 'mfhd' child box, in an app opened with GF_ISOM_OPEN_KEEP_FRAGMENTS; all guards on the path (lines 313, 326, 365) admit the witness, and none validates mfhd, so the unconditional dereference faults (DoS).

`mov->moov` is assigned only at line 58 and is immediately validated for non-NULL `mvhd` at lines 77-80 on every continuing path, so the later deref at line 476 is guarded (also repeated at lines 460-463).

Line 15 `assert(totSize >= mov->bytes_removed)`: provenance and attainable magnitude of `mov->bytes_removed` are not shown, so reachability of the assert / a CWE-617 verdict cannot be demonstrated; in a release build the u64 wrap only affects a seek position, not a memory sink.

verdict.summary: Out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) in compile_xclass_matchingpath: the property-value byte cc[1] of the XCLASS bytecode is consumed as a table offset (PRIV(ucp_typerange)[(int)cc[1]*2] at line 538, PRIV(ucd_caseless_sets)+cc[1] at lines 63 and 589) with no visible capacity or bound check anywhere in the fragment. cc[1] is an internal-helper parameter whose residual range is the full PCRE2_UCHAR domain, since the only guards on the path (loop ends at XCL_END, opcode asserts to XCL_PROP/XCL_NOTPROP, case labels on the property type) constrain the opcode and type bytes but never the value byte. This is a missing-bound/unvalidated-index flow whose out-of-domain derivation is confirmed by the shown arithmetic alone; any value at or above the (unshown) table length triggers an OOB read during JIT code generation.

evidence.reason: cc[1] is the bytecode property-value byte with residual range 0..255 (full PCRE2_UCHAR domain after the shown guards only verify the opcode is XCL_PROP/XCL_NOTPROP at line 516 and the type is PT_GC at line 537); the fragment imposes no upper bound on cc[1] before it is used as subscript (int)cc[1]*2, which spans 0..510. PRIV(ucp_typerange) has no capacity declared in the fragment, and line 540 repeats the same unbounded derivation with index (int)cc[1]*2+1, so the out-of-domain value reaches a direct array read — confirmed missing-bound OOB read, CWE-125.

In the generation phase the property branch admits XCL_PROP and XCL_NOTPROP (line 516-517) and, for type PT_CLIST (line 588), offsets the static ucd_caseless_sets table by the unvalidated byte cc[1] (residual range 0..255; no guard between line 516 and this statement bounds it). The resulting pointer is dereferenced at lines 593-594, 597, 610, and in the sentinel loop at 633-637, reading until NOTACHAR, with no visible table capacity — a confirmed missing-bound OOB read, CWE-125. The scan-phase gate at line 61 (PT_CLIST && PROP) does not execute on this path, and even where present it does not bound cc[1].

assumptions: SUPPORT_UNICODE is compiled in: all analyzed sinks (lines 63, 309, 353, 420, 538, 540, 589) are inside #ifdef SUPPORT_UNICODE blocks.

PRIV(ucd_*) tables (ucd_caseless_sets, ucp_typerange, ucd_boolprop_sets, ucd_script_sets) are finite static arrays whose sizes are not declared in this fragment and therefore cannot be used as capacities.

The XCLASS bytecode is well-formed enough that the scan/generation loops make forward progress and terminate on XCL_END (lines 32, 457); this follows from the shown loop mechanics, not from an external length field.
limitations: The primary witness is a range claim (any cc[1] value at or above the unshown table bound), not an exact demonstrated magnitude, so confidence is capped at 0.55.

Reachable-abort candidates (CWE-617) are demoted: SLJIT_ASSERT(compares > 0) at line 141 on an empty XCLASS, SLJIT_ASSERT(*cc == XCL_PROP || *cc == XCL_NOTPROP) at lines 59/261/300/338/401/516, and SLJIT_UNREACHABLE() at lines 134/720 on out-of-range opcode/property-type bytes require malformed bytecode the fragment neither derives nor proves the producer can emit, and SLJIT_ASSERT enforcement is debug-dependent.
The same missing-bound CWE-125 root cause also appears at lines 63-69, 309, 353, 420, and 540; they are additional sink sites of the primary finding, not independent CWEs.
On 16/32-bit code-unit builds, the (int)cc[1]*2 cast (line 538) can produce negative indices; this widens the range claim but was not separately confirmed.

If a caller-side validation stage (outside this fragment, e.g., in pcre2_compile) provably bounds cc[1] to the UCD table sizes, the flows are safe; no such invariant is visible in the fragment, and the rules prohibit using it in either direction.
No format-string, command, SQL, crypto, temp-file, or authentication sinks exist in this fragment; no error/status-handling flaw was found (all non-void returns are consumed correctly).

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability in the fragment. UCD table capacities (ucd_stage1/ucd_stage2, ucd_records, ucd_caseless_sets, ucd_boolprop_sets, ucd_script_sets) are not visible; index safety relies on the clamp constant (lines 222-224) and on upstream compile-time validation of property values / caseless-set indices (e.g., cc[1] at line 63 and the set reads in the BOOL/SCRIPT-EXTENSION blocks).

Generated-code-correctness details (the PT_CLIST pair optimization emitted when charoffset != 0 using `other_cases[1] ^ other_cases[0]` where the power-of-two pair tested is `other_cases[2] ^ other_cases[1]`, and the compares/invertcmp bookkeeping) were not audited for match-semantics impact; no memory-safety impact is demonstrated at the fragment level.

Guard 248 admits depth + 1 == old_files (both 50 after 50 unpopped pushes); the growth block 250-268 runs only when bigger != NULL (251) with no else, so on ALLOC_MULT failure execution falls through and this assignment indexes files[50], one past capacity (excess 1). The NULL return of ALLOC_MULT (250) is the unconstrained input reaching the sink; the forget block at 275-283 executes after this write and cannot bound it.

verdict.summary: The `maxrlvls` option value is parsed with atoi (line 166) and only upper-bounded by JPC_MAXRLVLS at line 167, which admits every negative int. The loop at lines 286-289 compares the unsigned counter `rlvlno` (uint_fast16_t, line 13) against the negative signed `tccp->maxrlvls`; the signed-to-unsigned conversion yields a huge loop bound, so the loop writes `tccp->prcwidthexpns[rlvlno]`/`prcheightexpns[rlvlno]` far beyond the per-resolution-level arrays (out-of-bounds write). The lower-bound guard `maxrlvls < 1` at line 380 executes after the loop and cannot protect it.

evidence.reason: Out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). The index `rlvlno` is driven by `tccp->maxrlvls` (loop condition line 286), whose residual range after the only pre-loop guard `if(tccp->maxrlvls > JPC_MAXRLVLS)` (line 167) is `INT_MIN..JPC_MAXRLVLS`, i.e. all negatives are admitted (`atoi` at line 166 produces them from the entry-point `optstr` value). For an admitted value `maxrlvls = -1`, the comparison `rlvlno < tccp->maxrlvls` at line 286 converts the negative int to a huge unsigned value (rank of uint_fast16_t >= rank of int on mainstream ABIs), so the body executes for rlvlno = 0,1,2,... writing indices far past JPC_MAXRLVLS — exceeding any per-resolution-level array whose bound the shown code states via JPC_MAXRLVLS. The lower-bound guard `if (cp->tccp.maxrlvls < 1)` at line 380 sits after this sink in path order and does not cover it.

assumptions: `tccp->maxrlvls` is signed `int`: it is assigned directly from `atoi()` (line 166) and compared with `1` (line 380); if it were unsigned, a negative atoi result would fail the line-167 check instead.

`prcwidthexpns`/`prcheightexpns` hold one entry per resolution level, so the only in-fragment bound on their index is `JPC_MAXRLVLS`, enforced by the guard at line 167 (values above JPC_MAXRLVLS are rejected).
`JPC_MAXRLVLS` is a positive constant, so `maxrlvls > JPC_MAXRLVLS` admits every negative int and 0.
limitations: The failure is ABI-dependent on the width of `uint_fast16_t` (line 13): if it is exactly 16-bit, integer promotion makes `rlvlno < maxrlvls` a signed comparison and `maxrlvls = -1` yields zero iterations (safe on that ABI only); on mainstream ABIs (glibc LP32/LP64, MSVC) it is 32- or 64-bit, where the negative bound is converted to a huge unsigned value and the OOB write occurs. This single facet caps confidence at 0.62.

`cp->numtiles = cp->numhtiles * cp->numvtiles;` (line 321) can conceivably wrap, but the tile-grid guard at 307-310 is wrap-safe (clauses 1 and 3 force `tilewidth >= imgareatlx - tilegrdoffx` without mod-2^32 wrap), bounding the product to roughly (width+2)*(height+2); a crash requires image dimensions near 2^16 and a downstream allocation sink not shown here — demoted.
`hsteplcm`/`vsteplcm` accumulation (lines 59-60) can wrap in uint_fast32_t, but no security-relevant consumer of the corrupted value is shown in the fragment.

`jas_eprintf` writes of user tags/values (lines 147-148, 156-157, 202-203, 209-210, 218-219) use literal format strings; log-injection via embedded control characters is unconfirmed because the tokenizer that produced those strings is not shown.
The `ilyrrates` allocation (line 325) occurs before the `numlyrs > 16384` cap (line 374); a huge count would require `jpc_atoaf` to produce it, and its internal caps are not shown.
The parse-loop status `ret` (line 106) is not checked after the loop, but partially parsed options are still subject to the later validation checks.

evidence.reason: arg1 derives from parameter arg1n (line 26, `arg1 = arg1n;`), whose declared type const char* leaves NULL in the domain; the only shown constraint on arg1n (line 34, `if (arg1n != (char *) NULL)`) skips reassignment when it is NULL, so the residual range includes NULL. On the admitted path, guard ordering is 56,58,60,62,64,69,122,153,184,218,246,266, none of which tests arg1 or arg1n, and line 266 admits option "-print" with any arg1. The sink at 268 passes arg1 to the %s conversion with no NULL check, dereferencing NULL and crashing (CWE-476). Confidence capped at 0.6 because the witness requires the caller to supply a NULL first argument (a fragile NULL precondition), though every step of the chain is shown.

verdict.summary: In the user-to-user branch of tgs_build_reply, the return of _krb5_principalname2krb5_principal at line 93 is discarded and the local krb5_principal p (declared uninitialized at line 70) is then consumed unconditionally by krb5_unparse_name at line 94 and _kdc_db_fetch at line 101. The additional ticket's sname/realm are attacker-controlled plaintext processed before any decryption (line 121), so an admitted request that makes the conversion fail leaves p NULL/indeterminate and crashes the KDC (CWE-476, unauthenticated DoS). Independently, the server lookup result is dereferenced on the HDB_ERR_WRONG_REALM path at line 176 with no NULL check (CWE-476).

evidence.reason: p is declared without an initializer at line 70 and its producing call at line 93 (_krb5_principalname2krb5_principal(context, &p, t->sname, t->realm)) is the only one in the function whose return is not checked (cf. lines 140-148, 634-640, 793-798). On the failure branch p retains an indeterminate value (NULL or uninitialized), and this statement passes it to krb5_unparse_name; the guard at lines 95-96 checks only the unparse result and executes after p has already crossed into the callee. The sname/realm come from the attacker-controlled plaintext of the additional ticket, reached before decryption at line 121, so the conversion failure is attacker-directed. NULL/indeterminate principal consumption crashes the KDC (CWE-476).

server is a lookup result initialized to NULL at line 20 and populated only by _kdc_db_fetch at lines 166-168; the HDB_ERR_WRONG_REALM branch at line 174 admits exactly that error return and no statement between lines 166 and 176 tests server against NULL. If the fetch returns WRONG_REALM without writing the output entry, server remains NULL and server->entry.principal->realm dereferences NULL, crashing the KDC (CWE-476). The missing NULL check is the defect; the output-written-on-error contract, if any, is not visible in this fragment.

assumptions: b->additional_tickets->val is an array of additional_tickets->len Ticket elements as produced by the ASN.1 decoder, making val[0] in-range whenever the len > 0 guards at lines 75-76 and 749-753 pass.
b->etype.val is an array of b->etype.len enctypes, so the reads at lines 303/314 are bounded by the loop condition at line 302 plus the equality guard at line 305.

The additional ticket's sname and realm are unauthenticated until krb5_decrypt_ticket at line 121, so lines 93-94 operate on attacker-controlled values.
limitations: Candidate A's exact crash behavior depends on krb5_unparse_name/_kdc_db_fetch handling of a NULL or indeterminate principal, which is callee-side and not shown; the out-of-domain argument at line 94 (and line 101) is confirmed from the shown code, so confidence is capped at 0.6.

Candidate B's NULL witness assumes _kdc_db_fetch can return HDB_ERR_WRONG_REALM without setting *server; the fragment shows no in-fragment constraint preventing this, but the callee contract is not visible, so confidence is 0.55.

Unchecked krb5_make_principal returns at lines ~232-233 and ~250-251 can leave sp NULL before krb5_unparse_name at lines ~236/~254; demoted to robustness because the only demonstrated trigger is allocation failure not shown to be attacker-directed.

The server_lookup loop on the HDB_ERR_WRONG_REALM path (lines 174-199) has no shown progress bound; non-termination would require the HDB to repeatedly return WRONG_REALM for the re-derived krbtgt principal, which is DB behavior not established here.

verdict.summary: Heap buffer overflow in block_insert(): the post-padding vim_memset at lines 102-103 writes (size_t)(ts_val - spaces) bytes, and that length is negative-valued whenever the unvalidated bdp->startspaces (line 31) / bdp->endspaces-derived spaces exceed ts_val (bdp->start_char_vcols / bdp->end_char_vcols, lines 30/38). The fragment imposes no bound spaces <= ts_val (the clamp at lines 75-76 only forces spaces >= 0), so (size_t)(ts_val - spaces) becomes ~2^64-1 and the write runs far past the 10-byte allocation computed at lines 79-81, which embeds the same unsafe ts_val - spaces term. Primary CWE-787 (out-of-bounds write); the signed-to-unsigned length conversion of the unvalidated subtraction is the root cause (CWE-195).

evidence.reason: Sink with unvalidated write length: ts_val = bdp->start_char_vcols (line 30) and spaces = bdp->startspaces (line 31) are unconstrained int fields; the only shown bound is the line 75-76 clamp spaces >= 0. For any admitted value with spaces > ts_val (e.g., ts_val=4, spaces=5, b_insert path, is_short==FALSE per lines 23-24, has_mbyte==FALSE so lines 63-65 are skipped), guards 32, 75, 97 and 99 all admit the path, and (size_t)(ts_val - spaces) = (size_t)(-1) = 2^64-1 bytes are written from newp+6 while the allocation at lines 79-81 is only STRLEN(oldp)+spaces+s_len+(ts_val-spaces)+count+1 = 1+5+1+(size_t)(-1)+3+1 = 10 bytes. The negative→size_t conversion of the unvalidated subtraction (CWE-195) yields the enormous length; the write exceeds the visible capacity by ~2^64 bytes (heap OOB write, CWE-787).

Second confirmed sink: on the append/is_short/!is_MAX path, spaces = (oap->end_vcol - bdp->end_vcol) + 1 (line 50) and count = spaces (line 51). No shown check bounds the difference; for an admitted value such as oap->end_vcol=10, bdp->end_vcol=12, spaces=-1 and count=-1. The clamp at lines 75-76 resets spaces to 0 but leaves count = -1, so the allocation at lines 79-81 is STRLEN(oldp)+s_len-1+1 = L+s_len bytes while the actual writes (offset + s_len pre-insert plus the STRMOVE tail copy including the NUL) total L + s_len + 1 bytes; the final NUL lands one byte past the allocation (CWE-787 via under-allocation from the un-clamped negative count).

assumptions: Destination capacity for the writes is the allocation size expression at lines 79-81 (STRLEN(oldp) + spaces + s_len + (spaces>0 && !bdp->is_short ? ts_val - spaces : 0) + count + 1), quoted as the only visible capacity.
has_mbyte is read at line 56 with no shown constraint; the F1 witness takes it FALSE so the multibyte adjustment block (lines 63-65) is skipped.
STRMOVE is treated by its name-implied semantics as copying the remaining string including its NUL terminator.
ml_get(lnum) (line 26) is assumed to return a NUL-terminated line, as implied by STRLEN(oldp) usage at line 79.
limitations: Real-world reachability of both findings may depend on block_prep invariants (startspaces < ts_val, endspaces <= ts_val, end_vcol <= oap->end_vcol for short lines, textcol <= line length) that are NOT visible in this fragment; per fragment-scope rules those unshown invariants cannot neutralize the missing-bound findings, but they cap confidence at range-analysis level (0.62 / ~0.55).

NULL dereference of parameter s at line 18 (STRLEN(s)) is demoted: NULL is not derived by any shown statement, and the degenerate-input discipline rejects NULL preconditions not produced by the shown code.

Potential OOB reads of oldp when offset > STRLEN(oldp) (mch_memmove line 86) and at the mb_head_off probes (lines 63/71 when offset+spaces or offset exceed the line length) have the same missing-bound structure but are not separately reported.

Narrowing of STRLEN(s) to unsigned s_len (line 18) for text longer than UINT_MAX truncates the same value on both the write (line 94) and the allocation (line 79), producing no overflow; not a finding.
Discarded return values of ml_replace, inserted_bytes and changed_lines (lines 118/122/133) gate no security-relevant decision.
Loop at lines 20-131 terminates (lnum strictly increments to oap->end.lnum); no non-termination finding.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. The only register-index sinks derived from attacker-visible inputs are protected by named guards: `if (idx > 0)` (L45) excludes non-positive `lv_idx` results from `gen_move(s, idx, sp, val)` (L47), routing them to `gen_setupvar` (L52); `if (sp)` (L65) excludes `sp == 0` from the `gen_move(s, cursp(), sp, 0)` copy (L66). The COLON2 branch's push/pop accounting (L69-L75) nets zero, so `cursp()` cannot underflow from the shown arithmetic. The `n` argument-count flow (L106-L152) stays within {1..15}, with 15 being OP_SEND's variable-length marker. Remaining concerns (safe-call register initialization at L99-L101, keyword/vararg packing at L112-L128, and `gen_move(s, top, cursp(), 1)` ordering at L138) cannot be confirmed because the callee and opcode semantics are outside the fragment.

assumptions: `cursp()`/`push()`/`pop()`/`pop_n` maintain a single integer stack depth, and each `codegen(x, VAL)` call increases depth by exactly one and leaves its result at the register the fragment later names via `sp = cursp()` — this invariant is derived from the fragment's own GVAR path (L15-L18 followed by L40).
`gen_move(dst, src, val)` reads `src` and writes `dst` without changing the stack depth, and `gen_setxv`/`genop_*` consume the register operands the fragment passes without hiding malformed values.

`OP_SEND`/`OP_SSEND` accept argument-count operand `n` in {0..15} with 15 being the variable-length encoding (consistent with the fragment's own `if (n < 14)` / `n = 15` logic at L106-L110 and L140-L145).
limitations: The negative/zero `lv_idx` register-index hazard is fully covered by `if (idx > 0)` (L45) and is demoted, not a finding.
The `sp == 0` COLON2 `gen_move` hazard is fully covered by `if (sp)` (L65) and the branch's net-zero stack arithmetic (L69-L75); demoted.
Whether `recv = cursp()-1` (L99) references an initialized receiver for the `noself`+`safe` path (L91-L101) depends on codegen register conventions not shown; unverifiable.

The keyword/vararg packing paths (L112-L128) and the final `pop(); OP_ARYPUSH` path (L143-L145) could not be conclusively validated because `gen_values`, `gen_hash`, `OP_ARRAY`, and `OP_ARYPUSH` stack bookkeeping semantics are outside the fragment; no concrete out-of-domain argument was derivable from the shown arithmetic.

The `gen_move(s, top, cursp(), 1)` at L138 and the `OP_SETMCNST` operand at L77 could not be confirmed to mis-generate bytecode without the VM opcode semantics; treated as a correctness concern, not a demonstrated memory-safety or injection finding.
`codegen_error` calls (L29, L33, L170) are the intended compiler error paths for the switch-routed node types, not attacker-admitted abort inputs.

verdict.summary: The XM pattern decoder reads from a heap buffer whose capacity is the file-supplied patdata (L289) while pc advances unboundedly (L308/L310/L311/L342/L343) inside loops bounded only by the file-supplied rows (L264) and channum (L49), so any pattern with rows*channum > patdata over-reads the heap (CWE-125). Additionally, rows*channum*6 (L278) overflows 32-bit int for large admitted values (e.g. 60000x60000 wraps to a 125,163,520-byte allocation while the loop writes 6 bytes * 3.6e9 iterations), corrupting the allocation size and permitting heap OOB writes (CWE-190).

evidence.reason: Heap OOB read (CWE-125): buffer is new mp_ubyte[phead[y].patdata] (L289) with patdata a file-supplied 16-bit value (L265); pc is initialized at L301 and advanced at L311/L316/L321/L326/L331/L336/L343 with no comparison against patdata anywhere in L288-L397. With patdata=1, rows=2 (L264), channum=2 (L49), buffer[0]=0x80, iteration (r=0,c=1) reads buffer[pc]=buffer[1], 1 byte past the 1-byte allocation; the value is then copied to slot[] (L315/L320/L325/L330/L335) and written to patternData (L373-L379), so the over-read also feeds module output and can crash the loader.

Same CWE-125 mechanism on the uncompressed branch: with pc already >= patdata (L311/L343 advance monotonically), memcpy reads 5 bytes starting beyond the buffer allocated at L289. With patdata=1 and any first-byte value whose high bit is clear, iteration 1 sets pc=5 and iteration 2 copies buffer[5..9], 4-9 bytes past the 1-byte allocation. No pc bound exists between L297 and this sink.

Integer overflow corrupting an allocation size (CWE-190): rows (L264, [0,65535]) and channum (L49, [0,65535]) are unvalidated file values; rows*channum*6 is computed in 32-bit int and wraps for rows*channum > 357,913,941. Example: rows=channum=60000 (both admitted members of the shown domains) yields 60000*60000*6 = 21,600,000,000, which wraps to 125,163,520 bytes, while the decode loop (L302-L303) performs 3.6e9 iterations writing patternData[bc..bc+5] (L373-L379, bc+=6 at L394): at t=20,860,587, bc=125,163,522 exceeds the wrapped capacity (heap OOB write); the same expression feeds memset at L286. For rows=channum=65535 the wrapped value is negative and converts to a near-2^64 size_t, causing huge-allocation/memset DoS.

assumptions: mp_uword values read via readWords/GET_WORD (rows, patdata, channum, ver) are 16-bit with domain [0,65535]; this is directly consistent with the shown reads (L49, L264-L265, L271-L272).
The arithmetic at L278/L286 is evaluated in 32-bit int (mp_uword promotes to int; the literal 6 is int), so rows*channum*6 wraps at 2^31 for the stated inputs.

The small allocations on the primary witness path (L278: 24 bytes; L289: 1 byte) succeed, and f.read at L297 delivers the pattern byte; otherwise the loader returns MP_OUT_OF_MEMORY before the witness is exercised.
MP_MAXORDERS >= 0 and MP_MAXINS >= 0 so the witness values ordnum=0/insnum=0 pass L56-L59.
limitations: smp[g+s] writes (L177-L203, L544-L571) with cumulative s: the only cap constant MP_MAXSAMPLES (L629/L677) is not valued in the fragment and is checked after the header-write loops in the 0x104 path and not at all on the 0x102/0x103 path; exact excess not derivable — demoted, no CWE.

smpReloc[nbu[sc]] indexing (L229/L232, L596/L599): nbu entries are unvalidated bytes [0,255] used as an index, but MP_MAXINSSAMPS (L4) is not valued in the fragment, so the missing bound cannot be quantified — demoted.
Unbounded hdrBuff allocation/read from header->hdrsize (L42-L45): no upper bound shown and field signedness unknown — DoS candidate only.

MODPLUG text block (L778-L783): len+1 wraps to 0 at len=0xFFFFFFFF before f.read(module->message,1,len) of ~4GB, but allocateSongMessage's allocation semantics are external to the fragment — candidate only.

All f.read*/readWords/readDwords return statuses are discarded; short reads leave zeroed (hdrBuff/insData) or uninitialized (buffer L289) bytes consumed as pattern data — robustness concern, not a confirmed finding.
insData parsing (L121-L162, L486-L528) consumes 114+8*XM_ENVELOPENUMPOINTS bytes and stays within the [230]-byte array only if XM_ENVELOPENUMPOINTS <= 14; the constant is unshown — demoted.
Potential negative read lengths from instr[y].size-33 (L107, L461) and instr[y].size-4 (L423) depend on the unshown signedness of TXMInstrument::size — demoted.
VERBOSE printf statements (L198, L451, L566) are compiled out and use no attacker format string — not findings.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. The EXIF parser is the patched form: every attacker-controlled length/index (number_entries, format, components, dir_offset, entry, offset) is bounded by visible guards, and the formatting into the fixed buffer[MaxTextExtent] is clamped to MaxTextExtent-1 after every iteration (EXIFMultipleValues/EXIFMultipleFractions, lines 40-41/66-67). Payload pointers p are bounded by dir_offset+number_bytes <= length (638-643), inline values by the 12-byte entry bound (610), and sub-IFD/next-IFD reads by preceding capacity checks (828, 852).

assumptions: LP64 platform: size_t/ssize_t are 64-bit; on this assumption components*tag_bytes[format] (max 2^31-1 * 8) cannot overflow, and the guard at line 625-626 is an exact backstop.
char buffer[MaxTextExtent] (line 649) declares the buffer capacity used in the EXIFMultipleValues/EXIFMultipleFractions macros.

ReadPropertyByte/ReadPropertySignedShort/ReadPropertyUnsignedShort/ReadPropertySignedLong read exactly the named widths and (for ReadPropertyByte) decrement the length counter; this is their name-implied semantics.
GetImageProfile/GetStringInfoLength/GetStringInfoDatum return a non-NULL datum when length >= 16 has been validated at lines 549-550.
EXIFTag is terminated by the sentinel entry {0x00000, ""} at lines 395-396, bounding the scan loops at 514-523 and 775-784.
limitations: On a 32-bit build (size_t/ssize_t 32-bit) the product at line 624 can wrap modulo 2^32 to a value >= components (e.g., components=0x28000000, format EXIF_FMT_DOUBLE -> 0x40000000), bypassing the `number_bytes < components` check; combined with a >= 1 GiB profile and a pass of line 642, an oversized read span is conceivable. This is environment-dependent and not demonstrable with the shown LP64 types, so it is demoted with no CWE.
Unchecked returns of NewSplayTree (576) and GetStringInfoDatum (532) are robustness concerns only: failures are not attacker-directed and no security-relevant operation consumes their failure state.

SetImageProperty (line 815) return is discarded while status is set to MagickTrue (line 818); a failed property set would produce an incorrect success flag, but no memory-safety or injection sink runs on the failure state.

The duplicate-tag check (843-847) compares saved directories against a fixed exif+tag_offset1 rather than the candidate exif+offset, so it does not prevent re-pushing an already-visited sub-IFD; this is contained by the splay-tree entry dedupe at lines 612-614, so no loop blowup is reachable within the shown code.

EXIF multiple-value and payload loops iterate up to components times, which scales with profile size; this is inherent resource usage proportional to a bounded input, not a distinct algorithmic-complexity finding.

verdict.summary: setup_seccomp checks the seccomp_rule_add() return with `if (r < 0 && r == -EFAULT)` at lines 218 and 236, which is equivalent to `r == -EFAULT` since -EFAULT > 0. The guard aborts only on -EFAULT (the one case the comment marks as tolerable 'unknown syscall'); every other negative return (e.g. -EINVAL, -ENOMEM, -E2BIG) is silently swallowed, so a failed blocklist rule is omitted while the code exports (line 267), installs (lines 272-273) and reports success (line 275). Under the default-ALLOW policy from seccomp_init (line 147, SCMP_ACT_ALLOW) the syscall stays permitted, shipping an incomplete seccomp filter (CWE-754).

evidence.reason: r is the int return of seccomp_rule_add() (lines 215/217) whose residual range after this guard retains {r < 0 && r != -EFAULT} (e.g. -EINVAL, -ENOMEM); since -EFAULT > 0 the guard equals `r == -EFAULT` and admits every other failure onto the continuation path. The rule is never re-checked or re-added, and execution proceeds to seccomp_export_bpf (line 267), filter installation (lines 272-273) and return TRUE (line 275), installing an incomplete default-ALLOW (line 147, SCMP_ACT_ALLOW) filter in which the blocklisted syscall remains permitted - primary CWE-754, improper check of the exceptional non-EFAULT error condition caused by the inverted comparison operator (contrast the correct `r != -EEXIST` pattern at lines 187/195).

Same mis-handled return-status guard for the nondevel blocklist: r from seccomp_rule_add() (lines 232/234) keeps the full {r < 0 && r != -EFAULT} subset after this check, so a failed rule for perf_event_open/personality/ptrace (lines 123-126) is silently ignored while the loop, export (line 267), install (lines 272-273) and return TRUE (line 275) complete - CWE-754 again, leaving the syscall unblocked under the SCMP_ACT_ALLOW default (line 147).

assumptions: Line 144 (`int i, r;`) makes r the int return value of the libseccomp calls.
Line 147 (`seccomp_init (SCMP_ACT_ALLOW)`) establishes a default-ALLOW policy, so a skipped block rule leaves the syscall permitted.
G_N_ELEMENTS at lines 207/224/245 bounds loop indices to the compile-time table sizes.
limitations: The confirmed finding's witness is a range (any r < 0 with r != -EFAULT) because the shown code cannot force a specific errno from seccomp_rule_add; confidence is therefore capped at 0.62 rather than the exact-witness band.
seccomp_rule_add_exact return values (lines 257, 262) are deliberately ignored per the comment at lines 241-243; treated as documented best-effort, not a confirmed flaw.
lseek (line 270) return is unchecked; the failure is environmental and its consequence depends on how the child consumes the fd, which is not shown.
bwrap is not NULL-checked before line 272, but it is only passed through to flatpak_bwrap_add_args_data_fd and never dereferenced in this fragment.
The sentinel loop at line 192 terminates only if the external arrays seccomp_x86_64_extra_arches / seccomp_aarch64_extra_arches are 0-terminated; those arrays are not shown.
arch is assumed NUL-terminated by the caller for the strcmp tests at lines 156-174; the fragment performs no buffer operation on arch.
Socket-family allowlist logic (lines 244-262) was traced for all CANBUS/BLUETOOTH flag combinations and blocks families 17-31 correctly; no gap was found.

verdict.summary: No confirmed vulnerability. All input-derived sizes flow into allocations or copies with exactly matching capacities: the GLOB_MARK append uses len = strlen+2 for a 2-byte strcpy write ending at len-1 (lines 849, 858); the gl_offs vector is guarded at line 41 so (gl_offs+1)*sizeof(char*) cannot wrap and the init loop at 49-50 writes exactly gl_offs+1 slots; both vector-append paths are guarded at 594/742 before realloc of (newcount+2) slots with writes only at newcount and newcount+1; the GLOB_BRACE buffer (pattern_len = strlen-1, line 91) is provably large enough for every alternative by the shown arithmetic; tilde and user-name concatenations copy exactly their allocation sizes. No injection, crypto, or authn/authz sinks are present.

assumptions: sizeof(char*) used symbolically in the overflow guards; on a 64-bit target it is 8, and the guards (41, 594, 742) leave the products exactly <= SIZE_MAX in both symbolic and concrete form.

glob_in_dir/prefix_array/is_dir (unshown helpers) return non-NULL heap strings appended into pglob's vector; used only to confirm that vector entries read at 846-860 are non-NULL, not to establish any capacity.
getpwnam_r/getlogin_r standard contracts (return 0 implies *result / s.data is valid) are relied on only to reject the line 376 NULL-deref candidate.
The recursive glob call at 675-679 initializes dirs via the same visible init block at lines 32-36 (flags lack GLOB_APPEND/GLOB_DOOFFS), so globfree(&dirs) paths are safe.
limitations: line 376 (strdup(p->pw_dir) after err==0): a non-conforming getpwnam_r that returned 0 with p==NULL would NULL-deref, but no shown path produces that state; robustness concern only, no CWE.
dirlen+2 (613) and home_len+dirlen (421) could wrap only for strings no smaller than ~SIZE_MAX, which cannot exist in a real address space; demoted as environment-impossible.

Deep GLOB_BRACE nesting recurses with per-frame alloca up to O(n^2) stack for a pattern of length n; a DoS-by-stack-exhaustion claim needs an unshown stack-size invariant and an unshown caller feeding attacker patterns, so it is recorded here without a CWE.
GLOB_NOSPACE from the recursive glob at 680-686 can leak dirs.gl_pathv (no globfree on that path); a single-shot leak that does not compound with attacker-controlled volume, so not a finding.

No sinks exist in the fragment for format-string, command, SQL/NoSQL, log, header, SSRF, XSS, or weak-crypto classes; file-system behavior is delegated to unshown glob_in_dir whose string arguments are in-domain.
